It may be masculine or feminine without restriction — contrary to those who made distinctions: its masculine is with regard to "the affair" and "the matter", and its feminine with regard to "the story", so you say: «هي زيدٌ قائمٌ». It is not made dual or plural, and it is not omitted except in places that will be mentioned, if Allah the Exalted wills. The Kufans call it "the pronoun of the unknown" (ḍamīr al-majhūl), and it has many rulings.
The second view: that «هو» is also the ḍamīr al-shaʾn and «مُحَرَّمٌ» is its khabar, [and «إخراجُهم» is nominative] as the object whose agent is not named [i.e. nāʾib fāʿil]. This is the doctrine of the Kufans, and al-Mahdawī followed them. They fled from the first view only because according to them [a khabar bearing a] nominative [pronoun] may not be fronted before the mubtadaʾ, so one does not say «قائمٌ زيدٌ» with «قائمٌ» as a fronted khabar. According to the Basrans this is [disallowed, for what you have learned: that the ḍamīr] al-shaʾn is explained only by a clause, and a derived noun governing a nominative after it belongs to the category of single words, not clauses, so the ḍamīr al-shaʾn is not explained by it.
The third: that «هو» refers to the expulsion, being a mubtadaʾ, «مُحَرَّمٌ» its khabar, and «إخراجُهم» a badal (substitute) from it. This is on one of two views, namely [the permissibility of substituting an overt noun for] a pronoun preceding it so as to explain it. Those who allowed that cited his saying:
596 - على حالةٍ لَوْ أنَّ في القومِ حاتِماً ... على جُودِه لَضَنَّ بالماءِ حاتِمِ
(In a state in which, were Ḥātim among the people, despite his generosity Ḥātim would have been stingy with water.)
So «حاتم» is a badal from the pronoun in «جودِه».
The fourth: that «هو» is the pronoun of the expulsion indicated by His saying «وتُخْرِجون», «مُحَرَّمٌ» its khabar, and «إخراجُهم» a badal from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in «مُحَرَّمٌ».
The fifth: the same, except that «إخراجُهم» is a badal from «هو». Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted these two views. This last one is questionable, because if you make «هو» the pronoun of the expulsion indicated by the verb, the pronoun is explained by it, as in {اعدلوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ} [al-Māʾida: 8]; then if you substitute for it the uttered «إخراجُهم», it is explained by that as well, so it would have to be explained by two things — unless it is said that these two things are in reality one thing, in which case it may be tolerated.
The sixth: the Kufans allowed «هو» to be an ʿimād (support), which the Basrans call the pronoun of separation (ḍamīr al-faṣl), fronted together with the khabar for the reason mentioned; the underlying order is: «وإخراجُهم هو مُحَرَّمٌ عليكم», so «إخراجُهم» is a mubtadaʾ, «مُحَرَّم» its khabar, and «هو» an ʿimād; when the khabar was fronted, it was fronted with it.
Al-Farrāʾ said: "Because the wāw here seeks a noun, and every place where it seeks a noun, the ʿimād is permissible." According to the Basrans this is disallowed for two reasons. The first: for them a condition of the faṣl is that it occur between two definite nouns, or between a definite noun and an indefinite one close to the definite in not admitting «أل», such as «أفعل من» and «مثل» and its sisters. The second: for them the faṣl may not be fronted together with what is attached to it. These views have places where they are investigated.
The seventh: Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It was said of «هو» that it is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-amr), the implied form being: 'and the matter is forbidden to you,' and «إخراجُهم» on this view is a badal from «هو»." End quote. The Shaykh said: "This is a mistake for two reasons. The first: explaining the pronoun of the matter by a single word, which neither a Basran nor a Kufan allows — the Basran because he stipulates a clause, and the Kufan because the single word must form, together with what follows it, something predicated of in meaning, as in «ظَنَنْتُه قائماً الزيدان». The second: he made «إخراجُهم» a badal from the pronoun of the matter, and it has preceded that it is not followed by an appositive."
The eighth: Ibn ʿAṭiyya also said: "It was said that «هو» is a separator (fāṣila) — this is the doctrine of the Kufans — and it is not here one that is an ʿimād; on this view «مُحَرَّم» is a mubtadaʾ and «اخراجُهم» a khabar." The Shaykh said: "What is transmitted from the Kufans is the reverse of this parsing, i.e. «إخراجُهم» is a delayed mubtadaʾ and «مُحَرَّم» a fronted khabar, the faṣl having been fronted with it as has passed; that is what agrees with the rules, and it avoids entailing the predication of a definite noun of an indefinite one without a necessity calling for it."
The ninth: Ibn ʿAṭiyya also transmitted from some that «هو» is the pronoun implied in «مُحَرَّم», fronted and made overt. The Shaykh said: "This is very weak, since there is no necessity calling for this pronoun to be detached after being latent and to be fronted. Also, it entails the passive participle being devoid of a pronoun, since on this view «مُحَرَّم» is a fronted khabar and «إخراجُهم» a mubtadaʾ, and no active or passive participle is found devoid of a pronoun except when it governs an overt noun in the nominative. Then this pronoun remains, and we do not know what its parsing is, since it can be neither a mubtadaʾ nor a fronted fāʿil." In the Shaykh's saying "it entails its being devoid of a pronoun" there is room for objection, since it is a pronoun made nominative by it, so it is not devoid of it; the most that can be said is that it became detached because of being fronted. And his saying "we do not know what its parsing is": it is known — it is nominative as fāʿil. His saying "and the fāʿil is not fronted" is not conceded, for the Kufan allows fronting the fāʿil, so it is possible that this speaker holds that view. There is no doubt that this is a poor, objectionable view, the like of which should not be allowed in [ordinary] speech, so how [could it be] in the Quran!! So the Shaykh is excused, and I am amazed at al-Qāḍī Abū Muḥammad [Ibn ʿAṭiyya], how he adduces these things, relating them, without following them with any disapproval.
This clause may be [understood as] omitted from the clauses mentioned before it, for four things have been mentioned, all of them forbidden, namely His saying: «تَقْتُلون أنفسَكم», «وتُخْرِجُون», «وتُظاهرون», «وتُفادون»; so the implied form would be: "you kill yourselves while killing them is forbidden to you," and likewise with the rest. And it may be that He singled out the expulsion with mention of the prohibition, even though all of them are forbidden, because of the disgrace of exile and banishment it involves, whose evil is cut off only by death; and killing, though graver than it, involves cutting off the evil. So expulsion from homes is the hardest of the four in this respect.
«المُحَرَّمُ» means "the forbidden", for «الحرام» [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense is the act of prohibiting] is preventing from something, and «الحَرام» is the thing from which one is prevented; one says: «حَرامٌ عليك» and «حَرَمٌ عليك». Its verification will come in [Sūrat] al-Anbiyāʾ.
His saying: {فَمَا جَزَآءُ مَن يَفْعَلُ}: two views are permissible regarding «ما». The first: that it is negating, «جزاء» a mubtadaʾ, and «إلاَّ خِزْيٌ» its khabar, this being an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh); the governing effect of «ما» according to the Ḥijāzīs is cancelled because the negation is broken by «إلاَّ». There is a long disagreement and extensive detail on this, the summary of which is that regarding its khabar occurring after «إلاَّ», the majority of the Basrans hold that it must be nominative without restriction, whether it is the first [noun] itself, or treated as such, or an adjective, or not; and they interpret his saying:
597 - وما الدهرُ إلاَّ مَنْجَنُوناً بأَهْلِه ... وما صاحبُ الحاجاتِ إلاَّ مُعَذِّبَا
(Time is nothing but a water-wheel turning with its people, and the one with needs is nothing but tormented.)
[Translator's note: the source prints the verse number as «59 - 7-».] as meaning that what makes «مَنْجَنوناً» and «مُعَذَّباً» accusative is omitted, i.e. "it turns the turning of a water-wheel" and "he is tormented with torment." Yūnus allowed the accusative without restriction, although al-Naḥḥās transmitted that there is no disagreement over the nominative in «ما زيدٌ إلا أخوك». If the second is treated as the first, as in «ما أنت إلا عِمامَتك تحسيناً وإلاَّ رِداءَك ترتيباً» ("you are nothing but your turban in beauty and your cloak in arrangement"), the Kufans allowed the accusative; and if it is an adjective, as in «ما زيدٌ إلا قائمٌ», al-Farrāʾ also allowed the accusative. The second: that it is interrogative, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, «جزاء» its khabar, and {إِلاَّ خِزْيٌ} a badal from «جَزَآءُ»; Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted it. «مَنْ» is a relative noun or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, and «يفعلُ» has no grammatical position on the first, and its position is genitive on the second.
His saying: «منكم» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «يفعل», so it is attached to an omitted [word], i.e. he does that while being one of you.
His saying: {فِي الحياة}: two views are permissible in it. The first: that it is in the position of nominative because it is a naʿt (adjective) of «خزي», so it is attached to an omitted [word], i.e. a disgrace existing in the life. The second: that its position is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf) of «الخِزْي», so it is accusative by it in implied terms.
«الجَزاء» is requital, whether good or evil. «الخِزْيُ» is abasement; one says «خَزِيَ» with kasra, «يخزى خِزْياً», so he is «خَزْيانُ», a woman «خَزْيا», and the plural is «خَزايا». Ibn al-Sikkīt said: "«الخِزْيُ» is falling into affliction; and «خَزِيَ الرجلُ في نفسِه يَخْزَى خَزَايَةً» when he is ashamed."
«الدُّنْيا» is on the pattern «فُعْلَى», the feminine of «الأدْنى», from «الدُنُوِّ», which is nearness; its alif is for the feminine, and «أل» is not dropped from it except by poetic necessity, as in his saying:
598 - يومَ ترى النفوسُ مَا أعَدَّتِ ... في سَعْي دُنْيَا طالمَا قد مُدَّتِ
(On the day when souls see what they prepared in the striving of a world that was long extended.)
Its yāʾ is from a wāw, and this is a regular rule: every «فُعْلَى» that is an adjective whose final radical is wāw has [the wāw] changed to yāʾ, as in «العُلْيَا» and «الدُّنْيا». As for their saying «القُصْوى» among those other than Tamīm, and «الحُلْوى» among all, it is anomalous. If «فُعْلى» is a noun, the wāw remains sound, as in his saying:
599 - أداراً بحزوى هِجْتِ للعَيْنِ عَبْرَةً ... فماءُ الهوى يَرْفَضُّ أو يَتَرَقْرَقُ
(O abode at Ḥuzwā, you have stirred a tear in the eye, so the water of passion pours down or glistens.)
It [«الدنيا»] has been used as nouns are used, so its qualified noun is not mentioned; He the Exalted said: {تُرِيدُونَ عَرَضَ الدنيا} [al-Anfāl: 67]. Ibn al-Sarrāj said in «al-Maqṣūr wa-l-Mamdūd»: "«الدُّنْيا» is feminine, shortened (maqṣūr), written with alif; this is the dialect of Najd and Tamīm. However, the Ḥijāz and Banū Asad join it and its like to the maṣdars having wāw, saying «دَنْوَى» like «شَرْوى»; and they do likewise with every «فُعْلى» whose final radical is wāw: they give its first letter fatḥa and change its yāʾ into wāw. As for the people of the first dialect, they give the dāl a ḍamma and change the wāw into yāʾ, because they find the wāw with the ḍamma heavy."
«يُرَدُّون» was read in the third person according to the well-known [reading]. There are two views on it. The first: that it is iltifāt (a shift of person), so it refers back to His saying «أفتؤمنون», having moved from the second-person pronoun to the third person. The second: that there is no iltifāt in it; rather it refers back to His saying «مَنْ يفعَل». Al-Ḥasan read «تُرَدُّون» in the second person, and the two preceding views apply to it: iltifāt with regard to His saying «مَنْ يفعل», and no iltifāt with regard to His saying «أفتؤمنون».
Likewise {وَمَا الله بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ} was read, among the well-known readings, in the third person and in the second person, and the discussion of both is as preceded.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
The words of the Exalted: {الذي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ}: «الذي» may be accusative or nominative.
The accusative is on five views. The most apparent: it is accusative by severance (qaṭʿ). Second: it is a naʿt (adjective) of «ربكم». Third: it is a badal (substitute) from it. Fourth: it is the object of «تتقون»; Abū al-Baqāʾ began with this. Fifth: it is an adjective of the adjective, i.e. of the first relative noun. But the preferred view is that an adjective is not itself qualified; rather, if something occurs that suggests this, it is made an adjective of the first, unless some impediment prevents it, in which case it is an adjective of the adjective, as in their saying «يا أيُّها الفارسُ ذو الجُمَّة» (O horseman with the long locks): «ذو الجُمَّة» is an adjective of «الفارس», not of «أيّ», because «أيّ» is qualified only by what was mentioned earlier.
The nominative is on two views. First, and it is the most correct: it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «هو الذي جَعَلَ» (He is the One who made). Second: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is His words after that, «فلا تَجْعَلُوا». This is questionable from two angles. First: its ṣila (relative clause) is past, so it does not resemble a condition, and the fāʾ is not added in its khabar. Second: the absence of a linking element (rābiṭ) — unless one follows the view of al-Akhfash, which is that the link may be the repetition of an overt noun when it has the same meaning, as in «زيدٌ قام أبو عبد الله» (Zayd — Abū ʿAbd Allāh stood), when Abū ʿAbd Allāh is Zayd's kunya. So here too the Divine Name stands in place of the pronoun, as if He had said: "He who made for you — do not set up rivals to Him."
«جَعَل» has two views. First: it is in the sense of «صَيَّر» (to make into), so it takes two objects: «الأرضُ» is the first object and «فراشاً» the second. Second: it is in the sense of «خَلَقَ» (to create), so it takes one object, namely «الأرضَ», and «فراشاً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
«والسماء بِنَآءً» is conjoined to «الأرض فراشاً» on both of the above analyses. «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the making, i.e. for your sake. الفراش is what is trodden and sat upon. البِنَاء is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of بَنَيْتُ; the yāʾ was changed into hamza only because it came at the end after an extra alif. It may be meant in the sense of the passive participle.
«أَنْزل» is conjoined to «جَعَلَ», and «من السماء» is attached to it; «مِن» is for the beginning of an extent. It may also be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «ماء», because when an adjective of an indefinite noun is placed before it, it becomes accusative as a ḥāl; in that case its meaning is partitive, and there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. «من مِياه السماءِ ماءً» (water from the waters of the sky).
The origin of «ماء» is مَوَه, as shown by their saying «ماهَتِ الرَّكِيَّةُ تَمُوه» (the well abounded in water), and by its plurals مياه and أَمْواه and its diminutive مُوَيْه. The yāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; on the stated origin مَوَه the letter concerned is the wāw] was vowelled with a fatḥa before it, so it was changed into alif. Then two "hidden" (khafī) letters met, the alif and the hāʾ, so they replaced the hāʾ with its sister, the hamza, because it is sturdier.
His words «فَأَخْرَجَ» are conjoined to «أَنْزَل», following upon it; «به» is attached to it, and the bāʾ in it is causal. «من الثمرات» is also attached to it, and «مِن» here is partitive.
Whoever made it redundant (zāʾida) went far astray, for two reasons. First: its being redundant in an affirmative context, and the noun it governs being definite — no Basran or Kufan holds this except Abū al-Ḥasan al-Akhfash. Second: it would mean that all fruits are provision for us, which contradicts reality, since many fruits are not provision. Al-Zamakhsharī made it explicative of the genus (li-bayān al-jins); this is questionable, since nothing precedes for it to explain — as if he meant that it explains «رزقاً» in meaning. «رزقاً» is apparently a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), governed by «أَخْرَجَ».
It is also possible that «من الثمرات» is in the position of the direct object, the implied form being «فأخرجَ ببعض الماء بعضَ الثمرات» (He brought forth by some of the water some of the fruits). In that case «رزقاً» has two views. First: it is a ḥāl, «الرزق» being in the sense of «المرزوق» (that which is provided), like الطِّحْن (flour, i.e. what is ground) and الرِّعْي (pasture, i.e. what is grazed). Second: it is a maṣdar, accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), the conditions for its being accusative being present.
«ماء» and «رزقاً» were made indefinite only to convey partition, because the meaning is: He sent down from the sky some water, and brought forth by it some fruits as some provision for you — since all their provision is not some of the fruits; that is only part of their provision.
Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted «من الثمراتِ» to be a ḥāl of «رزقاً», because had it come after it, it would have been an adjective; on this view it is attached to an omitted element. Al-Zamakhsharī made «من الثمرات» stand in the place of «الثمر» or «الثمار», meaning that it is a case of a plural of paucity standing in for a plural of multitude, as in {كَمْ تَرَكُواْ مِن جَنَّاتٍ} [al-Dukhān: 25] and {ثَلاَثَةَ قرواء} [al-Baqara: 228]. [Translator's note: so in the source; the Qur'anic wording is «ثَلَاثَةَ قُرُوءٍ».] There is no need for this, because a sound plural with the definite article of generality applies to multitude, so there is then no difference between «الثمرات» and «الثمار». For this reason the verifying scholars rejected the view of whoever criticised Ḥassān ibn Thābit, may Allah be pleased with him, for his line:
265 - لَنَا الجَفَنَاتُ الغُرُّ يَلْمَعْنَ في الضُّحى ... وأسيافُنا يَقْطُرْنَ من نَجْدةٍ دَما
(Ours are the bright bowls gleaming in the forenoon, and our swords drip blood out of valour.)
They said: he should have said «الجِفان» and «وسيوفُنا» [the plurals of multitude], because that is more laudatory. That is not correct, for the reason I have mentioned to you.
«لكم» may be attached to «أَخْرَج», or attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «رِزْقاً» — this if «الرزق» means "what is provided". If it means the maṣdar, then the kāf in «لكم» may be the object of the maṣdar, with the lām strengthening it, as in «ضربت ابني تأديباً له» (I struck my son to discipline him), i.e. «تأديبَه».
The words of the Exalted: {فَلاَ تَجْعَلُواْ للَّهِ أَندَاداً}: the fāʾ is causal: the prohibition of your taking rivals is caused by the bringing into being of these dazzling signs. «لا» is prohibitive, and «تَجْعلوا» is jussive (majzūm) by it, the sign of its being jussive being the dropping of the nūn. Here it is in the sense of «تُصَيِّروا» (to make into). Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it to be in the sense of «تُسَمُّوا» (to name). On both views it takes two objects: the first «أنداداً», and the second the preposition and its genitive noun before it, which must be placed first.
«أنداداً» is the plural of «نِدّ». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«أَنْدَاداً» is the plural of «نِد» and «نَديد»." His making it the plural of «نديد» is questionable, because أَفْعال is not attested as a plural of فَعيل in the sense of فاعل, except as in شَريف / أَشْراف, and it is not taken as a basis for analogy.
النِّدّ is the one who resists and rivals, whether it be [a like], an opposite or a contrary. It was said: it is the opposite — from Abū ʿUbayda. It was also said: the equal and the like; Ḥassān said:
266 - أَتَهْجُوه ولستَ له بِنِدٍّ ... فشرُّكما لخيركما الفِداءُ
(Do you satirise him when you are no match for him? May the worse of you two be ransom for the better!)
i.e. you are not his equal (kufʾ); and it has been transmitted so [with «بكُفْءٍ»]. Another said:
267 - نَحْمَدُ الله ولا نِدَّ له ... عندَه الخيرُ وما شاءَ فَعَلْ
(We praise Allah, who has no rival; with Him is all good, and what He wills He does.)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "النِّدّ is the like, and it is said only of a like who opposes. Jarīr said:
268 - أَتَيْماً تَجْعَلونَ إليَّ نِدَّاً ... وما تَيْمٌ لذي حَسَبٍ نَدِيدُ
(Do you make Taym a rival to me? Taym is no rival to a man of noble lineage.)
نادَدْتُ الرجلَ means I opposed him and contended with him, from نَدَّ يَنِدُّ نُدُوداً, i.e. to bolt." End of quotation. One also says «نَديدة», for intensiveness; Labīd said:
269 - لِكيلا يكونَ السَّنْدَرِيُّ نديدتي ... وأَجْعَلُ أَقْواماً عُموماً عَماعِمَا
(Lest al-Sandarī be my rival, and I make whole tribes into scattered bands.)
As for النَّدّ with fatḥa on the nūn, it is a high hillock; النَّدّ is also a perfume, and is not Arabic.
This clause is connected in meaning to His words «اعبدُوا», because the root of worship is affirming Oneness (tawḥīd). It may also be connected to «الذي» if you make it the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. He is the One who made for you these mighty signs and luminous proofs that testify to Oneness, so do not set up rivals to Him.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is connected to «لعلَّكم», on the basis that «تجعلوا» is accusative as {فَأَطَّلِعَ} [Ghāfir: 37] is accusative in the reading of Ḥafṣ, i.e. He created you that you might be God-fearing and fear His punishment, and so not liken Him to His creation." On his view, «لا» is negating, and the verb after it is accusative by an implied «أَنْ» in answer to the expression of hope (tarajjī). The Basrans do not permit this. The interpretation of «فأطَّلِع» and its parallels will come in its place, if Allah the Exalted wills.
The words of the Exalted: {وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ}: a clause consisting of a mubtadaʾ and khabar, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. The object of «العِلْم» (knowing) is left out, because the meaning is: you are among the people of knowledge; or it was omitted for brevity, i.e. you know the falsity of that.
As for the noun in «أنتم»: it was said that it is «أَنْ», and the tāʾ is a particle of address that varies according to the one addressed. It was also said: rather, the tāʾ is the noun, and «أَنْ» is a support (ʿimād) before it. It was also said: rather, the whole is a pronoun, a detached nominative pronoun. The rule of its mīm with regard to sukūn, vowelling, lengthening (ishbāʿ) and shortening (ikhtilās) is the rule of the mīm of «هم»; all of that has been treated before.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
The saying of the Exalted: {وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لاَ تُفْسِدُواْ فِي الأرض}: the verse. «إذا» is an adverb of future time, and it usually carries the meaning of a condition. It is used only for something certain or whose occurrence is preponderant; for that reason it does not put [the verb] in the jussive except in poetry, since it differs from the conditional particles, which are for something merely possible. Among instances of the jussive is the poet's saying:
182 - تَرفعُ لي خِنْدِفٌ واللهُ يَرْفَعُ لي ... ناراً إذا خَمَدَتْ نيرانُهم تَقِدِ
(Khindif raises for me — and Allah raises for me — a fire which, when their fires die down, blazes.)
Another said:
183 - واستَغْنِ ما أغناك ربُّك بالغِنى ... تُصِبْكَ خَصَاصةٌ فَتَجَمَّلِ
(Be content with wealth as long as your Lord enriches you; [and when] want befalls you, bear it with dignity.)
[Translator's note: the verse as quoted here lacks «وإذا» before «تُصِبْكَ», which is the word that makes it an example of jussive after «إذا».]
And another's saying:
184 - إذا قَصُرَتْ أسيافُنا كان وصلُها ... خُطانا إلى أعدائِنا فَنُضَارِبِ
(When our swords fall short, their extension is our steps towards our enemies, and so we fight.)
His saying «فَنُضَارِبِ» is jussive because it is conjoined to the position of his saying «كان وصلُها». Al-Farazdaq said:
185 - فقام أبو ليلى إليه ابنُ ظَالمٍ ... وكان إذا ما يَسْلُلِ السيفَ يَضْرِبِ
(So Abū Laylā, Ibn Ẓālim, rose up to him; and whenever he drew the sword, he would strike.)
It may be for past time, like «إذ», just as «إذ» may be for the future, like «إذا». It is also used for surprise (al-mufājaʾa); in that case, does it remain a time adverb, or does it become an adverb of place, or a particle? There are three views, the soundest being the first, by presumption of continuity (istiṣḥāb al-ḥāl). Is it declinable in function (mutaṣarrifa) or not? The apparent view is that it is not. The one who claimed that it is adduced as evidence the saying of the Exalted, in the reading of whoever read: {إِذَا وَقَعَتِ الواقعة لَيْسَ لِوَقْعَتِهَا كَاذِبَةٌ خَافِضَةً رَّافِعَةً إِذَا رُجَّتِ الأرض رَجّاً} [al-Wāqiʿa: 1-4], with {خَافِضَةً رَّافِعَةً} in the accusative: he made the first «إذا» a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the second its khabar (predicate), the implied sense being: "the time of the occurrence of the Event is the time of the shaking of the earth." [He also adduced] His saying: {حتى إِذَا جَآءُوهَا} [al-Zumar: 71] and {حتى إِذَا كُنتُمْ} [Yūnus: 22], making «حتى» a preposition and «إذا» genitive by it. The verification of that will come in its places. It is put in construct only with verbal clauses, contrary to al-Akhfash.
The saying of the Exalted: «قيل» is a past verb, passive. Its original form is «قُوِلَ», like «ضُرِبَ»; the kasra was found heavy on the wāw, so it was transferred to the qāf after its own vowel was removed; then the wāw became unvowelled after a kasra, so it was changed to yāʾ. This is the most eloquent of the dialectal forms. There is a second form in it, namely ishmām, and ishmām is an expression for making the vowel between ḍamma and kasra; and a third form, namely pure ḍamma, as in «قُوْلَ» and «بُوعَ»; the poet said:
186 - ليت وهل يَنْفَع شيئاً ليتُ ... ليت شباباً بُوْعَ فاشتريْتُ
(Would that — and does "would that" avail anything? — would that youth were sold [būʿa], so that I could buy it.)
Another said:
187 - حُوكَتْ على نِيْرَيْنِ إذ تُحاكُ ... تَخْتَبِطَ الشَّوْكَ ولا تُشَاكُ
(It was woven [ḥūkat] on two warp-threads when it was woven; it beats through thorns and is not pricked.)
Al-Akhfash said: "And «قُيْل» is permitted, with ḍamma on the qāf and the yāʾ", meaning with the yāʾ, not that the yāʾ also takes ḍamma. These three forms occur in «اختار», «انقاد», «رَدَّ», «حَبَّ» and the like; so you say «اختير» with kasra and with ishmām, and «اختُور»; likewise «انقيد» and «انقُود», and «رُدَّ» and «رِدَّ»; and they recited:
188 - وما حِلَّ مِنْ جَهْلٍ حُبا حُلَمائِنا ... ولا قائِلُ المعروفِ فينا يُعنَّفُ
(The sitting-cloths of our forbearing men are never loosed [ḥilla] out of folly, nor is one among us who speaks what is right rebuked.)
— with kasra on the ḥāʾ of «حِلَّ». And «ولو رِدُّوا» was read with kasra on the rāʾ. The rule for the verb whose agent is not named is that the first letter of the verb takes ḍamma absolutely; then, if it is past, the letter before the last takes kasra, either overtly, as in «ضُرِب», or by implication (taqdīran), as in «قِيلَ» and «اخْتِير»; and if it is imperfect, it takes fatḥa, overtly, as in «يُضْرَبُ», or by implication, as in «يُقال» and «يُختار». The second letter of the past may also take ḍamma if it begins with the tāʾ of reflexivity (muṭāwaʿa), as in «تُدُحْرج الحجرُ» ("the stone was rolled"), and the third if it begins with a connective hamza (hamzat waṣl), as in «انطُلِق بزيدٍ» ("Zayd was taken off").
Know that the condition for permitting the three forms in «قيل», «غيض» and the like is that it not cause ambiguity; if it causes ambiguity, one acts according to what avoids ambiguity. Thus some said, although Sībawayh permitted that without restriction. Al-Kisāʾī read with ishmām: {قيل} [al-Baqara: 11], {وغيض} [Hūd: 44], {وجيء} [al-Zumar: 69], {وحيل بينهم} [Sabaʾ: 54], {وسيق الذين} [al-Zumar: 71], {وسيىء بهم} [Hūd: 77] and {وسيئت وجوهُ} [al-Mulk: 27]. Hishām agreed with him in all of them, Ibn Dhakwān in «حيل» and what follows it, and Nāfiʿ in «سيئ» and «سيئَتْ»; the rest read with pure kasra in all of them. Ishmām has four meanings in the terminology of the Qur'an readers; that will come in [Sūrat] Yūsuf, if Allah the Exalted wills, at {مَا لَكَ لاَ تَأْمَنَّا} [Yūsuf: 11], for it is more fitting there.
«لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to «قيل»; the lām is for conveying (al-tablīgh). «لا» is a particle of prohibition that puts one verb in the jussive; «تُفْسِدوا» is jussive (majzūm) by it, the sign of its jussive being the omission of the nūn, because it is one of the five verb forms (al-amthila al-khamsa); and «في الأرضِ» is attached to it. What stands in place of the fāʿil (agent) [i.e. the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)] is the clause «لا تُفْسِدوا», because it is what is said in meaning; Abū al-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī chose this. The implied sense is: "and when this speech, or this utterance, is said to them"; so it is of the type of verbal predication (al-isnād al-lafẓī). It was also said: what stands in place of the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being: "and when it [a saying] is said to them"; and this latent pronoun is explained by the context of the speech, just as it explained it in His saying: {حتى تَوَارَتْ بالحجاب} [Ṣād: 32]. The meaning is: "and when a sound saying is said to them"; this qualified saying was made latent, and the clause after it came explicative, so it has no grammatical position. He said: "When semantic predication (al-isnād al-maʿnawī) is possible, one does not turn to verbal predication, and that is possible by what has preceded." Abū al-Baqāʾ preceded him in this view, for he said: "The object standing in place of the agent is a maṣdar (verbal noun), namely 'the saying', and it was made latent because the clause after it explains it; and it is not permitted for «لا تُفْسِدوا» to stand in place of the agent, because a clause cannot be an agent, so it cannot stand in place of an agent" — end of quote. The answer to that has preceded, namely that the meaning is: "and when this utterance is said to them". It is not permitted for «لهم» to stand in place of the agent except in the opinion of the Kufans and al-Akhfash, since according to them it is permitted to make something other than the direct object stand [in place of the agent] while a direct object is present. It is summed up from this that the clause «لا تُفْسدوا» is in the position of the nominative according to al-Zamakhsharī's view, and has no position according to the view of Abū al-Baqāʾ and those who followed him. The clause «قيل» and what falls within its scope is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being put in construct with it. What governs «إذا», according to the majority, is its apodosis (jawāb), namely «قالوا»; the implied sense being: "they said, 'We are only reformers,' at the time of the one saying to them, 'Do not cause corruption.'" [Translator's note: «وقتَ القائل لهم» presumably stands for «وقتَ قولِ القائل لهم», "at the time of the saying of the one who says to them".] Some said: "What we choose is that the clause that comes after it and follows it puts it in the accusative, and that what follows it is not in the position of the genitive by construct, because it is a conditional particle; so its ruling is the ruling of the adverbs used for conditional requital. Just as when you say «متى تقمْ أقمْ» ("whenever you stand, I stand"), «متى» is accusative by the verb of the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), so likewise «إذا»."
This speaker said: "What invalidates the doctrine of the majority is the permissibility of your saying «إذا قمت فعمورٌ قائمٌ» ("when you stand, then ʿAmr is standing") [Translator's note: «فعمورٌ» is a typo for «فعمرٌو»], and the occurrence of the «إذا» of surprise as its apodosis; for what follows the fāʾ and the «إذا» of surprise does not govern what precedes them." This is a clear objection.
His saying: {إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُصْلِحُونَ}: «إنَّ» is a particle restrained (makfūf) from governing by the redundant «ما»; for that reason a clause of any kind may follow it. It conveys restriction (al-ḥaṣr) according to some. Far off the mark is whoever claimed that «إنما» is compounded from the «إنَّ» of affirmation and the «ما» of negation, and that through the compounding a meaning arose that conveys restriction. Know that when the redundant «ما» follows «إنَّ» and its sisters, their governing is cancelled and their being specific to nouns goes away, as has passed — except «ليت», in which both treatments are permitted on the basis of what is heard. They recited the saying of al-Nābigha:
189 - قالتْ ألا ليتما هذا الحمامَُ لنا ... إلى حمامتِنا ونصفَُهُ فَقَدِ
(She said: "Would that these doves were ours, added to our dove, together with half of them — and that is enough.")
— with «الحمام» in the nominative and the accusative. Its governing is because its specificity [to nouns] remains, and its non-governing is by analogy with its sisters. Moreover, it has been related from Sībawayh concerning the verse that it is governing on the nominative reading as well, by making «ما» a relative meaning «الذي», like that in the saying of the Exalted: {إِنَّمَا صَنَعُواْ كَيْدُ سَاحِرٍ} [Ṭāhā: 69], with «هذا» the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ which is the referent, «الحَمام» a naʿt (adjective) of «هذا», and «لنا» the khabar of «ليت»; the referent is omitted even though the ṣila (relative clause) is not long. The implied sense is: "Would that that which is these doves were ours." This is better than claiming that it is not governing, because what requires governing — namely specificity — remains. Some claimed that when the redundant «ما» is attached to «إنَّ» and its sisters, governing is permitted in all of them.
«نحن» is a mubtadaʾ; it is a detached nominative pronoun for the speaker and those with him, or for one who magnifies himself. «مصلحون» is its khabar, and the clause is in the position of the accusative because it is quoted by «قالوا». The conditional clause, namely His saying «وإذا قيلَ لهم», is conjoined to the ṣila of «مَنْ», which is «يقولُ», i.e. "and among people is he who says, and among people is he who, when it is said to them, 'Do not cause corruption in the land,' they say …". It was also said: it may be resumptive. On these two views it has no grammatical position, for the reason given earlier; but it is part of a sentence on the first view and an independent sentence on the second. Al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it to be conjoined to «يَكْذِبُون», which is the khabar of «كانوا», so that its position is the accusative. Some refuted them on the grounds that what they permitted, on one of the two possibilities of «ما» in His saying {بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْذِبُونَ} — namely its being a relative meaning «الذي» — is a mistake, since there is no referent in it returning to the relative «ما»; and likewise if it is made maṣdariyya, for it needs a referent according to al-Akhfash and Ibn al-Sarrāj. The answer to this is that they permit that only while believing that «ما» is a particle relative (mawṣūla ḥarfiyya) [i.e. maṣdariyya]; as for the doctrine of al-Akhfash and Ibn al-Sarrāj, they are not bound to hold it. But it poses a difficulty for Abū al-Baqāʾ alone, for he considers «ما» being maṣdariyya weak, as has preceded.

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلاَئِكَةِ}: «إذ» is an adverb (ẓarf) of past time; it restricts the imperfect to the past. It is indeclinable (mabnī) because of its resemblance to a particle in its [minimal] formation and its need [for a complement]. Clauses follow it without restriction; if the clause is verbal, it is ugly to put the noun first and the verb last, e.g. «إذ زيدٍ قام» [Translator's note: so printed, with «زيدٍ» in the genitive; the intended example is presumably «إذ زيدٌ قام» (when Zayd stood)]. It is not declinable [i.e. does not leave the adverbial function] except by having a time-word annexed to it, e.g. «يومئذٍ» and «حينئذٍ». It is not a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), even though most of the parsers hold that, for they construe it as: "Remember the time of such-and-such." Nor is it an adverb of place, nor redundant (zāʾid), nor a particle of causation, nor of surprise (mufājaʾa), contrary to those who claim that. The clause to which it is annexed is sometimes omitted because it is known, and nunation (tanwīn) compensates for it, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {وَأَنتُمْ حِينَئِذٍ تَنظُرُونَ} [al-Wāqiʿa: 84]. In this case its kasra is not a kasra of declension, nor is its nunation the nunation of full declension (tanwīn al-ṣarf), contrary to al-Akhfash; rather, the kasra is for the meeting of two quiescent letters and the nunation is compensatory, as proven by the presence of the kasra where there is no annexation [to it]; he said:
327 - نَهَيْتُكَ عن طِلابِكَ أمَّ عمروٍ ... بعاقبةٍ وأنتَ إذٍ صَحيحُ
(I forbade you from pursuing Umm ʿAmr in the end, when you were then healthy.)
Al-Akhfash may say: its origin is «وأنتَ حينئذٍ», and when the muḍāf was omitted, the muḍāf ilayhi remained as it was and did not take its place, as in {والله يُرِيدُ الآخرة} [al-Anfāl: 67] with the genitive [i.e. read «الآخرةِ»]; but this is weak.
And {قَالَ رَبُّكَ} is a verbal clause in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it.
Know that there are nine aspects regarding «إذ». The best of them is that it is accusative by {قَالُواْ أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا}, i.e. they said that saying at the time of Allah the Exalted's saying to them: "I am placing upon the earth a successor." This is the easiest of the aspects. The second: that it is accusative by an implied «اذكُرْ» (remember); it has preceded that it is not declinable, so it does not occur as an object. The third: that it is accusative by «خَلَقَكم», which preceded in His saying {اتقوا رَبَّكُمُ الذي خَلَقَكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 1] [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse in this sūra is {اعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ} (al-Baqara: 21)], and the wāw is redundant. This is nothing, because of the length of the separation. The fourth: that it is accusative by «قال» after it. This is invalid, because the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern the muḍāf. The fifth: that it is redundant; this is attributed to Abū ʿUbayd. The sixth: that it is in the sense of «قد». The seventh: that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "The beginning of your creation was the time of your Lord's saying." The eighth: that it is accusative by a suitable verb, its implied form being: "Your creation began at the time of His saying that." These two are weak, because the time of the beginning of creation is not the time of the saying; and also because it is not declinable. The ninth: that it is accusative by an implied «أحياكم»; this is also rejected because of the difference of the two times.
«للملائكة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قال», and the lām is for conveying (tablīgh). «ملائكة» is the plural of «مَلَك». There is disagreement about «مَلَك» on six views, and that is because they disagreed about its mīm: is it radical or augmentative? Those who hold it radical disagreed: some of them said: [it is] «مَلَك», its pattern faʿal, from «المُلْك» (dominion), and its plural on the pattern faʿāʾila is anomalous, so the anomaly is in its plural only. Others said: rather, its origin is «مَلأَك», and the hamza in it is augmentative, as in «شَمْأَل»; then the vowel of the hamza was transferred to the lām and the hamza was dropped for lightness, and the plural came according to the original with the augment. These are two views among these [scholars]. Those who hold it augmentative also disagreed. Among them are those who said: it is derived from «أَلَك», i.e. "he sent," so its first radical is a hamza and its second radical a lām; this is indicated by his saying:
328 - أَبْلِغْ أبا دَخْتَنُوسَ مَأْلُكَةً ... غيرَ الذي قد يُقال مِلْكَذِبِ
(Convey to Abū Dakhtanūs a message, other than what may be said of lies.)
Another said:
329 - وغلامٌ أَرْسَلَتْه أمُّه ... بِأَلوكٍ فَبَذَلْنَا ما سَأَلْ
(And a lad whose mother sent him with a message, so we gave what he asked.)
Another said:
330 - أَبْلِغِ النُّعْمانَ عني مَألُكا ... أنَّه قد طالَ حَبْسي وانتظاري
(Convey to al-Nuʿmān from me a message: that my confinement and my waiting have grown long.)
So the origin of «مَلَك» is «مَأْلَك»; then the second radical was moved to the place of the first, and the first to the place of the second, so it became «مَلأَك» on the pattern maʿfal; then the vowel of the hamza was transferred to the lām and the hamza was dropped for lightness, so the pattern of «مَلَك» is maʿal, with the first radical dropped. Among them are those who said: it is derived from «لأَك», i.e. also "he sent," so its first radical is a lām and its second a hamza; then the vowel of the hamza was transferred and it was dropped as has preceded. This is indicated by the fact that this original form has been uttered; he said:
331 - فَلَسْتُ لإِنْسِيٍّ ولكنْ لِمَلأَكٍ ... تَنَزَّلَ من جَوِّ السماء يَصُوبُ
(You are not of a human, but of an angel who descended from the vault of the sky, swooping down.)
Then the plural came according to the original, so the hamza was restored on both views. The pattern of «ملائِكَة» on this view is mafāʿila, and on the view before it maʿāfila, by metathesis.
It has also been said: it is derived from «لاكَه يَلُوكه», i.e. he turned it about [in the mouth], because the angel turns the message about in his mouth. So the origin of «مَلَك» is «مَلْوَك»; the vowel of the wāw was transferred to the quiescent lām before it, so the weak letter [originally] vowelled with a fatḥa before it was changed into an alif, and it became «مَلاك» like «مَقَام»; then the alif was dropped for lightness, so its pattern is mafal, with the second radical dropped. The origin of «ملائكة» is «ملاوِكة», and the wāw was changed into a hamza. But the condition for changing wāw and yāʾ into hamza after the alif of mafāʿil is that they be augmentative, as in «عجائز» and «رسائل» — although that has occurred with a radical letter rarely: they said «مصائِب» and «منائِر», and «معائِش» has been read anomalously with the hamza. These are five views. The sixth: al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl said: "«الملك» has no derivation among the Arabs."
The hāʾ in «ملائكة» is for the feminine of the plural, as in «صَلادِمة». It has been said: it is for intensiveness, as in «علاَّمة» and «نسَّابة», but that is nothing. This hāʾ is sometimes dropped anomalously; the poet said:
332 - أبا خالدٍ صَلَّتْ عليكَ الملائِكُ
(O Abū Khālid, may the angels bless you.)
His saying: {إِنِّي جَاعِلٌ فِي الأرض خَلِيفَةً}: this clause is governed by «القول», so it is in the position of the accusative by it. «إنَّ» has a kasra here because it occurs after «القول» devoid of the meaning of supposition, being reported speech by it. If it is in the sense of supposition, two aspects apply in it: fatḥa and kasra; they recited:
333 - إذا قلتُ أني آيبٌ أهلَ بلدةٍ ... نَزَعْتُ بها عنه الوليَّةَ بالهَجْر
(Whenever I think that I am returning to the people of a town, I strip there from him [my camel] the saddle-cloth in the midday heat.)
It should have been with fatḥa only, in consideration of the meaning of supposition; but it may be said that the kasra was allowed in regard to the outward form of «القول».
«إنَّ» is of three kinds: a kind in which its kasra is obligatory, a kind in which its fatḥa is obligatory, and a kind in which both aspects are allowed. This is not the place to establish that; rather, it comes in the course of the sūras. But the general rule in that is: every place where a maṣdar (verbal noun) can stand in its stead, its fatḥa is obligatory, e.g. «بلغني أنك قائمٌ» (it reached me that you are standing); every place where [a maṣdar] cannot stand in its stead, its kasra is obligatory, as when it occurs after «القول», at the beginning, as a ṣila (relative clause) and as a ḥāl (circumstantial); and every place where it is possible for [a maṣdar] to stand in its stead, both aspects are allowed, as when it occurs after the fāʾ of the apodosis and after the «إذا» of surprise. This is the most precise of formulations of this rule.
In «جاعلٌ» there are two views. One of them: that it is in the sense of «خالق» (creator), so «خليفةً» is a mafʿūl bihi; and in that case there are two views regarding «في الأرض»: one of them, which is the clear one, that it is attached to «جاعلٌ»; the second, that it is attached to an omitted [element] because it is a ḥāl from the indefinite noun after it. The second view: that it is in the sense of «مُصَيِّر» (making into) — al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else — so «خليفةً» is the first object and «في الأرض» is the second, placed before it, and attached to an omitted [element] according to what has been established. «خليفة» may be in the sense of an active participle (fāʿil), i.e. "he succeeds you," or "he succeeds the jinn who were before him"; this is more correct because of the entry of the tāʾ of the feminine upon it. It has been said: [it is] in the sense of a passive participle (mafʿūl), i.e. every generation succeeds those who preceded it; the entry of the tāʾ in that case is not regular, unless it be said that «خليفةً» was treated like non-derived nouns (jawāmid), such as «النطيحة» and «الذبيحة». «خليفة» was made singular, even though the plural is intended, because Adam and his offspring are meant by it, but the mention of him sufficed, just as the mention of the father of a tribe suffices, e.g. «مُضَر» and «رَبِيعة». It has been said: the meaning is generic.
It has been read: «خليقةً» with qāf.
«خليفةً» is accusative by «جاعل», as has preceded, because it is an active participle. The active participle does the work of its verb without restriction if it has the alif and lām; and on condition of [denoting] the present or future, and of being supported (iʿtimād), if it does not have them. It may be annexed to what it governs for lightness, as long as there is no separation between them, as [there is] in this verse.
His saying: {قَالُواْ أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفْسِدُ}: it has preceded that «قالوا» governs «إذ قال ربُّك» and that this is the preferred [view]. The hamza in «أتجعل» is for interrogation in its usual sense. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "for wonder"; and it has been said: for affirmation (taqrīr), as in his saying:
334 - ألستُمْ خيرَ مَنْ ركب المَطايا ... وأنْدى العالمينَ بطونَ راحِ
(Are you not the best of those who ride mounts, and the most generous of all the worlds in the palms of hands?)
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "for seeking testimony (istishhād)," i.e. "Will You place in it one who will cause corruption like those who were before?" — and this is a strange expression. The first «فيها» is attached to «تَجْعَل» if it is said that it is in the sense of creating, and «مَنْ يُفْسِدُ» is a mafʿūl bihi; and if it is said that it is in the sense of «التصيير» (making into), then «فيها» is a second object placed before the first, which is «مَنْ يفسد». «مَنْ» may be a relative noun or an indefinite qualified noun (nakira mawṣūfa); on the first, the clause after it has no grammatical position, and on the second its position is the accusative. The second «فيها» is attached to «يُفْسِدُ». And «يَسْفِكُ» is conjoined to «يُفْسِدُ» on both considerations.
The majority read it in the nominative, and it has been read in the accusative as an answer to the interrogative after the wāw that entails combination (jamʿ), by an implied «أَنْ», as in his saying:
335 - أَتَبيتُ رَيَّانَ الجفونِ من الكَرى ... وأبيتَ منك بليلةِ المَلْسُوعِ
(Do you spend the night with eyelids sated with sleep, while I spend the night, because of you, in the night of one who has been stung?)
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "accusative by the wāw of diversion (wāw al-ṣarf)"; this is the terminology of the Kufans. The meaning of the wāw of diversion is that the verb required a [certain] case, and the wāw diverted it from that to the accusative. The well-known [reading] is «يَسْفِك» with kasra on the fāʾ; it has been read with ḍamma on it; it has also been read with ḍamma on the imperfect prefix, from «أَسْفك»; and it has also been read doubled, for multiplicity.
Al-safk is pouring, and it is used only of blood. Ibn Fāris and al-Jawharī said: "It is also used of tears." Al-Mahdawī said: "Al-safk is used only of blood, and it is sometimes used of scattering speech; one says «سَفَكَ الكلامَ», i.e. he scattered it."
«الدِّماء» is the plural of «دَم». No declinable noun consists of two letters, so it must have an omitted third, which is its final radical; it may be a wāw or a yāʾ, because they say in the dual «دَمَوان» and «دَمَيان»; the poet said:
336 - فَلَوْ أنَّا على حَجَرٍ ذُبِحْنا ... جَرَى الدَّميَانِ بالخبرِ اليقين
(Were we slaughtered on a stone, the two bloods would flow with certain news.)
Is the pattern of «دم» faʿl, with a quiescent middle radical, or faʿal, with a fatḥa? Two views. Its omitted letter is sometimes restored, and it is used with a final alif (maqṣūr), like «عصا» and others; on this is his saying:
337 - كَأَطُومٍ فَقَدَتْ بُرْغُزَها ... أَعْقَبَتْها الغُبْسُ منه عَدَماً
غَفَلَتْ ثم أَتَتْ تَطْلُبه ... فإذا هِيَ بِعِظامٍ ودَماً
(Like a wild cow that lost her calf — the grey wolves left her bereft of it; she was heedless, then came seeking it, and lo, there were bones and blood.)
Its mīm is also sometimes doubled; the poet said:
338 - أهانَ دَمَّكَ فَرْغَاً بعد عِزَّتِه ... يا عمروُ بَغْيُكَ إصراراً على الحَسَد
(Your transgression, O ʿAmr, persisting in envy, has made your blood unavenged and cheap after its being precious.)
The origin of «الدِّماء» is «الدِّماو» or «الدِّماي»; the weak letter was changed into a hamza because it occurs at the end after an augmentative alif, as in «كساء» and «رداء».
His saying: {وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ}: the wāw is for the ḥāl, and {وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ} is a clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. «بحمدك» is attached to an omitted [element] because it too is a ḥāl, and the bāʾ in it is for accompaniment, i.e. "we glorify, clothed in Your praise," as in «جاء زيد بثيابِه» (Zayd came with his clothes). So they are two overlapping ḥāls (mutadākhilatān), i.e. a ḥāl within a ḥāl. It has been said: the bāʾ is for causation, so it is attached to the glorification. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is possible that their saying «بحمدِكَ» is a parenthesis between the two statements, as though they said: 'And we glorify and sanctify' — then they interposed by way of submission, i.e. 'and You are the One praised for guiding to that.'" I say: it is as though he is attempting to make the bāʾ causal, but [with] what the bāʾ is attached to being an omitted verb suitable to the meaning, its implied form being: "glorification and sanctification came about for us because of Your praise."
Al-ḥamd here is a maṣdar annexed to its object, and its agent is omitted, its implied form being: "by our praising You." Some claimed that the agent is latent in it, and that is an error, because the maṣdar is a non-derived noun (jāmid) in which [a pronoun] is not latent — although a disagreement has been reported about the maṣdar occurring in the place of the verb, e.g. «ضرباً زيداً» (strike Zayd!): does it bear a pronoun or not? This has preceded.
«نُقَدِّسُ» is conjoined to «نُسَبِّح», so it is also a khabar of «نحن». Its object is omitted, i.e. "we sanctify ourselves and our deeds for You." And «لكم» [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in the verse is «لكَ»] is attached to it or to «نُسَبِّح», and its meaning is causation. It has been said: it is redundant, because what precedes it is transitive by itself; and that is weak, since it is only added when the governed word is placed first or the governing word is secondary (farʿ). It has been said: it makes [the verb] transitive, as in «سجدت لله» (I prostrated to Allah). And it has been said: it is for clarification (bayān), like it in your saying «سُقْياً لك» (may rain water you); on this [view] it is attached to an omitted [element] and is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "our sanctification is for You."
This construction is better than construing it as their saying «أعني» (I mean), because it is more suited to the context. Far-fetched is the one who claimed that the clause of His saying «ونحنُ نسبِّح» falls within the scope of an implied interrogative, its implied form being: "And do we glorify, or do we change?" Ibn ʿAṭiyya considered it good, together with holding [that it is] a pure interrogative in their saying «أتجعلُ». The majority reject this — I mean the omission of the interrogative hamza without mention of the correlative «أم». It is the opinion of al-Akhfash, and he counted among it His saying, Exalted is He: {وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَيَّ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 22], i.e. "And is that a favour…?", and the saying of the other:
339 - طَرِبْتُ وما شوقاً إلى البيضَ أَطْرَبُ ... ولا لَعِباً مني وذو الشَّيْبِ يَلْعَب
(I was moved with emotion — yet it is not out of longing for fair women that I am moved, nor in play on my part; and does the grey-haired man play?)
i.e. "And does the grey-haired…?", and the saying of the other:
340 - أفرحُ أَنْ أُرْزَأَ الكِرامَ وأَنْ ... أُوْرَثَ ذَوْداً شَصائِصاً نَبْلاً
(Shall I rejoice at being bereft of the noble ones, and at inheriting a small herd of dry, worthless camels?)
i.e. "Shall I rejoice…?" As for with «أمْ», it is permissible because it indicates [the hamza], as in his saying:
341 - فواللهِ ما أدري وإنْ كنتُ دارياً ... بسبْعٍ رَمَيْنَ الجمرَ أم بِثَمانِ
(By Allah, I do not know — though I am one who knows — whether they threw the pebbles with seven or with eight.)
i.e. "Was it with seven…?"
Al-tasbīḥ is declaring transcendence and freedom [from defects]. Its origin is from «السَّبْح», which is distance, and from it is «السابح» (the swimmer) in water. So the meaning of «سبحان الله» is: declaring Him transcendent and free from what does not befit His majesty; and from it is the poet's saying:
342 - أقولُ لَمَّا جاءَني فَخْرُهْ ... سُبْحانَ مِنْ علقمَةَ الفاخِر
(I say, when his boasting reached me: how far removed [I am] from ʿAlqama the boaster!)
i.e. declaring remote. It is exclusive to the Creator, Exalted is He. Al-Rāghib said about his saying «سبحان مِنْ علقمة»: "Its origin is «سبحانَ علقمةَ», by way of mockery, and he added «مِنْ» to it; and it has been said: its implied form is 'Glory be to Allah, on account of ʿAlqama.'" The apparent sense of his saying is that it may be said of other than the Creator, Exalted is He, by way of mockery; and there is an objection to this.
Al-taqdīs is purification, and from it are «الأرضُ المقدَّسَةُ» (the Holy Land), «بيت المَقْدِس» (Jerusalem) and «روحُ القُدُس» (the Holy Spirit); the poet said:
343 - فَأَدْرَكْنَه يَأخُذْنَ بالساقِ والنَّسا ... كما شَبْرَقَ الوِلْدَانُ ثوبَ المَقْدِسِ
(They [the hounds] overtook it, seizing it by the shank and the sciatic vein, as the boys tear apart the garment of the one who has been to the Holy House.)
i.e. the one purified for them. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is from «قَدَّسَ في الأرضِ» when one goes far into the land, so its meaning is close to the meaning of «نُسَبِّح»." End [of quotation].
His saying, Exalted is He: {قَالَ إني أَعْلَمُ مَا لاَ تَعْلَمُونَ}: the origin of «إنِّي» is «إنَّني»; three like letters came together, so we dropped one of them. Is it the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya) or the middle nūn? Two views; the correct one is the second. This resembles what preceded in {إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 14] and its kind.
The clause is in the position of the accusative by «القول». «أعلمُ» may be an imperfect verb, which is the apparent [view], and «ما» is a mafʿūl bihi; it is either an indefinite qualified noun or a relative noun, and on either construction the referent is omitted because it fulfils the conditions, i.e. "[what] you know it." Al-Mahdawī and Makkī — and Abū al-Baqāʾ followed them — said: "«أعلمُ» is a noun in the sense of «عالم» (knowing)," as in his saying:
344 - لَعَمْرُكَ ما أدري واني لأوْجَلُ ... على أيِّنا تَعْدُو المنيَّةُ أَوَّلُ
(By your life, I do not know — and I am indeed afraid — upon which of us death will first fall.)
So «ما» may be in the position of the genitive by annexation, or of the accusative by «أَعْلَمُ»; «أعلمُ» was not given nunation because it is a diptote, as in «هؤلاء حَوَاجُّ بيتَ الله» (these are pilgrims to the House of Allah). This is built on two weak principles: one of them, making afʿal in the sense of fāʿil without comparison; and the second, that afʿal, when it is in the sense of the active participle, does its work — and the majority do not establish [either of] these.
It has been said: «أعلمُ» is in its usual sense of being for comparison (tafḍīl), and that over which [He] is preferred is omitted, i.e. "more knowing than you," and «ما» is accusative by an omitted verb indicated by the afʿal, i.e. "I know what you do not know." It is not permissible for it to be made accusative by the elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl), because it is weaker [in government] than the [resembling] adjective, which is weaker than the active participle, which is weaker than the verb. This would be analogous to what they interpreted in the poet's saying:
345 - فلم أَرَ مثلَ الحيِّ حَيَّاً مُصَبَّحاً ... ولا مثلَنا يومَ التَقَيْنَا فوارِساً
أَكَرَّ وأحمى للحقيقةِ منهمُ ... وأضْرَبَ منا بالسيوفِ القوانِسا
(I have not seen a tribe raided at dawn like that tribe, nor horsemen like us on the day we met — more given to charging and more protective of what must be defended than they, and better striking than we with swords at the helmet-crests.)
So «القوانسَ» is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. by «ضَرَب», not by «أَضْرَبَ». But claiming the like of that in the noble verse is far-fetched, because of the omission of two things: that over which [He] is preferred, and what makes «ما» accusative.

semin-durr:98-98.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {مَن كَانَ عَدُوّاً}: the discussion of «مَنْ» is as has preceded, except that the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) here may be {فَإِنَّ الله عَدُوٌّ لِّلْكَافِرِينَ}. If it is said: where then is the linking element? The answer is from two angles. One: the overt noun has taken the place of the pronoun; the original was "then Allah is an enemy to them", and He used the overt noun to draw attention to the cause. The second: that by "the disbelievers" the general is meant, and generality is among the linking elements, because the first is subsumed under it. And it may be omitted, its implied form being: "whoever is an enemy to Allah has disbelieved", and the like. Some of them said: the wāw in His saying {وملائكته وَرُسُلِهِ وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكَالَ} is in the sense of "or"; he said: because whoever is hostile to any one of those mentioned, the ruling regarding him is the same. Some of them said: it is for itemisation; but there is no need for that, for this ruling is known. He mentioned Gabriel and Michael after they had first been subsumed, to draw attention to their superiority over the other angels; and likewise everything that is mentioned as particular after general. Some of them call this type tajrīd ("stripping out"), as if meaning by it that He stripped some of its members out of the first general term, singling it out for a distinction. This ruling — I mean mentioning the particular after the general — is specific to the wāw; it is not permissible with the other conjunctions.
Some of them made like this verse — I mean in mentioning the particular after the general to honour it — His saying: {فِيهِمَا فَاكِهَةٌ وَنَخْلٌ وَرُمَّانٌ} [al-Raḥmān: 68]. In this there is an objection, for «فاكهةٌ» belongs to the category of the unrestricted (muṭlaq), since it is indefinite in an affirmative context, and it has nothing to do with generality. If he meant that the name "fruit" applies to them both, in the sense of a word being true of what it can bear, and then He specified it, that is correct. He brought the name of Allah overtly in His saying {فَإِنَّ الله عَدُوٌّ} because had it been made a pronoun, saying "then He", it would have suggested that it refers to the conditional noun, so the meaning would be reversed, or that it refers to Michael because he is the nearest thing mentioned. Mīkāʾīl (Michael) is a foreign noun, and the discussion of it is like the discussion of Jibrīl: whether it is derived from the malakūt of Allah, or that mīk means "servant" and īl is the name of Allah, and whether its compounding is a construct compound or a blended compound; and what is correct in that has become known.
There are seven dialectal forms in it: مِيكال on the pattern of mifʿāl; it is the dialect of the Hijaz, and Abū ʿAmr and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read with it. [The poet] said:
632 - ويومَ بَدْرٍ لقِيناكم لنا عُدَدٌ ... فيه مع النصرِ مِيكالٌ وجِبريلٌ
(And on the day of Badr we met you, having reinforcements in it, along with victory: Michael and Gabriel.)
And his saying:
633 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . .
وكَذَّبوا مِيْكالا
(… and they denied Michael.)
The second: the same, except that after the alif there is a hamza [مِيكائِل]; Nāfiʿ read with it. The third: the same except with an added yāʾ after the hamza [مِيكائِيل]; it is the reading of the rest. The fourth: مِيكَئِيل like mīkaʿīl; Ibn Muḥayṣin read with it. The fifth: the same except that there is no yāʾ after the hamza, so it is like mīkaʿil [مِيكَئِل], and it has been read with. The sixth: ميكاييل with two yāʾs after the alif; al-Aʿmash read with it. The seventh: ميكاءَل with a hamza with fatḥa after the alif, as one says isrāʾal. Al-Māwardī related from Ibn ʿAbbās that jabr means ʿabd ("servant") in the non-diminutive, and mīkā means ʿubayd ("little servant") in the diminutive; so the meaning of Jibrīl is ʿAbd Allāh and the meaning of Mīkāʾīl is ʿUbayd Allāh. He said: "No one is known to have differed with Ibn ʿAbbās on this." His saying: {وَمَا يَكْفُرُ بِهَآ إِلاَّ الفاسقون}: this is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh), and it has preceded that al-Farrāʾ permits the accusative in it.

semin-durr:100-100.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {أَوَكُلَّمَا عَاهَدُواْ}: the majority read the wāw of «أَوَ كلما» with a vowel, and the grammarians disagreed about it in three views. Al-Akhfash said: the hamza is for interrogation and the wāw is redundant (zāʾida); this is according to his opinion that its redundancy is permissible. Al-Kisāʾī said: it is the conjunctive «أَوْ» which means "rather" (bal), and the wāw was merely given a vowel; this is supported by the reading of those who read it with sukūn. The Basrans said: it is the conjunctive wāw, with the interrogative hamza placed before it as is known. It has preceded that al-Zamakhsharī supposes, between the hamza and the conjunction, something to which what follows is conjoined; therefore he supposed here: "Did they disbelieve in the clear signs, and every time they made a covenant…?"
Abū al-Sammāl al-ʿAdawī read: «أَوْ كلَّما» with sukūn on the wāw, and about it too there are three views. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is conjoined to «الفاسقين»", and he supposed it in the sense of "except those who transgressed or broke [the covenant]" — meaning by this that he conjoined the verb to the noun because it is in its sense, like His saying: {إِنَّ المصدقين والمصدقات وَأَقْرَضُواْ} [al-Ḥadīd: 18], i.e. "those who gave charity and lent". On this there is discussion which will come in its sūra, if Allah the Exalted wills. Al-Mahdawī said: «أَوْ» is for breaking off the speech, equivalent to the disjunctive am, meaning that it is in the sense of bal; this is the opinion of the Kufans, and the precise statement of this view and what they adduced as evidence from the saying:
634 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . أو أَنْتَ في العَيْنِ أَمْلَحُ
(… or rather you are more comely to the eye.)
has preceded at the beginning of the sūra. Some of them said: it is in the sense of the wāw, so the two readings agree; the occurrence of «أو» in the sense of the wāw is established, as in the saying:
635 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ما بَيْنَ مُلْجِمِ مُهْرِه أو سافِعِ
(… between one bridling his colt and one grabbing [its forelock].)
{خطيائة أَوْ إِثْماً} [al-Nisāʾ: 112], {آثِماً أَوْ كَفُوراً} [al-Insān: 24]; so let this reading be likewise. This too is the opinion of the Kufans, as has preceded. That which puts «كُلَّما» in the accusative is what follows it, and the precise statement on it has preceded. The accusative of «عَهْداً» is on one of two views: either as a maṣdar (verbal noun) not running on the verb's own form, the original being «معاهدةً»; or as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), on the basis that «عاهدوا» is made to include the sense of «أَعْطَوا» ("they gave"), and the first object is omitted, the implied form being: "they gave Allah a covenant" [Translator's note: the text reads «عاهدوا الله عَهْدَاً»].
It has been read: «عَهِدُوا», so «عهْداً» is a maṣdar running on its own verb; and it has also been read: «عُوْهِدُوا», passive.
His saying: {بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ}: in this there are two views. One: that it belongs to the conjoining of clauses, and this is the apparent view; «بل» is then for a digression of transition (iḍrāb intiqāl), not of cancellation (ibṭāl), and you have learnt that «بل» is not truly called a conjunction except with single words. The second: that it is the conjoining of single words, «أكثرُهم» being conjoined to «فريقٍ», and «لا يؤمنون» a clause in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أكثرُهم». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "from the pronoun in «أكثرُهم»"; and what he said is permissible; it cannot be said [against him] that it is a ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi, because the muḍāf is part of the muḍāf ilayhi, and that is permissible. The benefit of this digression on this view is that since «فريق» applies to few and many, and casting aside was attributed to it, and what might spring to mind is the possibility that those casting aside the covenant were few, He made clear that those casting it aside were the majority, to repel the possibility mentioned. Al-nabdh is throwing; it is literal with bodies, and its attribution to the covenant is figurative.

semin-durr:101-101.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {الكتاب كِتَابَ الله}: «الكتابَ» is the second object of «أُوْتُوا», because it originally takes two objects; the first was put in the place of the agent — it is the wāw — and the second remained in the accusative. It has preceded that according to al-Suhaylī it is the first object. «كتابَ الله» is the object of «نَبَذَ», and «وراءَ» is in the accusative as an adverb, and what puts it in the accusative is «نَبَذَ». This is a proverbial image of their neglect of the Torah; the Arabs say: "He put this matter behind his back and behind his ear", i.e. he neglected it. Al-Farazdaq said:
636 - تَميمُ بنُ مُرٍّ لا تكونَنَّ حاجتي ... بِظَهْرٍ فلا يَعْيَا عليَّ جوابُها
(Tamīm ibn Murr, let not my need be put behind a back, so that its answer does not fail me.)
Al-nabdh is throwing, as has preceded. Some of them said: "Nabdh, ṭarḥ and ilqāʾ are close in meaning, except that nabdh is mostly said of something spread out and what is treated like it, and ilqāʾ of that in which a meeting between two things is considered." Among instances of nabdh meaning throwing is the saying:
637 - إنَّ الذين أَمَرْتَهُمْ أَنْ يَعْدِلُوا ... نَبَذُوا كتابَك واسْتَحَلُّوا المَحْرَما
(Those whom you ordered to act justly cast your letter aside and made the forbidden lawful.)
And Abū al-Aswad said:
638 - وخَبَّروني مَنْ كنتُ أرسلْتُ أنَّما ... أَخَذْتَ كتابي مُعْرِضاً بشِمالكا
نظْرتَ إلى عنوانِه فنبذْتَه ... كنَبْذِكَ نَعْلاً أَخْلَقَتْ مِنْ نِعالِكا
(The one I had sent told me that you took my letter, turning away, with your left hand; you looked at its address and cast it aside as you cast aside a worn-out sandal of yours.)
His saying: {كَأَنَّهُمْ لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ} is a clause in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); its possessor is «فريقٌ», even though it is indefinite, because of its specification by the description; and what governs it is «نَبَذَ». The implied form is: "resembling the ignorant". The object of knowledge is omitted, its implied form being: "that it is the Book of Allah, no doubt entering them about it"; and the meaning is that they disbelieved out of obstinacy.

semin-durr:113-113.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {اليهود}: «اليهود» is a well-known religious community. The yāʾ in it is radical, since it remains in the conjugation, and it is not from the root هَوَد of His words {هُوداً أَوْ نصارى} [al-Baqara: 111]. It has already been said that al-Farrāʾ claims that «هوداً» is originally يَهود with its yāʾ dropped, and it was also said at His words «والذين هادوا» that «اليهود» is an ascription to Judah (يهوذا) son of Jacob. Al-Shalawbīn said: "يَهُود has two aspects. The first: it is the plural of يهودي, so it is an indefinite, fully declined (triptote) noun. The second: it is a proper name of this tribe, so it is a diptote." End of quote. On the first, the alif and lām enter it; on the second is the poet's saying:
681 - أولئك أَوْلَى من يهودَ بمِدْحَةٍ ... إذا أنتَ يوماً قُلْتَها لم تُؤَنَّبِ
(Those are more worthy of praise than the Jews; if you one day utter it, you will not be blamed.)
And he said:
682 - فَرَّتْ يهودُ وأَسْلَمَتْ جيرانُها ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(The Jews fled and abandoned their neighbours.)
Were it said that «يهود» is transferred [as a name] from the imperfect verb, like يَزيد and يشكر, it would be a good view; and it is supported by their saying: they were named «يهود» from هاد يَهُود, meaning "to move".
His words: {لَيْسَتِ النصارى}: «ليس» is always a defective (nāqiṣ) verb, one of the sisters of kāna, and it is not conjugated. Its pattern is فَعِل with kasra on the middle radical; by rights its first radical should take kasra when it is attached to the tāʾ of the speaker and the like, to indicate the yāʾ, as in شِئْتُ; but since it is not conjugated, the first radical stayed as it was. Some say لُسْتُ with ḍamma on the first radical, and its pattern in this dialect is فَعُل with ḍamma on the middle radical; the occurrence of فَعُل with ḍamma on the middle radical in a verb whose middle radical is yāʾ is rare, nothing of it having come except «هَيُؤَ الرجلُ», when the man's appearance became fine. That «ليس» is a verb is the correct view, contrary to al-Fārisī in one of his two views, and those who followed him, in making it a particle like «ما». What shows that it is a verb is that the overt nominative pronouns are attached to it, and it has many rules. «النصارى» is its noun and «على شيء» its khabar (predicate). This may be one of the cases in which the adjective is omitted, i.e. "on anything worth counting", like His words «إنه ليس من أهلِك», i.e. "of your family who are saved", and the poet's saying:
683 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . لقد وَقَعْتِ على لَحْمِ
(You have indeed fallen upon meat.)
i.e. "a great [piece of] meat". Or it may be a negation by way of hyperbole: if applying [the word] "thing" to what they hold is denied — even though, according to some, "thing" is applied to the non-existent — that is hyperbole in not counting it of any account, and it becomes like their saying: "less than nothing".
His words: {وَهُمْ يَتْلُونَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause. The origin of يَتْلُون is يَتْلُوُوْنَ; it underwent weakening (iʿlāl) by dropping the final radical, and this is clear.
His words: {كَذَلِكَ قَالَ الذين لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ}: concerning this kāf there are two views. The first: it is in the position of the accusative, and in that case there are two possible construals. The first: it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) placed before its governor, the implied form being: "a saying like that saying said those who do not know". The second: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the definite, latent maṣdar indicated by «قال», the implied form being: "the like of that saying, they said it", i.e. those who do not know said the saying, it being the like of that saying. This is the opinion of Sībawayh, and the first is the opinion of the grammarians, as has been said more than once.
On these two views there are two aspects in «مثلَ قولهم». The first: it is accusative as a badal (substitute) from the position of the kāf. The second of the two aspects: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) governed by «يَعْلمون», i.e. those who do not know the like of the statement of the Jews and Christians [said] the like of their statement; that is, they said that by coincidence, even though they were ignorant of the statement of the Jews and Christians.
The second of the two views: it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause after it is the khabar, and the returning pronoun is omitted, the implied form being: "the like of that, those who do not know said it". The accusative of «مثلَ قولهم» is then either as a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, or as the object of «يعلمون», the implied form being: "the like of the saying of the Jews and Christians, those who do not know the belief of the Jews and Christians said". It may not be accusative as the object of «قال», because it has already taken its object, namely the pronoun returning to the mubtadaʾ. Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned that, and it is open to question in two respects. The first: the majority refuse to make the kāf a noun. The second: the omission of an accusative returning pronoun, which the grammarians explicitly declare forbidden, treating the poet's saying:
684 - وخالِدٌ يَحْمَدُ ساداتُنا ... بالحقِّ لا يُحْمَدُ بالباطِلِ
(And Khālid — our chiefs praise [him] rightly; he is not praised falsely.)
as poetic licence. The Kufans have a detailed position on this question.
His words: {بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ القيامة}: both are accusative, governed by «يحكُمُ», and «فيه» is attached to «يختلفون».

semin-durr:114-114.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ}: «مَنْ» is interrogative, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «أظلمُ», an elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl), is its khabar (predicate). The sense of the interrogative here is negation, i.e. "no one is more unjust than he". Since the meaning is thus, some people raised a question: this form recurs in the Quran — {وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افترى} [al-Anʿām: 21], {وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّن ذُكِّرَ بِآيَاتِ رَبِّهِ} [al-Sajda: 22], {فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّن كَذَبَ علَى الله} [al-Zumar: 32] — and each of them entails that no one is more unjust than the one mentioned in it; so how is someone else described with that? There are three answers to this. The first — mentioned by this questioner — is that each is restricted to the meaning of its ṣila (relative clause), as though He said: "no one among those who hinder is more unjust than one who hinders the mosques of Allah", "no one among the fabricators is more unjust than one who fabricates against Allah", "no one among the liars is more unjust than one who lies against Allah", and likewise whatever else of it has come. The second: the restriction is relative to precedence: since no one preceded them in the like of it, He judged them more unjust than those who came after them following their path in that; and the meaning of this comes back to precedence in hindering, fabricating and the like. The third: this is a negation of being-most-unjust, and negating being-most-unjust does not require negating being-unjust, because negating the restricted does not indicate negating the absolute. And since it does not indicate negating being-unjust, there is no contradiction, because it contains an affirmation of equality in being-most-unjust; and once equality in being-most-unjust is established, none of those so described exceeds another, since they are equal in that. The meaning becomes: "no one is more unjust than one who hinders, one who fabricates, and one who was reminded", and there is no difficulty in these being equal in being-most-unjust; nor does that indicate that one of them exceeds another in injustice — just as when you say "no one is more learned in law than Zayd, Bakr and Khālid", it does not indicate that one of them is more learned than the other; rather you have denied that anyone is more learned than them. It may not be said that one who hinders the mosques of Allah and strives for their ruin without fabricating a lie against Allah is less unjust than one who combines all these things, so they would not be equal in being-most-unjust; because these verses are all about the disbelievers, and they are equal in being-most-unjust even if the paths to it differ.
«مَنْ» may be relative, in which case the clause after it has no grammatical position, or indefinite-qualified (mawṣūfa), in which case the clause is in the position of the genitive as its adjective. «مساجد» is the first object of «مَنَع». It is the plural of مَسْجِد, which is the noun of place of prostration (sujūd). By rights it should have come on the pattern مَفْعَل with fatḥa, since the middle radical of its imperfect takes ḍamma, but its kasra is irregular, as are some words to be mentioned. «مَسْجَد» with fatḥa has been heard, according to the basic rule, and its jīm is sometimes replaced by yāʾ; from that is «المَسْيِد» in one dialect.
His words: {أَن يُذْكَرَ}: an accusative-governing particle and the verb it puts in the accusative. There are four aspects in it. The first: it is the second object of «مَنَع»; one says: مَنَعْتُه كذا (I denied him such-and-such). The second: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "out of aversion that [His name] be mentioned". The Shaykh said: "So the omission of a muḍāf becomes necessary, i.e. 'entry into the mosques of Allah' and the like." The third: it is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from «مساجد», i.e. he prevented the mention of His name in them. The fourth: it is on the dropping of the preposition, the origin being «مِنْ أَنْ يُذْكَرَ»; in that case the two well-known positions apply, as to whether it is in the position of the accusative or the genitive. «في خَرابِها» is attached to «سَعَى». There is disagreement about «خراب». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is a quasi-maṣdar (ism maṣdar) meaning 'ruining' (takhrīb), like سَلام meaning تسليم, and the quasi-maṣdar is annexed to its object because it operates as the verb does." This is on one of the two views on the quasi-maṣdar, whether it governs or not; and they cite in support of its governing:
685 - أَكْفْراً بعد رَدِّ الموتِ عني ... وبعد عَطائِك المئةَ الرِّتاعا
(Ingratitude, after you warded off death from me, and after your giving the hundred grazing [camels]?)
Others said: it is the maṣdar of خَرِبَ المكان يخرَب خَراباً (the place fell into ruin), so the meaning is: he strove that they fall into ruin of themselves through neglect of keeping them in repair. One says: منزلٌ خَرابٌ and خَرِب (a ruined dwelling), as in the poet's saying:
686 - ما رَبْعُ مَيَّةَ معمورٌ يَطِيفُ [به] ... غَيْلانُ أَبْهى رُبَىً من رُبْعِها الخَرِب
(The abode of Mayya, inhabited, with Ghaylān circling [it], is not more splendid in its hills than her ruined abode.)
So on the first it is annexed to its object, and on the second annexed to its agent.
His words: {مَا كَانَ لَهُمْ أَن يَدْخُلُوهَآ}: «لهم» is the khabar of «كان», placed before its noun, and its noun is «أَنْ يدخُلوها», since it is interpreted as a maṣdar, i.e. "entry was not for them". The negated clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «أولئك».
His words: {إِلاَّ خَآئِفِينَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «يَدْخُلوها». This is an emptied exception from the states, since the implied meaning is: "entry was not for them in any state except in the state of fear".
