Ubayy read «خُيَّفاً», which is the plural of خائف, like ضارب and ضُرَّب; the origin is خُوَّف, like صُوَّم, but he replaced the two wāws with two yāʾs, which is permissible; they say صُوَّم and صُيَّم. The construction was first taken according to the wording of «مَنْ», so it was made singular in His words «مَنَع» and «سعى», and secondly according to its meaning, so it was made plural in His words «أولئك» and what follows.
His words: {لَّهُمْ فِي الدنيا خِزْيٌ}: this clause and what follows have no grammatical position, being resumptive from what precedes. It may not be a ḥāl, because their disgrace is established in every state, not restricted to the state of entering the mosques specifically.

semin-durr:38-38.t:
His saying: {قُلْنَا اهبطوا}: He repeated His saying «قُلْنا» only because the two descents differ with respect to what each is connected with: with the first descent [He connected the enmity, and with the second He connected the coming of guidance. It has also been said: "because the first descent] is from the Garden to heaven, and the second from heaven to the earth." Some considered this far-fetched because of His saying: {وَلَكُمْ فِي الأرض مُسْتَقَرٌّ}. [Translator's note: the printed text has «واستَعْبَدَه», evidently a misprint for «واستبعده» (considered it far-fetched); rendered by sense.] Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Al-Naqqāsh related that the second descent is only from the Garden to heaven, and the first in the order of the verse is only to the earth, and it is the last in occurrence." End of quotation. It has also been said: it was repeated by way of emphasis, as in your saying: قُمْ قُمْ (stand, stand). The pronoun in «منها» refers to the Garden or to heaven.
His saying: «جميعاً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «اهبِطوا», i.e. "together": either at one time or at separate times, because what is meant is sharing in the basic act. This [is] the difference between جاؤوا جميعاً (they all came) and جاؤوا معاً (they came together): your saying «معاً» entails their coming all at one time, because of the accompaniment which «مع» indicates, unlike «جميعاً», which conveys only that none of them stayed behind from coming, without touching on the unity of time. This question arose between Thaʿlab and someone else; that man did not know it, and Thaʿlab informed him of it.
«جميع» is originally one of the words of tawkīd (emphasis), like «كُل», and some counted it with them. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "جميعاً is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «اهبِطوا»; it is neither a maṣdar (verbal noun) nor an active participle, but it is a substitute for them, indicating them, as though He had said: 'a descending all together' or 'descending all together'." It seems he means that the ḥāl in reality is omitted and that «جميعاً» is a tawkīd of it; however, supposing it as a maṣdar negates making it a ḥāl, except by an interpretation that is not needed. Some said: the implied form is: "We said: descend, together; so they descended all together" — the ḥāl was omitted from the first because the second indicates it, and the governor was omitted from the second because the first indicates it. This is a strained construction to which no necessity calls.
His saying: {فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّي هُدًى فَمَن تَبِع} … the verse. The fāʾ is ordering and sequential. «إمَّا» is originally the conditional إن with «ما» added to it for emphasis. «يأتينَّكم» is in the position of the jussive by the condition, because it has been made indeclinable (mabnī) owing to its being attached to the nūn of emphasis. It has also been said: rather it is declinable absolutely; and it has been said: indeclinable absolutely. The correct view is the detailed one: if the nūn is directly attached to it, as in this verse, it is indeclinable; otherwise it is declinable, as in: هل يقومانِّ؟ It was made indeclinable on fatḥa seeking lightness; it has also been said: rather it was made indeclinable on sukūn and vowelled with fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Al-Zajjāj and al-Mubarrad held that a verb occurring after the conditional إن reinforced by «ما» must be emphasized with the nūn; they said: for that reason the Revelation has come only with it. Sībawayh held that it is permissible, not obligatory, because of how often it has come in poetry without emphasis; its frequent occurrence without emphasis indicates that it is not obligatory. Of that is his saying:
387 - فإمَّا تَرَيْني كابنةِ الرَّمْلِ ضاحياً ... على رِقَّةٍ أَحْفَى ولا أَتَنَعَّلُ
(If you see me like the daughter of the sand [the snake?], exposed to the sun, going barefoot on thin soles and wearing no sandals…)
And another's saying:
388 - يا صاحِ إمَّا تَجِدْني غيرَ ذي جِدَةٍ ... فما التَخلِّي عن الخُلاَّنِ من شِيَمي
(O friend, if you find me without wealth, yet abandoning friends is not among my traits.)
And another's saying:
389 - زَعَمَتْ تُماضِرُ أنَّني إمَّا أَمُتْ ... يَسْدُدْ أُبَيْنُوها الأَصاغِرُ خُلَّتي
(Tumāḍir claimed that if I die, her little sons will fill the gap I leave.)
[Translator's note: the verse numbers here are printed in the source as «38 - 9-», «39 - 0-», «39 - 1-», i.e. 389, 390, 391.]
And another's saying:
390 - فإمَّا تَرَيْني ولِي لِمَّةٌ ... فإنَّ الحوادثَ أودى بِها
(If you see me [now without] the locks I once had, misfortunes have done away with them.)
And another's saying:
391 - فإمَّا تَرَيْني لا أُغَمِّضُ ساعةً ... مِن الدهرِ إلا أَنْ أَكِبَّ فَأَنْعَسَا
(If you see me not closing my eyes for an hour of time unless I bend over and doze…)
And another's saying:
392 - إمَّا تَرَيِْني اليومَ أمَّ حَمْزِ ... قارَبْتُ بينَ عَنَقي وجَمْزِي
(If you see me today, O Umm Ḥamz, having shortened the distance between my brisk pace and my leaping…)
Al-Mahdawī said: "«إما» is the conditional إنْ, with «ما» added to it so that the nūn of emphasis may properly enter the verb; had «ما» been dropped, the nūn would not enter. So «ما» reinforces the beginning of the utterance and the nūn reinforces its end." Ibn ʿAṭiyya followed him. Someone said: "This which the two of them held — that the nūn is necessary for the verb of the protasis when إنْ is joined with «ما» — is the doctrine of al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjāj." End of quotation. But there is nothing in their words indicating that the nūn is necessary, as you see; the most it contains is that they made the addition of «ما» to «إنْ» a condition for the soundness of emphasizing it with the nūn; as for whether the emphasis is necessary or not, they did not touch on it. Emphasis of the protasis has come without «إنْ», as in his saying:
393 - مَنْ نَثْقَفَنْ منهم فليس بآئِبِ ... أبداً وقتلُ بني قُتَيْبَةَ شافي
(Whoever of them we catch will never return, and the killing of Banū Qutayba is a cure.)
«مني» is attached to «يَأْتِيَنَّ», and it is for the beginning of the extent, figuratively. It may also be in the position of a ḥāl from «هُدَىً», because it is originally the adjective of an indefinite noun put before it; it parallels what preceded in His saying, Exalted is He: {مِن رَّبِّهِ كَلِمَاتٍ} [al-Baqara: 37]. «هُدى» is the fāʿil (agent). The fāʾ together with what comes after it, in His saying {فَمَن تَبِعَ}, is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the first condition, and the fāʾ in His saying, Exalted is He, {فَلاَ خَوْفٌ} is the apodosis of the second; the [second] condition [and its apodosis have occurred as the apodosis of the first. It has been transmitted from al-Kisāʾī that His saying {فَلاَ خَوْفٌ} is the apodosis of both conditions] together. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said, after transmitting it from al-Kisāʾī: "So it has been related, and it is questionable; there is no reason to differ from Sībawayh here. The disagreement is only in the likes of His saying: {فَأَمَّآ إِن كَانَ مِنَ المقربين فَرَوْحٌ} [al-Wāqiʿa: 88-89], where Sībawayh says: the apodosis of one of the two conditions is omitted because His saying «فَرَوْحٌ» indicates it, while the Kufans say «فَرَوْح» is the apodosis of both conditions. As for this verse, the meaning prevents «فلا خوف» from being the apodosis of both conditions." It has also been said: the apodosis of the first condition is omitted, its implied form being: "If guidance comes to you from Me, then follow it", and His saying {فَمَنْ تَبِع} is an independent clause. This too is far-fetched.
«مَنْ» may be conditional, which is the apparent view; it may also be a relative, the fāʾ entering its khabar (predicate) by assimilating it to the condition; but there is no need for this.
If it is conditional, «تبع» is in the position of the jussive, and likewise «فلا خَوْفٌ», since they are protasis and apodosis; if it is a relative, «تَبِع» has no position. When it is said to be conditional, it is also a mubtadaʾ (subject), but there is a well-known disagreement over its khabar. The more correct view is that it is the verb of the protasis, as proven by the fact that a pronoun must refer from the protasis verb to the conditional noun, while that is not necessary in the apodosis. You say: مَنْ يَقُمْ أُكْرِمْ زيداً (whoever stands, I shall honour Zayd), [and there is no pronoun in «أُكرم زيداً» referring to «مَنْ»; had it been the khabar, a pronoun would have been necessary in it]; and if you said «مَنْ يَقُمْ زيداً أُكْرِمْه», referring the hāʾ to «مَنْ», it would not be permissible, because the protasis verb lacks the pronoun. It has also been said: the khabar is the apodosis; those holding this must bring in it a pronoun referring to the conditional noun, so that «مَنْ يَقُمْ أُكْرِمْ زيداً» is not permissible in their view — yet it is permissible. This is what Abū al-Baqāʾ adduced. The precise treatment of the necessity of a pronoun referring from the apodosis to the conditional noun will come at His saying, Exalted is He: {مَن كَانَ عَدُوّاً لِّجِبْرِيلَ} [al-Baqara: 97]. It has also been said: the protasis and apodosis together are the khabar, because the useful information is obtained only from both. And it has been said: whichever contains a pronoun referring to the mubtadaʾ is the khabar.
The well-known reading is «هُدَايَ»; it has also been read هُدَيَّ, changing the alif into yāʾ and assimilating it into the yāʾ of the first person. This is the dialect of Hudhayl; they say for عَصاي: عَصَيَّ. Their poet said, lamenting his sons:
394 - سَبَقوا هَوَيَّ وأَعْنَقُوا لِهَوَاهُمُ ... فَتُخُرِّمُوا ولكلِّ جَنْبٍ مَصْرَعُ
(They outran my wish and hastened to their own desire, and so were cut off — and every side has its place of falling.)
It is as though, since they could not give what the first-person yāʾ requires — a kasra on what precedes it — because it is an alif, they brought what is akin to the kasra and changed the alif into yāʾ. This is a regular usage in their dialect, unless the alif is that of the dual, for they keep it, as in: جاء مسلمايَ وغلامايَ.
His saying: {فَلاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ}: it has preceded that it may be the apodosis of the condition, and so in the position of the jussive; and that it may be the khabar of «مَنْ» if it is said to be a relative — which is preferable because it is matched by the relative in His saying {والذين كَفَرواْ} — and so in the position of the nominative. «لا» may govern like laysa, so that «خوفٌ» is its noun and «عليهم» is in the position of the accusative as its khabar; and it may be non-governing, so that «خوفٌ» is a mubtadaʾ and «عليهم» is in the position of the nominative as its khabar. This is preferable to the former for two reasons. The first: its governing like laysa is rare, and it is established only by something open to interpretation, namely his saying:
395 - تَعَزَّ فلا شيءٌ على الأرضِ باقياً ... ولا وَزرٌ ممَّا قضى اللهُ واقِيَا
(Be consoled, for nothing on earth is lasting, and there is no refuge that shields from what Allah has decreed.)
The second: the clause after it, {وَلاَ هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ}, determines that «لا» in it is non-governing, because it does not govern definite nouns; so making it non-governing here matches what comes after it. Someone erred and made it govern a definite noun, adducing his saying:
396 - وحَلَّتْ سوادَ القلبِ لا أنا باغياً ... سِواها في حُبِّها مُتَراخِيا
(She settled in the core of the heart; I am not seeking another besides her, nor slackening in my love for her.)
so that «أنا» is its noun and «باغياً» its khabar. It was said: there is no proof in it, because «باغياً» is a ḥāl whose governor is omitted, and that is in reality the khabar, its implied form being: "nor am I seen seeking"; or the implied form is: "nor am I seen (لا أُرَى) seeking", and when the verb was omitted, the pronoun became detached.
It has been read «فلا خَوْفُ» in the nominative without tanwīn. The best view of it is that an annexation is implied, i.e. "fear of anything"; it has also been said: because it is in the intention of the article al-; and it has been said: the tanwīn was dropped for lightness. It has also been read «فلا خوفَ», indeclinable on fatḥa, because it is the lā of exculpation (lā al-tabriʾa, i.e. generic negation), which is more emphatic in negation. But people preferred the nominative reading. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "For two reasons. The first: that something has been conjoined to it in which only the nominative is possible, namely His saying «ولا هم», because it is definite and «لا» does not govern definite nouns; so it is preferable that what it is conjoined to be likewise, so that the two clauses match." Then he compared it with their saying «قام زيد وعمراً كلَّمْتُه» (Zayd stood, and ʿAmr I spoke to him), meaning in the preference for the accusative in the clause of preoccupation (ishtighāl) for the sake of matching. Then he said: "The second reason is from the side of meaning, namely that the indeclinable form indicates negation of fear from them altogether, and that is not what is meant; rather what is meant is negating it from them in the Hereafter. If it is said: why should not the reason for the nominative be that this speech is mentioned as the reward of those who follow the guidance, and it does not befit that slight fear be negated from them while the presence of great fear is imagined? It is answered: with the nominative the negation of great fear may be implied, its implied form being: 'no great fear is upon them', so that the presence of slight fear is imagined — the reverse of what was supposed in the question. So it is clear that the reason for the nominative is what we mentioned." End of quotation.
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلاَ هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ}: it has preceded that it is a negated clause and that the correct view is that «لا» is non-governing; «يَحْزنون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and on that weak view it would be in the position of the accusative.
Al-khawf: alarm and fright. One says: خافَ يخاف, so he is خائِف (afraid). The origin is خَوِف on the pattern of عَلِمَ [Translator's note: the printed text has «بزون», a misprint for «بوزن» (on the pattern of)]. It is made transitive by the hamza and by doubling; the Exalted said: {وَنُخَوِّفُهُمْ} [al-Isrāʾ: 60]. It is only about a future matter. Al-ḥuzn is the opposite of joy, taken from al-ḥazn, which is rugged ground, as though it were rugged anxiety; it is only about a past matter. One says: حَزِن يَحْزَن حُزْناً وحَزَناً. It is made transitive by the hamza, as in أَحْزَنْتُه, and حَزَّنْتُه with the same meaning, so faʿʿala and afʿala are of one meaning. It has also been said: أَحْزَنَه means he caused him grief. It has also been said: the fatḥa makes the verb transitive, as in شَتِرَتْ عينُه (his eyelid was split) and شَتَرها الله (Allah split it); this is on the view of those who hold that a vowel makes the verb transitive. It has been read in both dialectal forms, «حَزَنَه» and «أَحْزَنه», and their precise treatment will come.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
The saying of the Exalted: {ألا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ المفسدون}: the verse. «ألا» is a particle of alerting (tanbīh) and of opening (istiftāḥ). It is not compounded from the interrogative hamza and the negating «لا»; rather, it is simple. But it is a word shared between alerting and opening — in which case it enters upon a clause, whether nominal or verbal — and between proposal (al-ʿarḍ) and specification (al-takhṣīṣ) [Translator's note: «التخصيص» is probably a corruption of «التحضيض», urging], in which case it is specific to verbs, overtly or by implication. It may also be the «لا» of generic negation with the interrogative hamza entering upon it; it has rulings, some of which preceded at His saying {لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ} [al-Baqara: 2]. It may be for wishing (al-tamannī), and then it is treated like «ليت» in some of its rulings. Some permitted it to be an answer in the sense of «بلى» ("yes indeed"): someone says «لم يقم زيد» ("Zayd did not stand"), and you say «ألا», meaning "yes indeed, he did stand"; this is strange.
«إنهم» is «إنَّ» and its noun. «هم» may bear three aspects. One: that it is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the noun of «إنَّ», because the detached nominative pronoun may be used to emphasise all kinds of attached pronoun. [Second:] that it is a separating pronoun (faṣl). [Third:] that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «المفسدون» its khabar (predicate), both of them [together] being the khabar of «إنَّ» [Translator's note: the source has «خيرٌ» for «خبرٌ», a typo]. On the first two views «المفسدون» alone is the khabar of «إنَّ». In this clause various kinds of emphasis were brought, among them: the opening and alerting; the emphasis by «إنَّ»; and by bringing [Translator's note: the text reads «وبالإِتيانِ وبالتأكيدِ», where something after «وبالإِتيانِ» seems to have dropped out] the emphasis or the separation by the pronoun; and the definiteness in the khabar — by way of intensifying the rebuttal of them in what they claimed with their saying «إنما نحن مصلحون». For they put forth the answer as a nominal clause emphasised with «إنما», to indicate thereby the firm establishment of the quality for them; so Allah rebutted them with something more eloquent and more emphatic than what they claimed.
The saying of the Exalted: {ولكن لاَّ يَشْعُرُونَ}: the wāw conjoins this clause to what precedes it. «لكن» means correction (al-istidrāk), a meaning that never leaves it. It is a conjunction with single words, and it occurs only between two contraries or two contradictories; regarding two things that are merely different there is a disagreement, e.g. «ما قام زيدٌ لكن خرج بكر» ("Zayd did not stand, but Bakr went out"). Some adduced as evidence for that the saying of Ṭarafa:
190 - ولستُ بحَلاَّلِ التِّلاعِ لِبَيْتِهِ ... ولكن متى يَسْترفدِ القومُ أَرْفِدِ
(I am not one who camps in the ravines for [the sake of hiding] his tent; but whenever the people seek aid, I give aid.)
For his saying «متى يسترفدِ القوم أرفدِ» is neither a contrary nor a contradictory of what precedes it, but merely different from it. Some said: there is no proof in this for what is claimed, because his saying «لستُ بحلاَّل التِّلاعِ لبيته» is a metonymy (kināya) for negating stinginess, i.e. "I do not camp in the ravines out of stinginess", and his saying «متى يسترفد القوم أرفد» is a metonymy for generosity; it is as though he said: "I am not stingy, but generous." So here it occurs between two contraries. It does not govern when lightened (mukhaffafa), contrary to Yūnus; and it has many rulings.
The meaning of correction in this verse needs extra reflection and consideration. That is because, when they were forbidden from engaging in the like of the corruption they used to practise, and they countered that by [claiming] that they were reformers in it, and the Exalted informed that they are the corrupters, they were worthy of knowing that it was as the Exalted had informed and that they should not claim that they were reformers. So He corrected for them this meaning which they had missed, namely their lack of awareness of that. Similar to it is your saying «زيدٌ جاهلٌ ولكن لا يعلم» ("Zayd is ignorant, but he does not know"): inasmuch as he is characterised by ignorance, and ignorance has become a quality subsisting in him, he ought to know this quality in himself, because a person ought to know the qualities his self comprises; so you corrected [the statement] by [adding] that he does not know this quality subsisting in him, by way of intensifying [the description of] his ignorance.
The object of «يَشْعرون» is omitted: either an ellipsis for brevity (ḥadhf ikhtiṣār), i.e. "they are not aware that they are corrupters", or an ellipsis of restriction (ḥadhf iqtiṣār) — and this is better — i.e. they have no awareness at all.

semin-durr:131-131.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {إِذْ قَالَ لَهُ رَبُّهُ}: Concerning «إذ» there are five views, the soundest of which is that it is accusative (manṣūb) by «قال أَسْلَمْتُ», i.e.: he said "I have submitted" at the time of Allah's saying to him "Submit". The second: that it is a badal (substitute) from His saying «في الدنيا». The third: that it is accusative by «اصطفيناه». The fourth: that it is accusative by an implied (muqaddar) «اذكر» ("remember"); Abū al-Baqāʾ and al-Zamakhsharī mentioned this. On the assumption that it is governed by «اصطفيناه» or by an implied «اذكر», His saying «قال أسلمْتُ» remains disconnected from what precedes it, unless the omission of a conjunction is assumed, i.e.: "so he said", or it is made the answer to an implied question, i.e.: What was his answer? And it was said: He said "I have submitted". The fifth: one of them went far and made it, together with what follows it, in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the governing word being «اصطَفَيْناه».

In His saying {إِذْ قَالَ لَهُ رَبُّهُ} there is iltifāt (a shift of person), since had it come in keeping with its sequence it would have been said "when We said", because it comes after «ولقَدِ اصْطَفَيْناه». Its converse, in going out from the third person to the second person, is the poet's saying:
730 - باتَتْ تَشَكَّى إليَّ النفسُ مُجْهِشَةً ... وقد حَمَلْتُكَ سبعاً بعدَ سَبْعينا
(My soul spent the night complaining to me, on the verge of tears: "I have carried you seven years after seventy.")

His saying {لِرَبِّ العالمين} contains a grandeur that is not in saying «لك» ("to You") or «لربّي» ("to my Lord"), because if he acknowledges that He is the Lord of all the worlds, he acknowledges that He is his Lord and more besides, unlike the former; therefore he turned away from the two expressions. And in His saying «أَسْلْمِ» there is the omission of an object, its implied form being: "submit to your Lord".

semin-durr:71-71.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {لاَّ ذَلُولٌ}: the well-known reading is «ذلولٌ» in the nominative, as a naʿt (adjective) of بقرة, with negating «لا» placed in between, as was said regarding {لاَّ فَارِضٌ}; or as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is not ذلول", the clause made of this mubtadaʾ and khabar being in the position of the nominative as an adjective of بقرة. It has also been read «لا ذَلولَ» with fatḥa on the lām, taking it as the «لا» of exoneration (al-tabriʾa, i.e. the lā of generic negation), with the khabar omitted, its implied form being "there is no ذلول there" or something similar. But the meaning does not suit this reading; therefore al-Akhfash said: "لا ذلولٌ is an adjective, and it is not permissible to put it in the accusative."

الذَّلول is the cow that has been made tractable by work. One says بَقَرةٌ ذَلول, evidently tractable (الذِّل, with kasra on the dhāl), and رجلٌ ذَليل, evidently abased (الذُّل, with ḍamma). This was discussed at His words {الذلة} [al-Baqara: 61].

His words: {تُثِيرُ الأرض}: there are many views about this clause. The most apparent is that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in «ذلول», the implied sense being: "it is not made tractable while ploughing up [the earth]".

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "According to some it is a clause in the position of an adjective of بقرة, [i.e.] 'not tractable, ploughing up'." He also said: "It is not permissible for this clause to be in the position of a ḥāl, because it would be from an indefinite." As for his words "in the position of an adjective", it follows from them that the cow was one that ploughed up the earth, and the majority did not hold this, though some did, and its explanation will come shortly. As for his words "it is not permissible for it to be a ḥāl" — meaning from «بقرة», because it is indefinite — the answer is: we do not concede that it is a ḥāl from بقرة; rather it is from the pronoun in «ذلولٌ», as explained above. Or we say: rather it is a ḥāl from an indefinite that has been qualified and specified by His words {لاَّ ذَلُولٌ}, and when an indefinite is qualified, a ḥāl from it is acceptable by agreement.

It is also said that it is resumptive. Its being resumptive is on two ways. First: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it ploughs". Second: it is resumptive in its own right without implying a mubtadaʾ; rather it is a verbal clause begun simply to give information about that.

A group refused the view that it is resumptive, among them al-Akhfash ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān, and he gave two reasons. First: after it comes {وَلاَ تَسْقِي الحرث}; had it been resumptive, it would not be sound for «لا» to come between it and the wāw. Second: had it ploughed up the earth, the ploughing would have made it tractable, and Allah the Exalted has denied that of it by His words لا ذلولٌ. End of quotation. This [second] meaning is the very one by which I refused that «تثيرُ» be an adjective of بقرة, because the consequence is shared. For this reason Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is permissible, on the view of those who affirm this aspect" — meaning its ploughing and not watering — "that تُثير be in the position of the nominative as an adjective of بقرة."

Some have answered the second reason by saying that "ploughing up the earth" is an expression for its frisking and liveliness, as Imruʾ al-Qays said:

545 - يُهيلُ ويُذْري تُرْبَهُ ويُثيرُه ... إثارةَ نَبَّاثِ الهَواجِرِ مُخْمِسِ
(He scatters and winnows its soil and stirs it up, like the stirring of one who digs in the midday heat on the fifth day of thirst.)

i.e. it ploughs up the earth out of frisking and liveliness, not by ploughing and work.

Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is also said that it is resumptive." Then he said: "It is far from correct, for two reasons. First: His words {وَلاَ تَسْقِي الحرث} are conjoined to it and the conjoined is negated, so the thing it is conjoined to must be likewise, because in meaning they are one. Do you not see that you do not say مررتُ برجلٍ قائمٍ ولا قاعدٍ, but rather لا قاعدٍ without a wāw? So it must be here." And he mentioned the second reason as given above. He also permitted «تُثير» to be in the position of the nominative as an adjective of ذَلول — and the disagreement over whether a descriptive may itself be described has been given to you before.

So these are six aspects. Their summary: it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «ذَلولٌ», or from «بقرة»; or an adjective of بقرة, or of ذلول; or resumptive with an implied mubtadaʾ, or without one.

His words: {وَلاَ تَسْقِي الحرث مُسَلَّمَةٌ لاَّ شِيَةَ فِيهَا}: the discussion of this is as in what precedes it: being an adjective of بقرة or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The first لا is for negation" — meaning the one entering on «ذلولٌ» — "and the second is added/ to emphasise the first, because the meaning is: 'not a tractable one that ploughs and waters', on the basis that the two verbs are adjectives of ذلول, as if it were said: 'not tractable, ploughing and watering'."

It has been read «تُسْقي» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, from أَسْقى. Ploughing up the earth (إثارة الأرض) is moving it and turning it over; from this comes {وَأَثَارُواْ الأرض} [al-Rūm: 9], i.e. by ploughing and cultivation. In the hadith: «أثيروا القرآن، فإنه عِلْمُ الأولين والآخرِين» ("Turn over the Qurʾān, for it is the knowledge of the first and the last"), and in one narration: «مَنْ أرادَ العِلمَ فَلْيُثَوِّرِ القرآن» ("Whoever wants knowledge, let him turn over the Qurʾān").

مُسَلَّمةٌ is from سَلِمَ له كذا, i.e. it was free [of defects]. «شية» is a maṣdar: وَشَيْتُ الثوبَ أَشِيهِ وَشْياً وشِيَةً ("I embroidered the garment"). Its fāʾ (first radical) was dropped because in the imperfect it falls between a yāʾ and a kasra, and then the rest of the paradigm was made to follow it. Its pattern is عِلة, and like it are صِلة, عِدة and زِنة. It denotes a patch differing from the [main] colour. From it comes ثَوْبٌ مَوْشِيٌّ, i.e. woven in two or more colours, and ثور مَوْشِيُّ القوائم, i.e. a bull with piebald legs. The poet said:

546 - من وحشِ وَجْرَةَ مَوْشِيٍّ أَكارِعُه ... طاوِي المصيرِ كسَيْفِ الصيْقَلِ الفَرِدِ
(One of the wild beasts of Wajra, its shanks marked with spots, lean-bellied, like the matchless sword of the burnisher.)

From it comes «الواشي» for the talebearer, because he يَشي his speech, i.e. embellishes it and mixes it with lies. Some said: he is not called واشٍ until he alters his speech and embellishes it. One says ثورٌ أَشْيَه, فرس أَبْلَق, كبشٌ أَخْرَج, تيسٌ أَبْرَق and غرابٌ أَبْقَع, all of them meaning piebaldness. «شِيَةَ» is the noun of لا, and «فيها» is its khabar.

His words: {الآن جِئْتَ}: «الآن» is accusative by جِئْتَ. It is an adverb of time that implies the present and restricts the imperfect to it, according to the majority of grammarians. Some said: this is predominant, but it has come where it cannot be for the present, as in His words {فَمَن يَسْتَمِعِ الآن} [al-Jinn: 9] and {فالآن بَاشِرُوهُنَّ} [al-Baqara: 187]; had it implied the present, it would not have come with the verb of a condition and with an imperative, both of which are explicit for the future. This speaker expressed it in a formulation that agrees with his doctrine: "«الآن» is for a time all or part of which is present", meaning by "or part of it" something like {فَمَن يَسْتَمِعِ الآن يَجِدْ لَهُ}. It is indeclinable (mabnī).

There is disagreement about the reason for its indeclinability. Al-Zajjāj said: "Because it contains the meaning of pointing, for the meaning of أفعلُ الآن is 'this time'." It is also said: because it resembles a particle in keeping to a single form, in that it is not dualised, pluralised or diminutised. It is also said: because it contains the meaning of the particle of definition, namely alif-lām, like أمسِ; and this alif-lām in it is redundant (zāʾida), as shown by its indeclinability — no word defined by al- is known except as declinable — and the alif-lām became fixed in it as it did in الذي and التي and their kind. This is attributed to al-Fārisī. It is rejected on the ground that containment (taḍmīn) is abbreviation, so how can a thing be abbreviated and then something like its very wording be brought?

It keeps to adverbial use and is generally not inflected [in other functions]. Yet it occurs as a mubtadaʾ in his words, upon him be peace: «فهو يَهْوى في قَعْرِها الآنَ حينَ انتهى» ("so it is falling into its depth; now is when it has reached [the bottom]"): الآن is a mubtadaʾ and is mabnī on fatḥa for the reason given, and «حين» is its khabar, mabnī because it is annexed to a non-declinable. And it occurs in the genitive in his words:

547 - أإلى الآن لا يَبِينُ ارْعِواءُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Until now, is no desisting apparent? …)

Some claimed it is declinable, citing his words:

548 - كأنَّهما مِلآْنِ لم يتَغَيَّرا ... وقد مَرَّ للدارَيْنِ من بعدنا عَصْرُ
(As though from now the two had not changed, though an age has passed over the two abodes since us.)

meaning «من الآن», which he put in the genitive with kasra. But this may be mabnī on kasra.

Al-Farrāʾ claimed that it was transferred from a past verb, its origin being آنَ in the sense of حانَ ("it is time"), that al- entered it as a redundant addition, and that its being mabnī on fatḥa was retained. He made it like their saying «ما رأيته مذ شَبَّ إلى دَبَّ» ("I have not seen him from when he grew up to when he crept [in old age]"), and his saying, upon him be peace, «وأَنْهاكم عن قيلَ وقال» ("I forbid you 'it was said' and 'he said'"). He was answered that al- does not enter what is transferred from a past verb, and that it ought then to have been permissible to decline it, like its counterparts. Another view is reported from him: that its origin is «أوان», the alif was dropped and then the wāw was changed to alif; on this view its alif is from a wāw. Al-Rāghib put it under the root «أين», so its alif would be from a yāʾ. [The correct view is the first.]

It has been read «قالوا الآن» pronouncing [the hamza] fully without transfer, which is the reading of the majority; «قالُ لان», transferring the vowel of the hamza to the lām before it and dropping the hamza, which is a regular analogical rule, and so read Nāfiʿ, and Ḥamza with disagreement reported from him; and «قالو لاَن», keeping the wāw of قالوا, because it had only been dropped for the meeting of two quiescents, and the lām has now received a vowel by the transfer of the hamza's vowel to it; they took that into account, just as they said «لَحْمَر» for الأحمر. The verification of this will come, if Allah the Exalted wills, at {عَاداً الأولى} [al-Najm: 50]. A fourth way has been reported: «قالوا ألآن», cutting the hamza of connection (hamzat al-waṣl), and it is far-fetched.

His words: «بالحقِّ»: two aspects are possible. First: that it is the bāʾ of transitivity, like the hamza, as though it were said: أَجَأْتَ الحقَّ ("you have brought the truth"), i.e. you have mentioned it. Second: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «جِئْتَ», i.e. "you have come accompanied by the truth", or "with the truth with you".

His words: {وَمَا كَادُواْ يَفْعَلُونَ}: كادَ, its noun and its khabar. Most often its khabar is free of أَنْ; anomalous is his saying:

549 - قد كادَ من طولِ البِلى أَنْ يَمْحَصا ...
(From long decay it had almost been worn smooth.)

— the reverse of عسى. Its meaning is nearness to the action. A good number of its rulings have already been given, together with [the claim] that its negation is affirmation and its affirmation negation, and the answer to that, at His words {يَكَادُ البرق} [al-Baqara: 20], so let reference be made there.

semin-durr:72-72.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {فادارأتم فِيهَا}: a verb and its fāʿil (agent). The fāʾ is causal, because the mutual repelling was caused by the killing. The killing is ascribed to all of them, even though it issued only from one or two, as has been said, because it occurred among them; this is a common figurative usage.

The origin of ادَّارأتم is تَدارَأْتُم, of the pattern تفاعَلْتم, from الدَّرْء, which is repelling. The tāʾ met the dāl, which is close to it [in articulation]; assimilation was intended, so the tāʾ was changed to dāl and made quiescent for the assimilation. Since one cannot begin with a quiescent letter, the hamza of connection (hamzat al-waṣl) was brought in to begin with, and there remained ادَّارأتم; the original being «ادْدَارَأْتم», which was then assimilated. This is regular in every verb of the pattern تَفَاعَل or تفعَّل whose first radical is dāl, such as تَدَايَنَ / ادَّايَنَ and تَدَيَّن / ادَّيَّن; or ẓāʾ, ṭāʾ, ḍād or ṣād, such as تَطَاير / اطَّاير, تَطَيَّر / اطَّيَّر, تَظَاهَرَ / اظَّاهر, and تَطَهَّر / اطَّهَّر. The maṣdar (verbal noun) is on the pattern التفاعُل or التفعُّل, such as تدارؤ and تطهُّر, with regard to the original. This is a useful principle in all the paradigms, so let it be reflected upon.

His words: {والله مُخْرِجٌ مَّا كُنْتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ}: «الله» is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) and «مُخْرجٌ» is its khabar (predicate). ما is a relative noun, in the position of the accusative governed by the active participle. If it is said: the active participle does not govern when it has a past meaning unless it carries alif-lām — the answer/ is that this is the narration of a past state, and the active participle in it is not past; this is like the words of Allah the Exalted {وَكَلْبُهُمْ بَاسِطٌ ذِرَاعَيْهِ} [al-Kahf: 18]. Al-Kisāʾī makes it govern unrestrictedly and cites this and the like as evidence.

«ما» may be a nominal relative, in which case a resumptive pronoun is needed, its implied form being "bringing out that which you were concealing". It may also be maṣdariyya, the maṣdar standing in the place of the object, i.e. "bringing out what you concealed (مكتومَكم)".

This clause has no grammatical position because it is parenthetical between the conjoined and that to which it is conjoined, namely «فادَّارَأْتم» and «فقلنا اضرِبوه»; al-Zamakhsharī said this. The pronoun in «اضربوه» refers to the soul (النفس), interpreting it in the sense of "the person" and "the human being", or to the slain man indicated by His words «والله مُخْرِجٌ ما كنتم تكتمون». The clause «اضربوه» is in the position of the accusative governed by the verb "say".

semin-durr:73-73.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {كَذَلِكَ يُحْيِي الله}: «كذلك» is in the position of the accusative because it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being: "Allah gives life to the dead with a giving of life like that giving of life"; so it is attached to an omitted element, i.e. "a giving of life being like that giving of life". Or because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the definite maṣdar, i.e. "and He shows you the showing, in its state of resembling that giving of life" [Translator's note: so in the text; the context suggests "He gives life with the giving of life (يحيي الإحياء)"]; it was said before that this is the doctrine of Sībawayh. الموتى is the plural of «مَيِّت», which has already been discussed.

His words: {وَيُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِهِ}: the seeing here is visual, so the hamza is for transitivity and has given the verb a second object, namely «آياتِه»; the meaning is: "He makes you see His signs". «كم» is the first object. The origin of يُريكم is يُأَرْإيكم: the hamza of the pattern أَفْعل was dropped in the imperfect for the reason given at «يُؤْمنون» and its kind, leaving يُرئيكم; then the vowel of the hamza was transferred to the rāʾ and the hamza dropped for lightening. This transfer is obligatory in the root «رأى» and its paradigm, unlike other [verbs] whose second radical is hamza, such as نَأَى يَنْأَى. Not transferring in رأى and its paradigm is permitted only in poetic necessity, as in his words:

550 - أُري عَيْنَيَّ ما لم تَرْأَياهُ ... كِلانا عالمٌ بالتُّرَّهاتِ
(I show my two eyes what they have never seen; each of us is versed in idle tales.)

semin-durr:23-23.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَإِن كُنْتُمْ فِي رَيْبٍ مِّمَّا نَزَّلْنَا على عَبْدِنَا فَأْتُواْ}: «إنْ» is a conditional particle that makes two verbs jussive (majzūm), a protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and an apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). It is used only for what may possibly occur, and it is the mother of the category; for that reason what it makes jussive is often omitted, and sometimes the protasis and apodosis are omitted together. The poet said:
270 - قالَتْ بناتُ العَمِّ يا سَلْمى وإنْ ... كانَ فقيراً مُعْدِماً قالَتْ: وإنْ
(The cousins said: "O Salmā, even if he is poor and destitute?" She said: "Even if.")
i.e. even if he is poor I will marry him.
«إنْ» may be negating, in which case it is sometimes operative and sometimes inoperative; it may be the lightened form [of «إنّ»]; and it may be redundant (zāʾida), both regularly and irregularly. Some permitted it to be in the sense of «إذْ», and some in the sense of «قد». It has many rules.
«في ريب» is the khabar (predicate) of «كان», so it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted element. The position of «كان» is jussive; although it is past in wording, it is future in meaning.
Al-Mubarrad claimed that the incomplete (nāqiṣa) «كان» has a rule with «إنْ» that the other incomplete verbs do not have: he claimed that, owing to the strength of «كان», the conditional «إنْ» does not turn its meaning to the future, but it keeps its past meaning. Abū al-Baqāʾ followed him in this, explaining it by its frequent use without denoting an event. This is rejected by the majority, because making something conditional (taʿlīq) can only be in the future; and they interpreted whatever apparently says otherwise, such as {إِن كَانَ قَمِيصُهُ قُدَّ} [Yūsuf: 26], either by implying «يَكُنْ» after «إنْ», or as being about its becoming clear, the implied form being «إنْ يكُنْ قميصُه» (if his shirt is) or «إن يَتبيَّنْ كونُ قميصِه» (if it becomes clear that his shirt is). When this meaning was hidden from some, they made «إنْ» here equivalent to «إذْ».
His words «في ريبٍ» are figurative (majāz), in that He made doubt a container surrounding them, like a place, because of how often it occurred from them. «مِمَّا» is attached to an omitted element because it is a naʿt (adjective) of «ريب», so it is in the position of the genitive; «مِنْ» is causal or for the beginning of an extent, and it may not be partitive. It may also be attached to «ريب», i.e. if you doubt because of [what We sent down], so «مِنْ» here is causal. «ما» is a relative noun or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, and on both views the referring pronoun is omitted, i.e. «نَزَّلناه» (We sent it down).
The doubling in «نزَّلنا» here is for making transitive (taʿdiya), synonymous with the transitivizing hamza; this is shown by the reading «أنْزَلْنا» with hamza. Al-Zamakhsharī made the doubling here indicate its being sent down in instalments at different times. Someone said: "What he held regarding the doubling of the word here is what is expressed as intensification (takthīr), i.e. one does [that] time after time, and this is indicated by doubling and expressed as multitude." He said: "He overlooked a rule, namely that the doubling indicating this has as its condition, usually, that it be in verbs that are transitive before doubling, such as جَرَّحْتُ زيداً (I wounded Zayd repeatedly) and فتَّحْتُ الباب (I opened the doors); one does not say جَلَّس زيدٌ. And «نَزَّل» was not transitive before doubling; it was only its doubling that made it transitive.
[He said] 'usually' because doubling has occasionally come indicating multitude in an intransitive verb, as in «مَوَّت المالُ» (the livestock died in numbers). Also, doubling that indicates multitude does not make an intransitive verb transitive, as with «موَّت المال», whereas «نَزَّل» was intransitive and became transitive by doubling; this shows that its doubling is for transference, not for intensification. Also, the word of the Exalted {لَوْلاَ نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ القرآن جُمْلَةً وَاحِدَةً} [al-Furqān: 32] would need interpretation. Also, doubling has come where intensification is impossible, as in the words of the Exalted {وَقَالُواْ لَوْلاَ نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ} [al-Anʿām: 37] and {لَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْهِم مِّنَ السمآء مَلَكاً رَّسُولاً} [al-Isrāʾ: 95], except by a very far-fetched interpretation, since the meaning is not that they demanded the repeated sending down of a sign, nor that He made the repeated sending down of an angel-messenger conditional on there being angels on the earth."
In His words «نَزَّلْنا» there is iltifāt (a shift of person) from the third person to the first, because before it comes {اعبدوا رَبَّكُمُ}; had the speech continued on that basis, it would have been said «ممَّا نَزَّلَ على عبدِه» (of what He sent down upon His servant), but He shifted for magnification. «على عبدنا» is attached to «نزَّلنا», and it is made transitive with «على» because it conveys elevation (istiʿlāʾ), as if what is sent down took firm hold of the one upon whom it is sent down and covered him; for this reason most of the Qur'an has it made transitive with it rather than with «إلى», which conveys only reaching the end-point and arrival. The annexation in «عبدِنا» conveys honour, as in the poet's words:
271 - يا قومِ قلبي عندَ زهْراءِ ... يَعْرِفُه السامعُ والرائي
لا تَدْعُني إلاَّ بيا عبدَها ... فإنه أَشْرَفُ أسمائي
(O my people, my heart is with Zahrāʾ — whoever hears or sees knows it. Do not call me except "O her servant", for that is the noblest of my names.)
It was read «عبادِنا» (Our servants). It was said: the intended meaning is the Prophet (peace be upon him) and his community, because the benefit of what was sent down accrues to them. It was also said: the intended meaning is all the prophets, peace be upon them.
The words of the Exalted «فَأْتُواْ»: the apodosis of the condition. The fāʾ here is obligatory, because what comes after it cannot by itself be a protasis. The origin of «فأْتُوا» is اإْتِيُوا, like اضْربوا: the first hamza is the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl), brought in in order to begin with a vowelless letter, and the second is the first radical of the word. Two hamzas met, so the second had to be changed into yāʾ, as in «إيمان» and its like. The ḍamma on the yāʾ, which is the last radical, was felt heavy, so it was made implied; the yāʾ became vowelless, followed by the vowelless wāw of the pronoun, so the yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and the tāʾ was given ḍamma for harmony. So the pattern of «ايتوا» is افْعُوا. This hamza is needed only at the start of speech; in connected speech it is dispensed with, and the hamza that is the first radical returns, because it was changed into yāʾ only because of the kasra that preceded it, which has now gone — as in «فَأْتوا» and its like. The hamza that is the first radical may be dropped in the imperative, as in the poet's words:
272 - فإنْ نحنُ نَنْهَضْ لكم فَنَبُرَّكُمْ ... فَتُونا فعادُونا إذاً بالجرائمِ
(If we rise up for you and treat you kindly, then come to us — and then show us enmity with crimes [if you will].)
He means «فَأْتونا», like His words «فَأْتوا». «بسورة» is attached to «أتوا».
The words of the Exalted: {مِّن مِّثْلِهِ}: there are three views about the hāʾ. First: it refers to «ما نَزَّلنا», so «مِن مثله» is an adjective of «سورة», attached to an omitted element as has been established, i.e. "a sūra that is of the like of what was sent down, in its eloquence, its telling of the unseen, and so on"; the meaning of «مِنْ» is then partitive. Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Mahdawī permitted it to be explicative (li-l-bayān); they two and Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it to be redundant, but that only works on the view of al-Akhfash.
Second: it refers to «عبدِنا», so «من مثله» is attached to «أْتُوا», and the meaning of «مِنْ» is the beginning of an extent. On this view it may also be an adjective of «سورة», i.e. "a sūra coming from a man like Our servant".
Third: Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It refers to the rivals (al-andād), in the singular form, as in His words {وَإِنَّ لَكُمْ فِي الأنعام لَعِبْرَةً نُّسْقِيكُمْ مِّمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ} [al-Naḥl: 66]." I say: there is no need for that, and the meaning also rejects it.
السُّورة is the high rank; al-Nābigha said:
273 - ألم ترَ أنَّ الله أعطاكَ سُورةً ... ترى كلَّ مَلْكٍ دونَها يَتَذَبْذَبُ
(Do you not see that Allah has given you a lofty rank, below which you see every king wavering?)
The sūra of the Qur'an was named so because its possessor is ennobled by it and it raises him. It was also said: it is derived from السُّؤْر, which is the remainder; from it comes «أَسْأَروا في الإِناء» (they left a remainder in the vessel). Al-Aʿshā said:
274 - فبانَتْ وقد أَسْأَرَتْ في الفؤا ... دِ صَدْعاً على نَأَيِها مُسْتطيرا
(She departed, having left in the heart, despite her distance, a crack spreading far.)
i.e. she left behind. This is supported by the fact that Tamīm and others pronounce it with hamza, saying «سُؤْرة». The sūra of the Qur'an was named so because it is a portion of it; on this view the word is lightened from the hamza. It was also said: it is derived from سُور البِناء (the wall of a building), because it surrounds its reciter and protects him like the wall of a city. But the plural of the Qur'anic «سورة» is سُوَر, with fatḥa on the wāw, while the plural of «سورة» of a building is سُوْر, with sukūn; so they distinguished between them in the plural.
The words of the Exalted: {وادعوا شُهَدَآءَكُم}: this is an imperative clause conjoined to the imperative before it, so it is also in the position of the jussive. The pattern of «ادْعُوا» is افْعُوا, because the last radical of the word is dropped as a sign of the sukūn in the imperative, which corresponds to the jussive in the imperfect. The wāw is the pronoun of the agents. «شهداءَكم» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the plural of «شهيد», like ظريف [/ظُرَفاء]. It was also said: rather, the plural of «شاهد», like شاعر [/شُعَراء]. The first is preferable, because فُعَلاء is regular for فَعِيل but not for فاعل. الشهادة is presence.
{مِّن دُونِ الله} is attached to «ادْعُوا», i.e. call, apart from Allah, your witnesses, and do not call Allah to witness; it is as if He said: call, other than Allah, whoever will testify for you. It may also be attached to «شهداءَكم», the meaning being: call those whom you have taken as gods apart from Allah and claimed would testify for you to the validity of your worshipping them; or your helpers apart from the friends of Allah, i.e. those whose help you seek apart from Allah. Or the meaning of «مِنْ دونِ الله» may be "before Allah", as in the poet's words:
275 - تُريك القَذَى مِنْ دونِها وهي دونَه ... لوجهِ أخيها في الإِناءِ قُطُوبُ
(It shows you the mote in front of it, while it is in front of the mote; it frowns in the vessel at the face of its companion.)
i.e. it shows you the mote in front of it, while it is in front of the mote, because of its thinness and clearness.
Abū al-Baqāʾ chose that {مِّن دُونِ الله} be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «شهداءكم», the governing element being omitted. He said: "Its implied form is: your witnesses, apart from Allah or apart from Allah's helpers."
«دونَ» is one of the adverbs of place. According to the well-known view it is not inflected except in being made genitive by «مِنْ». Al-Akhfash claimed that it is inflected, and counted among such cases the word of the Exalted {وَمِنَّا دُونَ ذَلِكَ} [al-Jinn: 11]; he said: «دونَ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «منَّا» its khabar, and it is indeclinable (mabnī) only because it is annexed to an indeclinable word. Its being nominative as a khabar is anomalous in the poet's words:
276 - ألم تَرَ أنِّي قد حَمَيْتُ حقيقتي ... وباشَرْتُ حدَّ الموتِ والموتُ دونُها
(Have you not seen that I defended what I must protect, and touched the edge of death, with death before it?)
It is one of the nouns that are necessarily annexed in wording and meaning. As for «دون» meaning "inferior", that is an adjective like other adjectives: you say «هذا ثوبٌ دونٌ» (this is an inferior garment) and «رأيت ثوباً دوناً», i.e. inferior; and it is not what we are dealing with.
The words of the Exalted: {إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ}: this is a condition whose apodosis is omitted because it is indicated, its implied form being «إنْ كنتم صادِقين فافعلوا» (if you are truthful, then do so). What the truthfulness relates to is omitted. The apparent implied form is: "if you are truthful in your being in doubt about what was sent down upon Our servant, that it is from Us". It was also said: [truthful] in what you are able to do by way of rivalling it; He stated this explicitly of them in another verse, where the Exalted said, relating their words: {لَوْ نَشَآءُ لَقُلْنَا مِثْلَ هذا} [al-Anfāl: 31].
الصدق is the opposite of lying; it has been treated before, so it may be learned from there. الصديق (friend) is derived from it, because of his truthfulness in affection and good counsel. الصِّدْق among spears is the hard one.

semin-durr:39-39.t:
His saying: {والذين كَفَرواْ, to His saying: خَالِدُونَ}: «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what follows it is the ṣila (relative clause) and the referring pronoun. «بآياتنا» is attached to كذَّبوا. The verse may also belong to the chapter of governing (al-iʿmāl), because «كفروا» calls for it, and it would be a case of the second governing, given the omission from the first, the implied form being: "they disbelieved in Us and denied Our signs". «أولئك» is a second mubtadaʾ and «أصحابُ» its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of the first. «أولئك» may also be a badal (substitute) of the relative noun or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of it, with «أصحابُ» the khabar of the relative mubtadaʾ. His saying: {هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ} is a nominal clause in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because that is stated explicitly in several places; the Exalted said: {أَصْحَابُ النار خَالِدِينَ} [al-Taghābun: 10]. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it to be a ḥāl from «النار»; he said: "because it contains a pronoun referring to it, and what governs it is the meaning of the annexation or the implied lām." End of quotation. What is involved in that is already known.
It may also be in the position of the nominative as a khabar of أولئك; in that case it has been given two predicates, one of them a single word, namely «أصحابُ», [and the other] a clause; the disagreement over this is already known.
«فيها» is attached to «خالدون». They said: from the first statement what is stated in the second has been omitted, and from the second what is stated in the first, the implied form being: "whoever follows My guidance, no fear and no grief will overtake him, and he is a companion of the Garden; and whoever disbelieves and denies, grief and fear will overtake him, and he is a companion of the Fire", because the division requires that. They compared it with the poet's saying:
397 - وإني لَتَعْروني لِذِكْراكِ فَتْرَةٌ ... كما انتفَضَ العصفورُ بلَّلَه القَطْرُ
(At the mention of you a languor seizes me, as the sparrow shudders when the rain has wetted it.)
Al-āya, [linguistically], is a sign. Al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī said:
398 - تَوَهَمْتُ آياتٍ لها فَعَرَفْتُها ... لستةِ أعوامٍ وذا العامُ سابِعُ
(I made out signs of her [abode] and recognized them after six years, and this year is the seventh.)
A verse of the Quran was called [an āya] because it is a sign of the separation of what precedes it from what follows it. It has also been said: it was so called because it gathers letters of the Quran, so it would be from their saying: «خرج بنو فلان بآيتِهم», i.e. with their whole company. The poet said:
399 - خَرَجْنا مِن النَّقْبَيْنِ لا حَيَّ مِثْلُنا ... بآياتِنا نُزْجي اللِّقاحَ المَطافِلاَ
(We came out of the two mountain passes — no tribe is like us — with our whole company, driving the milch-camels with their young.)
The grammarians disagreed over its pattern. The doctrine of Sībawayh and al-Khalīl is that it is faʿala, the origin being أَيَية with fatḥa on the middle radical; the yāʾ was vowelled and what preceded it had fatḥa, so it was changed into alif. This is anomalous, because when two weak letters come together, the latter is the one modified, since it is the locus of change, as in هوى and حوى. Like it in anomaly are غاية, طاية and راية.
The doctrine of al-Kisāʾī is that its pattern is آيِيَة, on the pattern fāʿila, so analogy would require assimilation, giving آيَّة like دابَّة; but that was abandoned for lightness, and they dropped its middle radical, just as they lightened كَيْنونة, whose origin is كيَّنونة with a doubled yāʾ. They weakened this on the ground that the form كيَّنونة is heavier, so lightening suits it, unlike this one.
The doctrine of al-Farrāʾ is that it is faʿla with a quiescent middle radical, and Abū al-Baqāʾ chose it. He said: "Because it is from تَأَيَّا القوم, i.e. they gathered; and they said in the plural: آياء, so the [first] yāʾ appeared, and the final hamza is a substitute for a yāʾ; its pattern is afʿāl, and the second alif is a substitute for a hamza which is the first radical of the word. Had its middle radical been wāw, they would have said in the plural: آواء. Then they changed the quiescent yāʾ into alif contrary to analogy." End of quotation. He means that a weak letter is not changed unless it is vowelled and what precedes it has fatḥa.
Some of the Kufans held that its pattern is أَيِيَة, with a kasra on the middle radical, like نَبِقَة, and it was then modified; in anomaly this is like the doctrine of Sībawayh and al-Khalīl. It has also been said: its pattern is faʿula, with ḍamma on the middle radical. And it has been said: its origin is أياة, with the second letter modified, and it was then transposed by putting the final radical first and the middle radical last; this is weak. These are six doctrines, none of which is free from anomaly.

semin-durr:87-87.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَقَفَّيْنَا مِن بَعْدِهِ بالرسل} ...: the doubling in «قَفَّيْنا» is not for transitivisation (taʿdiya), since if it were so it would take two objects, because before doubling it takes one object, as in «قَفَوْت زيداً» ("I followed Zayd"); rather it has been made to include (ḍummina) the meaning of «جِئْنا» ("We brought"), as though it were said: "and We brought after him the messengers." If it is said: it may be doubly transitive, in the sense that the first object is omitted and the second is «بالرسل», the bāʾ in it being redundant (zāʾida), its construal being: {وَقَفَّيْنَا مِن بَعْدِهِ بالرسل} [Translator's note: so in the source; the intended construal is presumably one with the first object supplied and the bāʾ dropped] —
the answer is that its frequent occurrence in the Quran in this way makes this construal unlikely. There will be further explanation of this in [Sūrat] al-Māʾida, if Allah the Exalted wills.
The root form of «قَفَّينا» is «قَفَّوْنا», but when the wāw occurred as the fourth letter it was changed into yāʾ. Its derivation is from «قَفَوْتُه», when you follow his nape (qafā); then the usage was extended and it was applied to every follower, even if the time of the follower is far from that of the one followed. Umayya said:
601 - قالَتْ لأختٍ له قُصِّيه عن جُنُبٍ ... وكيفَ تَقْفُو ولا سَهْلٌ ولا جَبَلُ
(She said to a sister of his: "Follow his track from a distance" — but how can she follow when there is neither plain nor mountain?)
«القَفا» is the back of the neck; it is also called «القافية», and from it is the rhyme (qāfiya) of poetry, because it follows the structure of the speech and is its end. The meaning of «قَفَّيْنا» is "We made to follow", as in His saying: {ثُمَّ أَرْسَلْنَا رُسُلَنَا تَتْرَى} [al-Muʾminūn: 44].
{مِن بَعْدِهِ} is attached to (mutaʿalliq) it, and likewise «بالرُسل». It is the plural of «رسول» in the sense of «مُرْسَل» (one sent), and «فُعُل» is not regular for «فَعُول» in the sense of «مَفْعول». The sukūn of the middle radical is the dialect of the Ḥijāz, and Yaḥyā and al-Ḥasan read with it; the ḍamma is the dialect of Tamīm. The Seven read according to the dialect of Tamīm, except Abū ʿAmr where it is annexed to «نا», «كم» or «هم», for he read with sukūn because of the succession of vowels.
His saying: «عيسى» is a non-Arabic proper name, and for that reason it is a diptote. The grammarians spoke about its pattern and derivation on the supposition that it was Arabic in origin. Sībawayh said: "Its pattern is «فِعْلى», and the yāʾ in it is an attachment (mulḥaqa) [making it conform] to quadriliteral roots, like the yāʾ of «مِعْزَى»" — meaning by "yāʾ" the alif; he called it yāʾ because it is written with yāʾ. Al-Fārisī said: "Its alif is not for the feminine, as in «ذِكْرى», as is shown by their declining it [as a triptote] when indefinite." ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd al-Ṣayrafī said: "Its pattern is «فِعْلَل»," so the alif for him is radical, in the sense that it is changed from a radical letter. Ibn al-Bādhish refuted that against him on the grounds that yāʾ and wāw are not radicals in quadriliteral roots. So whoever said that «عِيسى» is derived from «العَيْس», which is whiteness mixed with a reddish tinge — like Abū al-Baqāʾ and others — is not correct, because derivation and morphological inflection do not apply to a non-Arabic word. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It was said: «عيسى» in Syriac is «أَيْسوع»."
His saying: «ابنَ مريم» is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) or a badal (substitute); it may also be a naʿt (adjective), but the first is more appropriate, because «ابن مريم» has functioned like a proper name for him. Qualification by «ابن» has rulings specific to it which will come explained, if Allah the Exalted wills; and the derivation of «ابن» and its root form have preceded.
«مَرْيم» is originally, in Syriac, an adjective meaning "servant", then it was used as a name, and for that reason it is a diptote. In the language of the Arabs it is the woman who mixes much with men, like «الزِّير» among men, who is the one who mixes much with women. Ruʾba said:
602 - قلتُ لِزِيرٍ لم تَصِلْهُ مَرْيَمُهْ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I said to a ladies' man whom his "maryam" did not join...)
The yāʾ of «الزير» is from a wāw, because it is from «زار يَزُور»; it was changed because of the kasra before it, like «الرِّيح». So the word «مريم» became shared between the two languages. Its pattern according to the grammarians is «مَفْعَل», not «فَعْيَل». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Because «فَعْيَل» with fatḥa on the first letter is not established among the patterns, as it is established in the like of «عِثْيَر» and «عِلْيَب»." Some established «فَعْيَل» and counted among it the like of «ضَمْيَد», the name of a place, «مَدْيَن» on the view that its mīm is radical, and «ضَهْيَا» with the short ending, which is the woman who does not menstruate, or who has no breasts — because it is derived from «ضاهَأَتْ», i.e. she resembled, since she resembled men in that; it may also be given the long ending, as al-Zajjāj said. Ibn Jinnī said: "As for «ضَمْيد» and «عَثْيَر», they are fabricated," so there is no evidence in them for the existence of «فَعْيَل». The soundness of the yāʾ in «مريم» is contrary to analogy, since it ought to have been weakened by transferring the vowel of the yāʾ to the rāʾ and then changing the yāʾ into alif, as in «مَباع» from «البَيْع»; but it is anomalous, [as are] «مَزْيَد» and «مَدْيَن». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«مَرْيَم» is a non-Arabic proper name; had it been derived from «رامَ يريم» it would have been «مَرِيم» with a quiescent yāʾ. Among proper names there has occurred [the form] with fatḥa on the yāʾ, such as «مَزْيَد», and that is contrary to analogy."
His saying: {وَأَيَّدْنَاهُ} is conjoined to His saying: {وَآتَيْنَا عِيسَى}. The majority read «أيَّدْناه» on the pattern «فَعَّلْناه»; Mujāhid and Ibn Muḥayṣin read — and it is narrated from Abū ʿAmr — «آيَدْنَاه» on the pattern «أَفْعَلْناه». The root form is «أَاْيَدَ» with two hamzas, the second of them quiescent, so the second had to be changed into alif, as in «أَأْمَنَ» and its class. The middle radical, which is the yāʾ, remained sound, as it remained sound in «أَغْيَلَت» and «أَغْيَمَت»; this is an anomalous retention of soundness, except in the verb of wonder (taʿajjub), as in «ما أَبْيَنَ» and «أَطْوَل». It is related from Abū Zayd that the soundness of «أَغْيَلَت» is regular. If it is said: why was «آيَدْناه» not weakened as the like of «أَبَعْناه» was weakened, so that it need not be construed as anomalous? The answer is that if it were weakened — by casting the vowel of the middle radical onto the first radical, so that two quiescent letters, the middle and final radicals, meet, so that the middle radical is elided because of the meeting of two quiescents; then two hamzas with fatḥa come together, so the second must be changed into wāw, as in «أَوادِم»; then the wāw is vowelled after a fatḥa and is changed into alif, so that the word becomes «أَادْناه» — that would lead to weakening both the first and the middle radicals. Since weakening it would lead to that, it was rejected, unlike «أَبَعْناه» and «أَقَمْناه», in which there is only weakening of the middle radical. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "If you say: why was the yāʾ which is the middle radical not elided, as it was elided in the like of «أَسَلْناه» from «سالَ يَسالُ»? It is said: had they done that, two weakenings would have followed one another: one of them changing the second hamza into alif, and then eliding the alif substituted for the yāʾ because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the alif before it; the word would have become «آدْناه», so the first and middle radicals would have been elided — and «أسلناه» is not like that, because there only the middle radical is elided."
Al-Zamakhsharī said in [Sūrat] al-Māʾida: "«آيَدْتُك» on the pattern «أَفْعَلْتُك»," and Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "on the pattern «فاعَلْتُك»," then he said: "It appears that the root form in both readings is «أَفْعَلْتُك», and then the weakening differed." End quote.
What appears is that «أيَّد» is «فَعَّل», because its imperfect comes as «يُؤَيِّدُ» with doubling; had «أَيَّد» with doubling been on the pattern «أَفْعَلَ», its imperfect would have been «يُؤْيِدُ», like «يُؤْمِنُ» from «آمَنَ». As for «آيَدَ», i.e. with prolongation, the transmission of its imperfect needs to be based on what is heard: if «يُؤايِدُ» like «يُقاتِل» is heard, then it is «فاعَل»; if «يُؤْيِدُ» like «يُكْرِمُ» is heard, then «آيد» is «أَفْعَل». The Shaykh mentioned all of this in al-Māʾida. Then he said: "Ibn ʿAṭiyya's statement 'the weakening differed' is not clear" — and that is correct. However, his saying "what appears is that «أيَّد» in the reading of the majority is «فَعَّل», not «أَفْعَل», etc." is questionable, because it suggests that something else is possible, which is impossible: how could it be imagined that «أيَّدَ» with doubling in the reading of the majority is on the pattern «أَفْعَل»? This is something that does not occur.
«الأَيْدُ» is strength. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib said:
603 - الحمدُ للهِ الأَعزِّ الأكرمِ ... أَيَّدَنا يومَ زُحوفِ الأشْرَمِ
(Praise be to Allah, the Mightiest, the Most Generous, who strengthened us on the day of al-Ashram's advancing hosts.)
The correct view is that «فَعَّل» and «أَفْعَل» here have one meaning, which is "We strengthened him." Some distinguished between them, saying: "As for the prolonged form, its meaning is strength; as for the short form, its meaning is support and help" — and this in reality is no distinction. The Arabs have substituted jīm for the yāʾ in «آيَدَ» on the pattern «أَفْعَل», saying «آجَدَهُ», i.e. he strengthened him. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "One says: «الحمدُ لله الذي آجَدَني بعد ضَعْفٍ وأَوْجَدني بعد فَقْر» ('Praise be to Allah who strengthened me after weakness and enriched me after poverty')." This is just as they substituted jīm for its yāʾ [in «يد»], saying «لا أَفْعَل ذلك جَدَ الدهرِ», i.e. «يدَ الدهر» ("I will not do that ever"); it is a substitution that is not regular.
His saying: {بِرُوحِ القدس} is attached to «أيَّدْناه». Ibn Kathīr read «القُدْس» with a quiescent dāl, and the rest with ḍamma; they are two dialects: the ḍamma for the Ḥijāz and the sukūn for Tamīm, and that has preceded. Abū Ḥaywa read «القُدُوس» with a wāw. There is also a dialectal form with fatḥa on the qāf and the dāl. Its meaning is purity or blessing, as preceded at His saying «ونقدِّسُ لك». «الروح» originally is a name for the part by which life comes about in a living being — al-Rāghib said this — and what is meant by it is Jibrīl, upon him be peace, because of the saying of Ḥassān:
604 - وجبريلٌ رسولُ الله فينا ... وروحُ القُدْسِ ليس له كِفَاءُ
(And Jibrīl, Allah's messenger, is among us, and the Spirit of Holiness, who has no equal.)
He was so named because through him hearts come to life.
His saying: {أَفَكُلَّمَا جَآءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ}: the hamza here is for clarification (tawḍīḥ) [Translator's note: so in the source; probably a scribal error for «التوبيخ», reproach] and rebuke, and the fāʾ is for conjunction: it conjoined this clause to what precedes it, and the interrogative particle was given importance and fronted. The verification of that has passed, and [also] that al-Zamakhsharī supplies a clause between the hamza and the conjunction to which to conjoin it. This clause may be conjoined to what precedes it without omission of anything, as though He said: "We gave, O Children of Israel, your prophets what We gave them; so whenever a messenger came to you..." It is also possible to supply something omitted before it, i.e. "so you did what you did; then whenever a messenger came to you...". The discussion of «كلما» has preceded at His saying:
{كُلَّمَا أَضَآءَ} [al-Baqara: 20]. What makes it accusative here is «استكبرتم». «رسول» is «فَعُول» in the sense of «مَفْعُول», i.e. «مُرْسَل»; «فَعُول» in the sense of «مَفْعول» is rare — there occurs of it «الرَّكُوب» and «الحَلُّوب», i.e. that which is ridden and that which is milked. It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning «الرسالة» (message); al-Zamakhsharī said this, and he cited:
605 - لقد كَذَبَ الواشون ما فُهْتُ عندَهم ... بِسِرٍّ ولا أَرْسَلْتُهُمْ برَسول
(The slanderers have lied: I uttered no secret before them, nor sent them with any message.)
i.e. «برسالة». Of this, according to him, is: {إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ العالمين} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 16].
His saying: {بِمَا لاَ تهوى أَنْفُسُكُمْ} is attached to His saying «جاءكم». «جاء» is transitive by itself at times, as in this verse, and by a preposition at other times, as in «جِئْتُ إليه». «ما» is a relative noun meaning «الذي», and the returning pronoun is omitted because the conditions are fulfilled; the implied form is: «بما لا تهواه». «تهوى» is the imperfect of «هَوِي» with kasra on the middle radical, and its final radical is from yāʾ because its middle radical is wāw, and the class of «طَوَيْتُ» and «شَوَيْتُ» is more frequent than the class of «قوَّة» and «حُوَّة». There is no evidence in «هَوِيَ», because the middle radical has kasra, and it is like «شَقِي» from «الشَّقاوة»; their saying «هَوَيان» in the dual of its maṣdar is the clearest proof of that. The meaning of «تَهْوَى» is: it loves and chooses. The basic meaning of «الهَوَى» is inclination; it was so called because it makes its possessor fall (yahwī) into the Fire, and for that reason it is mostly used only of what has no good in it; but it is sometimes used of what is good. In the sound ḥadīth there is ʿUmar's saying about the captives of Badr: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ inclined to what Abū Bakr said and did not incline to what I said." And from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her: "By Allah, I see your Lord only hastening to fulfil your desire (hawāk)." Its plural is «أَهْواء»; He the Exalted said: {بِأَهْوَائِهِم} [al-Anʿām: 119]. It is not pluralised as «أَهْوِية», even though «نَدَى» and «أَنْدِية» occurs; the poet said:
606 - في ليلةٍ من جُمادى ذاتِ أَنْدِيَةٍ ... لا يُبْصِرُ الكلبُ في ظَلْمائها الطُّنُبا
(On a dewy night of Jumādā, in whose darkness the dog cannot see the tent-ropes.)
As for «هوى يَهْوي», with fatḥa in the past and kasra in the imperfect, its meaning is falling. «الهَوِيُّ» with fatḥa on the hāʾ is going downward, and «الهُوِيُّ» is going upward; the verification of all that will come. He attributed the verb to the souls rather than to the addressees — He did not say «بما لا تَهْوون» — to draw attention to the fact that the evil act is mostly attributed to the soul, as in: {إِنَّ النفس لأَمَّارَةٌ بالسواء} [Yūsuf: 53], {بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكُمْ أَنفُسُكُمْ} [Yūsuf: 18], {فَطَوَّعَتْ لَهُ نَفْسُهُ} [al-Māʾida: 30]. «استكبر» means «تَكَبَّرَ» (to be arrogant).
His saying: {فَفَرِيقاً كَذَّبْتُمْ}: the fāʾ conjoins the clause «كَذَّبْتم» to «استكبرتم». «فريقاً» is a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object), fronted so that the verse-endings agree; likewise {وَفَرِيقاً تَقْتُلُونَ}. There must be something omitted, i.e. «فريقاً منهم» ("a party of them"). The meaning is that from their arrogance there arose their hastening to reject one party of the messengers and to kill others. He put rejection first because it is the first evil they do, and because it is common to the one killed and others, for those killed were also rejected by them; it was not stated explicitly [for them] only because He mentioned something uglier than it in deed. «تقتلون» was brought as an imperfect either because it is future, since they were seeking to kill the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — together with what it involves of agreement with the verse-endings and fawāṣil — or because past action is meant [Translator's note: the source's «أن الأمر فظيع» lacks a connective here; the sense is "because the matter is so atrocious"] and it was intended to make it present in the souls and depict it in the hearts. Al-Rāghib allowed {فَفَرِيقاً كَذَّبْتُمْ} to be conjoined to His saying «وأَيَّدْناه», with «أفكلما» and what follows it being a separation between them by way of disapproval. The first is more apparent, although what he said is possible.

semin-durr:132-132.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {ووصى}: It has been read from «وصَّى», and in it there is the sense of multiplicity with respect to the object enjoined; and «أَوْصى» as a four-letter verb, which is the reading of Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir, and so it is in the codices of Medina and Syria. It has been said that «أَوْصى» and «وصَّى» have one meaning.

The pronoun in «بها» has six views. The first: that it refers back to the milla (religion) in His saying: {وَمَن يَرْغَبُ عَن مِّلَّةِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ}. The Shaykh said: "And with it al-Zamakhsharī began, and [al-Mahdawī] and others did not mention it." But al-Zamakhsharī — may Allah have mercy on him — did not mention this; he only mentioned its referring back to His saying «أَسَلَمْتُ», interpreting it as "the word". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The pronoun in «بها» is for His saying {أَسْلَمْتُ لِرَبِّ العالمين}, on the interpretation of 'the word' and 'the sentence'; similar to it is the returning of the pronoun in His saying {وَجَعَلَهَا كَلِمَةً بَاقِيَةً} [al-Zukhruf: 28] to His saying {إِنَّنِي بَرَآءٌ مِّمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ إِلاَّ الذي فَطَرَنِي} [al-Zukhruf: 28] «[Translator's note: the latter citation is printed as al-Zukhruf: 28 in the source; the verse is al-Zukhruf 26–27.]»; and His saying «كلمةً باقيةً» is evidence that the feminine is on the sense of 'the word'." End quote. The second: that it refers back to the word understood from His saying «أَسْلَمْتُ», as its establishment from al-Zamakhsharī has preceded. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "And it is more correct, because it is the nearest thing mentioned." The third: that it refers back to something coming later, namely the word understood from His saying: {فَلاَ تَمُوتُنَّ إَلاَّ وَأَنْتُم مُّسْلِمُونَ}. The fourth: that it refers back to the word of sincere devotion (kalimat al-ikhlāṣ), even though there has been no [mention] of it. The fifth: that it refers back to obedience, it too being known. The sixth: that it refers back to the injunction (al-waṣiyya) indicated by His saying «ووصَّى». And «بها» is attached to «وصَّى», and «بنِيه» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

His saying: {وَيَعْقُوبُ}: The majority read it nominative, and there are two views on it. The more apparent of them: that it is conjoined to «إبراهيم», its object being omitted, i.e.: and Jacob too enjoined his sons. The second: that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with its khabar (predicate) omitted, its implied form being: "and Jacob said: O my sons, Allah has chosen…". Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd Allāh and ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid read it accusative, conjoined to «بَنيه», i.e.: and Abraham enjoined Jacob too.

His saying: {يَا بَنِيَّ} has two aspects. The first: that it is part of what Abraham said, and that is on the view that Jacob is conjoined to Abraham, or on its reading in the accusative. The second: that it is part of what Jacob said, if we say that its nominative is as a mubtadaʾ, and then the speech of Abraham has been omitted because of the indication of it, its implied form being: "And Abraham enjoined his sons: O my sons". On every assumption, the clause «يا بَنِيَّ» and what follows it is [accusative] by an omitted verb of saying in the opinion of the Basrans, i.e.: "and he said: O my sons", and by the verb of enjoining, since it carries the meaning of saying, in the opinion of the Kufans. The rajaz poet said:
731 - رَجُلانِ مِنْ ضَبَّةَ أَخْبرانَا ... إنَّا رَأَيْنا رجلاً عُرْيانا
(Two men of Ḍabba informed us: "We saw a naked man.")
with the hamza [of «إنَّا»] given kasra, on the implying of a verb of saying, or by treating "informing" as "saying". Its connection with the injunction is supported by the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: «أَنْ يا بَنِيَّ», with explicative «أَنْ»; and it is not permissible for it to be maṣdar-forming here, since there is nothing from which a maṣdar (verbal noun) could be cast. Those who refuse to make it explicative — and they are the Kufans — make it redundant (zāʾida).

Yaʿqūb (Jacob) is a foreign proper name, and for that reason it is diptote. Whoever claims that he was named Yaʿqūb because he was born right after (ʿaqib) his brother al-ʿĪṣ (Esau), they being twins, or because his posterity (ʿaqib) and offspring became numerous, has erred; because it would then have had to be fully declinable, since it would be an Arabic derived word. Yaʿqūb is also the male partridge; if a male is named with it, it is declinable; the plural is yaʿāqiba and yaʿāqīb.

And «اصطفى»: its alif is from a yāʾ, that yāʾ being converted from a wāw, because it is from al-ṣafwa (the choicest); when the word became four letters or more, it was changed into a yāʾ and then changed into an alif. And «لكم» means "for your sake", and the alif and lām in «الدين» are for prior reference (al-ʿahd). «[Translator's note: the source prints «الذين»; the verse word is «الدِّين».]»

His saying: {فَلاَ تَمُوتُنَّ إلا}: This is in form a prohibition of death, but in reality it is a prohibition of their being in a state other than Islam when they die, like your saying: "Do not pray except while you are humble". Your prohibition to him is not of prayer; it is only of abandoning humility in the state of his prayer. The subtle point in bringing the particle of prohibition onto prayer, while it is not prohibited, is to show that prayer in which there is no humility is as if it were no prayer «[Translator's note: the source reads «كالصلاة» ("like prayer"); the sense requires "like no prayer", probably «كلا صلاة».]», as if he said: I forbid it to you if you do not pray it in this state. Likewise the meaning in the verse is to show that their dying not in the state of steadfastness in Islam is a death in which there is no good, and that what is due to this death is that it not be made to befall them.

The origin of «تموتُنَّ» is «تموتُونَنَّ»: the first nūn is the sign of the nominative, and the second, doubled one is for emphasis. Three similar letters came together, so the nūn of the nominative was elided, because the nūn of emphasis is more deserving of remaining, since it indicates an independent meaning. Then two quiescent letters met: the wāw and the first, assimilated nūn; so the wāw was elided for the meeting of two quiescents, and the ḍamma remained indicating it; and thus is every case of its like. {إَلاَّ وَأَنْتُم مُّسْلِمُونَ}: This is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh) from the general states, and «أنتم مسلمون» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), as though He, Exalted is He, said: "Do not die in any state except in this state"; and the governing word in it is what precedes «إلاَّ».

semin-durr:115-115.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَللَّهِ المشرق والمغرب}: a clause connected with His words «مَنَعَ مساجدِ الله، وسعى في خَرابِها»; that is, if someone strives to prevent the mention of Him the Exalted and to ruin His houses, that does not prevent performing worship elsewhere, because the East and the West and what is between them belong to Him the Exalted. The explicit mention of the East and the West rather than anything else is for one of two reasons. The first: their nobility, in that they were assigned to Allah the Exalted.
