What appears to be the reason for rejecting it is that the verb after «مَنْ», namely «اشتراه», is past in wording and meaning, for the purchase had occurred and been concluded; so making it a condition is not valid, because the verb of the condition, even if past in wording, must be future in meaning.
Al-khalāq is the share. Al-Zajjāj said: "Its use is mostly in good things." As for the saying:
664 - يَدْعُون بالوَيْلِ فيها لا خَلاقَ لَهُمْ ... إلا سَرابيلُ من قَطْرٍ وأغلالُ
(They cry woe therein; they have no share except garments of molten pitch, and shackles.)
it bears three aspects. One: that it is by way of mockery of them, as in the saying:
665 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... تَحِيَّةُ بَيْنِهم ضَرْبٌ وجَيِعُ
(… the greeting among them is a painful blow.)
The second: that it is a disconnected exception, i.e. "but they have garments of such-and-such". The third: that it was used for evil, rarely. Al-khalāq is also worth/standing; [the poet] said:
666 - فما لَكَ بيتٌ لدى الشامخاتِ ... وما لَكَ في غالِبٍ مِنْ خَلاقِ
(You have no house among the lofty ones, and you have no standing among Ghālib.)
i.e. no worth or rank; and it is close to the first. About the accusative pronoun in «اشتراه» there are four views: it refers to sorcery, or disbelief, or their measure [Translator's note: كَيْلِهم, so in the source; perhaps a corruption] for which they sold sorcery, or the Qurʾān, because they took books of sorcery in exchange for it. The discussion of His saying «ولَبِئْس ما» and what people have mentioned about it has preceded. The lām in «لَبِئْسَما» is the response of an omitted oath, its implied form being: "By Allah, evil indeed is…", and the thing specified for censure is omitted, i.e. sorcery or disbelief.
His saying: {لَوْ كَانُواْ يَعْلَمُونَ}: the apodosis of «لو» is omitted, its implied form being: "if they knew the blameworthiness of that, they would not have sold their souls for it". This is better than Abū al-Baqāʾ's supposition: "if they benefited from their knowledge they would have refrained from buying sorcery", because the more the supposed element is drawn from the wording, the better. The pronoun in «به» refers to sorcery or disbelief, and in «يَعْلَمُون» it refers to the Jews by agreement. Know that there is a question of meaning here, which al-Zamakhsharī and others mentioned, and it depends on the reference of the pronoun in «عَلِمُوا» and «يَعْلَمُون». That is, al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how did He first affirm knowledge for them in «ولقد عَلِمُوا» by way of emphasis with an oath, then deny it of them in His saying {لَوْ كَانُواْ يَعْلَمُونَ}? I say: its meaning is: if they acted on their knowledge; He made them, when they did not act on it, as though they were stripped of it." This is based on his view that the two pronouns in «عَلِموا» and «يَعْلَمون» are for one thing. Others answered on this supposition that what is meant by the second knowledge is intellect, because knowledge is among its fruits, so when the root is negated its fruit is negated; or that the objects of the two knowledges differ, i.e. they knew its harm in the Hereafter and did not know its benefit in this world [Translator's note: so in the source]. But if you refer the pronoun in «عَلِموا» to the devils, or to those in Solomon's presence, or to the two angels, there is no difficulty, because then the one to whom knowledge is attributed differs.

semin-durr:136-136.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {قولوا}: Concerning this pronoun there are two views. The first: that it is for the believers, and what is meant by "what was sent down to them" on this view is the Qurʾān. The second: that it refers back to those who said "Be Jews or Christians", and what is meant by "what was sent down to them" is either the Qurʾān or the Torah and the Gospel. The clause «آمنَّا» is in the position of accusative by «قولوا». He repeated the relative noun in His saying {وَمَآ أُنزِلَ إلى إِبْرَاهِيمَ} because what was sent down to us differs from what was sent down to him; had He not repeated it, it would have suggested that what was sent down to us is what was sent down to him. He did not repeat it with «عيسى» because he did not differ from the law of Moses except in a very small amount; so what Jesus was given is the very thing Moses was given, except for a little. And what was sent down to us was put first in mention, even though it was later in being sent down, to honour it.

And al-asbāṭ is the plural of sibṭ; they are among the offspring of Jacob like the tribes (qabāʾil) among the offspring of Ishmael. Their derivation is from al-sabṭ, which is succession; they were so called because they are a people who follow one another in succession. It has been said: it is metathesised from al-basṭ (spreading); and it has been said: from al-sabaṭ, with the middle letter vowelled, the plural of sabaṭa, which is intertwined trees. Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn were called the two asbāṭ (grandsons) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ because of the spreading of their progeny; then every son of a daughter came to be called "sibṭ".

His saying: {وَمَآ أُوتِيَ موسى}: In «ما» two aspects are permissible. The first: that it is in the position of genitive, conjoined to what is believed in; and this is the apparent one. The second: that it is in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and {وَمَا أُوتِيَ النبيون} is conjoined to it. Concerning the khabar (predicate) there are two aspects. The first: that it is «مِنْ ربهم». The second: that it is «لا نفرِّقُ»; so the Shaykh mentioned. However, in his making «لا نفرِّقُ» the khabar of «ما» there is a difficulty that is not hidden, in respect of there being no pronoun returning to it. It is also permissible for the first «ما» to be conjoined to the genitive noun, and the second «ما» to be a mubtadaʾ, with the two aspects concerning its khabar. The Shaykh can escape the lack of a returning pronoun by [saying] that it is omitted, its implied form being "we make no distinction concerning it" (lā nufarriqu fīhi); and the omission of a returning pronoun made genitive by «في» is regular, as some have mentioned, and he recited:
745 - فيومٌ علينا ويومٌ لنا ... ويومٌ نُسَاءُ ويَوْمٌ نُسَرّ
(A day against us and a day for us; a day we are grieved and a day we are gladdened.)
i.e.: we are grieved in it and we are gladdened in it.

His saying: {مِن رَّبِّهِمْ} has three aspects. The first — and it is the apparent one —: that it is in the position of accusative, «مِنْ» being for the beginning of the extent, and it is attached to the second «أُوتِيَ» if we refer the pronoun back to the prophets only, not to Moses and Jesus; or to the first «أوْتِيَ», the second being a repetition, given that it is dropped in Āl ʿImrān, if we refer the pronoun back to Moses, Jesus and the prophets. The second: that it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun returning to the relative noun, and so it is attached to something omitted, its implied form being: "and what he was given, being from their Lord". The third: that it is in the position of nominative because it falls as a khabar, if we make «ما» a mubtadaʾ; its verification has preceded.

His saying: {بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ}: It is attached to «لا نُفَرِّقُ». In «أحد» there are two views. The more apparent of them: that it is the one that keeps to negation, whose hamza is original; so it is for generality and has individuals under it, and for that reason the entry of «بين» onto it is sound without implying a conjoined element, as in: "The wealth is between the people". The second: that it is the one whose hamza is a substitute for a wāw, in the sense of «واحد» (one); on this view a conjoined element must be implied for the entry of «بَيْنَ» onto something multiple to be sound, but it was omitted because the meaning is understood, the implied form being: "between one of them [and another]". Its parallel and like is the saying of al-Nābigha:
746 - فما كان بين الخيرِ لو جاءَ سالماً ... أبو حُجُرٍ إلا ليالٍ قلائِلُ
(Had Abū Ḥujur come safely, there would have been between the good [and me] only a few nights.)
i.e.: between the good and me. And «له» is attached to «مسلمون»; it was put first out of concern for it, because the pronoun refers to Allah the Exalted, or for the harmony of the verse-endings (fawāṣil).

semin-durr:90-90.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {بِئْسَمَا اشتروا} ...: «بئسَ» is a non-inflecting (ghayr mutaṣarrif) past verb whose meaning is blame. It governs only a noun made definite by «أل», or one annexed to what contains it, or a pronoun explained by an indefinite noun, or «ما» according to the view of Sībawayh. There are several dialectal forms of it: «بَئِسَ» with kasra on the middle radical, and [a form] lightened [«بَئْسَ»] — this is the original; and «بِئِس» with kasra on the first radical in harmony with the middle radical, and [a form] lightened [«بِئْسَ»] — this is the harmonised form, and it is the best-known usage. Like it is «نِعْمَ» in all the rulings and dialectal forms mentioned. The Kufans claimed that they are both nouns, adducing as proof the entry of a preposition upon them in their sayings: «ما هي بِنِعْمَ الولد، نصرُها بكاءٌ وبِرُّها سَرِقة» ("She is no excellent child: her help is weeping and her kindness is theft") and «نِعْمَ السيرُ على بِئس العَيْر» ("excellent is the journey on a wretched donkey"), and his saying:
609 - صَبَّحَكَ اللهُ بخيرٍ باكرِ ... بنِعْمَ طيرٍ وشبابٍ فاخِرِ
(May Allah greet your morning with early good, with an excellent omen-bird and splendid youth.)
The Basrans explained it as an omitted qualified noun whose adjective has taken its place, the implied form being: "she is not a child of whom it is said: excellent is the child." It has many rulings. After it there must be a noun specified for praise or blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ aw al-dhamm), which may be omitted when there is a contextual indication. This is the ruling of «بئس».
As for the «ما» occurring after it, as in this verse: the grammarians differed greatly about it, and the reports from them are extremely confused. They differed on whether it has a grammatical position or not. Al-Farrāʾ held that together with «بئس» it is one thing, compounded as «حَبَّذا» is compounded — Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmitted this — and al-Mahdawī transmitted from him that he allows «ما» together with «بئس» to be like «كُلَّما». The apparent sense of these two reports is that it has no grammatical position. The majority held that it has a position; then they differed: is its position nominative or accusative? Al-Akhfash held that it is in the position of accusative as a tamyīz (specification), the clause after it being in the position of accusative as its adjective, and the fāʿil (agent) of «بئس» is a pronoun which «ما» explains; the noun specified for blame is His saying {أَن يَكْفُرُواْ}, because it is to be interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun). The implied form is: "wretched is it as a thing for which they sold [themselves]: their disbelief." Al-Fārisī held this in one of his two views, and al-Zamakhsharī chose it. On this view the noun specified for blame may also be omitted, with «اشتَرَوا» as its adjective in the position of nominative, the implied form being: "wretched as a thing is a thing — or a disbelief — for which they sold [themselves]," as in his saying:
610 - لنِعْمَ الفتى أَضْحَى بأَكْنافِ حَائِل ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Excellent indeed is the youth who came to be in the environs of Ḥāʾil...)
i.e. «فتىً أَضْحى» ("a youth who came to be"); and {أَن يَكْفُرُواْ} is a badal (substitute) from that omitted noun, or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is that they disbelieve." Al-Kisāʾī held that «ما» is also accusative in position, but he supplied after it another «ما», a relative noun meaning «الذي», and made the clause «اشتَرَوا» its ṣila (relative clause); this relative «ما» is the noun specified for blame. The implied form is: "wretched as a thing is that for which they sold themselves." So «اشتروا» has no position on this view, and {أَن يَكْفُرُواْ} on this view is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, as preceded. In sum, regarding the clause occurring after «ما», on the view that it is accusative, there are three views: first, that it is its adjective, so it is in the position of accusative; or [second,] the ṣila of the omitted «ما», so it has no position; or [third,] an adjective of the noun specified for blame, so it is in the position of nominative.
Sībawayh held that its position is nominative as the fāʿil of «بئس». Sībawayh said: it is a complete (tāmma) definite noun, the implied form being «بئس الشيءُ» ("wretched is the thing"); on this view the noun specified for blame is omitted, i.e. "a thing for which they sold themselves." This view was also attributed to al-Kisāʾī. Al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī also held that «ما» is a relative noun meaning «الذي», the clause after it being its ṣila; Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmitted this from Sībawayh, and it is one of the two views of al-Fārisī. The implied form is: "wretched is that for which they sold themselves: that they disbelieve," so «أن يكفروا» is the noun specified for blame. The Shaykh said: "What Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmitted from Sībawayh is a misattribution to him." Al-Mahdawī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya also transmitted from al-Kisāʾī that «ما» may be maṣdariyya, the implied form being «بئسَ اشتراؤُهم» ("wretched is their purchase"), so that «ما» together with what is in its domain is in the position of nominative. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is objected to on the grounds that «بئس» does not enter upon a specific noun made definite by annexation to a pronoun." The Shaykh said: "This is binding only if he stated explicitly that it is the nominative [fāʿil] of «بئس». But if he made it the noun specified for blame and made the fāʿil of «بئس» a [latent] pronoun, with the tamyīz omitted because the meaning is understood — the implied form being «بئسَ اشتراءً اشتراؤُهم» ('wretched as a purchase is their purchase') — then the objection is not binding." I say: it is on this basis — I mean making the fāʿil of «بئس» a pronoun latent in it — that Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed «ما» to be maṣdariyya, for he said: "The fourth: that it is maṣdariyya, i.e. «بئسَ شِراؤُهم», and the fāʿil of «بئس» on this view is a [latent] pronoun, because the maṣdar here is specific, not generic" — meaning that it cannot then be the fāʿil. However, this view is invalidated by the pronoun in «به» referring back to «ما», whereas no pronoun refers back to the maṣdariyya [«ما»], since it is a particle according to the majority. The exposition of the proofs of each party is mentioned in the extensive works. This is the final word on «بئسما» and «نِعِمَّا», and Allah knows best.
His saying: {أَن يَكْفُرُواْ}: it has preceded that it may be the noun specified for blame, so that there are the three views: either a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause before it — with no need for a link (rābiṭ), because the generality stands in its place, since the «أل» in the fāʿil of «نعم» and «بئس» is generic, or because the clause is the mubtadaʾ itself; or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted. It has preceded that it may be a badal, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, according to what has been established and verified. Al-Farrāʾ allowed it to be in the position of genitive as a badal from the pronoun in «به», if you make «ما» complete (tāmma).
His saying: {بِمَآ أنَزَلَ الله} is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يكفُروا». It has preceded that «كفر» is transitive by itself at times and by a preposition at other times. «ما» is a relative noun meaning «الذي», and the returning pronoun is omitted, its implied form being «أَنْزله». Making it an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective is weak, and likewise making it maṣdariyya with the maṣdar standing in place of the object, i.e. «بإنزالِه», meaning "in what was sent down."
His saying: {بَغْيَاً}: there are three views on it. The most apparent: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), fulfilling the conditions for the accusative. There are two views regarding what makes it accusative. The first, and it is the apparent one, is «يكفروا», i.e. the cause of their disbelief is transgression (al-baghy). The second is {اشتروا}, and al-Zamakhsharī's words incline to this, for he said: "It is the cause of {اشتروا}." The second of the three views: that it is accusative as a maṣdar by a verb indicated by what preceded, i.e. «بَغَوْا بَغْيَاً» ("they transgressed a transgression"). The third: that it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), and regarding its possessor there are the two preceding views: either the fāʿil of {اشتروا} or the fāʿil of {يَكْفُرُواْ}; the implied form being: "they sold, transgressing," or "they disbelieve, transgressing."
«البَغْيُ» originally means corruption, from their saying «بَغَى الجُرْحُ», i.e. the wound became corrupted; al-Aṣmaʿī said this. It was also said: it is intense seeking, and of this is His saying, Exalted is He: {مَا نَبْغِي} [Yūsuf: 65]. The rajaz poet said:
611 - أُنْشِدُ والباغي يُحِبُّ الوِجْدانْ ... قلائِصاً مختلفاتِ الألْوانْ
(I seek out — and the seeker loves finding — young she-camels of differing colours.)
And of this is «البَغِيُّ» (the harlot), because of her intense seeking of it.
His saying: {أَن يُنَزِّلُ الله}: there are two views on it [Translator's note: so in the source, which then lists three]. The first: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, made accusative by «بَغْياً», i.e. the cause of the transgression is Allah's sending down His bounty upon Muḥammad, upon him be peace. The second: that it is by removal of the preposition, the implied form being: «بَغْياً على أَنْ يُنَزِّلَ», i.e. "out of envy that He sends down"; so the well-known disagreement comes into it: is it in the position of accusative or in the position of genitive? The third: that it is in the position of genitive as a badal from «ما» in His saying {بِمَآ أنَزَلَ الله}, a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), i.e. «بإنزال الله»; so it would be like the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
612 - أَمِنْ ذِكْر سلمى أَنْ نَأَتْكَ تَنُوصُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Is it from remembering Salmā — that she has gone far from you — that you shrink back...?)
Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read every imperfect of «أَنْزَل» without doubling, except what there is consensus on doubling, in [Sūrat] al-Ḥijr: {وَمَا نُنَزِّلُهُ إِلاَّ} [al-Ḥijr: 21]. Both departed from this principle: Abū ʿAmr doubled {على أَن يُنَزِّلٍ آيَةً} [verse 37] in al-Anʿām, and Ibn Kathīr doubled in al-Isrāʾ: {وَنُنَزِّلُ مِنَ القرآن} [al-Isrāʾ: 82] and {حَتَّى تُنَزِّلَ عَلَيْنَا كِتَاباً} [al-Isrāʾ: 93]. The rest [read] with doubling in every imperfect, except Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī, who departed from this principle and read without doubling: {وَيُنَزِّلُ الغيث} [verse 34] at the end of Luqmān, and {وَهُوَ الذي يُنَزِّلُ الغيث} [verse 28] in al-Shūrā. The hamza and the doubling are for transitivisation; it has preceded whether there is a difference between them, and the verification of each of the two views. The Quran readers have mentioned reasons for the consensus on doubling in that place and why each one departed from his principle, which would take long to mention; the most apparent of all that is that it is a combining of the dialects.
His saying: {مِن فَضْلِهِ}: «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent, and there are two views on it. The first: that it is an adjective of an omitted qualified noun which is the object of «يُنَزِّل», i.e. "that Allah sends down something coming from His bounty," so it is in the position of accusative. The second: that «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), which is the view of al-Akhfash; in that case it is not attached to anything, and the noun in the genitive by it is the object, i.e. «أَنْ يُنَزِّلُ الله فضله» ("that Allah sends down His bounty").
His saying: {على مَن يَشَآءُ} is attached to «يُنَزِّلَ». «مَنْ» may be a relative noun or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, and the pronoun returning to the relative noun or the qualified noun is omitted because the conditions permitting omission are fulfilled; the implied form is: "upon the one whom He wills," or "upon a man whom He wills." Abū al-Baqāʾ supplied it as genitive, for he said, after allowing «مَنْ» to be qualified or relative: "The object of «يشاء» is omitted, i.e. He wills its descent upon him; and «يشاء» may mean 'He chooses and selects.'" End quote.
You have learned that a returning pronoun in the genitive is not omitted except under conditions, which are not present here, so there is no need for this construal.
His saying: {مِنْ عِبَادِهِ}: there are two views on it. The first: that it is a ḥāl from the omitted pronoun which returns to the relative noun or the qualified noun, and the annexation implies honour. The second: that it is an adjective of «مَنْ» after an adjective, on the view that it is indefinite; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. It is weak, because when the preposition-phrase and the clause come together in the chapter of the naʿt (adjective), beginning with the preposition-phrase before the clause is more appropriate, since it is closer to the single word. So it is in the position of accusative on the first view and of genitive on the second, and on both views it is necessarily attached to an omitted [word], for the reason you know.
His saying: {فَبَآءُو بِغَضَبٍ}: the bāʾ is for the ḥāl, i.e. they returned clothed in anger, i.e. having anger upon them; that has preceded. His saying: {على غَضَبٍ} is in the position of genitive, because it is an adjective of His saying «بغضب», i.e. "being upon anger," meaning with successive anger. Are the two angers different because of their different causes — the first for their forebears' worship of the calf and the second for their disbelief in Muḥammad, [upon him be] peace; or the first for their disbelief in ʿĪsā and the second for their disbelief in Muḥammad, may Allah bless them both and grant them peace — or are they one thing, mentioned twice to intensify the situation and for emphasis? It is a well-known disagreement.
His saying: {مُّهِينٌ} is an adjective of «عذاب». Its root form is «مُهْوِن», because it is from «الهَوان» (abasement), and it is the active participle of «أَهان يُهين إهانةً», like «أَقامَ يُقيم إقامةً». The kasra of the wāw was transferred to the quiescent letter before it, so the wāw became quiescent after a kasra and was changed into yāʾ. «الإهانة» is humiliation and disgrace. He said «وللكافرين» and did not say «ولهم», to draw attention to the cause requiring the humiliating punishment.

semin-durr:186-186.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ أُجِيبُ}: regarding «أُجيب» there are two views. The first: it is a clause in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as a naʿt (adjective) of «قَرِيبٌ». The second: it is a second khabar (predicate) of «إنِّي», since «قريب» is the first khabar.

A verb of saying must be implied after the fāʾ of the apodosis, its implied form being: "then say to them: I am near." We needed this implied form only because what follows upon the condition is the informing of nearness. And His words «أجيب» came in accordance with the pronoun that precedes the khabar; the khabar was not taken into account, so that it would be said «يُجيبُ» in the third person in accordance with His word «قريبٌ», because the better known of the two ways of the Arabs is the first, as in the words of Allah the Exalted: {بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ تَجْهَلُونَ} [al-Naml: 55], and in another place {بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ تُفْتَنُونَ} [al-Naml: 47], and the words of the poet:
853 - وإنَّا لَقَوْمٌ ما نرى القَتْلَ سُبَّةً ... إذا ما رَأَتْهُ عامِرٌ وسَلُولُ
(We are a people who do not see being killed as a disgrace, though ʿĀmir and Salūl regard it so.)
Had he taken the khabar into account he would have said: «مَا يَرَوْنَ القَتْلَ».

In His words {عَنِّي} and «إنِّي» there is a shift (iltifāt) from the third person to the first person, because before it is «ولتُكَّبِّروا الله», and the overt noun in this respect is like the third-person pronoun. The kāf in «سألَكَ» is for the Prophet ﷺ, even though he has not been mentioned; however, His words {أُنْزِلَ فِيهِ القرآن} indicate him, since its implied form is: "in which the Quran was sent down upon the Messenger ﷺ." In His words «فإني قريب» there is a figurative expression (majāz) for the swiftness of His answering the call of the one who calls upon Him; otherwise He is exalted above sensory nearness, being exalted above place. Its parallel is: {وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ الوريد} [Qāf: 16], and "He is between you and the necks of your riding camels."

As for what governs «إذا», the Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "It is His word «أُجيبُ»", meaning the second «إذا»; so the implied form is: "I answer his call at the time of his calling." It may be for mere adverbiality, or it may be conditional with its apodosis omitted because «أُجِيْبُ» indicates it; in that case this uttered «أُجيبُ» is not what governs it, but rather that omitted one; or it is itself the apodosis according to those who allow placing it before the condition. As for the first «إذا», what governs it is that implied verb of saying. The hāʾ in «دعوة» is not the one indicating a single instance, as in ضَرْبَة and قَتْلَة, but the one upon which the maṣdar (verbal noun) is built, as in رَحْمة and نَجْدة; therefore it does not indicate singleness.

The two yāʾs in His words «الداع - دعانِ» are among the "additional" (zawāʾid) yāʾs according to the readers. This means that the Companions did not give them a written form in the Muṣḥaf; so among the readers are those who drop them following the script, both in pause and in continuous reading; among them are those who retain them in both cases; and among them are those who retain them in continuous reading and drop them in pause. The total of these additional yāʾs is sixty-two, and knowledge of this is referred to the books of qirāʾāt. Abū ʿAmr and Qālūn retained these two yāʾs in continuous reading and dropped them in pause.

His words: {فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُواْ لِي}: regarding the istifʿāl form here there are two views. The first: it is for requesting, in its usual sense, the meaning being: "let them seek My answering"; Thaʿlab said this. The second: it has the meaning of the ifʿāl form, so that istafʿala and afʿala have one meaning. Several words of this kind have come: أقرَّ and استقرَّ; أبَلَّ المريضُ and اسْتَبَلَّ (the sick man recovered); أحصدَ الزرعُ and استحصد (the crop was ready for harvest); استثار الشيء and أثارَه; استعجله and أَعْجَله; and among them استجابَهُ and أجَابَهُ. When istafʿala has the meaning of afʿala, it has come transitive by itself and with a preposition, except that in the Quran it has only come made transitive by a preposition, as in {فاستجبنا لَهُ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 84], «فاستجاب لَهُمْ»; and of its being transitive by itself is the poet's saying:
854 - وداعٍ دَعَا يا مَنْ يُجيبُ إلى النَّدى ... فلم يَسْتَجِبْه عند ذاك مُجيبُ
(Many a caller called out: "O who will answer the call to generosity?" — yet no answerer answered him then.)
Someone might say: this verse may be among those from which a preposition has been omitted.

The lām is the lām of command. Al-Rummānī distinguished between أَجاب and استجاب: «استجاب» is used only where there is acceptance of what one was called to, as in {فاستجبنا لَهُ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 76] and {فاستجاب لَهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ} [Āl ʿImrān: 195], whereas «أجاب» is more general, because one may answer by refusing; so he made between them a relation of general and particular.

The majority read «يَرْشُدون» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the shīn, its past being رَشَدَ with fatḥa. Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Abī ʿAbla — with a disagreement in what is transmitted from them — read it with kasra on the shīn; and it has been read with fatḥa on it, its past being رَشِد with kasra. It has also been read «يُرْشَدون» as passive, and it has been read «يُرْشِدُونَ» with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the shīn, from أَرْشد; on this reading the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is omitted, its implied form being: "they guide others."

semin-durr:42-42.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلاَ تَلْبِسُواْ الحق بالباطل}: the bāʾ [here] has the meaning of adhesion (ilṣāq), as in your saying: خَلَطْتُ الماءَ باللبن (I mixed water with milk), i.e. do not mix truth with falsehood so that it is not distinguished. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If it is a connective (ṣila), like the one in your saying لَبَسْتَ الشيء بالشيء (you confused one thing with another) and خَلَطْتُه به, the meaning is: do not write in the Torah what is not in it, so that the revealed truth becomes mixed with the falsehood you wrote. If it is the bāʾ of instrument (istiʿāna), like the one in your saying كتبْتُ بالقلَمِ (I wrote with the pen), the meaning is: do not make the truth confused by means of your falsehood which you write." So he permitted two aspects in it, as you see. By his word «صلة» he does not mean that it is redundant; rather he means that it connects the verb [to its object], as has preceded. The Shaykh said: "In his making it instrumental there is far-fetchedness and a turning away from the apparent sense without necessity." I do not know what this considering far-fetched is, given the clarity of this fine meaning.
His saying: {وَتَكْتُمُواْ الحق}: there are two aspects in it. The first, which is the more apparent: that it is jussive, being conjoined to the verb before it; He forbade them each act separately, i.e. do neither this nor that. The second: that it is accusative by an implied «أَنْ» in answer to the prohibition, after the wāw which requires concomitance, i.e. do not combine confusing truth with falsehood and concealing it. Of this kind is:
411 - لاَ تَنْهَ عن خُلُقٍ وتأتيَ مِثْلَه ... عارٌ عليكَ إذا فَعَلْتَ عظيمُ
(Do not forbid a trait while committing its like — a great shame upon you if you do.)
«أَنْ» together with what is in its domain is to be interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), so the verb before it must also be interpreted as a maṣdar, so that a noun may properly be conjoined to its like; the implied form is: "let there not be from you confusing truth with falsehood and concealing it", and likewise [all] its parallels. The Kufans said: "accusative by the wāw of divergence (wāw al-ṣarf)", whose meaning has preceded. The first aspect is better because it is a prohibition of each act separately. As for the second aspect, it is a prohibition of combining, and the prohibition of combining two things does not entail the prohibition of each one separately except by external evidence.
Al-labs: mixing and blending. One says: لَبَسْتُ عليه الأمرَ أَلْبِسُه: I mixed what is clear in it with what is obscure. Of this is al-Khansāʾ's saying:
412 - ترى الجلِيسَ يقولُ الحقَّ تَحْسَبُه ... رُشْداً وهيهاتَ فانظُرْ ما به التبسا
صَدِّقْ مقالتَه واحذَرْ عَداوَتَهُ ... والبِسْ عليه أموراً مثلَ ما لَبَسا
(You see the companion speaking the truth and you take it for right guidance — far from it! So look at what has been confused in it. Believe his words but beware his enmity, and confuse matters for him as he has confused.)
Al-ʿAjjāj said:
413 - لَمَّا لَبَسْنَ الحقَّ بالتجنِّي ... غَنِيْنَ واسْتَبْدَلْنَ زيداً مِنِّي
(When they confused the truth with false accusation, they became content and took Zayd in exchange for me.)
Also of this is:
414 - وقد لَبَسْتُ لهذا الأمرَ أَعْصُرَهُ ... حتى تَجَلَّل رأسي الشيبُ فاشْتَعلا
(I have lived through the ages of this affair, until grey hair covered my head and blazed.)
And «في فلان مَلْبَسٌ», i.e. there is enjoyment in so-and-so. He said:
415 - ألا إنَّ بعدَ العُدْمِ للمَرْءِ قُِنْوَةً ... وبعدَ المشيبِ طولَ عُمْرٍ ومَلْبَسَا
(Indeed, after destitution a man has acquisition, and after grey hair long life and enjoyment.)
[Translator's note: the verse number is printed «41 - 5-», i.e. 415.]
And the saying of al-Farrār:
416 - وكتيبةٍ لَبَّسْتُها بكتيبةٍ ... حتى إذا التَبَسَتْ نَفَضْتُ لها يَدِي
(Many a squadron I have thrown into confusion with another squadron, until, when they were entangled, I shook my hand free of them.)
may be from this, or from clothing (al-libās). The noble verse admits both meanings, i.e. do not cover the truth with falsehood.
Al-bāṭil is the opposite of truth, and it is what passes away, as in Labīd's saying:
417 - ألا كلُّ شيءٍ ما خلا اللهَ باطِلُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Indeed, everything other than Allah is vain…)
One says: بَطَل يَبْطُلُ بُطولاً وبُطْلاً وبُطْلاناً. Al-baṭal is the brave man, so called because he nullifies the courage of others. It has also been said: because his blood is shed with impunity, so it is faʿal in the sense of mafʿūl; and it has been said: because he sheds the blood of others with impunity, so it is in the sense of fāʿil.
One says بَطُل [with ḍamma] يَبْطُل بُطولاً وبَطالة, i.e. he became brave. Al-Nābigha said:
418 - لَهُمْ لِواءٌ بأيدي ماجدٍ بَطَلٍ ... لا يقطَعُ الخَرْقَ إلا طَرْفُه سامي
(They have a banner in the hands of a glorious hero; none crosses the open desert but one whose gaze is lofty.)
And بَطَل الأجيرُ with fatḥa, بِطالة with kasra: when the hired man is idle, so he is بَطَّال; and ذهب دَمُه بُطْلاً with ḍamma, i.e. his blood went unavenged.
His saying: {وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ} is a clause of mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Its governor is either تَلْبِسوا or تَكْتُموا, but the governing of «تكتموا» is preferable for two reasons. The first: it is nearer. The second: concealing the truth while knowing it is more severely blameworthy, and there is a kind of correspondence in it. The question cannot belong to the chapter of governing (al-iʿmāl), because that requires an implied pronoun, and a ḥāl cannot be represented by a pronoun, since it can only be indefinite; for that reason they forbade making it the subject of a statement with «الذي». If it is said: the question belongs to the chapter of iʿmāl in the sense that we have omitted from the first what we have stated in the second without any pronoun, so that the said forbidden thing is not entailed, the implied form being: "do not confuse truth with falsehood while you know, and do not conceal the truth while you know" — the answer is that this is not called iʿmāl, because iʿmāl requires that a pronoun be implied in the ungoverning element and then omitted. Ibn ʿAṭiyya permitted this clause not to be a ḥāl, for he said: "It may be a testimony against them that they knew a particular truth in the matter of Muḥammad, upon him be peace; He did not testify that they have knowledge [absolutely]. On this view the clause is not in the position of a ḥāl." What he said is questionable.
It has been read anomalously: «وَتَكْتُمونَ» in the nominative, and they explained it as a ḥāl. This is not correct, because it is an affirmative imperfect, which ought not to be joined with the wāw; whatever has occurred of that kind is interpreted by implying a mubtadaʾ before it, as in their saying: «قُمْتُ وأَصُكُّ عينَه» (I stood and I strike his eye), and another's saying:
419 - فَلَمَّا خَشِيْتُ أظافيرَهُمْ ... نَجَوْتُ وأَرْهُنُهُمْ مالِكَا
(When I feared their claws, I escaped, leaving Mālik with them as a pledge.)
i.e. "and I strike", "and I leave them as pledge", and likewise "and you conceal" (وأنتم تَكْتُمون). However, another difficulty is entailed by it, namely that they are forbidden confusing absolutely, whereas the ḥāl is a restriction on the preceding clause, so they would have been forbidden with a restriction, and that is not intended — unless it is said that it is an inseparable (lāzima) ḥāl. Al-Zamakhsharī supposed it as «كاتِمين» (concealing), making it a ḥāl, and the aforementioned difficulty applies to it — unless he meant an explanation of the meaning, not an explanation of the i'rab. It may also be an informative clause conjoined to a request clause, as though He, Exalted is He, were reproaching them for concealing the truth while knowing that it is the truth. The object of knowing is not intended, because the meaning is: "while you are people of knowledge". It has also been said: it was omitted because it is known, the implied form being: "you know truth from falsehood". Al-Zamakhsharī supposed it as: "while you know, in the state of your knowledge, that you are confusing and concealing", making the object the confusing and concealing understood from the two preceding verbs; and this is very good.
His saying: {وَأَقِيمُواْ الصلاة}: this clause and what follows it are conjoined to the clause before it, conjoining a command to a prohibition. The origin of أَقيموا is «أَقْوِمُوا», and what was done to {يُقِيمُونَ} [al-Baqara: 3] was done to it, as has preceded. The origin of آتُوا is اَأْتِيُوا with two hamzas, like أَكْرِموا; the second was changed into alif because it was quiescent after a hamza with fatḥa; the ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt heavy and was dropped, so two quiescent letters met, the yāʾ and the wāw; the yāʾ was dropped because it is the first, and the tāʾ was given its vowel. It has also been said: rather it was given ḍamma in conformity with the wāw, as the end of «اضْرِبُوا» and the like is given ḍamma. Its pattern is afʿū, with the final radical dropped.
The alif of «الزكاة» is from wāw, because of their saying zakawāt and زَكا يَزْكُو. It is growth; it has also been said: purity; and it has been said: its origin is fine praise, and of this is «زَكَّى القاضي الشهودَ» (the judge declared the witnesses upright). Al-zakā is [the even number], which became a pair by the addition of another single one to it; and al-khasā is the odd number. He said:
420 - كانوا خَسَاً أوزَكاً من دون أربعةٍ ... لَمْ يَخْلُقوا وجُدودُ الناسِ تَعْتِلجُ
(They were odd or even, fewer than four, when they were not yet created, and the fortunes of people jostle one another.)
His saying: {مَعَ الراكعين} is accusative by اركَعوا. Al-rukūʿ is repose and bending; of this is his saying:
421 - أُخَبِّرُ أَخْبارَ القرونِ التي مَضَتْ ... أَدِبُّ كأِّني كُلَّما قُمْتُ راكِعُ
(I relate the reports of the generations that have passed, creeping along as if, whenever I stand, I am bowing.)
It has also been said: submission and abasement; of this is the poet's saying:
422 - ...
لا تُهينَ الفقيرَ علَّكَ أَنْ تَرْ
كَعَ يوماً والدهرُ قَدْ رَفَعَهْ ...
(Do not humiliate the poor man; perhaps one day you will be brought low while time has raised him up.)

semin-durr:157-157.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أولئك}: a mubtadaʾ (subject); «صلواتٌ» is a second mubtadaʾ, and «عليهم» is its khabar (predicate) placed before it; the clause is the khabar of His saying «أولئك». It is also possible that «صلوات» is the fāʿil (agent) of His saying «عليهم». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "because it has been strengthened by occurring as a khabar." The clause made of His saying «أولئك» and what follows it is the khabar of «الذين» according to one of the views given earlier, or it has no grammatical position according to the others. «قالوا» is what governs «إذا», because it is its answer; the discussion of that has been given before, and it has been given whether or not it entails repetition.

His saying: {إِنَّا للَّهِ}: «إنَّ», its noun and its khabar are in the position of the accusative by the verb of saying. The original form is «إنَّنا» with three nūns; the last one of «إنَّ» was omitted, not the first, because its omission is familiar, and because it is at the extremity, and extremities are more apt for omission. One should not say: "If the second one had been omitted, it would be the lightened form (mukhaffafa), and the lightened form does not govern according to the most eloquent usage, so it ought to have been made inoperative and the nominative pronoun would then be detached, since it has no effect on it; the absence of that shows that the omitted one is the first nūn" — [one should not say this] because this omission is an omission due to the succession of identical letters, not that omission familiar in «إنَّ».

«أصابَتْهم مصيبةٌ» is a case of dissimilar paronomasia (tajānus mughāyir), since one of the two words of the root is a noun and the other a verb; similar to it are: {أَزِفَتِ الآزفة} [al-Najm: 57] and {وَقَعَتِ الواقعة} [al-Wāqiʿa: 1].

His saying: {وَرَحْمَةٌ}: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الصلاة», even though it has its meaning — for prayer (ṣalāt) from Allah is mercy — because of the difference between the two words, as in his saying:
778 - وقَدَّمَتِ الأدِيمَ لراهِشَيْهِ ... وأَلْفَى قولَها كَذِباً ومَيْنَا
(She offered the hide to [cut] his two wrist-veins, and he found her speech to be a lie and a falsehood.)
and his saying:
779 - أَلا حَبَّذا هِنْدٌ وأرضٌ بها هندٌ ... وهندٌ أتى مِنْ دونِها النَّأْيُ والبُعْدُ
(How lovely is Hind, and a land where Hind is — and Hind, between whom and me have come remoteness and distance.)

His saying: {مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ}: there are two views on it. One: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted element, because it is a naʿt (adjective) of «صلوات», and «مِنْ» marks the beginning; it is then in the position of the nominative, i.e.: blessings being from their Lord. The second: that it is attached to the verbal sense implied in His saying «عليهم», if we make it put «صلوات» in the nominative as an agent. On the first [view] He has omitted the naʿt after «رحمة», i.e.: and mercy from Him; on the second there is no need for that. His saying {وأولئك هُمُ المهتدون} is parallel to: {وأولئك هُمُ المفلحون} [al-Baqara: 5].

semin-durr:158-158.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِنَّ الصفا}: «الصَّفا» is its noun and {مِن شَعَآئِرِ الله} its khabar (predicate). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "In the speech there is an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being: the circumambulation of al-Ṣafā, or the running of al-Ṣafā." The alif of «الصَّفا» derives from a wāw, as shown by its being changed to wāw in the dual — they said «صَفَوان» — and the derivation also indicates it, since it is from «الصَّفْو», which is purity. «الصَّفا» is smooth stone; it is also said: that with which nothing else, such as clay or dust, is mixed. Its singular and collective are distinguished by the feminine tāʾ, as in: «صفاً كثيرٌ» (much rock) and «صفاة واحدة» (one rock). «الصَّفا» is sometimes pluralised on the patterns «فُعول» and «أَفْعال»: they said «صُفِيٌّ», with kasra or ḍamma on the ṣād, like «عِصِيّ», and «أصْفاء». The original forms are «صُفُوو» and «أَصْفاو»; the two wāws in «صُفُوو» were changed to two yāʾs, and the wāw in «أصفاء» to a hamza, like «كساء» and its class.

«المَرْوَةُ»: small stones — said to be soft, or said to be hard, or said to be sharp-edged, or said to be white, or said to be black. In the verse the two are proper names (ʿalam) of two well-known hills. The alif and lām in them are for predominance (ghalaba), as in «البيت» and «النجم». Its plural is «مَرْوٌ», as in his saying:
780 - وترى المَرْوَ إذا ما هَجَّرَتْ ... عن يَدَيْها كالفَراشِ المُشْفَتِرّْ
(And you see the flints, when she travels in the midday heat, [flying] from her forelegs like scattering moths.)
«الشعائر» is the plural of «شَعيرَة», which is a sign; it is also said: the plural of «شِعارة». What is meant by it in the verse is the rites of the Ḥajj. The better form is «شعائِر» with hamza, because of the added letter of prolongation, which is the reverse of «معائِش» and «مصائب».

His saying: {فَمَنْ حَجَّ البيت}: «مَنْ» is conditional, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); «حَجَّ» is in the position of the jussive (majzūm); «البيتَ» is accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), not as an adverb; and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is His saying «فلا جُناحَ». «الحَجُّ» linguistically means: heading for [a place] time after time. [The poet] said:
781 - لِراهِبٍ يَحُجُّ بيتَ المَقْدِسِ ... في مِنْقَلٍ وبُرْجُدٍ وبُرْنُسِ
(For a monk who repeatedly visits Jerusalem, in sandals, a coarse woollen garment and a hooded cloak.)
«الاعتمار» is visiting; it is also said: heading for [a place] in general. Then the two became proper names for meanings by predominance, like «البيت» and «النجم» for concrete things.

And His saying: {فَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِ}: the evident view is that «عليه» is the khabar of «لا», and «أَنْ يَطَّوَّفَ» is originally «في أَنْ يَطَّوَّفَ», the preposition being omitted, so the two views on its position apply: accusative or genitive. On this view the pause is at His saying «بهما». After that they permitted weak views, among them: that the speech is complete at His saying «فلا جُناحَ», with the khabar of «لا» omitted — Abū al-Baqāʾ took its implied form to be: "there is no sin in the Ḥajj" — and one begins with His saying: {عَلَيْهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ}, so that «عليه» is a fronted khabar and «أَنْ يطَّوَّفَ» is equivalent to a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, for the circumambulation is obligatory. Abū al-Baqāʾ said here: "The good [analysis] on this view is that «عليه» is a khabar and «أَنْ يَطَّوَّفَ» a mubtadaʾ."

Among them: that {عَلَيْهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ} is a case of incitement (ighrāʾ), so that «أَنْ يَطَّوَّفَ» is in the position of the accusative, as when you say «عليك زيداً», i.e. keep to him; but incitement directed at an absent person is weak. Sībawayh related: «عليه رجلاً لَيْسَني» (let him take a man other than me), and said: it is anomalous (shādhdh).

Among them: that «أَنْ يطَّوَّفَ» is in the position of the nominative as a second khabar of «لا», the implied sense being: no sin is the circumambulation of them. And among them: that «أَنْ يطَّوَّفَ» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «عليه», with the governor of the ḥāl being the governor of the khabar, the implied sense being: there is no sin upon him while he circumambulates them. These two views are worthless; I have mentioned them to draw attention to their error, and there is no benefit in mentioning the reason for the error, since it is clear on the slightest reflection.

The reading of the majority is «أَنْ يَطَّوَّفَ» without «لا». Anas, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Sīrīn and Shahr ibn Ḥawshab read: «أَنْ لا يَطَّوَّفَ»; they said: and likewise in the codices of Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh [Ibn Masʿūd]. In this reading there are two possibilities. One: that it is redundant (zāʾida), as in His saying: {أَلاَّ تَسْجُدَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 12], and his saying:
782 - وما أَلومُ البيضَ ألاَّ تَسْخَرا ... لَمَّا رَأَيْنَ الشَّمَطَ القَفَنْدَرا
(I do not blame the fair women for mocking when they saw ugly grey hair.)
In that case the meaning of the two readings is the same. The second: that it is not redundant, in the sense that removing the sin in doing a thing is removing it in leaving it, since it is a choice between doing and leaving, as in: {فَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَآ أَن يَتَرَاجَعَآ} [al-Baqara: 230]. The reading of the majority then removes the sin in performing the circumambulation explicitly, and this one removes the sin in leaving it explicitly.

The majority read «يَطَّوَّفَ» with the ṭāʾ and the wāw doubled. The original form is «يَتَطَوَّف», and its past was originally «تَطَوَّفَ». When assimilation was wanted for lightness, the tāʾ was changed to ṭāʾ and assimilated into the ṭāʾ; a connecting hamza (hamzat waṣl) was then needed because its first letter became quiescent due to the assimilation, so it was brought in [«اطَّوَّف»], and its imperfect came accordingly: «يَطَّوَّف», the connecting hamza dropping because the assimilated letter is protected by the imperfect prefix. Its maṣdar is «التطَّوف», reverting to the original «تَطَوَّفَ».

Abū al-Sammāl read: «يَطُوف», light, from «طاف يَطُوف», and it is straightforward. Ibn ʿAbbās read: «يَطَّاف», with the ṭāʾ doubled together with the alif. Its origin is «يَطْتَوِف» on the pattern «يَفْتَعِل», and its past «اطْتَوَف», «افْتَعَل». The wāw was vowelled and what precedes it had fatḥa, so it was changed to alif; the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl pattern came after the ṭāʾ, so it had to be changed to ṭāʾ and the ṭāʾ assimilated into it, as they said «اطَّلَب يَطَّلِبُ», the original being «اطْتَلَب يَطْتَلِبُ». So it became «اطَّاف», and its imperfect came accordingly: «يَطَّاف». This is the morphology of this word: the tāʾ of iftiʿāl is changed to ṭāʾ and the first ṭāʾ is assimilated into it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "So «يَطْتَاف» came about; the tāʾ, after being made quiescent, was assimilated into the ṭāʾ according to the school of those who permit assimilating the second into the first, as occurred in «مُدَّكِر»; those who do not permit that said: the tāʾ was changed to ṭāʾ, then the ṭāʾ was assimilated into the ṭāʾ. There is a problem in this, because the radical letter is assimilated into the augment, and that is weak."

What Ibn ʿAṭiyya said contains an error in two respects. One: his claiming the assimilation of the second into the first, which has no parallel; only the first is assimilated into the second. The second: that he said "as occurred in «مُدَّكِر»", because on his statement it ought to have been said «مُذَّكِر» with the dotted dhāl, and this is a poor dialectal form; the good form is only with the undotted dāl, because we changed the tāʾ of iftiʿāl after the dotted dhāl into an undotted dāl, so two close letters came together, and we changed the first of them into the kind of the second and assimilated. The verification of that will come.

The maṣdar of «اطَّاف» is «الاطِّياف», on the pattern «الافْتعال». The original is «اطَّواف»; what precedes the wāw received kasra, so it was changed to yāʾ. The wāw returned to its original [form, rather than alif] only because the cause of its change to alif was removed. This is made clear by their saying «اعتاد اعتياداً», the original being «اعتِواد», and what I have told you was done to it.

His saying: {وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيْراً}: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «تَطَوعَّ» here and in the verse coming after it: «يَطَّوَّعْ» with yāʾ as an imperfect verb [Translator's note: the source's wording is garbled here; the sense is that Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «يَطَّوَّعْ», a jussive imperfect, here and in the later verse], and the rest read: «تَطَوَّع» as a past verb. On their reading «مَنْ» can only be conditional, since it governs the jussive. The original of «يَطَّوَّع» is «يَتَطَوَّع», and it was assimilated in the manner given above for «يطّوّف». It [«مَنْ»] is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), according to the correct view, as its verification has been given. His saying «فإنَّ الله» is a clause in the position of the jussive because it is the apodosis, and there must be an implied returning pronoun, i.e.: Allah is appreciative of him. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "If you make «مَنْ» a condition, there is no omitted pronoun in the speech, because the pronoun of «مَنْ» is in «تطوَّع»." This contradicts what I reported to you earlier from the grammarians: that when the conditional particle is a noun, there must be a pronoun in the apodosis referring back to it; the verification of that has been given.

As for the reading of the majority, it admits two views. One: that it is conditional, and the discussion is as given above. The second: that it is a relative noun and «تَطَوَّعَ» its ṣila (relative clause), which then has no grammatical position; it is again in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ and «فإنَّ الله» its khabar, the fāʾ entering because of the conditional meaning it contains, with the returning pronoun omitted as stated, i.e.: appreciative of him.

«خيراً» is accusative on one of several views. Either by dropping the preposition, i.e. «تَطَوَّع بخيرٍ» (volunteers with good), and when the preposition was omitted it became accusative, as in his saying:
783 - تَمُرُّونَ الدِّيار ولم تَعُوجُوا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(You pass by the dwellings and do not turn aside…)
and this is not analogically regular. The second: that it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e.: a good volunteering. The third: that it is a ḥāl from that implied maṣdar taken as definite; this is the doctrine of Sībawayh and has been given more than once. Or by making «تَطَوَّعَ» imply (taḍmīn) a transitive verb, i.e.: whoever does [good, volunteering it]. In sum, from what has been given, His saying: {فَإِنَّ الله شَاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ} admits two views: one, the jussive, on the view that «مَنْ» is conditional; the second, the nominative, on the view that it is a relative noun.

semin-durr:137-137.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {بِمِثْلِ مَآ آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ}: Concerning the bāʾ there are views. The first: that it is redundant (zāʾida), like it in His saying {وَلاَ تُلْقُواْ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 195] and His saying: {وهزى إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ} [Maryam: 25], and his saying:
747 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... سُودُ المَحاجِرِ لا يَقْرَأْنَ بالسُّوَرِ
(… black around the eyes, they do not recite the sūras.)
The second: that it is in the sense of «على», i.e.: "if they believe in Allah on the like of your belief". The third: that it is for seeking assistance (al-istiʿāna), like it in "I carved with the adze" and "I wrote with the pen"; the meaning is: if they enter into faith with a testimony like your testimony. On these aspects, what is believed in is omitted, «ما» is maṣdar-forming, and the pronoun in «به» refers back to Allah the Exalted; the implied form is: if they believe in Allah with a faith like your faith in Him. And «مثل» here has two views. The first: that it is redundant, the implied form being: «بما آمنْتُم به» ("in what you have believed in"), and this is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās. Al-Bayhaqī mentioned from Ibn ʿAbbās: "Do not say «بمثلِ ما آمنتم [به]», for Allah has no like; rather say «بالذي آمنتم به»", and this is narrated as a reading [from] Ubayy. Its parallel in redundancy is the poet's saying:
748 - فَصُيِّروا مثلَ كعصفٍ مَأْكُولْ
(So they were made like the like of eaten straw.)
Some of them said: This is a figure of speech: you say "This is a matter that the like of you does not do", i.e.: you do not do it; and the meaning is: if they believe in that which you have believed in. Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported it, and it comes down to cancelling «مثل» and treating it as redundant. The second: that it is not redundant, and the likeness is connected with belief, i.e.: if they hold a belief like your belief; or connected with the Book, i.e.: if they believe in a Book like the Book in which you have believed; and the meaning is: if they believe in the Qurʾān, which confirms what is in the Torah and the Gospel. This interpretation negates the redundancy of the bāʾ.

And «ما» in His saying {بِمِثْلِ مَآ آمَنْتُمْ} has two aspects. The first: that it is in the sense of «الذي», and what is meant by it is then either Allah the Exalted — by the preceding interpretation — according to whoever permits «ما» to apply to those possessing knowledge, as in {والسمآء وَمَا بَنَاهَا} [al-Shams: 5]; or the Book sent down. The second: that it is maṣdar-forming, and that has preceded. The pronoun in «به» also has two aspects. The first: that it refers back to Allah the Exalted, as has preceded. The second: that it refers back to «ما», if it is said that it is in the sense of «الذي».

His saying: {فَقَدِ اهتدوا}: It is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition in His saying «فإنْ آمنوا», and the apodosis is not omitted as it is in His saying {وَإِن يُكَذِّبُوكَ فَقَدْ كُذِّبَتْ رُسُلٌ} [Fāṭir: 4]; because the denial of the messengers there is past and realised, so we needed to imply an apodosis; whereas here their guidance has not yet occurred, so it is future in meaning, even though it is presented in the wording of the past.

His saying: {فِي شِقَاقٍ}: It is the khabar of His saying «هم». He made schism a container for them, they being contained in it, as an exaggeration in reporting its dominance over them; and it is more eloquent than your saying "they are schismatics". Similar to it is: {إِنَّا لَنَرَاكَ فِي سَفَاهَةٍ} [al-Aʿrāf: 66], and the like. And al-shiqāq is a maṣdar of shāqqahu yushāqquhu, like ḍārabahu ḍirāban; its meaning is opposition and enmity. Concerning its derivation there are three views. The first: that it is from al-shiqq, which is the side; that is because each of the two opponents comes to be in a side other than his companion's, i.e.: his flank. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
749 - إذا ما بَكَى مِنْ خَلْفِها انْصَرَفَتْ له ... بشِقًّ وشِقٌّ عندَنا لم يُحَوَّلِ
(Whenever he cried behind her, she turned to him with one side, while one side with us was not moved.)
i.e.: with a side. «[Translator's note: the source says «يَصير في شِقِّ صاحبِه» ("comes to be in his companion's side"); I have rendered it as the evident sense — each being in a side other than his companion's.]» The second: that it is from al-mashaqqa (hardship), for each of them is eager for what is hard on his companion. The third: that it is from their saying "I split the staff between me and you", and they used to do that at the time of their mutual enmity. The fāʾ in His saying «فَسَيَكْفِيكَهُم» conveys that the sufficing follows immediately upon their schism. The sīn was brought rather than «سوف» because it is nearer in time than it by its original setting. A muḍāf (annexed noun) must be omitted, i.e.: He will suffice you against their schism; because persons are not "sufficed against"; only their actions are sufficed against. What He suffices with here is omitted, i.e.: with those whom Allah guides, or with the splitting of their unity.

semin-durr:174-174.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مِنَ الكتاب}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). There are two interpretations of the one to whom it refers (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl). The first: that it is the pronoun referring back to the relative noun, its implied form being "Allah sent it down, it being part of the Book"; so the governing word in it is «أَنْزَلَ». The second: that it is the relative noun itself, so the governing word in the ḥāl is «يكتمون».
His words: {وَيَشْتَرُونَ بِهِ}: the pronoun in «به» may refer to the relative «ما», or to the concealing (al-katm) understood from His words «يكتمون», or to the Book. The most apparent of these is the first, and it is then on the basis of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "they purchase by concealing what He sent down".
His words: {إِلاَّ النار}: an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh), because before it there is a governing word that requires it. This is a figurative use of speech: He made that which is a cause of the Fire [the Fire] «[Translator's note: the bracketed word is added for sense; the text reads «جَعَل ما هو سببٌ للنار».]», like their saying «So-and-so ate blood», meaning the blood-money that is due because of the blood. The poet said:
820 - فلو أَنَّ حَيَّاً يقبلُ المالَ فِدْيةً ... لَسُقْنا إليه المالَ كالسيلِ مُفْعَما
ولكنْ أبى قومٌ أُصيب أخوهمُ ... رِضا العارِ واختاروا على اللبنِ الدِّما
(Had any tribe accepted wealth as ransom, we would have driven wealth to it like a brimming torrent; but a people whose brother was struck down refused to be content with disgrace, and chose blood over milk.)
And he said:
821 - أَكَلْتُ دماً إنْ لم أَرْعُكِ بِضَرَّةٍ ... بعيدةِ مَهْوى القِرْطِ طَيِّبَةِ النَّشْرِ
(May I have eaten blood [i.e. accepted blood-money] if I do not frighten you with a co-wife, long-necked and sweet of scent.)
And he said:
822 - يَأْكُلْن كَلَّ ليلةٍ إكافا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(They eat a pack-saddle every night…)
He means: the price of a pack-saddle.
His words: {فِي بُطُونِهِمْ}: three interpretations are permissible. The most apparent: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to His words «يأكلون», being an adverbial of place for it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «It involves the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the passage of their bellies"»; but there is no need for the implied form he gave. The second: that it is attached to something omitted, as a ḥāl from «النار». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «The better view is that the ḥāl here is anticipated (muqaddara), because at the time of eating it is not in their bellies; it only comes to that. The implied form is: being established, or being, in their bellies». He said: «This entails placing the ḥāl before the particle of exception, which is weak — unless the object is made to be omitted and «في بطونهم» a ḥāl from it or an adjective of it, i.e. "in their bellies something"»; meaning that «إلا النار» would then be accusative as a complete exception, since it is excepted from that omitted element. However, he said after that: «This statement is figurative in meaning, and the i'rab follows the rule of the wording». The third: that it is an adjective or a ḥāl from the omitted object of «كُلوا» «[Translator's note: so in the text; the verb in this verse is «يأكلون».]», as was established above.

semin-durr:175-175.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَمَآ أَصْبَرَهُمْ}: there are five views about this «ما». The first — the view of Sībawayh and the majority — is that it is a complete indefinite noun, neither relative nor qualified, and that its meaning is wonder (taʿajjub); so when you say «ما أحسنَ زيداً» (how handsome Zayd is!), its meaning is: "something has made Zayd handsome". The second — to which al-Farrāʾ went — is that it is interrogative, accompanied by the meaning of wonder, as in {كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ} [al-Baqara: 28]. The third — attributed to al-Akhfash — is that it is a relative noun. The fourth — also attributed to him — is that it is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective. On these four views it is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); its khabar (predicate) on the first two views is the verbal clause after it, while on al-Akhfash's two views the khabar is omitted, since the clause after it is either a ṣila (relative clause) or an adjective. They likewise differed over the «أَفْعل» that comes after it: is it a noun — the view of the Kufans — or a verb? The latter is correct. On this disagreement rests a disagreement over the accusative of the noun after it: is it a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), or likened to the mafʿūl bihi? These doctrines have proofs, objections and answers for which this is not the place.
What is meant by wonder here and in the rest of the Quran is the announcement that their state is such that one ought to wonder at it; otherwise wonder is impossible with respect to Him, the Exalted. The meaning of «على النار» is [i.e.] "for the deeds of the people of the Fire"; this is a figurative use of speech.
The fifth: that it is negative, i.e. "Allah did not make them patient in the Fire". Abū al-Baqāʾ reported it, and it is worthless.

semin-durr:176-176.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ الله}: They differed over the grammatical position of «ذلك»: it has been said to be nominative, and it has been said to be accusative. Those who say it is nominative differed on three views. The first: that it is the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb, i.e. "that became due to them". The second: that «ذلك» is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and «بأنَّ الله» its khabar (predicate), i.e. "that punishment is deserved because of what Allah sent down in the Quran concerning the unbeliever's deserving punishment". The third: that it is a khabar whose mubtadaʾ is omitted, i.e. "the matter is that", the reference being to the punishment. Whoever said it is accusative gave as its implied form: "We did that", and the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to that omitted element and has a causal sense.

semin-durr:78-78.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَمِنْهُمْ أُمِّيُّونَ}: «منهم» is a fronted khabar (predicate), so it is attached to an omitted element, and «أمِّيُّون» is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject). On the opinion of al-Akhfash it may be a fāʿil (agent) of the adverbial expression before it, even though that does not lean on [anything]; I explained earlier what it leans on.

أمِّيُّون is the plural of أُمّيّ, one who neither writes nor reads. There is disagreement about what it is related to. It is said: to the mother (الأُم), and in this there are two senses. First: that he is in the state of his mother who bore him in not knowing writing, and not like his father, because writing is not among women's occupations. Second: that he is in the state in which his mother bore him, not having changed from it or moved on. It is also said: it is related to الأُمَّة in the sense of stature and natural form, meaning that he has of the people nothing but that. It is also said: it is related to the community (الأُمَّة) in its simplicity before it came to know things, as they say عامِّي, i.e. in the manner of the common people. From Ibn ʿAbbās: "They were called أمِّيُّون because they did not believe in the Mother of the Book." Abū ʿUbayda said: "They were called أُمِّيُّون because of the sending down of the Book upon them, as though they were related to the Mother of the Book."

Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «أُمِيُون» with a light yāʾ, as though he found the succession of two doublings heavy.

His words: {لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ}: a verbal clause in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of أمِّيُّون, as though it were said: "unlettered, not knowing".

His words: {إِلاَّ أَمَانِيَّ}: this is a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because "wishful fancies" are not of the genus of the Book, nor included under what it denotes; and that is what the disjoined [exception] is. But its condition is that its inclusion be conceivable in some way, as in His words {مَا لَهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِلاَّ اتباع الظن} [al-Nisāʾ: 157]/ and the words of al-Nābigha:

556 - حَلَفْتُ يميناً غيرَ ذي مَثْنَوِيَّةٍ ... ولا عِلْمَ إلا حُسْنُ ظنٍّ بصاحبِ
(I swore an oath without reservation — and I have no knowledge, only a good opinion of a companion.)

because by mentioning knowledge, opinion is called to mind. For this reason it is not permissible to say: "The horses neighed, except a donkey."

Know that the disjoined [exception] is of two kinds: a kind toward which the governor can properly be directed, such as "the people came except a donkey"; and a kind toward which it cannot, such as the grammarians' examples: "it increased only what it decreased" and "it benefited only what it harmed". In the first there are two dialects: the dialect of the Ḥijāz requires the accusative, and the dialect of Tamīm treats it like the joined [exception], so after negation and the like both the accusative and agreement (itbāʿ) are permitted. The noble verse is of the first kind, so its accusative admits two aspects. First: as a disjoined exception. Second: that it is a badal (substitute) from الكتاب. «إلا» in the disjoined [exception] is construed by the Basrans as «لكن» and by the Kufans as «بل».

The apparent sense of Abū al-Baqāʾ's words is that it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) by an omitted verb, for he said: "{إِلاَّ أَمَانِيَّ} is a disjoined exception, because wishful fancies are not of the genus of knowledge; «إلاَّ» in such a case is construed as «لكنْ», i.e. 'but they wish it wishes'." So for him it belongs to the chapter of the emptied (mufarragh) disjoined exception, and it becomes parallel to "I knew nothing but supposition". This is questionable.

الأمانيّ is the plural of أُمْنِيَّة, with doubled yāʾ in both. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Lightening it is permissible in both." Abū Jaʿfar read it lightened, dropping one of the two yāʾs for lightening. Al-Akhfash said: "This is as is said in the plural of مفتاح: مفاتح and مفاتيح." Al-Naḥḥās said: "Dropping is more frequent in the weak [roots]", and recited the words of al-Nābigha:

557 - وهل يُرْجِعُ التسليمَ أو يَكْشِفُ العمى ... ثلاثُ الأَثافي والرسومُ البلاقِعُ
(Can the three hearthstones and the desolate traces return a greeting, or remove blindness?)

Abū Ḥātim said: "Everything of this kind whose singular has come doubled, you have both options in the plural", and its basis goes back to what al-Akhfash said.

The pattern of أُمْنِيَّة is أُفْعُولة, from منَّى يُمَنِّي, when one recites and reads. He said:

558 - تَمَنَّى كتابَ اللهِ آخرَ ليلِهِ ... تَمَنِّىِ داودَ الزبورَ على رِسْلِ
(He recited the Book of Allah at the end of his night, as David recited the Psalms, unhurriedly.)

Kaʿb ibn Mālik said:

559 - تَمَنَّى كتابَ اللهِ أوَّلَ لَيلهِ ... وآخِرَه لاقى حِمامَ المقادِرِ
(He recited the Book of Allah at the beginning of his night, and at its end he met the death decreed.)

And Allah the Exalted said: «إلا إذا تَمَنَّى ألقى الشيطانُ في أُمْنِيَّتِهِ», i.e. he recited and read. On this view the origin is أُمْنُوية, which underwent the change that ميِّت and سيِّد undergo, as has been discussed. It is also said: الأمنيّة is lying and fabrication. It is also said: what a person wishes for and desires. It is also said: what he estimates and conjectures, from مَنَّى when he lied, wished or estimated, as in his words:

560 - لا تأْمَنَنَّ وأنْ أمْسَيْت في حَرَمٍ ... حتى تُلاقِي ما يَمْني لكَ الماني
(Do not feel secure, even if you are in a sanctuary at evening, until you meet what the Determiner determines for you.)

i.e. what the Estimator estimates for you.

Al-Rāghib said: "المَنْي is measure (القَدْر); from it comes «المَنا», by which things are weighed; and from it المَنِيَّة, which is the term of death measured out for living beings. التمنِّي is estimating something in the soul and picturing it there; that may be from supposition and conjecture, and it may be built on reflection and a basis. But since most of it is from conjecture, lying has the greater hold on it, so most wishing is picturing what has no reality. الأُمْنِيَة is the image that arises in the soul from wishing for a thing. And since lying is picturing what has no reality and expressing it in words, wishing became like the starting point of lying [so it was used to express it; from this is the saying of ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him: 'I have not sung, nor have I تَمَنَّيْتُ (lied), since I embraced Islam']."

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The derivation from مَنَّى, when he estimated, [is] that the one who wishes estimates in his soul and conjectures what he wishes for; and likewise the fabricator; and the reciter estimates that such-and-such a word comes after such-and-such." So he made a shared measure among these meanings, and it is clear.

His words: {وَإِنْ هُمْ إِلاَّ يَظُنُّونَ}: «إنْ» is negative in the sense of ما. When it is negative, the well-known view is that it does not govern as Ḥijāzī «ما» does; some permitted that and attributed it to Sībawayh, and they recited:

561 - إنْ هُوَ مستولياً على أَحَدٍ ... إلاَّ على أَضْعَفِ المجانين
(He has no mastery over anyone, except over the weakest of madmen.)

«هو» is its noun and «مستولياً» its khabar. So His word «هم» is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, not the noun of «إنْ», since it does not govern on the well-known view; «إلاَّ» is for the emptied exception; and «يَظُنُّونَ» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «هم». The two objects of ظنّ are omitted because they are known, or by way of restriction (iqtiṣār), which is a matter of disagreement.

semin-durr:79-79.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَوَيْلٌ لِّلَّذِينَ يَكْتُبُونَ}: وَيْلٌ is a mubtadaʾ (subject). Beginning with it is permitted although it is indefinite, because it is an imprecation against them, and imprecation is among the things that license [an indefinite mubtadaʾ], whether it is a prayer for someone, as in «سلامٌ عليكم», or against him, as in this verse. The preposition and its genitive noun after it is the khabar (predicate), so it is attached to an omitted element.

Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Had it been in the accusative, it would have an aspect, construed as: 'Allah has made woe binding on them'; and the lām would be explicative, because the noun was not mentioned before the maṣdar." He means that the lām after the accusative is for clarification, so it is attached to an omitted element. And by his words "because the noun …" he means that if it had been mentioned before «ويل», so that you said "Allah has made woe binding on Zayd", it would not need clarification, unlike if it comes later. The wording of al-Jarmī suggests that the nominative is obligatory when it is cut off from annexation, but al-Akhfash stated explicitly that the accusative is permissible, for he said: "The accusative is permissible by implying a verb, i.e. 'Allah has made woe binding on them'."

Know that ويل and its sisters — وَيْح, وَيْس, وَيْب and عَوْل — are among the maṣdars (verbal nouns) put in the accusative by verbs not from their own root, and those verbs must be implied; it is not permissible to make them overt at all, because they [the maṣdars] have been made a substitute for pronouncing the verb. When it is separated from annexation, the nominative is better, as in «وَيْلٌ له»; and if it is annexed, it is accusative, as stated. Although al-Jarmī's wording suggests that the nominative is obligatory when it is cut off from annexation — for he said: "When you bring in the lām you use the nominative and say: ويلٌ له, وَوَيْحٌ له" — it is as though he means "in most cases". The Arabs did not use a verb from it because of the weakness of its second and first radicals. Ibn ʿArafa reported «تَوَيَّلَ الرجلُ» when he invoked woe, but this does not refute [the above], because it is like their saying «سَوَّفْتَ» and «لَوْلَيْتَ» when you say to him سوف and لو.

The meaning of الوَيْل is the intensity of evil; al-Khalīl said this. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: الوَيْل is lamenting, and الوَيْل is [also] expressing pity. Sībawayh said: "وَيْل is for one who has fallen into destruction, and وَيْح is a rebuke to one who is on the brink of destruction." It is also said: الويل is grief. Are وَيْل, وَيْح, وَيْس and وَيْب of one meaning, or is there a difference between them? There is disagreement; what Sībawayh distinguished among some of them has been given. Some said: وَيْل is in imprecation against someone, and وَيْح and what follows are expressions of pity for him. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the origin of وَيْل is وَيْ, i.e. grief, as you say وَيْ لفلان, i.e. grief to him; then the Arabs joined it to the lām, considered [the lām] part of it, and declined it. This is very strange. One says وَيْل and وَيْلة with tāʾ. Imruʾ al-Qays said:

562 - له الويلُ إنْ أَمْسى ولا أمُّ عامرٍ ... لَدَيْهِ ولا البَسْباسَةُ ابنةُ يَشْكُرا
(Woe to him if he comes to evening with neither Umm ʿĀmir nor al-Basbāsa daughter of Yashkur with him.)

And he also said:

563 - ويومَ دَخَلْتَ الخِدْرَ خِدْرَ عُنَيْزَةٍ ... فقالَتْ: لَكَ الوَيْلاتُ إنَّك مُرْجِلي
(And the day I entered the litter, the litter of ʿUnayza, and she said: "Woes to you! You will make me go on foot.")

ويلات is the plural of وَيْلَة, not the plural of وَيْل as Ibn ʿAṭiyya claimed,/ because pluralising a masculine with alif and tāʾ is not analogical.

His words: {بِأَيْدِيهِمْ}: attached to (mutaʿalliq) يكتبون. Making it a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الكتاب» is far-fetched. الكتاب here is in the sense of "what is written", so it is accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); making it a maṣdar in its proper sense is far-fetched. This belongs to the chapter of emphasis, for writing is not done other than with the hand; like it are {وَلاَ طَائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ} [al-Anʿām: 38] and {يَقُولُونَ بِأَفْوَاهِهِم} [Āl ʿImrān: 167]. It is also said: the benefit of mentioning it is that they did it themselves and did not command others to do it, for your saying "so-and-so did such-and-such" may mean that he commanded it to be done without doing it himself, as in "the prince built the city"; so this was brought to remove that figurative sense. It is also said: its benefit is to show their audacity and openness, for the one who does the deed himself is more deeply involved than one who does not. These two views are close to emphasis, for the basis of emphasis is removing the supposition of a figurative sense. Ibn al-Sarrāj said: "The mention of the hands is an allusion to their having fabricated that of their own accord and from themselves." What he said does not necessarily follow.

الأيدي is the plural of يَد. The origin is أَيْدُيٌ with ḍamma on the dāl, like فَلْس / أَفْلُس in the plural of paucity. The ḍamma before the yāʾ was found heavy, so it was changed to kasra for harmony, as in بِيْض, plural of أَبْيض, the original being بُيْض with ḍamma on the yāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the ḍamma is on the bāʾ], like حُمْر, plural of أحمر. This is the opinion of Sībawayh — I mean that he keeps the letter and changes the vowel — and the doctrine of al-Akhfash is the reverse. The verification of their two doctrines will come at the mention of «معيشة», if Allah the Exalted wills.

The origin of يَد is يَدْي with sukūn on the middle radical. It is also said: يَدَي with a vowel on it; then the weak letter had a vowel and the letter before it had fatḥa, so it was changed to alif and it became يداً, like رَحىً. On this is based the dual يديان, and also his words:

564 - يا رُبَّ سارٍ باتَ لن يُوَسَّدا ... تحتَ ذِراعِ العَنْسِ أو كفَّ اليَدا
(How many a night traveller spent the night with no pillow but the foreleg of his strong she-camel, or the palm of his hand.)

The well-known [usage] in its dual is not restoring its third radical. Allah the Exalted said {بَلْ يَدَاهُ مَبْسُوطَتَانِ} [al-Māʾida: 64] and {تَبَّتْ يَدَآ أَبِي لَهَبٍ} [al-Masad: 1]. The restoration is anomalous in his saying «يَدَيان»:

565 - يَدَيَان بَيْضَاوان عِندَ مُحَلِّمٍ ... قد يَمْنَعانِكَ أَنْ تُضَامَ وتُقْهَرا
(Two white [generous] hands belonging to Muḥallim, which may protect you from being wronged and overpowered.)

أيادٍ is the plural of the plural, like كَلْب / أَكْلُب / أكالب.

In His words {يَكْتُبُونَ الكتاب} there must be an omission by which the meaning is sound. Al-Zamakhsharī construed it as: "they write the distorted book"; others construed it as a ḥāl from الكتاب: "they write the book distorted". This implication was needed only because disapproval is not directed at one who writes the Book with his hand unless he distorts and alters it.

His words: {لِيَشْتَرُواْ}: the lām is the lām of kay, which has been discussed. The pronoun in «به» refers to what they pointed to by their saying {هذا مِنْ عِنْدِ الله}, and «ثمناً» is its object. The verification of the bāʾ entering on what is not the price was given at His words {وَلاَ تَشْتَرُواْ بِآيَاتِي ثَمَناً قَلِيلاً} [al-Baqara: 41], so let reference be made there. The lām is attached to يقولون, i.e. "they say that for the sake of purchasing". Whoever made it attached to the [notion of] being (al-istiqrār) contained in His words {مِنْ عِنْدِ الله} went far astray.

His words: {مِّمَّا كَتَبَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ}: attached to ويل, or to the [notion of] being in the khabar. «مِنْ» is causal. «ما» is a nominal relative and the resumptive pronoun is omitted. It may also be an indefinite qualified by a description — though this is not as strong as the first — and the resumptive is also omitted, i.e. "[which] they wrote (it)". It may also be maṣdariyya, i.e. "because of their writing". {وَوَيْلٌ لَّهُمْ مِّمَّا يَكْسِبُونَ} is like what preceded it. «الوَيْل» is repeated only to convey that destruction attaches to each of the two acts separately, not to the two together. And «كَتَبَتْ» was placed before «يَكْسبون» only because the writing comes first and its result is the earning of wealth: writing is the cause and earning the effect, so the composition came in accordance with this.

semin-durr:121-121.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {الذين آتَيْنَاهُمُ}: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). Concerning its khabar (predicate) there are two views. The first: it is «يَتْلُونه», and the clause «أولئكَ يؤمنون» is then either resumptive, which is the correct view, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) on a weak view whose like was given at the beginning of the sūra.
