So the meaning of أَلْقيتُ الشيء is "I made it لُقَىً (a thing cast aside)"; it is fuʿal in the sense of mafʿūl, just as طريد is faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl. It is as if it were said: "do not make yourselves a thing cast aside unto destruction."

semin-durr:49-49.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَإِذْ نَجَّيْنَاكُم مِّنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ}: «إذْ» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to «نعمتي», and likewise the adverbs after it, such as «وإذا واعَدْنا» and «وإذا قُلتم». It has been read «أَنْجَيْتُكُم» in the singular. This is an address to those present in the time of the Messenger, upon him be peace, so an omitted muḍāf must be supposed, i.e. "We saved your fathers", as in {حَمَلْنَاكُمْ فِي الجارية} [al-Ḥāqqa: 11]; or because the saving of the fathers is a cause of the existence of the sons. The origin of al-injāʾ and al-najāt is casting onto a najwa of the ground, which is a raised part of it, so as to be safe from harms; then al-injāʾ came to be applied to everyone who succeeds and comes out of straitness into ampleness, even if not cast onto a raised place.
«من آلِ» is attached to it, and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent. There is disagreement over «آل» on three views. Sībawayh and his followers said: its origin is أَهْل; the hāʾ was changed into hamza because of its closeness to it, just as they said ماء whose origin is ماه; then the hamza was changed into alif because it was quiescent after a hamza with fatḥa, as in آمَنَ and آدَم. For that reason, when it is put in the diminutive it returns to its origin, and you say: أُهَيْل. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Some said أُوَيْل, the alif being changed into wāw, without returning it to its origin, just as they did not return «عُيَيَدْ» to its origin in the diminutive", meaning they did not say «عُوَيد», since it is from عاد يعود; they said: lest it be confused with ʿūd (wood). This is questionable, because the grammarians said: whoever believes it to be from «أهل» puts it in the diminutive as أُهَيْل, and whoever believes it to be from آل يَؤُولُ, i.e. returned, puts it in the diminutive as أُوَيْل. Al-Naḥḥās held that its origin is likewise «أَهْلَ», except that the hāʾ was changed into alif without first being changed into hamza; its diminutive, in his view, is أُهَيْل. Al-Kisāʾī said: أُوَيْل; what concerns it has preceded. Some said: it is derived from آل يَؤُول, i.e. returned, because a person returns to his family (āl); the wāw was vowelled and what preceded it had fatḥa, so it was changed into alif; its diminutive is أُوَيْل, as in مال / مُوَيل and باب / بُوَيْب; this is ascribed to al-Kisāʾī. Its plural is آلون and آلين, which is anomalous, like أهلِين, because it is neither an adjective nor a proper name. There is disagreement over its meaning: it has been said: «آلُ الرجل» are his kin, like his ahl; it has been said: whoever is of his party, even if not related to him; and it has been said: whoever follows him and is of his religion, even if not related to him. He said:
444 - فلاَ تَبْكِ مَيْتاً بعد مَيْتٍ أَجَنَّهُ ... عليٌّ وعَبَّاسٌ وآلُ أبي بَكْرِ
(Do not weep for any dead man after a dead man whom ʿAlī, ʿAbbās and the family of Abū Bakr buried.)
For this reason it has been said: the āl of the Prophet are those who believe in him until the end of time, and whoever does not believe in him is not of his āl, even if related to him by lineage, like Abū Lahab and Abū Ṭālib. The grammarians disagreed whether it may be annexed to a pronoun or not. Al-Kisāʾī, Abū Bakr al-Zubaydī and al-Naḥḥās held that this is not permissible, so one may not say: «اللهم صلِّ على محمدٍ وآلهِ» (O Allah, bless Muḥammad and his family), but rather «وعلى آلِ محمد». A group, among them [Ibn] al-Sīd, held that it is permissible, adducing his saying, upon him be peace, when he was asked, "O Messenger of Allah, who are your āl?" and he said: "My āl are every pious person until the Day of Resurrection." They also cited the saying of Abū Ṭālib:
445 - لا هُمَّ إنَّ المَرْءَ يَمْ ... نَعُ رَحْله فامنَعْ حَلالَكْ
وانصُرْ على آل الصَّلي ... ب وعابِديه اليومَ آلَكْ
(O Allah, a man defends his dwelling, so defend Your sanctuary; and give Your people (āl) victory today over the people of the Cross and its worshippers.)
And the saying of Nudba:
446 - أنا الفارسُ الحامي حقيقةَ والدي ... وآلي كما تَحْمي حقيقةَ آلِكا
(I am the horseman who protects what is sacred to my father and my family, as you protect what is sacred to your family.)
They also disagreed over whether it may be annexed to non-rational beings, so that one says: آلُ المدينةِ (the people of the city), آلُ مكةَ. The majority forbade it; al-Akhfash said: "We have heard it with towns; they said أهلُ المدينةِ and آلُ المدينة." It is annexed only to one who has standing and importance, so one does not say: آلُ الإِسكاف (the family of the cobbler) or آلُ الحَجَّام (the family of the cupper). It is one of the nouns necessarily annexed in meaning, not in wording. You have now learned the rules peculiar to it, as distinct from its origin, which is «أَهْل».
All this concerns «آل» meant as family. As for «آل» which is the mirage, it has nothing whatever to do with what we are discussing; its plural is أَأْوال and its diminutive أُوَيْل only, as in مال, أَمْوال, مُوَيْل.
His saying: «فِرْعَون» is genitive by annexation, but it is a diptote because of foreignness and definiteness. There is disagreement whether it is a personal proper name or a generic proper name, for everyone who ruled the Copts and Egypt is called Firʿawn, like Kisrā for everyone who ruled the Persians, Qayṣar for everyone who ruled the Byzantines, al-Qayl for everyone who ruled Ḥimyar, al-Najāshī for everyone who ruled Abyssinia, and Baṭlaymūs for everyone who ruled the Greeks. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Firʿawn is a proper name for whoever ruled the Amalekites, like Qayṣar for the Byzantines. Because of the arrogance of the Pharaohs they derived from it تَفَرْعَنَ فلانٌ, when one is arrogant and tyrannical." And among the witticisms of some of them [Translator's note: the printed text has «بعضم», a misprint for «بعضهم»]:
447 - قد جاءَهْ الموسى الكَلُومُ فَزَاد في ... أَقْصَى تَفَرْعُنِه وفَرْطِ عُرَامِه
(The wounding razor [mūsā] came to him, and he increased in the utmost of his pharaonic arrogance and the excess of his fierceness.)
Al-Masʿūdī said: "No explanation of Firʿawn in Arabic is known." The [apparent sense of] al-Jawharī's words is that it is derived from the meaning of arrogance, for he said: "The arrogant are al-farāʿina; and تَفَرْعَنَ, and he has farʿana, i.e. cunning and craft." In the ḥadīth: "We have seized the Pharaoh of this community" — unless he means the sense of what al-Zamakhsharī said, mentioned above.
His saying: «يَسُومونكم سوءَ العذابِ»: this clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «آل», i.e. while they were inflicting. It may also be resumptive, merely informing of that, and it would then be the narration of a past state; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said something to this effect, but it is not apparent. It has also been said: it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they inflict on you"; there is no need for that either. «كم» is the first object and «سوء» the second object, because «سام» is transitive to two objects, like أعطى; its meaning is: he dealt him such-and-such and imposed it on him, or charged him with it. Of this is the saying of ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm:
448 - إذا ما المَلْكُ سامَ الناسَ خَسْفاً ... أَبَيْنا أَنْ نُقِرَّ الخَسْفَ فِينا
(When the king imposes humiliation on people, we refuse to let humiliation settle among us.)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its origin is from سَام السِّلْعَةَ, when one seeks the merchandise, as though it means: they seek for you the worst punishment and desire it for you." It has also been said: the origin of al-sawm is continuance; of this is sāʾimat al-ghanam (grazing sheep), because of their continuing to graze.
The meaning is: they continue to torment you. "The worst of punishment" is its most severe and most hideous, even though all of it is bad, as though it is the ugliest of it relative to the rest. Al-sūʾ: everything that afflicts a person, of worldly or otherworldly matters. It is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), and it is made feminine with alif; the Exalted said: {أَسَاءُواْ السواءى} [al-Rūm: 10]. Someone permitted «سوء» to be the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being "they inflict on you a bad infliction" — so he supposed it. He also said: "It may be in the sense of 'the infliction of punishment'", as though he means by that that it is accusative as a kind of maṣdar, as in «قَعَدَ جلوساً» (he sat a sitting), because the worst of punishment is a kind of infliction.
His saying, Exalted is He: «يُذَبِّحُون»: this clause may be explicative of the clause before it, and its explaining it is in two ways. The first: that it is resumptive, and so has no grammatical position, as though it were asked: "How was their inflicting punishment?" and the answer was: "They slaughter." The second: that it is a badal (substitute) of it, as in his saying:
449 - متى تَأْتِنا تُلْمِمْ بِنا في ديارنا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Whenever you come to us, visiting us in our homes…)
and {وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذلك يَلْقَ أَثَاماً} [al-Furqān: 68]; for that reason the conjunction was left out. It may also be a second ḥāl, not on the basis that it is a badal of the first, according to the view of those who permit multiple ḥāls. Abū al-Baqāʾ forbade this aspect, arguing that the ḥāl resembles the direct object, and a governor does not govern two objects of this description; this is his building on one of two views. It may also be a ḥāl from the agent of «يَسُومونكم». It has been read «يَذْبَحُون» without doubling; the first is the reading of the majority, because the slaughtering was repeated.
If it is asked: why was the conjunction wāw not brought here, as it was brought in Sūrat Ibrāhīm? The answer is that explanation is intended here, as has preceded, while in Sūrat Ibrāhīm its meaning is: they torment you with slaughter and with other than slaughter. It has also been said: the wāw may be redundant there, so it would be like the verse of al-Baqara; the proponent of this view adduced as proof of the redundancy of the wāw his saying:
450 - فَلَمَّا أَجَزْنَا ساحةَ الحِّي وانْتَحَى ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(When we had crossed the courtyard of the tribe, and [a hollow] turned aside…)
And his saying:
إلى المَلِكِ القَرْم وابنِ الهُمَامِ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(To the king, the chief, and the son of the valiant lord…)
[Translator's note: this verse carries no number in the source; the next numbered verse is 452.]
The first answer is the more correct.
Al-dhabḥ: its origin is splitting; of it is «المَذابحُ» for the channels cut by torrents in the ground. «أبناء» is the plural of ibn, in which it returns to its origin and its final radical is restored, either wāw or yāʾ, according to what has preceded. The origin is «أَبْناو» or «أبناي»; the weak letter was changed into hamza because it is final after an augmentative alif. What is meant by them is the infants; it has also been said: the men, and they were called "sons" in consideration of what they had been.
His saying: {وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ} is conjoined to what precedes it. Its origin is يَسْتَحْيِيُون; it was modified by dropping the yāʾ after dropping its vowel, the explanation of which has preceded; so its pattern [Translator's note: the printed text has «فوزتُه», a misprint for «فوزنُه»] is yastafʿūn. What is meant by "the women" is the infant girls; they were called women only because of what they would come to be. It has also been said: what is meant is other than infants, as was said about "the sons". The final radical of «النساء» is apparently wāw, since it appears in its synonyms niswān and niswa; it may also be yāʾ, derived from al-nisyān (forgetting). Is nisāʾ the plural of niswa, or the plural of imraʾa in terms of meaning? Two views.
His saying: {وَفِي ذَلِكُمْ بلاء مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ}: the preposition-phrase is a fronted khabar, and «بلاءٌ» is the mubtadaʾ. Its final radical is wāw, because it appears in the verb, as in بَلَوْتُه, أَبْلُوه, {وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 155]; it was changed into hamza. Al-balāʾ is in good and in evil; the Exalted said: {وَنَبْلُوكُم بالشر والخير فِتْنَةً} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 35], because trial is testing: Allah tests His servants with good so that they give thanks, and with evil so that they are patient. Ibn Kaysān said: "أبلاهُ and بَلاه are used in good", and he cited:
452 - جَزَى اللهُ بالخَيراتِ ما فَعَلا بكم ... وأَبْلاهُمَا خيرَ البلاءِ الذي يَبْلُو
(May Allah requite with good things what the two of them did for you, and grant them the best of the favour with which He tries.)
So he combined the two forms. It has also been said: most commonly, in good one says أَبْلَيْتُه, in evil بَلَوْتُه, and in testing ابتلَيْتُه and بَلَوْتُه. Al-Naḥḥās said: "The demonstrative in His saying «وفي ذلكم» may point to the saving, which is a beloved good, and it may point to the slaughter, which is a hateful evil." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Al-balāʾ is the ordeal if «ذلك» points to what Pharaoh did, and the favour if it points to the saving." This is good. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«ذلكم» points to the whole matter, since it is good, so it is like a single present thing." It seems he means that it points to both matters together, the saving and the slaughter; for this reason he said after it: "and al-balāʾ is in good and evil". This is not far-fetched; like it is:
453 - إنَّ للخيرِ وللشَّرِّ مَدَى ... وكِلا ذلك وَجْهٌ وقَبَلْ
(Good and evil each have a limit, and each of that has a face and an aspect one confronts.)
{مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ} is attached to «بلاءٌ», and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent, figuratively. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is nominative as an adjective of «بلاء», and so attached to an omitted element." This is questionable, in that when two adjectives come together, one explicit and the other interpreted, the explicit one is put first — so much so that some people regard anything else as poetic licence. «عظيمٌ» is an adjective of «بلاء»; its meaning has preceded in full at the beginning of the sūra.

semin-durr:107-107.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ}: this is an interrogative whose meaning is affirmation (taqrīr); therefore it did not need a counterpart conjoined to it with «أم». And «أَمْ» in His saying «أم تُريدون» is disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa); this is what is correct in the verse. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Its apparent sense is pure interrogation, so the counterpart here, according to a group, is «أَمْ تريدون»; and some said: «أَمْ» is disjunctive, so the counterpart is omitted, its implied form being: 'or do you know?'. This is if the address is meant for his community, upon him be peace; but if he himself is meant by it, the counterpart is omitted, nothing else. Both views are related." End quote. This is not satisfactory, because of what has passed, that what is meant by it is affirmation; so it is like His saying: {أَلَيْسَ الله بِكَافٍ عَبْدَهُ} [al-Zumar: 36], {أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ} [al-Sharḥ: 1]. Interrogation in the sense of affirmation is very frequent, especially when it enters upon a negation, as I have exemplified for you.
In His saying {أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ الله} there are two shifts (iltifāt). One: a departure from addressing a group, namely {خَيْرٍ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ}. The second: a departure from the pronoun of the speaker magnifying Himself to the third person with the overt noun, so He did not say: "Do you not know that We…"; and that is because of the glorification and magnification it conveys. {أَنَّ الله على كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ}: «أَنَّ» and what is within its domain either stand in the place of two objects, as is the school of the majority, or of one, the second being omitted, as is the school of al-Akhfash, according to the disagreement that has preceded.
His saying, Exalted is He: {لَهُ مُلْكُ} . . .: two aspects are permissible for «مُلْك». One: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is fronted before it, and the clause is in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar of «أنَّ». The second: that it is in the nominative as an agent (fāʿil), put in the nominative by the preposition before it according to al-Akhfash. It cannot be said that the preposition here is supported by occurring as the khabar of «أَنَّ», so that it puts the agent in the nominative according to everyone, because the information is not completed by it, so it is not made a khabar. Al-mulk with ḍamma is the thing owned, and likewise it is with kasra, except that the form with ḍamma is used only in contexts of vastness and the extension of authority.
His saying: {وَمَا لَكُمْ مِّن دُونِ الله مِن وَلِيٍّ}: two aspects are permissible for «ما». One: its being Tamimi, so it has no government, «لكم» being a fronted khabar and «مِنْ وليّ» a postponed mubtadaʾ in which «مِنْ» is added, so it is not attached to anything. The second: that it is Hijazi; that is according to those who permit fronting its khabar when it is an adverb or a prepositional phrase; so «لكم» is in the position of the accusative as a fronted khabar, and «مِنْ وليّ» its postponed noun, «مِنْ» in it also being redundant (zāʾida). And {مِّن دُونِ الله} has two aspects. One: that it is attached to what «لكم» is attached to, namely the implied stability [istiqrār], and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent. The second: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from His saying {مِن وَلِيٍّ وَلاَ نَصِيرٍ}, because it is originally a naʿt (adjective) of the indefinite, and when it was fronted before it, it was put in the accusative as a ḥāl; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. On this view it is attached to something omitted other than what «لكم» is attached to [Translator's note: the source has «الذين», evidently for «الذي»]. «ولا نصير» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the wording of «ولي»; had it been read in the nominative, according to the position, it would have been permissible. He used the pattern faʿīl in «وليّ» and «نَصير» because it is more intensive than fāʿil, and because «وليّ» is more frequently used than «والٍ» — which is why the latter did not come in the Qurʾān except in Sūrat al-Raʿd — and also for the harmony of the verse-endings. In His saying «لكم» there is a transition from addressing one to addressing a group, and there is a fitness in it: the thing negated became explicit in generality by the addition of «مِنْ», so it was fitting that those from whom it is negated be likewise; so it was made plural for that.
His saying, Exalted is He: {أَمْ تُرِيدُونَ} . .: it has preceded that this «أَمْ» may be connective (muttaṣila), the counterpart of His saying «ألم تَعْلَمْ», or disjunctive — and this is the apparent one — so it is supposed as «بل» and the hamza, and it is a digression of transition from one story to another. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«أَمْ» here is disjunctive, since there is no hamza in the speech which occupies its place such that with «أم» it means 'which of the two'; and the hamza of His saying «ألم تعلمْ» has nothing to do with «أم»; the meaning is: rather, do you want…?" So he moved from one speech to another. The origin of «تُريدون» is turwidūn, because it is from rāda yarūdu, as preceded; the vowel of the wāw was transferred onto the rāʾ, so the wāw became vowelless after a kasra and was turned into a yāʾ. It has been said: «أم» is for interrogation and this clause is cut off from what precedes it; and it has been said: it is in the sense of «بل» alone. These two views are weak.
His saying: {أَن تَسْأَلُواْ}: a governor of the subjunctive and what it governs, in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of His saying «تُريدون», i.e. "do you want to ask your Messenger?".
His saying: «كما سُئِلَ» is attached to «تَسْأَلوا», and the kāf is in the position of the accusative; there are the two well-known suppositions about it. Sībawayh's supposition is that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun of the omitted maṣdar, i.e. "that you ask it, i.e. the asking, in the state of its being like the asking of Moses' people of him". The supposition of others — the majority of grammarians — is that it is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "that you ask your Messenger an asking resembling such-and-such". «ما» is maṣdariyya, i.e. "like the asking of Moses". Al-Ḥawfī permitted it to be in the sense of «الذي», so a referring pronoun must be supposed, i.e. "like the asking which Moses was asked". «موسى» is the object of a verb whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil); the agent was omitted because it is known, i.e. "as Moses' people asked".
The well-known reading is «سُئِل» with ḍamma on the sīn and kasra on the hamza. Al-Ḥasan read: «سِيل» with kasra on the sīn and a yāʾ after it, from sāla yasālu, like khiftu akhāfu. Is the alif in «سال» originally a hamza or not? Disagreement on that has preceded, and its precise statement will come at «سَأَلَ». It has also been read with the hamza eased to a sound between [hamza and yāʾ] (bayna bayna).
«من قبلُ» is attached to «سُئل», and «قبلُ» is indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because the muḍāf ilayhi is definite, i.e. "before your asking". This is emphasis; otherwise it is known that Moses' being asked preceded their asking.
His saying: {بالإيمان}: there are two aspects. One: that it is the bāʾ of exchange, the precise statement of which has preceded. The second: that it is causal. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may be an object of «يتبدَّل», the bāʾ being causal, as in your saying: I bought the garment with a dirham." In this example of his there is an objection.
{فَقَدْ ضَلَّ سَوَآءَ السبيل}: it has been read with the dāl assimilated into the ḍād and with it pronounced distinctly. Regarding «سواءَ», Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«سواء السبيل» is an adverb in the sense of the middle of the way and its most level part." This is correct, for «سَواء» has come in the sense of middle; the Exalted said: {فِي سَوَآءِ الجحيم} [al-Ṣāffāt: 55]; ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar said: "I kept writing until my middle (sawāʾī) gave out"; and Ḥassān said:
674 - يا ويحَ أصحابِ النبيِّ ورَهْطِه ... بعدَ المُغَيَّبِ في سَواءِ المُلْحَدِ
(Alas for the Companions of the Prophet and his kin, after the one hidden in the middle of the grave-niche!)
And of its coming in the sense of fairness is the saying of Zuhayr:
675 - أَرُونا خُطَّةً لا عيبَ فيها ... يُسَوِّي بيننا فياه السَّواءُ
(Show us a plan with no fault in it, in which fairness makes us equal.) [Translator's note: «فياه» is so in the source, apparently for «فيها».]
Al-sabīl (the way) is masculine and feminine: {قُلْ هذه سبيلي} [Yūsuf: 108]. The clause from His saying «فَقَدْ ضَلَّ» is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition, and the fāʾ is obligatory here because it is not fit to be a condition.

semin-durr:109-109.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَدَّ كَثِيرٌ مِّنْ أَهْلِ الكتاب لَوْ يَرُدُّونَكُم}: the discussion of «لو» is like the discussion of it at His saying: {يَوَدُّ أَحَدُهُمْ لَوْ يُعَمَّرُ} [al-Baqara: 96]. Whoever made it maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar) there made it so here, and said: it is the object of «يَوَدُّ», i.e. "many wished your being turned back". Whoever refused made its apodosis omitted, its implied form being: "if they could turn you back as disbelievers, they would be pleased — or glad — at that". Some said: its implied form is "if they could turn you back as disbelievers, they would wish that", so «وَدَّ» indicates the apodosis and is not the apodosis, because «لو» is not preceded by its apodosis, like the condition. This supposition which this speaker supposed is corrupt; that is because «لو» is a particle for what would have occurred upon the occurrence of something else, so his supposition entails that their wishing that did not occur — since what is affirmative in wording is negative in meaning — whereas the point is that their wishing that is occurring, by agreement. So supposing "they would be pleased" and the like is what is correct. And about «يَرُدُّ» here there are two views. One — and it is the clear one: that it is the one that takes two objects in the sense of «صَيَّر» ("to make become"), so the pronoun of those addressed is the first object and «كفاراً» the second object. Of the occurrence of «رَدَّ» in the sense of «صَيَّر» is the saying:
676 - رمى الحَدَثانُ نسوةَ آلِ حربٍ ... بمِقْدارٍ سَمَدْنَ له سُمودا
فَرَدَّ شعورَهُنَّ السُّودَ بيضاً ... وَرَدَّ وجوهَهُنَّ البِيضُ سُودا
(The calamities of time struck the women of the house of Ḥarb with a decree at which they stood stunned; it turned their black hair white and turned their white faces black.)
Abū al-Baqāʾ made «كفاراً» a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object pronoun, on the basis that it is the verb taking one object; and this is weak, because a ḥāl can usually be dispensed with, while this is indispensable.
«مِنْ بعدِ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يَرُدُّونكم», and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent.
His saying: {حَسَداً} is in the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and it has the conditions permitting its accusative; what governs it is «وَدَّ», i.e. what drives their wishing to turn you back as disbelievers is their envy of you. They permitted two other aspects in it. One: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl, and it was not made plural only because it is a maṣdar, i.e. "envying"; this is weak, because the occurrence of a maṣdar as a ḥāl is not regular. The second: that it is in the accusative as a maṣdar by an implied verb from its own root, i.e. "they envy you with envy". The first is the most apparent of the three.
His saying: {مِّنْ عِنْدِ أَنْفُسِهِمْ}: for this prepositional phrase there are three aspects. One: that it is attached to «وَدَّ», i.e. they wished that from the side of their desires, not from the side of religiosity; and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent. The second: that it is a naʿt (adjective) of «حَسَدا», so it is in the position of the accusative, attached to something omitted, i.e. "an envy being from their side and their desire"; its meaning is close to the first. The third: that it is attached to «يردُّونكم», and «مِنْ» is causal, i.e. the turning back would be from their own side and direction and by their leading astray.
His saying: «مِّن بَعْدِ مَا» is attached to «وَدَّ», and «مِنْ» is for beginning, i.e. their wishing that began from the time the truth became evident and clear to them, so their disbelief is obstinacy. «ما» is maṣdariyya, i.e. "after the truth's becoming clear". Al-ḥasad (envy) is wishing the removal of a person's blessing; the maṣdar is ḥasad and ḥasāda.
Al-ṣafḥ is close to pardon; it is taken from turning away with the side (ṣafḥa) of the neck. It has been said: its meaning is passing over, from taṣaffaḥtu al-kitāb, i.e. I passed over its leaves. Al-Ṣafūḥ is among the names of Allah; and al-ṣafūḥ is also a woman who covers her face, turning away; [the poet] said:
677 - صَفُوحٌ فما تَلْقاكَ إلاَّ بِحِيلةٍ ... فمَنْ ملَّ منها ذلك الوصلَ مَلَّتِ
(Averting her face, she meets you only by some stratagem; and whoever tires of that union with her, she tires of him.)
His saying: {وَمَا تُقَدِّمُواْ لأَنْفُسِكُم مِّنْ خَيْرٍ} is like His saying: {مَا نَنسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ} [al-Baqara: 106]: «ما» may be a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) or stand in the place of the maṣdar, and for «مِنْ خيرٍ» the four aspects that are in «من آية» are permissible: its being a direct object, a ḥāl, a tamyīz (specification), or attached to something omitted. «مِنْ» is partitive; its precise statement has preceded, so let it be consulted there. «لأنفسِكم» is attached to «تقدِّموا», i.e. for the life of your souls, and that was omitted. «تَجِدُوه» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition; it is the verb taking one object, because it is in the sense of finding/attaining, and its maṣdar is al-wijdān with kasra on the wāw, as preceded. A muḍāf must be omitted, i.e. "you will find its reward". Al-Zamakhsharī made the hāʾ refer to «ما», and he means that, because the good sent ahead is a cause that has passed away and is not found; only its reward is found. His saying: «عند الله» admits two aspects. One: that it is attached to «تجدوه». The second: that it is attached to something omitted, as a ḥāl from the object, i.e. "you will find its reward stored up and prepared with Allah". The adverbial sense here is figurative, as in «لك عندَ فلانٍ يدُ» ("you have a favour with so-and-so").

semin-durr:127-127.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَإِذْ يَرْفَعُ}: «إذ» is conjoined to the «إذ» before it, so the discussion of both is the same. «يرفعُ» has the meaning of the past «رفَعَ», because «إذ» is one of the particles that restrict the imperfect to the past. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the narration of a past state (ḥikāyat ḥāl māḍiya)." The Shaykh said: "This is open to question." «القواعد» is the plural of قاعدة, which is the foundation and base for what is above it; it is an adjective that has come to be used predominantly [as a noun], and its meaning is "the firm one"; from it is «قَعَّدك الله», i.e. I ask Allah to make you firm. The meaning of raising them is building upon them, because when something is built on them, they are moved from the state of lowness to height. As for «القواعد» among women, its singular is «قاعِد» without tāʾ, because the masculine has no share in it, since it is from قَعَدَتْ عن الزوج (she ceased [hoping] for a husband). He did not say «قواعد البيت» with annexation because of the magnification of the thing explained that lies in explanation after vagueness.
His words: {مِنَ البيت}: there are two aspects in it. The first: it is attached to «يرفع», and its meaning is the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya). The second: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «القواعد», so it is attached to something omitted, the implied form being "being part of the House", and the meaning of «مِنْ» is partitive.
His words: {وَإِسْمَاعِيلُ}: there are two views on it. The first — and it is the apparent one — is that it is conjoined to «إبراهيم», so it is an agent sharing with him in the raising, and His words {رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّآ} are in the position of the accusative by an implied saying, that saying being in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from both of them, i.e. "they raise [it], saying: our Lord, accept". This is supported by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd], with the verb of saying made explicit; he read: «يقولان ربَّنا تقبَّلْ» [Translator's note: the source repeats the clause "This is supported by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, with the verb of saying made explicit; he read «يقولان ربَّنا تقبَّلْ»" twice; it is translated once], i.e. saying that. It is also permissible that this saying not be a ḥāl, but a clause conjoined to what precedes it, and it is what governs the «إذ» before it, the implied form being: "they say: our Lord, accept, when they raise", i.e. at the time of their raising.
The second: the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl, and «إسماعيلُ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is an omitted saying, which is what governs His words «ربَّنا تَقبَّلْ»; so Abraham is the one raising, and Ismāʿīl only the one supplicating. They said: because Ismāʿīl was at that time a small child; and they related this from ʿAlī, upon him be peace. The implied form is: "and when Abraham was raising, Ismāʿīl saying: our Lord, accept from us". In bringing the word «الربّ» there is an intimation, through the mention of this attribute, of nurturing and setting right. «تقبَّلْ» means «اقبْلَ» (accept), so تفعَّل here has the meaning of the bare form. The discussion of the like of {إِنَّكَ أَنتَ السميع} has already been given: that «أنت» may be a tawkīd (emphasis), a mubtadaʾ, or a separating pronoun (faṣl). The attribute of hearing was put first, even though the request for acceptance comes after the deed, because of proximity, as in His words {يَوْمَ تَبْيَضُّ وُجُوهٌ وَتَسْوَدُّ وُجُوهٌ فَأَمَّا الذين اسودت} [Āl ʿImrān: 106]; and the attribute of knowledge was put later because it is a verse-ending (fāṣila), and because it encompasses things heard and others.
His words: {مُسْلِمَيْنِ}: the second object of «الجَعْل», since it means "rendering"; the first object is «نا». Ibn ʿAbbās read «مسلمِين» in the plural form, and there are two interpretations of that. The first: they treated the dual as the plural; those who make the dual a plural adduced it as evidence. The second: they meant themselves and their family, such as Hājar.
His words {لَّكَ}: there are two aspects in it. The first: it is attached to «مُسْلِمَيْن», since it means "we make our faces sincerely Yours", as in {أَسْلَمْتُ وَجْهِيَ للَّهِ}, so the object is omitted because the meaning is understood. The second: it is a naʿt (adjective) of «مُسْلِمَيْن», i.e. two who submit, settled [in that] for You, i.e. surrendering. The first is stronger in meaning.
His words: {وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِنَآ أُمَّةً مُّسْلِمَةً}: there are two views on it. The first — and it is the apparent one — is that «مِنْ ذريتنا» is an adjective of an omitted qualified noun, which is the first object, and «أمة مسلمة» is the second object, the implied form being: "and make a group of our offspring a community submissive [to You]". In «من» there are then three views. The first: it is partitive. The second — allowed by al-Zamakhsharī — is that it is explicative (tabyīn); he said: as in His words {وَعَدَ الله الذين آمَنُواْ مِنْكُمْ} [al-Nūr: 55]. The third: it is for the beginning of the extent of the making; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this.
The second of the two views: «أمَّةً» is the first object, and «مِنْ ذريتنا» is a ḥāl from it, because it was originally an adjective of an indefinite noun, and when it was put before it, it became accusative as a ḥāl; and «مُسْلِمَةً» is the second object. The origin is «واجعَلْ أمةً من ذريتنا مسلمةً», so the wāw originally entered upon «أمة», and He only separated them by His words «مِنْ ذرِّيَّتنا». This is permissible because it is part of the conjoined speech. [Translator's note: this is the view being reported.] There is room for question in allowing that, for grammarians like Abū ʿAlī and others forbade separating, by an adverb, between a conjunction consisting of a single letter and the conjoined noun, and they treated the poet's saying:
722 - يوماً تَراها كشِبْه أَرْدِيَةِ ال ... عَصْبِ ويوماً أَديمَها نَغِلاً
(One day you see her like the striped Yemeni cloaks, and one day [you see] her skin spoiled.)
as poetic licence; so separation by a ḥāl is even further. What he allowed becomes the parallel of your saying «ضَرَبَ الرجلَ ومتجردةً المرأةَ زيدٌ» (Zayd struck the man, and, unclothed, the woman), and this is not eloquent. It is not permissible for the implied «اجعَلْ» to mean "create" and "bring into being", so that it is transitive to one object, with «من ذريتنا» attached to it and «أمةً» as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). For if it is a conjoining of single words, sharing in the first governor is necessary, and the first governor does not mean "create" but "render"; and if it is a conjoining of clauses, only what is indicated by what is uttered is omitted, and what is uttered does not mean creating, so neither does what is omitted. Do you not see that they forbade, in His words {هُوَ الذي يُصَلِّي عَلَيْكُمْ وَمَلاَئِكَتُهُ} [al-Aḥzāb: 43], that the implied form be "and His angels pray", because of the difference in what the two kinds of ṣalāt denote, and interpreted it as a meaning common to both? His words «لكَ» have the two aspects given above after «مسلِمَيْنِ».
His words: {وَأَرِنَا مَنَاسِكَنَا}: the apparent [view] is that the seeing here is visual. «رأى» is originally transitive to one object, and when the hamza of transfer entered, it gave it a second object; so «نا» is the first object and «مناسِكَنا» the second.
Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be transferred from «رأى» in the sense of «عَرَفَ» (knew), so that it is likewise transitive to two, as has been said. Some, as Ibn ʿAṭiyya related, allowed it to be here mental (qalbiyya); the mental [verb] before transfer is transitive to two, as in the poet's saying:
723 - وإنَّا لَقومٌ ما نرى القَتْلَ سُبَّةً ... إذا ما رَأَتْه عامرٌ وسَلُولُ
(We are a people who do not consider being killed a disgrace, when ʿĀmir and Salūl consider it so.)
And al-Kumayt said:
724 - بأيِّ كتابٍ أم بأيَّةِ سُنَّةٍ ... ترى حُبَّهم عاراً عليَّ وتَحسِبُ
(By what Book, or by what Sunna, do you consider loving them a shame upon me, and reckon [it so]?)
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Whoever holds this must have the verb transitive to three; he escapes it by [saying] that, when made transitive by the hamza from mental seeing, it is found [taking two objects] like the non-transitivised form"; and he cited the saying of Ḥuṭāʾiṭ ibn Yaʿfur:
725 - أَريني جواداً مات هَزْلاً لأَنني ... أرى ما تَرَيْنَ أَوْ بخيلاً مُخَلَّدا
(Show me a generous man who died of emaciation, so that I may see what you see, or a miser made immortal.)
He means that the mental «عَلِم» is transitive to two, whether bare of the hamza or not. In that case it would resemble cases where فَعِل and أَفْعل have one meaning, which is strange. But his making the verse of Ḥuṭāʾiṭ about mental seeing is not conceded; rather its meaning is visual seeing — do you not see that his saying "a generous man who died" is among the objects of sight? So in establishing that the mental «أعلَم» is transitive to two, evidence is needed. Some said: "It is here visual and mental together, because the Hajj is only completed by matters, some of which are known and some seen"; on this he must either combine the literal and the figurative, or use a homonym in both its meanings at once.
The majority read «أَرِنَا» with full kasra on the rāʾ here, in al-Nisāʾ, and in al-Aʿrāf «أَرِني أنظرْ», and in Fuṣṣilat {أَرِنَا الذين} [Fuṣṣilat: 29]. Ibn Kathīr read with sukūn in all of them, and Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim agreed with him in Fuṣṣilat. There is disagreement [in transmission] from Abū ʿAmr: al-Sūsī relates from him agreement with Ibn Kathīr in all of them, and al-Dūrī relates from him a slurred (ikhtilās) kasra in them. As for the kasra, it is the basic form; the slurring is good and well known; and the sukūn is for lightness: they likened the connected to the separate and made its kasra quiescent, as they said فَخْذ for فَخِذ and كتْف for كتِف.
Some faulted the transmitter of this reading, saying: the kasra of the rāʾ has become an indication of the omitted hamza, for its origin is «أَرْءِنا», then [the vowel] was transferred; al-Zamakhsharī said this, following others. Al-Fārisī said: "The faulting is worthless, because it is a mutawātir reading; as for the kasra of the rāʾ, it has become like the basic form, because the hamza is rejected in usage." He also said: "Do you not see that they assimilated in {لَّكِنَّ هُوَ الله رَبِّي} [al-Kahf: 38], the origin being «لكنْ أنا»? They transferred the vowel and dropped [the hamza], then assimilated. So the loss of the vowel in «أَرِنا» is no worse than its loss in assimilation." Also, the sukūn has been heard in this word explicitly from the Arabs; [the poet] said:
726 - أَرْنا إدواةَ عبْدِ الله نَمْلَؤُها ... من ماءِ زمزمَ إن القومَ قد ظَمِئوا
(Show us ʿAbd Allāh's water-skin, that we may fill it from the water of Zamzam; the people have grown thirsty.)
The origin of «أَرِنَا» is أَرْءِنا; the vowel of the hamza was transferred to the rāʾ and the hamza was dropped. More detailed discussion than this was given at His words {حتى نَرَى الله} [al-Baqara: 55].
«المناسِك»: its singular is مَنْسَك, with fatḥa and kasra on the middle radical, and it has been read with both; the form with fatḥa is the regular one, since the middle radical of its imperfect takes ḍamma. «المنسَك» is the place of «النسُك», which is worship.
His words: {فِيهِمْ}: concerning this pronoun there are two views. The first: it refers back to the meaning of «الأمة», since had it referred to its wording He would have said «فيها»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. The second: it refers back to «الذرية», by the interpretation given earlier. It has been said: it refers back to the people of Mecca, and this is supported by {الذي بَعَثَ فِي الأميين رَسُولاً} [al-Jumuʿa: 2].

semin-durr:165-165.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَن يَتَّخِذُ}: «مَنْ» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is the prepositional phrase before it. Two views are possible on it. One: that it is a relative noun. The second: that it is an indefinite described noun (mawṣūfa). On the first, the clause after it has no grammatical position; on the second its position is nominative, i.e.: a party or a person taking. The pronoun in «يتَّخذ» was put in the singular in accordance with the wording of «مَنْ».

His saying: {مِن دُونِ الله}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يتَّخذ». What is meant by «دون» here is «غَيْر» (other than). Its origin is to be an adverb of place, rarely declined; it conveyed the meaning of «غير» only figuratively. That is because when you say «اتخذتُ من دونِك صديقاً», its origin is: I took a friend from a direction and place below your direction and place; so it is a figurative adverb. And when the place from which the friend is taken is [other than] your place, your direction being lower than it and below it, it must be "other", because it is not it. Then the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place while still being "other", so its indication of otherness came about in this way, not by way of original linguistic coinage. Something of this was established at the beginning of the sūra. «يتَّخِذُ» is «يَفْتَعِل» from «الأخْذ», and it is transitive to one object, namely «أَنْداداً». The discussion of «أنداداً» and its derivation has also been given.

His saying: {يُحِبُّونَهُمْ}: there are three views on this clause. The first: that it is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of «مَنْ» on one of its two views, the nominative pronoun referring back to it in consideration of the meaning, after consideration of the wording in «يتَّخِذُ». The second: that it is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of «أنداداً», the accusative pronoun referring back to them; what is meant by them is the idols, and He used the plural of rational beings only because they treated them as rational beings; or what is meant by them is whatever was worshipped besides Allah, rational and other, and the rational were then given precedence over the others. The third: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «يَتَّخِذ», the nominative pronoun referring back to what the pronoun in «يتَّخِذُ» refers back to, and it was put in the plural in accordance with the meaning, as stated.

His saying: {كَحُبِّ الله}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative: either as a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e.: they love them with a love like the love of Allah; or as a ḥāl from the maṣdar made definite, as has been established more than once. «الحُبُّ» is wanting what you see or think to be good. Its origin is from «حَبَبْتُ فلاناً»: I struck the core (ḥabba) of his heart, as in «كَبِدْتُه» (I struck his liver). «أَحْبَبْتُه»: I made my heart exposed to loving him. But the commonest usage is to say «أَحْبَبْتُه فهو محبوب»; «مُحَبّ» is rare, as in his saying:
799 - ولقد نَزَلْتِ فلا تظنِّي غيرَه ... مني بمنزلةِ المُحَبِّ المُكْرَمِ
(You have taken up with me — think nothing else — the station of the beloved and honoured one.)
«الحُبُّ» is originally the maṣdar of «حَبَّه», and by analogy it should have had fatḥa on the ḥāʾ. Its imperfect is «يَحُبُّ» with ḍamma, which is the analogical rule for the doubled «فَعَل» verb, and its [imperfect with] kasra is anomalous. «محبوب» is commoner than «مُحَبّ», and «مُحِبّ» is commoner than «حابّ». «الحبّ» has been pluralised because of the diversity of its kinds; [the poet] said:
800 - ثلاثَةُ أحبابٍ فَحُبُّ علاقةٍ ... وحُبُّ تِمِلاَّقٍ وحُبُّ هو القتلُ
(Three loves: the love of attachment, the love of flattery, and a love that is death itself.)

«الحُبّ» [here] is a maṣdar annexed to its object, with the agent omitted, its implied form being: like their love of Allah, or like the believers' love of Allah, meaning that they made the two loves equal: the love of the rivals and the love of Allah. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«حُبّ» is a maṣdar annexed to the object in wording, and it is in the implied form annexed to the implied (muḍmar) agent, its implied form being: like your love of Allah, or like their love of Allah, according to how each group construed it." End of quotation. His saying "to the implied agent" means that the agent is of the category of pronouns, namely «كُمْ» or «هِمْ»; or he calls omission "implying" (iḍmār), which is a widespread usage. He does not mean that the agent is latent in the maṣdar as it is latent in verbs, because that is a weak view of some, rejected on the ground that the maṣdar is a generic noun, and nothing is latent in a generic noun because it is non-derived.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«كحُبِّ اللهِ»: like the veneration of Allah and submission to Him, i.e. as Allah is loved, on the basis that it is a maṣdar formed from the passive; it was unnecessary to mention who loves Him only because there is no ambiguity." End of quotation. As for his making the maṣdar from the passive, that is one of three views: I mean permissibility without restriction. The second: disallowing it without restriction, and that is correct. The third: distinguishing between verbs that are used only in the passive, for which it is permitted — as in «عَجِبْتُ من جنونِ زيدٍ بالعلمِ» (I wondered at Zayd's being mad about knowledge), and the noble verse belongs to this, since «حُبّ» is predominantly passive — and others, for which it is not permitted. Those who permitted it without restriction adduced the saying of ʿĀʾisha: «نهى رسول الله صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عن قَتْلِ الأبتر وذو الطُّفْيَتَيْن» (The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the killing of the short-tailed [snake] and the one with two stripes), with «ذو» in the nominative, conjoined to the position of «الأبتر», because it is in the implied form an object whose agent is not named, i.e.: that the short-tailed one be killed. The exposition of these views has a place other than this.

Al-Zajjāj rejected the assumption of those who took the agent of the maṣdar to be the believers or their pronoun, and said: "It is worthless; the proof of its refutation is His saying afterwards: {والذين آمَنُواْ أَشَدُّ حُبّاً للَّهِ}." He preferred that the agent of the maṣdar be the pronoun of those who take [rivals], i.e.: they love the idols as they love Allah, "because they associated them with Allah the Exalted, and so made Allah and their idols equal in love." The proof al-Zajjāj gave is clear, because equating the unbelievers' love of their idols with the believers' love of Allah contradicts His saying: {والذين آمَنُواْ أَشَدُّ حُبّاً للَّهِ}, for in it equality is negated.

Abū Rajāʾ read: «يَحُبُّونهم», from the triliteral «حَبَّ»; «أَحَبَّ» is commoner. In the proverb: «مَنْ حَبَّ طَبَّ» (whoever loves becomes skilled [in pursuing his beloved]).

His saying: {أَشَدُّ حُبّاً للَّهِ}: the one surpassed is omitted, namely those who take rivals, i.e.: stronger in love for Allah than those who take rivals [are] for their idols. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "What «أشدّ» is connected with is omitted, its implied form being: stronger in love for Allah than the love of these for the rivals"; the meaning being that the believers love Allah more than these love their idols. It may also mean that the believers love Allah the Exalted more than these takers [of rivals] love Him, because they associated nothing else with Him.

He used «أشدّ» as a means of arriving at the elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl) from the root of love, because «حُبَّ» is passive, and one does not form the verb of wonder from a passive, nor build an elative from it; so He used something with which that is permissible. As for their saying «ما أحبَّه إليّ» (how dear he is to me), it is anomalous, with disagreement on that among the grammarians. «حباً» is a tamyīz (specification) transferred from the mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: their love for Allah is stronger.

His saying: {وَلَوْ يَرَى الذين}: the answer of «لو» is omitted, and there is disagreement over its implied form, which becomes clear only after mentioning the readings transmitted in the words of this noble verse. Ibn ʿĀmir and Nāfiʿ read: «ولو ترى» with the tāʾ of address, and «أن القوة» and «أن الله» with both [hamzas] having fatḥa. Ibn ʿĀmir read: «إذ يُرَوْن» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, and the rest with fatḥa on it [Translator's note: the source has «بفتحِهما» (on both), apparently for «بفتحها»]. Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and the Kufans read: «ولو يرى» with the yāʾ of the third person, and «أنَّ القوة» and «أنَّ الله» both with fatḥa. Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, Shayba, Yaʿqūb and Abū Jaʿfar read: «ولو تَرَى» with address, and «إن القوة» and «إن الله» both with kasra. A group read: «ولو يرى» with the yāʾ of the third person, and «إن القوة» and «إن الله» both with kasra.

With that established, they differed over the implied form of the answer of «لو». Some placed it before His saying «أن القوة», and some placed it after His saying «وأنَّ الله شديدُ العذابِ», which is the view of Abū al-Ḥasan al-Akhfash and al-Mubarrad. As for those who placed it before «أنَّ القوةَ», «أنَّ القوةَ» is governed by that answer. Its implied form on the reading «ترى» with address and fatḥa on both «أنَّ» is: you would know, O listener, that all power belongs to Allah; what is meant by this address is either the Prophet, peace be upon him, or every listener. On the reading with kasra on «إنّ», the implied form is: you would say: all power belongs to Allah — the disagreement over who is meant by the address being as stated — or the implied form is: you would find their state enormous, «إنَّ» having kasra only because it carries the meaning of giving a reason, as in your saying: "If you came to Zayd he would treat you well; he is generous to guests", where your saying "he is generous to guests" is the reason for your saying "he would treat you well".

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Its implied form is: if you saw those who did wrong in the state of their seeing the punishment, their terror at it and their finding it enormous, they would acknowledge it, they would acknowledge [Translator's note: the phrase is repeated thus in the source] that all power belongs to Allah." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] took issue with him, saying: "He ought to have said 'at the time of their seeing the punishment', giving a synonym of «إذ», which is the time, not the state. Moreover, his implied answer of «لو» is not consequent on what follows «لو», because the listener's or the Prophet's (peace be upon him) seeing the wrongdoers at the time of their seeing [the punishment] does not entail their acknowledgement that all power belongs to Allah. It is parallel to your saying: 'O Zayd, if you saw ʿAmr at the time he was beaten, he would acknowledge that Allah has power over him', for his acknowledging Allah's power is not consequent on Zayd's seeing." End of quotation.

Its implied form on the reading «يرى» in the third person is: they would know that power…, if the agent of «يرى» is «الذين ظلموا»; and if it is a pronoun referring back to the listener, the implied form is: he would know that power….

As for those who placed it after His saying «شديدُ العذاب», its implied form on the reading «ترى» with address is: you would find enormous what befell them; and the fatḥa of «أنَّ» is on the basis that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e.: because all power belongs to Allah; and its kasra has the meaning of giving a reason, as in: "Honour Zayd, he is learned; and slight ʿAmr, he is ignorant"; or it is a parenthetical clause between «لو» and its omitted answer. Its implied form on the reading «ولو يرى» in the third person, if the agent of «يرى» is the listener's pronoun, is: he would find that enormous; and if its agent is «الذين», the implied form is: they would find enormous what befell them, and the fatḥa of «أنَّ» is on the basis that it is governed by «يرى», on the assumption that the agent is «الذين ظلموا». Seeing here may be seeing of the heart, so that «أنَّ» takes the place of its two objects, or seeing with the eye, so that it is in the position of a single object.

As for the reading «يرى الذين» in the third person with kasra on both «إنَّ», the answer is an omitted verb of saying, and they have kasra because they occur after the verb of saying. Its implied form, on the agent being the pronoun of the one seeing [Translator's note: the source has «الرأي», evidently for «الرائي»], is: he would say: power…; and on its being «الذين»: they would say…; the object of «يرى» is then omitted, i.e.: if he saw their state. It is also possible that the answer is "he would find [it] enormous" or "they would find [it] enormous", according to the two views, and they have kasra only as a resumption.

The omission of the answer of «لو» is widespread and common, and its omission is frequent in the Qur'an. The benefit of its omission is to make it [seem] enormous and to let the soul go in every direction concerning it, unlike if it were mentioned, for then the listener would confine his concern to it. Its omission occurs frequently in their poetry and prose. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
801 - وجَدِّكَ لو شيءُ أتانا رسولُه ... سِواك ولكن لَمْ نَجِدْ لَكَ مَدْفَعا
(By your fortune, had any messenger other than you come to us [we would have refused him]; but we found no way of turning you away.)
And al-Nābigha said:
802 - فما كان بين الخيرِ لو جاءَ سالماً ... أبو حُجُرٍ إلاَّ ليالٍ قلائِلُ
(There were between [us and] the good news — had Abū Ḥujur come back safe — only a few nights.)

«إذ», an adverb of past time, entered in the midst of these future matters to bring the matter near and affirm its occurrence, just as the past form has taken the place of the future for that reason, as in His saying: {ونادى أَصْحَابُ الجنة} [al-Aʿrāf: 44] and {ونادى أَصْحَابُ النار} [al-Aʿrāf: 50], and as al-Ashtar said:
803 - بَقَّيْتُ وَفْرِي وانحرَفْتُ عن العُلَى ... ولَقِيْتُ أضيافي بوجهِ عَبُوسِ
إِنْ لم أشُنَّ على ابن حربٍ غارةً ... لم تَخْلُ يوماً من نِهاب نفوسِ
(May I have hoarded my wealth, turned away from high things, and met my guests with a frowning face, if I do not launch upon Ibn Ḥarb a raid that is never for a day free of the plundering of lives.)
He put «بَقَّيْتُ» and «انحرَفْتُ», which are in the past form, in place of the future, because they are made dependent on a future, namely his saying «إنْ لم أشُنَّ».

It is also said: He put «إذ» in place of «إذا». And it is said: the time of the Hereafter is connected to the time of this world, so one of them took the place of the other, because what adjoins a thing takes its place. So it is with every place where the like of this occurs, and it is frequent in the Qur'an.

The reading of Ibn ʿĀmir «يُرَوْنَ العذاب» is passive, from «أَرَيْتُ», transferred from «رَأَيْتُ» in the sense of «أبصرتُ» (I saw), so it became transitive to two objects: the first of them took the place of the agent, namely the wāw, and the second is «العذابُ». The reading of the rest is clear.

Al-Rāghib said: "His saying «أنَّ القوة» is a badal (substitute) from «الذين»", and he said: "It is weak." The Shaykh said: "The meaning becomes: if you saw Allah's power and His might over those who did wrong." And it is said in al-Muntakhab: "The reading with yāʾ is, according to some, preferable to the reading with tāʾ, because the Prophet, peace be upon him, and the believers already know the extent of what the unbelievers will witness, whereas the unbelievers do not know it, so the verb must be attributed to them." This is worthless, for both readings are mutawātir (mass-transmitted).

His saying: {جَمِيعاً}: a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in the prepositional phrase serving as khabar, because its implied form is: "that power is wholly Allah's". It is not permissible for it to be a ḥāl from «القوة», for the governor of the ḥāl is the governor of the one whose state it describes, and «أنَّ» does not govern a ḥāl. This is problematic, for they permitted «ليت» to govern a ḥāl, and likewise «كأنَّ», because of the verbal meaning in them — wishing and comparison — so the same ought to be permitted in «أنَّ» because of the meaning of emphasis in it. «جميع» is originally «فَعِيل» from «الجَمْع», and is like a collective noun (ism jamʿ); for that reason it is sometimes followed by a singular — the Exalted said: {نَحْنُ جَمِيعٌ مُّنتَصِرٌ} [al-Qamar: 44] — and sometimes by a plural — the Exalted said: {جَمِيعٌ لَّدَيْنَا مُحْضَرُونَ} [Yā Sīn: 32]. It is put in the accusative as a ḥāl, and is used for tawkīd (emphasis) with the meaning of «كل», indicating comprehensiveness as «كل» does; it has no indication of being together in time. You say: «جاء القومُ جميعُهم» (the people all came), and it does not follow that their coming was at one time. That was given in the distinction between it and «جاؤوا معاً» (they came together).

semin-durr:218-218.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {إِنَّ الذين آمَنُواْ}: إنَّ and its noun (ism); «أولئك» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «يَرْجُون» is its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of «إنَّ». This is better than taking «أولئك» as a badal (substitute) for «الذين» with «يرجُون» as the khabar of «إنَّ».

These three attributes were brought in an order matching what actually happened, since faith comes first, then emigration, then striving (jihād). Faith was given a relative noun (mawṣūl) of its own because it is the root of emigration and striving, while emigration and striving were joined under a single relative noun because both are branches of it. The khabar of «إنَّ» was given as a demonstrative because it comprehends the preceding attributes. The repetition of the relative noun relates to the attributes, not to the persons, for the persons are one and the same, described by the three attributes; so it belongs to the category of conjoining some attributes to others while the one described is single. And you are not to say that the repetition of the relative noun indicates that the persons described differ, on the grounds that this is how it actually was. «يَرْجُون» was used to indicate renewal, and that at every moment they produce fresh hope.

al-muhājara (emigration) is a mufāʿala form from al-hajr, and it is moving from one land to another; the root meaning of al-hajr is abandoning. al-mujāhada (striving) is a mufāʿala form from al-juhd, which is drawing out one's capacity and expending one's utmost effort; al-ijhād is expending one's utmost effort in seeking what is aimed at. al-rajāʾ (hope) is longing (al-ṭamaʿ). al-Rāghib said: it is a supposition that entails the attainment of something in which there is joy; and it is sometimes used for fear. He recited:

940 - إذا لَسَعَتْه النحلُ لَم يَرْجُ لَسْعَها ... وخالَفَها في بَيْتِ نُوبٍ عَواسلِ
(When the bees stung him he did not "yarju" their sting, but went against them into the home of honey-making bees.)

that is, he did not fear. And Allah the Exalted said: {لاَ يَرْجُونَ لِقَآءَنَا} [Yūnus: 7], that is, they do not fear. Is its use in this sense literal (ḥaqīqa) or figurative (majāz)? Some claimed that it is literal, and it would then be a case of homonymy (ishtirāk lafẓī); others claimed that it is one of the words with opposite meanings (al-aḍdād), which is also homonymy. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is not good," meaning that hope and fear are not opposites, since they can occur together. That is why al-Rāghib said, after reciting the verse above: "The explanation of [that] is that hope and fear entail one another," and Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Hope is always accompanied by fear, just as fear is accompanied by hope." Others claimed it is figurative, because of the mutual entailment we reported from al-Rāghib and Ibn ʿAṭiyya.

al-Jāḥiẓ answered regarding the verse that its meaning is: he did not hope for healing from their sting and its removal, so rajāʾ keeps its usual meaning. As for His words {لاَ يَرْجُونَ لِقَآءَنَا}, that is, they do not hope for the reward of meeting Us, so rajāʾ also keeps its usual meaning; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. al-Aṣmaʿī said: "When rajāʾ is joined to a particle of negation it means fear, as in this verse and the āya." This is open to question, since negation does not change what words signify.

«رحمة» is written here with a (long) tāʾ: either following the dialect of those who pause on the feminine tāʾ with a tāʾ, or in consideration of its form in connected speech. In the Qurʾān it occurs in seven places, all written with tāʾ: here; in al-Aʿrāf: {إِنَّ رَحْمَةَ الله} [al-Aʿrāf: 56]; in Hūd: {رَحْمَةُ الله وَبَرَكَاتُهُ} [Hūd: 73]; in Maryam: {ذِكْرُ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّكَ} [Maryam: 2]; in al-Rūm: {فانظر إلى آثَارِ رَحْمَتِ الله} [al-Rūm: 50]; and in al-Zukhruf: {أَهُمْ يَقْسِمُونَ رَحْمَتَ رَبِّكَ. . . وَرَحْمَتُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ} [al-Zukhruf: 32].

semin-durr:83-83.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا}: «إذ» is conjoined to the adverbs before it; what has been said about it — whether it is fully inflectable or not — has been given. «أَخَذْنا» is in the position of the genitive, i.e. "and remember the time of Our taking their covenant", or something like that.

His words: {لاَ تَعْبُدُونَ}: it has been read with yāʾ and with tāʾ, and this is clear. Whoever read it in the third person [did so] because the ruling of overt nouns is the third person; whoever read it in the second person — that is iltifāt (a shift of person), and its wisdom is that it is more conducive to the addressee's acceptance of the command and prohibition directed at him. Abū al-Baqāʾ took the second-person reading as implying the verb "say". He said: "It is read with tāʾ on the construal: 'We said to them: you shall not worship except Allah'." Taking it as iltifāt is better.

As for the i'rab of this negated clause, there are eight aspects. The most apparent: that it explains the taking of the covenant. That is, when Allah the Exalted mentioned that He took the covenant of the Children of Israel, there was in that a vagueness as to what the covenant was, so He brought this clause to explain it; it then has no grammatical position.

Second: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «بني إسرائيل», and then there are two aspects in it. One: that it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), meaning: "We took their covenant, they being destined to [maintain] monotheism forever as long as they lived". The other: that it is a concomitant ḥāl, meaning: "We took their covenant, they binding themselves to remain upon monotheism"; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and Quṭrub and al-Mubarrad preceded him in it. This is questionable, in that the ḥāl comes from the muḍāf ilayhi/ outside the places where that is permitted, according to the correct view, contrary to those who permit it from the muḍāf ilayhi without restriction. It cannot be said that the muḍāf ilayhi is in meaning governed by ميثاق — since ميثاق is either a maṣdar (verbal noun) or in its ruling, so what follows would be either agent or object — and that is [not] permissible, because one of the conditions for a maṣdar's governing, when it does not stand in place of the verb, is that it can be resolved into a maṣdariyya particle and a verb, and this cannot be resolved into them: were you to construe "and when We took that We make a covenant with the Children of Israel" or "that the Children of Israel make a covenant with Us", it would not be sound. Do you not see that if you said "I took Zayd's knowledge", it could not be construed as "I took that Zayd knows"? For this reason Ibn al-Ṭarāwa refused, in Sībawayh's chapter heading «هذا بابُ علم ما الكِلمُ من العربية», that the maṣdar be construed as a maṣdariyya particle and a verb, and he rejected and censured those who permitted it.

Third: that it is the answer to an omitted oath indicated by the word الميثاق, i.e. "We made them swear", or "We said to them: By Allah, you shall not worship…". This aspect is attributed to Sībawayh, and al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ and al-Mubarrad agreed with him.

Fourth: that it is on the construal of the omission of a preposition and the omission of أَنْ, the implied sense being: "We took their covenant on condition that you not worship", or "that you not worship". The preposition was dropped, because its dropping is regular with أَنَّ and أَنْ, as has been said more than once; then subjunctive «أَنْ» was dropped, so the verb after it became nominative. Its parallel is the words of Ṭarafa:

568 - أَلا أَيُّهذا الزاجري أحضرُ الوغى ... وأَنْ أشهدَ اللذاتِ هل أَنْتَ مُخْلِدي
(O you who chide me for being present at battle and for attending pleasures — can you make me immortal?)

And they reported from the Arabs: «مُرْهُ يَحْفِرَها» ("command him to dig it"), i.e. "that he dig it"; the implied sense being "from my being present" and "that he dig it". This is questionable, for implying «أَنْ» is not analogical; it is permitted only in places that the grammarians have enumerated, and they made anything else anomalous and rare. This is the correct view, contrary to the Kufans. When «أَنْ» is dropped, the correct view is that both the subjunctive and the nominative are permissible; «مُرْه يَحْفِرها» and «أَحْضُر الوغى» have been transmitted both ways. This is the opinion of al-Mubarrad and the Kufans, contrary to Abū al-Ḥasan [al-Akhfash], who required the nominative. The discussion has a place other than this that is more suitable for it. Al-Zamakhsharī supported this fourth aspect with the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]: «لاَ تَعْبُدوا», as a prohibition.

Fifth: that it is in the position of the accusative governed by an omitted verb "say", that saying being a ḥāl, its implied form being: "saying to them: you shall not worship except Allah". It would then be a statement with the meaning of a prohibition; this is supported by the reading of Ubayy mentioned before, and with this the conjoining of «وقولوا» to it becomes clear. Al-Farrāʾ held this.

Sixth: that subjunctive «أَنْ» is implied, as above, but it with what falls within its scope is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from «ميثاق». This is close to the first view, in that this clause explains the covenant; and it is subject to the objection mentioned before, namely the dropping of «أَنْ» outside the analogical places.

Seventh: that it is in the accusative by an omitted verb "say", that saying not being a ḥāl but mere information, the implied sense being "and We said that to them"; it would be a statement with the meaning of a prohibition. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "As you say: 'You go to so-and-so and say such-and-such to him', meaning a command. It is more eloquent than an explicit command and prohibition, because it is as though [the addressee] hastened to comply and desist, and He is reporting it. The reading of Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh «لا تعبدوا» supports it, and the verb 'say' must be intended." End of quotation. It is a very fine statement.

Eighth: that the implied form is «أَنْ لا تعبدون», this being explicative «أَنْ», because in His words {أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَ بني إِسْرَائِيلَ} there is vagueness, as said before, and it contains the meaning of saying; then explicative «أَنْ» was dropped. Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned this. Claiming the omission of the particle of explanation is obviously questionable.

His words: {إِلاَّ الله}: an emptied (mufarragh) exception, because what precedes it needs it; its verification was given earlier. In it there is iltifāt from the first person to the third, since had the speech run on its course it would have said "you shall not worship except Us", because of His words «أَخَذْنَا». This iltifāt carries an indication of the greatness of this Name and of His uniqueness in it which is not in the pronoun. Also, the nouns occurring [around it] are overt, so it was fitting that overt should neighbour overt.

His words: {وبالوالدين إِحْسَاناً}: there are five aspects in it. First: that the bāʾ is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «إحساناً», on the basis that it is a maṣdar standing in the place of an imperative verb, the implied sense being "and do good to (بـ) parents"; the bāʾ is synonymous with «إلى» in this meaning: you say أَحْسَنْتُ به and إليه. [Or] in the sense that on this aspect there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "and make excellent the dutifulness to parents", meaning: make excellent towards them your dutifulness to them. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "An objection to this view is that what the maṣdar governs comes before it." What Ibn ʿAṭiyya made an objection to this view does not hold on the doctrine of the majority, for their doctrine is that what is governed by a maṣdar standing in place of an imperative verb may come before it: you say ضرباً زيداً, and if you wish زيداً ضرباً. It is the same for them whether we assign the governing to the implied verb or to the maṣdar standing in place of its verb: fronting is permissible for them. What is barred is only fronting what is governed by a maṣdar that resolves into a maṣdariyya particle and a verb, as was explained just now. It holds only on the doctrine of Abū al-Ḥasan, for he bars fronting what is governed by a maṣdar standing in place of the verb, and in that he differed from the majority.

Second: that it is attached to an omitted element. That omitted element may be construed as an imperative verb, in keeping with His words {لاَ تَعْبُدُونَ}, which has the meaning of prohibition as said before, as though He said: "Do not worship except Allah, and do good to parents." It may also be construed as a statement in keeping with the wording of «لا تعبدون», the implied form being "and you shall do good". Al-Zamakhsharī construed it with both these possibilities. «إحساناً» is then accusative as a maṣdar emphasising that omitted verb. This is questionable in that the omission of the governor of an emphatic [maṣdar] is explicitly stated to be impermissible; and there is a discussion of this for which this is not the place.

Third:/ that the implied sense is "and take care of (استوصُوا) parents", so the bāʾ is attached to this implied verb, and «إحساناً» is then accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

Fourth: its implied sense is "and We enjoined them regarding parents", so the bāʾ is attached to the omitted element too, and «إحساناً» is then accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for the sake of Our doing good to those enjoined about", in that the doing good is caused by Our enjoining concerning them; or [to] those enjoined, because of the reward from Us that follows for them when they do good to them.

Fifth: that the bāʾ and what it governs are conjoined to His words {لاَ تَعْبُدُونَ}, if it is said that maṣdariyya «أَنْ» is implied; so from it and what follows it a maṣdar is formed to which this genitive phrase is conjoined, the implied sense being: "We took their covenant to devote worship solely to Allah, and to parents", i.e. "and to dutifulness to parents", or "to doing good to parents". The bāʾ is then attached to الميثاق because of the meaning of the verb in it, for adverbial expressions and the like are governed by the "scents of verbs". «إحساناً» is then accusative as a maṣdar from that omitted muḍāf, namely البِرّ, because it has its meaning, or [from] الإحسان which we construed.

The apparent one among these aspects is only the second, because of the absence of the implication that is necessary in the others, and because the occurrence of the maṣdar standing in place of an imperative verb is regular and widespread. What it governs was put first only out of concern for it and to call attention to the fact that they are more deserving of good than those mentioned with them.

الوالدان are the father and the mother; each of them is called والد. He said:

569 - ألا رُبَّ مولودٍ وليسَ لَهُ أبٌ ... وذي وَلَدْ لَمْ يَلْدَهُ أبوانِ
(How many a one born who has no father, and one with a child whom two parents did not beget.)

It is also said: one does not say والدة with tāʾ for the mother; rather "the two والد" was said of her and the father by giving the masculine predominance. الإحسان is bestowing favour on another. It is also said: rather it is more general than bestowing favour. It is also said: it is what benefits everything.

His words: {وَذِي القربى} and what follows it are conjoined to what is in the genitive by the bāʾ. The sign of the genitive in it is the yāʾ, because it is one of the Six Nouns, which are nominative with wāw, accusative with alif and genitive with yāʾ, under conditions mentioned by the grammarians. As to whether their declension is by letters or by something else, the grammarians have ten doctrines about it, and this is not the place to mention them. It is one of the nouns that are bound to annexation in form and meaning, to generic nouns, so that by it one can reach the qualification of an indefinite by a generic noun, as in مَرَرْتُ برجلٍ ذي مالٍ ("I passed by a man possessing wealth"). Its annexation to a pronoun is barred except in poetic necessity or rare speech, as in his words:

570 - صَبَحْنا الخَزْرَجِيَّةَ مُرْهَفاتٍ ... أبانَ ذوي أَرُومَتِها ذَوُوها
(In the morning we fell upon the Khazrajī [tribe] with sharpened blades, whose owners cut off the people of its root.)

And al-Kisāʾī recited:

571 - إنما يَعْرِفُ المَعْ ... روفَ في الناس ذَوُوه
(Only those who possess kindness recognise kindness among people.)

On this is based their saying: "O Allah, bless Muḥammad and ذَويه (his own people)." Its annexation to a proper name is very rare, and it is of two kinds: obligatory, when they are joined by original coinage, as in ذي يزن and ذي رَعين; and permissible, when they are not joined by original coinage, as in ذي قَطَري and ذي عمرو, i.e. "the bearer of this name". Rarer than that is its annexation to the pronoun of the addressee, as in his words:

572 - وإنَّا لَنَرْجُو عاجلاً منكَ مثلَ ما ... رَجَوْناه قِدْماً من ذَويك الأفاضلِ
(We hope soon from you for the like of what we hoped long ago from your excellent kinsmen.)

«ذو» also comes as a relative noun in the sense of الذي and its derived forms; the well-known [usage] then is that it is indeclinable and masculine [in form]. It has many rulings mentioned in the books of grammar.

«القُرْبى» is the muḍāf ilayhi; its alif is for the feminine. It is a maṣdar like الرُّجْعى and العُقْبى, and it is applied to kinship by lineage and by the womb. Ṭarafa said:

573 - وظُلْمُ ذوي القُرْبى أشدُّ مضاضةً ... على الحُرِّ مِنْ وَقْعِ الحُسامِ المُهَنَّدِ
(The injustice of kinsfolk is more painful to the free man than the blow of the Indian-forged sword.)

He also said:

574 - وَقرَّبْتُ بالقُرْبى وجَدِّك إنه ... متى يَكُ أَمْرٌ للنَّكِيثَةِ أَشْهَدِ
(I drew close through kinship — by your fortune! — for whenever there is an affair that tests one's strength, I am present.)

The root indicates nearness, the opposite of distance.

His words: {واليتامى}: its pattern is فَعالى, and its alif is for the feminine. It is the plural of يتيم, like نديم / نَدامى, and this plural is not analogical. اليُتْم is being alone; from it comes «اليتيم», because he is alone without his two parents or one of them; and دُرَّةٌ يتيمةٌ ("a unique pearl") when it has no equal. It is also said: اليُتْم is slowness, and from it comes صبيٌّ يتيم, because kindness is slow to reach him. It is also said: it is neglect, because the child is neglected as regards what is good for him. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: "Orphanhood among humans is through loss of the father, and among others through loss of the mother." Al-Māwardī said: "Orphanhood among people is also through loss of the mother." The first is what is known among the lexicographers. One says يَتُم يَيْتُم يُتْماً, like كرُم يكرُم and عَظُم يَعْظُم عُظْماً; and يَتِمَ يَيْتَم يَتْماً, like سَمِعَ يَسْمَع سَمْعاً. These are two well-known dialects reported by al-Farrāʾ. One says: أَيْتمه اللهُ إيتاماً, i.e. He did that to him.

The sign of the genitive in القربى and اليتامى is a kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif, even though it is [the alif] of the feminine, because a diptote, when annexed or when al- enters it, takes the genitive with kasra. Is it then called declinable (munṣarif) or merely "genitive-taking" (munjarr)? There are three views; the third distinguishes between the case where one of its two causes is being a proper name — then it is called munṣarif, as in «يَعْمُرُكمْ» — and the case where it is not — then it is called munjarr, as in بالأحمر. القربى and اليتامى are of this latter kind.

His words: «والمساكين»: the plural of مِسْكين. They call it "a plural that has no counterpart among singulars" and "a plural on the pattern of the ultimate plurals (muntahā al-jumūʿ)", and it is one of the causes that stand in place of two causes [for diptosy]; its verification will come shortly in this sūra.

The discussion of its derivation was given at the mention of المَسْكَنة. There is disagreement about it: is it in the sense of الفقير (the poor), or worse off than him, as in His words {مِسْكِيناً ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ} [al-Balad: 16], i.e. his skin cleaves to the dust, unlike the فقير, who has something? He said:

575 - أمَّا الفقيرُ الذي كانَتْ حَلُوبَتُه ... وَفْقَ العِيالِ فلم يُتْرَكْ له سَبَدُ
(As for the poor man whose milch-camel was just enough for the household, not a tuft of hair was left to him.)

Or is he better off, because Allah assigned them some property, saying {أَمَّا السفينة فَكَانَتْ لِمَسَاكِينَ} [al-Kahf: 79]? This is a well-known disagreement among the scholars, both jurists and lexicographers.

His words: {وَقُولُواْ لِلنَّاسِ حُسْناً}: this clause is conjoined in meaning to His words {لاَ تَعْبُدُونَ}, as though He said: "Do not worship except Allah, and do good to parents, and say…"; or to the implied «أَحْسِنوا», as was established at His words {وبالوالدين إِحْسَاناً}. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it to be governed by an omitted verb "say", its implied form being: "And We said to them: say…"

It has been read حَسَناً with two fatḥas, حُسُناً with two ḍammas, حُسْنى without tanwīn like حُبْلى, and إحساناً from the quadriliteral.

As for the reading «حُسْناً» with ḍamma and sukūn, it admits several aspects. First, which is the apparent one: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) occurring as a qualifier of an omitted element, its implied form being "and say to people a حُسْن speech", i.e. one possessing goodness. Second: that it is used as a qualifier by way of hyperbole, as though the speech itself were made goodness. Third: that it is an adjective on the pattern فُعْل, not originally a maṣdar, but like الحُلْو and المُرّ, so that it has the meaning of «حَسَن» with two fatḥas; there would then be two dialects in it, حُسْن and حَسَن, like البُخْل / البَخَل, الحُزْن / الحَزَن and العُرْب / العَرَب. Fourth: that it is accusative as a maṣdar derived from the meaning, for the meaning is: "and let your speech be good with goodness".

As for the reading «حَسَناً» with two fatḥas, which is the reading of Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī, it is an adjective of an omitted element, its implied form being "a good speech", as was said in one of the aspects of «حُسْناً».

As for «حُسُناً» with two ḍammas, the ḍamma of the sīn is in harmony with the ḥāʾ, so it has the meaning of «حُسْناً» with sukūn, and the aforementioned aspects apply to it.

As for whoever [read] «حُسْنى» without tanwīn, حُسْنى is a maṣdar like البُشْرى and الرُّجْعى.
