When an exception follows several clauses and could properly refer back to each of them, is it restricted to the last or not? There is a well-known disagreement. If some evidence indicates its restriction to one of the clauses, that is acted upon, and the verse is of this kind, for the meaning leads to its referring back to the first clause, not the second, for the reason I mentioned to you.

The two Ḥaram readers [Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr] and Abū ʿAmr read «غَرفة» with a fatḥa on the ghayn, and the rest with a ḍamma.

It is said that both have the sense of the maṣdar (verbal noun), except that they came on a pattern other than that of the verb's maṣdar, like nabāt from anbata; had it come on the verb's maṣdar, it would have been said ightirāfan. It is said that both mean "what is scooped", like al-ukl meaning "what is eaten". It is also said that the form with fatḥa is a maṣdar intended to indicate a single occurrence, since «فَعْلَة» indicates a single instance, and the form with ḍamma has the sense of the passive participle. Where you make them maṣdars, the object is omitted, its implied form being: "except whoever scoops water"; and where you make them mean the object, they are a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), so no implied object is needed.

It is reported from Abū ʿAlī [al-Fārisī] that he preferred the reading with ḍamma, because in the reading with fatḥa he would make it a maṣdar, and the maṣdar does not match the verb in its pattern; it would only come by way of omitting the augment letters, whereas making it mean the object does not require that, so it was preferable.

His words: {بِيَدِهِ}: it may be attached to «اغَتَرف», and this is the apparent one. It may also be attached to something omitted as a naʿt (adjective) of «غُرْفة»; this is more evident on our view that «غُرفة» means the object than on our view that it is a maṣdar, for on this the apparent sense of the bāʾ is locative, i.e. a scoop that is in his hand.

His words: {إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً}: this is the well-known reading. ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] and Ubayy read «إلا قليلٌ». Its interpretation is that this speech, though affirmative in wording, is negative in meaning, for it is equivalent to: "they did not obey him except a few of them"; for that reason he made it follow what precedes it in case. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This is from their inclining toward the meaning and setting the wording aside, and it is an important chapter of the science of Arabic. Since the meaning of «فَشَرِبُوا منه» is «فلم يُطيعوه» ('they did not obey him'), he construed it on that. Similar is the saying of al-Farazdaq: «لم يَدَعْ من المالِ إلا مُسْحَتاً أو مُجَلَّفُ»" — referring to his words:

1025 - وَعَضُّ زمانٍ يابنَ مروانَ لم يَدَعْ ... من المالِ إلا مُسْحَتاً أو مُجَلَّفُ
(And the bite of a time, O son of Marwān, that has left of wealth nothing but what is wiped out or what is mostly gone.)

For the meaning of «لم يَدَعْ من المالِ إلا مُسْحَتاً» is "nothing of wealth remained except what is wiped out (mushatun)"; for that reason he conjoined «مُجَلَّفُ» to it in the nominative, in consideration of the meaning I mentioned to you. There are two other aspects in the verse, the first of them . . . . [Translator's note: the text breaks off here in the source; the two aspects are not given.]

It is necessary to address this question because of its general usefulness. So I say: when an affirmative exception occurs in their speech, such as «قام القومُ إلا زيداً», the well-known view is that the accusative as an exception is obligatory. Some said: what follows «إلا» may follow what precedes it in case, so you say «مررت بالقومِ إلا زيدٍ» with «زيد» in the genitive. They differed over the nature of this following. Some put it that it is a naʿt of what precedes, saying that one may qualify with «إلا» and what follows it absolutely, whether what it follows is definite or indefinite, a pronoun or an overt noun; this departs from the analogy of the chapter of the naʿt, for what you know from before. Some of them said: only an indefinite noun, or one made definite by the generic al, may be qualified by it, because of the latter's closeness to the indefinite.

Some said: when the grammarians say "naʿt" here, they mean only ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). An example of following with what comes after «إلاَّ» is his words:

1026 - وكلُّ أَخٍ مفارقُه أخوه ... لَعَمْرُ أبيكَ إلا الفرقدانِ
(Every brother will be parted from by his brother — by your father's life — except the two Farqad stars.)

His words: {جَاوَزَهُ هُوَ والذين آمَنُواْ}: «هو» is a detached nominative pronoun giving tawkīd (emphasis) to the pronoun latent (mustatir) in «جاوَزَ».

His words: {والذين} admits two aspects. The more evident is that it is conjoined to the pronoun latent in «جاوَزَ», because the condition is present, namely emphasising what is conjoined to with the detached pronoun. The second is that the wāw is that of the ḥāl. They said: it follows from the ḥāl reading that they crossed with him. This one makes «الذين» a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) «قالوا: لا طاقة», so the meaning becomes: "When he crossed it, the situation being that those who believed said this saying" — and the meaning is not on that.

The hāʾ of «جاوزه» may be assimilated into the hāʾ of «هو», and no account is taken of the separation by the vowel-extension of the hāʾ (ṣilat al-hāʾ), because it is weak — although some considered the assimilation weak, saying: "unless the hāʾ is pronounced hurriedly (tukhtalas)", meaning so that no separator remains. It is the reading of Abū ʿAmr. He also assimilated the wāw of «هو» into the wāw of the conjunction, with a disagreement in what is transmitted from him. The rationale of the assimilation is clear, since two identical letters meet with their conditions. Those who pronounced it distinctly — Ibn Mujāhid and his followers — said: "Because when the wāw is assimilated it becomes quiescent, and when it becomes quiescent it is truly a quiescent wāw preceded by a ḍamma, so it becomes like «آمنوا وكانوا»; just as that is not assimilated, this is not assimilated." This reasoning is corrupt for two reasons. First, it becomes like «آمنوا وكانوا» only after assimilation, so how can that be said? Also, they assimilated {يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ} [al-Baqara: 254], which is analogous to {فِي يَوْمٍ} [Ibrāhīm: 18] and {الذى يُوَسْوِسُ} [al-Nās: 4], by exactly what they reasoned with. [Translator's note: only one reason is explicitly introduced as "first"; the "also" appears to serve as the second.]

The condition of this assimilation in this word according to Abū ʿAmr is that the hāʾ have a ḍamma, as in this verse, and similarly {هُوَ والملائكة} [Āl ʿImrān: 18] and {هُوَ وَجُنُودُهُ} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 39]. If the hāʾ is quiescent, assimilation is impossible, as in {وهو وليُّهم} [al-Anʿām: 127]; yet were the disagreement also to apply to it, that would not be far-fetched, for it has a model in His words {خُذِ العفو وَأْمُرْ} [al-Aʿrāf: 199] — indeed it is more fitting, because the quiescence of this one is incidental, unlike {العفو وَأْمُرْ}.

His words: {لاَ طَاقَةَ لَنَا}: «لنا» is the khabar of «لا», so it is attached to something omitted. It may not be attached to «طاقة», nor may what follows it, namely «اليوم» and «بجالوت», because it would then become "lengthened" (muṭawwal), and the lengthened noun is accusative with nunation, whereas this, as you see, is indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa. Rather «اليوم» and «بجالوت» are attached to the notion of settledness (al-istiqrār) to which «لنا» is attached.

Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted «بجالوت» to be the khabar of «لا», «لنا» then being either for clarification (tabyīn) or attached to something omitted as a naʿt of «طاقة».

Al-ṭāqa is ability; its middle radical is wāw, because it is from al-ṭawq, which is ability. It is a maṣdar with the omission of the augment letters, for it is from «أَطَاق»; analogous to it are: ajāba jābatan, aghāra ghāratan, aṭāʿa ṭāʿatan.

«جالوت» is a foreign noun, a diptote, without derivation. It is not faʿalūt from jāla yajūlu, as preceded regarding Ṭālūt. Like the two of them is Dāwūd.

His words: {كَم مِّن فِئَةٍ}: «كم» is predicative (khabariyya), for its meaning is multiplicity; this is indicated by the reading of Ubayy «وكائن», which is for multiplicity. Its position is the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, «من فئةٍ» is its tamyīz (specification), and «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) in it. Most often its specifier and the specifier of «كائن» come in the genitive with «مِنْ», and for this reason the Revelation came on that. «مِنْ» may be omitted, and then its specifier is genitive by annexation, not by an implied «مِن», according to the correct view. It may also be accusative by analogy with the specifier of interrogative «كم», just as the [specifier of the] interrogative may be genitive by analogy with it, under conditions mentioned in grammar. An example of the specifier of «كائن» coming in the accusative is the poet's saying:

1027 - اطرُدِ اليأسَ بالرجاءِ فكائِنْ ... آلماً حُمَّ يُسْرُهُ بعدَ عُسْرِ
(Drive off despair with hope, for how many a sufferer has had his ease decreed after hardship.)

They also permitted «من فئةٍ» to be in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of «كم», so it is attached to something omitted. «غَلَبَت»: this clause is the khabar of «كم», the implied form being: "many of the small companies are overcoming the large companies."

Concerning «فئة» there are two views. The first is that it is from fāʾa yafīʾu, i.e. returned, its middle radical having been elided, its pattern being filā. The second is that it is from faʾawtu raʾsahu, i.e. I broke it, its final radical having been elided, its pattern being fiʿa like miʾa, except that the final radical of miʾa is a yāʾ and the final radical of this one is a wāw. Its meaning is sound on each of the two derivations, for a group of people return to one another, and they are also a piece of the people, like the broken pieces of the head.

His words: {بِإِذْنِ الله}: there are two aspects. The more evident is that it is a ḥāl, so it is attached to something omitted, the implied form being: "accompanied by Allah's facilitation for them". The second is that the bāʾ is for transitivity, and its genitive noun is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) in meaning; for this reason Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "And if you wish, you may make it a mafʿūl bihi."

His words: {والله مَعَ الصابرين} are a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and admit two aspects. The first is that its position is the accusative as part of what they said. The second is that it has no grammatical position, being a resumptive statement by which Allah the Exalted informs.

semin-durr:233-233.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {والوالدات يُرْضِعْنَ}: this is like His saying {والمطلقات يَتَرَبَّصْنَ}, so let it be consulted. «الوالد» and «الوالدة» are two predominant adjectives (ṣifatān ghālibatān) that run the course of primitive (non-derived) nouns, and for that reason the noun they qualify is not mentioned.
His saying {حَوْلَيْنِ} is accusative (manṣūb) as an adverbial of time (ẓarf al-zamān), and describing them as «كاملين» (complete) removes any loose usage, since «الحولان» (the two years) may be applied to two years that fall short by a month or two. «الحَوْل» is the year, so called because of its turning (taḥawwul); «الحَوْل» is also «الحَيْل» (power), and one says: «لا حولَ ولا قوة» and «لا حَيْلَ ولا قوة».
His saying: {لِمَنْ أَرَادَ}: in this preposition and its genitive noun there are three views. The first: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يُرْضِعْنَ», the lām being causal, and «مَنْ» refers to the fathers, i.e. the mothers suckle for the sake of whoever of the fathers wishes the suckling to be completed; this is parallel to your saying «أَرْضَعَتْ فلانةٌ لفلانٍ ولدَه» (So-and-so suckled So-and-so's child for him). The second: it is explicative (li-l-tabyīn), and so it is attached to something omitted, this lām being like the lām in His saying, Exalted is He: {هَيْتَ لَكَ} [Yūsuf: 23], and in their saying «سُقْياً لك» (may you be watered). The lām makes clear the one for whom the watering is prayed and the one being called with «هَيْتَ»; that is, when He mentioned that the mothers suckle their children for two complete years, He made clear that this ruling is only for whoever wishes to complete the suckling. «مَنْ» may then mean the mothers alone, or them together with the fathers; all of that is possible. The third: this lām is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), so it is attached to something omitted, the implied form being: «ذلك الحكمُ لِمَنْ أرادَ» (that ruling is for whoever wishes). On this view «مَنْ» refers to the mothers and the fathers together.
His saying: {أَن يُتِمَّ الرضاعة}: «أَنْ» and what falls within its scope are in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «أراد», i.e. for whoever wishes its completion. The majority read «يُتمَّ الرَّضاعة» with a ḍamma-marked yāʾ, from «أتَمَّ», with the governing effect of the subjunctive-making «أنْ», with «الرَّضاعة» accusative as a direct object, and with a fatḥa on its rāʾ. Mujāhid, al-Ḥasan, Ibn Muḥayṣin and Abū Rajāʾ read «تَتِمَّ» with a fatḥa on the tāʾ, from «تَمَّ», with «الرضاعة» nominative as the fāʿil (agent). Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read likewise, except that they put a kasra on the rāʾ of «الرضاعة»; this is a dialect form, like «الحَضارة» and «الحِضارة». The Basrans say: fatḥa on the rāʾ with the feminine hāʾ, and kasra without the hāʾ; the Kufans claim the reverse. Mujāhid read — and it is also narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās —: {أَنْ يُتِمُّ الرَّضاعة} with «يُتِمُّ» in the nominative. About this there are two views. The first is the view of the Basrans: that it is the subjunctive-making «أَنْ», left without governing effect by analogy with its sister «ما», since both share the function of forming a maṣdar (verbal noun). They cited for this the saying of the poet:
989 - إني زعيمٌ يا نُوَيْ ... قَةُ إنْ أَمِنْتِ من الرَّزاحِ
أنْ تهبطِين بلادَ قَوْ ... مٍ يَرْتَعُون من الطِّلاحِ
(I guarantee, O little she-camel, if you are safe from exhaustion, that you will descend upon the land of a people who graze on the ṭalḥ trees.)
and the saying of another:
990 - يا صاحبيَّ فَدَتْ نفسي نفوسَكما ... وحيثما كُنتما لُقِّيتما رَشَدا
أَنْ تقرآنِ على أسماءَ ويَحْكُما ... مني السلامَ وألاَّ تُشْعِرا أَحَدا
(O my two companions, may my soul be a ransom for yours, and wherever you are may you meet right guidance: [I ask] that you convey — woe to you both — my greeting to Asmāʾ, and that you let no one know.)
He left it without governing effect, and for that reason the nūn of the nominative remained. They refused to make it the «أنْ» lightened from the heavy «أنّ» for two reasons [Translator's note: the source text repeats "for two reasons, one of the two reasons" here, apparently a copying slip]: the first is that nothing separates it from the verbal clause after it; the second is that what precedes it is not a verb of knowledge and certainty.
The second view, which is the view of the Kufans, is that it is the «أنْ» lightened from the heavy «أنّ», and that its occurrence in the place of the subjunctive-making «أنْ» is anomalous, just as the occurrence of the subjunctive-making «أَنْ» in its place is anomalous in the poet's saying:
991 -. . . . . . . . . . . . قد علموا ... أَنْ لا يُدانِينَا في خَلْقهِ أحدُ
(… they have known that no one approaches us in his nature.)
Mujāhid read «الرَّضْعَة» on the pattern of «القَصْعة». «الرَّضْع» is sucking the breast. A mean person is called «راضع» (a sucker), because he fears that if he milks the ewe the sound of milking will be heard from him and milk will be asked of him, so he sucks the ewe's udder with his mouth.
His saying: {وَعلَى المولود لَهُ}: this preposition and its genitive noun is a fronted khabar, and the mubtadaʾ is His saying «رِزْقُهن». The «أل» in «المولود» is a relative (mawṣūla), and «له» stands in the place of the agent of «المولود» (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent), and it is the referent-pronoun (ʿāʾid) of the relative; its implied form is: «وعلى الذي وُلِدَ له رِزْقُهُنَّ» (and upon the one for whom [the child] was born is their provision). The agent — the mothers — was omitted, as was the object — the children — and this preposition and its genitive noun was put in the place of the agent.
Some people have mentioned that there is no disagreement about putting a preposition and its genitive noun in the place of the agent except from al-Suhaylī, who disallowed it. It is not as this speaker mentioned, and I will set out the schools of the scholars on this question, saying, with Allah's help: the Kufans and the Basrans disagreed on this question. The Basrans allowed it absolutely. As for the Kufans, they said: it must be one of two cases: either the preposition is redundant (zāʾida), in which case it is allowed, as in «ما ضُرب من أحد» (no one at all was struck); or it is not redundant, in which case it is not allowed in their view. And, by agreement among them, the genitive noun may not be in the position of the nominative. Then, after this agreement, they disagreed about what stands in the place of the agent. Al-Farrāʾ held that the preposition alone is in the position of the nominative, just as «يقوم» in «زيد يقوم» is in the position of the nominative. Al-Kisāʾī and Hishām held that the object of the verb is a pronoun latent (mustatir) in it, and it is a vague pronoun in that what is meant by it is what the verb indicates — a maṣdar, a time or a place — without any indicator pointing to one of them. Some of them held that what stands in the place of the agent is the pronoun of the maṣdar, so that when you say «سِيرَ بزيدٍ» (Zayd was made to travel) the implied form is «سير هو», i.e. the travelling, because the verb's indication of its maṣdar is strong; some of the Basrans agree with them on this. These views have proofs, objections and answers that this place cannot bear, so let them be sought in the books of the grammarians.
His saying: {بالمعروف}: it may be attached to each of His saying «رزقُهنَّ» and «كسوتُهنَّ», the question being one of the chapter of al-iʿmāl (competition of two governors for one word), with the second given the governing role, since had the first been given it, a pronoun would have been placed in the second, and it would have been said: «وكسوتهنَّ به بالمعروفِ». This is if «الرزق» and «الكسوة» are meant as the two maṣdars; it has already been stated that «الرزق» can be a maṣdar, even though Ibn al-Ṭarāwa refuted al-Fārisī on that in His saying: {مَا لاَ يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ رِزْقاً مِّنَ السماوات والأرض} [al-Naḥl: 73], as its verification will come in [Sūrat] al-Naḥl. If, however, what is meant by them is the noun for the thing provided and the thing clothed with — like «الطِّحْن» (what is ground) and «الرِّعْي» (what is grazed) — then a muḍāf must be omitted, its implied form being «اتِّصال» (delivery), «دفع» (handing over) or the like, by which the meaning is sound, and «بالمعروف» is attached to something omitted as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of them both.
Abū al-Baqāʾ made the governor of this ḥāl the «استقرار» (being established) implied by «على».
The majority read «كِسْوَتِهِنَّ» with a kasra on the kāf; Ṭalḥa read it with a ḍamma. They are two dialect forms for both the maṣdar and the noun of the thing clothed with. Its verb takes two objects, which are like the two objects of «أعطى» in that both or one of them may be omitted either for brevity (ikhtiṣāran, with an indicator) or by restriction (iqtiṣāran, without one). It has been said that it may take one object, and they cited:
992 - وَأْركَبُ في الروعِ خَيْفانَةً ... كسا وجَهَا سَعَفٌ مُنْتَشِرْ
(And in the fray I ride a swift, slender mare whose face is covered by a spreading forelock.)
They made it imply the meaning of «غَطَّى» (to cover). This is open to consideration, since it is possible that one of the two objects was omitted because something indicates it, i.e. «كسا وجهَها غبارٌ» or the like [Translator's note: i.e. "the spreading forelock clothed her face with dust", or similar].
His saying: {لاَ تُكَلَّفُ نَفْسٌ}: the majority read «تُكَلَّفُ» as passive (built for the object), «نفسٌ» standing in the place of the agent — and the agent is Allah the Exalted — and «وُسْعَها» is a second object; it is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh), because «كَلَّفَ» takes two objects. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Had «الوُسْع» been made nominative here it would not be allowed, because it is not a badal (substitute)."
Abū Rajāʾ read: {لاَ تَكَلَّفُ نفسٌ} with a fatḥa on the tāʾ, the original being «تتكلف»; one of the two tāʾs was omitted for lightness — either the first or the second, according to a disagreement on that which has preceded — so «نفسٌ» is the agent and «وُسْعَها» the direct object, likewise an emptied exception. Abū al-Ashhab also narrated from Abū Rajāʾ: {لا يُكَلِّفُ نفساً}, with the verb attributed to the pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, so «نفساً» and «وُسْعَها» are two objects.
«التكليف» is imposing an obligation. Its root is from «الكَلَف», which is a trace of blackness on the face; the poet said: 993 - يَهْدِي بها أَكْلَفُ الخَدَّيْنِ مُخْتَبِرٌ ... من الجِمالِ كثيرُ اللَّحْمَ عَيْثُومُ
(Leading them is a tested camel with darkened cheeks, among the camels, heavy-fleshed and massive.)
And «فلانٌ كَلِفٌ بكذا» means: he is enamoured of it.
His saying: {لاَ تُضَآرَّ}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «لا تضارُّ» with the rāʾ nominative and doubled. Its justification is clear, since it is an imperfect verb not entered by any subjunctive- or jussive-making particle, so it is nominative. This reading is in harmony with what precedes it, in that it conjoins a clause that is declarative in wording and prohibitive in meaning to a declarative one, and the reading of the rest points to this, as will come. The rest of the Seven read it with a fatḥa on the doubled rāʾ. Its justification is that «لا» is prohibitive and thus jussive-making, so the final rāʾ took sukūn for the jussive, and before it is a sukūn-bearing rāʾ assimilated into it; two sukūns met, so we gave a vowel to the second, not the first, even though the original is assimilation. The vowel was a fatḥa — although the basic rule when two sukūns meet is kasra — because of the alif, since it is the sister of the fatḥa. For that reason, when the Arabs truncated (rakhkhamat, in the vocative) «إسحارّ», which is the name of a plant, they said «إسحارَ» with a light rāʾ bearing a fatḥa: when they deleted the final rāʾ, the first rāʾ remained with sukūn and the alif before it also with sukūn, so two sukūns met; the alif does not accept a vowel, so they gave a vowel to the second, the rāʾ, and the vowel was a fatḥa because of the alif before it. They did not use a kasra, even though it is the basic rule, for the reason I mentioned to you of taking the alif into account.
Al-Ḥasan read it with a kasra on the doubled rāʾ, according to the basic rule for the meeting of two sukūns, not taking the alif into account. Abū Jaʿfar read it with sukūn on the doubled rāʾ, as though he treated continuing speech like pausing and so gave it sukūn. It is also narrated from him and from Ibn Hurmuz with sukūn on a light (undoubled) rāʾ. This allows two explanations. The first: that it is from «ضارَ يَضير», the sukūn being from treating continuing speech like pausing.
The second: that it is from «ضارَّ يُضارُّ» with a doubled rāʾ; he only found it heavy to repeat a letter which is itself a repeated (trilled) letter, so he deleted the second of them and combined two sukūns — I mean the alif and the rāʾ — either by treating continuing speech like pausing, or because the alif stands in the place of a vowel, being a letter of prolongation.
Al-Zamakhsharī claimed "that Abū Jaʿfar only slurred (ikhtalasa) the ḍamma, and the narrator imagined that he gave it sukūn, but it is not so." End of quote. Something on this has preceded at {يَأْمُرُكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 67] and the like.
Further, the reading with sukūn on the rāʾ may be from a nominative, so it would be like the reading of Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr, or from a fatḥa, so it would be like the reading of the rest. The first is preferable, since giving sukūn in place of a ḍamma is more common than in place of a fatḥa, because of the latter's lightness.
Ibn ʿAbbās read it with a kasra on the first rāʾ and without assimilation (fakk). It is narrated from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: «لا تضارَرْ» with a fatḥa on the first rāʾ and without assimilation. This is the dialect of the Ḥijāz — I mean separating [the two] identical letters where the second of them has sukūn for the jussive or for pausing, as in «لم تَمْرُرْ» and «امرُرْ»; the Banū Tamīm assimilate. The Revelation came in both dialects, as in {وَمَن يَرْتَدِدْ مِنْكُمْ عَن دِينِهِ} [al-Māʾida: 54] in al-Māʾida, which was read among the Seven in both ways; its explanation will come clearly.
Further, the reading of whoever doubled the rāʾ — with ḍamma, fatḥa, kasra or sukūn — or made it light may be with the first rāʾ having a fatḥa, so the verb is passive and «والدةٌ» is an object whose agent is not named (i.e. nāʾib fāʿil), the agent having been omitted because it is known; the reading of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, supports this. Or it may have a kasra, so the verb is active and «والدةٌ» is then its agent; the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās supports this.
On this latter possibility there are three views about the object. The first — and it is the apparent one — is that it is omitted, its implied form being: «لا تُضَارِرْ والدةٌ زوجَها بسببِ ولدِها» (let no mother harm her husband because of her child) by [demanding] what he cannot afford of provision, clothing and the like, «ولا يضارِرْ مولودٌ له زوجتَه بسبب ولدِه» (nor the one to whom the child is born harm his wife because of his child) regarding the provision and clothing due to her; so the bāʾ is causal. The second — said by al-Zamakhsharī — is that «تُضارَّ» means «تَضُرُّ» (to harm), and that the bāʾ belongs to its ṣila, i.e. "let no mother harm her child by neglecting its nourishment and care, and let the father not harm it by taking it away from her after it has become attached to her." End of quote. By his saying "the bāʾ belongs to its ṣila" he means that it is attached to it and makes it transitive to the object, as it does in «ذهبت بزيدٍ» (I took Zayd away), «ضارَّ» meaning «أضرَّ» — «فاعَلَ» in the sense of «أَفْعَل» — like «ضاعفْتُ الحِسابَ» and «أَضْعَفْتُه», «باعَدْته» and «أبعدْتُه»; it has already been stated that «فاعَلَ» comes in the sense of «أَفْعَل». On this view, the very noun made genitive by this bāʾ is the direct object in meaning, and the bāʾ is for transitivity, as I mentioned in the comparison with «ذَهَبْتُ بزيدٍ», which means «أَذْهبته».
The third: that the bāʾ is redundant (mazīda), and that «ضارَّ» means «ضَرَّ», so «فاعَلَ» is in the sense of the bare «فعَلَ»; the implied form is: "let no mother harm her child through poor nourishment and lack of care, and let no father harm his child by taking it from its mother after it has become attached to her," and the like. «فاعَل» has come in the sense of bare «فَعَل», as in «واعَدْته» and «وعَدْتُه», «جاوَزْته» and «جُزْته»; however, what is common in «فاعَل» is that it indicates participation between its nominative and its accusative, which is why its nominative is accusative in the underlying sense and its accusative nominative in the underlying sense. Hence the first explanation is weightier than al-Zamakhsharī's explanation and what follows it, and al-Zamakhsharī's explanation is more sound than what follows it.
«له» is in the position of the nominative because it stands in the place of the agent.
His saying: {لاَ تُضَآرَّ وَالِدَةٌ} contains evidence for what the grammarians say: that when a masculine and a feminine come together, one conjoined to the other, the ruling of the verb preceding them follows the first of them. You say «قامَ زيدٌ وهندٌ» (Zayd and Hind stood), adding no feminine marker, and «قامَتْ هندٌ وزيدٌ» (Hind and Zayd stood), adding the marker; the noble verse is of this kind. Nothing is excepted from this except where the feminine is figurative (majāzī), in which case it is good not to take the feminine into account even if it comes first, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {وَجُمِعَ الشمس والقمر} [al-Qiyāma: 9].
It is not hidden how much of the science of rhetoric (ʿilm al-bayān) these clauses contain. Among it is disjunction and conjunction (al-faṣl wa-l-waṣl). As for disjunction — the absence of conjoining — between His saying {لاَ تُكَلَّفُ نَفْسٌ} and His saying «لا تضارَّ»: it is because «لا تُضارَّ» is like an explanation of the clause before it, since if a soul is not charged except with its capacity, no harm occurs, neither to the mother nor to the one to whom the child is born. Likewise He did not conjoin {لاَ تُكَلَّفُ نَفْسٌ} to what precedes it, because it, together with what follows it, is an explanation of His saying «بالمعروف». As for conjunction — the conjoining between His saying «والوالداتُ يُرْضِعْنَ» and His saying «وعلى المولودِ له رزقُهن» — it is because they are two different clauses, each containing a ruling not in the other. Among it is presenting the first clause as mubtadaʾ and khabar and making the khabar a verb, because suckling is something constantly renewed. «الوالدات» was annexed to the children [Translator's note: the source says "the mothers were annexed to the children"; in the verse it is «أولادهن» that is annexed to the mothers' pronoun] to draw attention to their tenderness and to urge them to suckle. «الوالدات» was brought in a general (ʿumūm) wording even though it is a plural of paucity, because a plural of paucity, when adorned with «أل», becomes general; likewise «أولادَهُنَّ» is general because it is annexed to the pronoun of the general term, even though it too is a plural of paucity. Among it is presenting the second clause as mubtadaʾ and khabar, the khabar being a preposition and its genitive noun with the particle «على», which indicates figurative superiority (istiʿlāʾ) in obligation; the khabar was fronted out of concern for it. Provision was put before clothing because it is the more important for the continuation of life and because it recurs every day. The third [clause] was presented as a verb and its nominative, its nominative being made indefinite in the context of negation so as to be general and to include what preceded on account of it, namely the ruling on the mothers regarding suckling and on the one to whom the child is born regarding the provision and clothing obligatory upon him towards the mother. The fourth was presented likewise because it is like a clarification of what precedes it and a detailing after a summary, and for that reason it was not conjoined to it, as I mentioned to you.
Since charging a soul beyond its capacity and one spouse harming the other are among the things that recur and are renewed, He brought these two clauses as verbal clauses and introduced the particle of negation «لا» on them, because it is mostly assigned to the future.
As for the reading of those who made it jussive, it is prohibitive, and it is for the future only. He annexed the child to the mother and to the one to whom the child is born to draw attention to tenderness and to evoke sympathy. He put the mention of the mother's not harming first [Translator's note: the source text has «الوالد» (the father) here, but the verse mentions the mother («والدة») first, and the following clause speaks of beginning with the mothers' ruling], in keeping with the two preceding clauses, since He began with the ruling on the mothers and followed with the ruling on the father. Were it not for fear of tedium, and that this book is not composed for this discipline, I would have mentioned what this noble verse bears of that.
His saying: {وَعَلَى الوارث مِثْلُ ذلك}: this is a clause made of a mubtadaʾ and a khabar; the khabar was fronted for concern — and what it contains is not hidden. It is conjoined to His saying {وَعلَى المولود لَهُ رِزْقُهُنَّ}, and what lies between them is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ), because it is like an explanation of His saying «بالمعروف», as was pointed out earlier.
The alif and lām in «الوارث» are a substitute for the pronoun, according to those who hold that view. They then disagreed about that pronoun: does it refer to the one to whom the child is born, i.e. the father — as though it were said «وعلى وارِثِه», i.e. the heir of the one to whom the child is born — or does it refer to the child itself, i.e. the child's heir? This follows their disagreement about the heir.
Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar read «الوَرَثَة» (the heirs) in the plural form. What is pointed to by His saying «مثلُ ذلك» is what is obligatory of provision and clothing; this is better than the view of whoever says that it points to provision and clothing [themselves], with what is for the singular pointing to two, as in His saying {عَوَانٌ بَيْنَ ذلك} [al-Baqara: 68]. It is only better because it does not require an interpretation. It has been said that what is pointed to is the absence of harming; and it has been said: the standard wage; and other things.
His saying: {عَن تَرَاضٍ}: there are two views about it. The first — and it is the apparent one — is that it is attached to something omitted, since it is a naʿt (adjective) of «فِصالاً», and thus is in the position of the accusative, i.e. «فصالاً كائناً عن تراضٍ» (a weaning arising from mutual consent). Al-Zamakhsharī gave its implied form as «صادراً عن تراضٍ» (issuing from mutual consent); this is open to consideration in that it is a specific (muqayyad) notion of being [Translator's note: the omitted attachment of a prepositional phrase is normally a general verb of being such as «كائن», not a specific one like «صادر»]. The second [Translator's note: the source has «والثني», a slip for «والثاني»]: that it is attached to «أراد», said by Abū al-Baqāʾ; it has no meaning except with strained effort. «عن» is for passing beyond (mujāwaza) figuratively, because mutual consent is an abstract notion, not a concrete thing.
«تراض» is the maṣdar of «تفاعَل», so its middle radical has a ḍamma; its original form on the pattern «تفاعُل» is «تراضُوٌ». The same was done to it as was done to «أَدْلٍ», the plural of «دَلْو»: changing the wāw to yāʾ and the ḍamma to kasra, since in declinable nouns there is no wāw preceded by a ḍamma, other than in the plural [Translator's note: so the source; the rule is usually stated as no word-final wāw preceded by ḍamma], without this being done to it for lightness.
His saying {مِّنْهُمَا} is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of «تَراضٍ», so it is attached to something omitted, i.e. «تراضٍ كائنٍ أو صادرٍ منهما» (mutual consent being, or issuing, from them both). «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya).
His saying: {وَتَشَاوُرٍ}: it [i.e. the adjective «منهما»] was omitted because what precedes it indicates it, the implied form being «وتشاورٍ منهما» (and consultation from them both). It is possible that the consultation is from one of them with someone other than the other, so that the opinions of both and of others agree on what is beneficial.
His saying: {فَلاَ جُنَاحَ}: the fāʾ is [the fāʾ of] the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the like of this clause has preceded. Before this apodosis there must be a clause that has been omitted, so that the meaning is sound thereby; its implied form is «فَفَصَلاه» (and so they weaned him) or «فَعَلا ما تراضيا عليه» (they did what they mutually agreed upon), «فلا جُناحَ عليهما» (then there is no blame on them both) in the weaning or in the separating.
His saying: {أَن تسترضعوا}: «أنْ» and what falls within its scope are in the position of the accusative as the object of «أراد». About «استرضع» the grammarians have two views. The first: it takes two objects, the second of them through a preposition, the implied form being «أَنْ تسترضعوا المراضعَ لأولادِكم» (that you seek wet-nurses for your children); the first object was omitted, as was the preposition from the second. It is parallel to «أمرتُ الخيرَ» (I commanded the good), where you mentioned the thing commanded and did not mention the one commanded, because the second of them is other than the first, and with any two objects that are such, you have the choice between mentioning both, omitting both, and mentioning the first without the second and the reverse. The second: it is transitive to both by itself, but the first object was omitted; this is the opinion of al-Zamakhsharī, who compared the noble verse with your saying «أنجح الحاجة» and «استَنْجَحَتْه الحاجة». This would be a transfer upon a transfer, because the original is «رَضِعَ الولدُ» (the child sucked), then you say «أَرْضَعَت المرأةُ الولدَ» (the woman suckled the child), then you say «استرضَعْتُها الولد» (I sought from her the suckling of the child). Thus said the Shaykh [i.e. Abū Ḥayyān].
This is open to consideration, because his saying «رضِع الولدُ» implies the belief that this is intransitive, which you then made transitive with the hamza of transfer, and then made transitive a second time with the sīn of «استفعال». It is not so, because «رَضِع الولدُ» is transitive; the most that can be said is that its object is not mentioned, its implied form being «رَضِع الولدُ أمَّه» (the child sucked its mother), because the root requires a direct object, like «ضَرَبَ». Also, making transitive by the sīn is a view that is shunned. The sīn is for requesting (ṭalab), in its usual function, as in «استسقيتُ زيداً ماءً» (I asked Zayd for water to drink) and «استطْعَمْته خبزاً» (I asked him for bread to eat); just as «ماءً» and «خبزاً» are accusative not by removal of the preposition, so too «أولادكم». [There has come] «استفعل» for requesting while being made transitive to the second [object] by a preposition, even though the «أَفْعَل» that is its origin takes two objects, as in «أفهمني زيدٌ المسألةَ» (Zayd made me understand the question) and «استفهمتُه عنها» (I asked him to explain it); «عن» may be omitted, but it did not come in the manner of «استَسْقَيْت» and «استطعمت», where the second of the two is accusative not by removal of the preposition.
In this speech there is a shift (iltifāt) and a variation (takwīn): as for the shift, it is a departure from the third-person pronoun in His saying «فإنْ أرادوا» [Translator's note: the verse reads «فَإِنْ أَرَادَا», with a dual pronoun, as the next sentence itself says] to the second person in His saying «وإنْ أردْتُم», since those addressed are the fathers and the mothers [Translator's note: the source has «الباء», a copying slip for «الآباء» (the fathers)]. As for the variation in the pronouns, the first is a dual pronoun and this is a plural pronoun, and what is meant by both is the fathers and the mothers as well. It is as though He referred with this plural pronoun back to the mothers and the one to whom the child is born, but gave predominance to the masculine, i.e. the one to whom the child is born, even though it is singular in wording. «فلا جُناحَ» is the apodosis.
His saying: {إِذَا سَلَّمْتُم مَّآ آتَيْتُم}: «إذا» is conditional, its apodosis omitted because the first condition and its apodosis indicate it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "That meaning is what governs «إذا», and it is attached to what «عليكم» is attached to." This is apparently an error, because he first made what governs it that meaning indicated by the first condition
and its apodosis, so his saying secondly "and it is attached to what «عليكم» is attached to" is a contradiction — unless it be said that an alif may have dropped from the copyist, the original being «أو هو متعلقٌ» (or it is attached), in which case it is sound. However, if that were so, «إذا» would be purely adverbial and not conditional, whereas the words of this author indicate that it is conditional in both views, even on the supposition of excusing him.
The majority read «آتيتم» with the long vowel (madd) here and in al-Rūm: {وَمَآ آتَيْتُمْ مِّن رِّباً} [al-Rūm: 39]; Ibn Kathīr read both short («أتيتم»). It is narrated from ʿĀṣim «أوتيتم» as passive, i.e. what Allah has enabled you to do. As for the reading of the majority, it is clear, because «آتى» means «أعطى» (to give), so it takes two objects: one of them a pronoun referring to the relative «ما», the other a pronoun referring to the wet-nurses, the implied form being «ما آتيتموهنَّ إياه» (what you gave them); «هُنَّ» is the first object, because it is the agent in meaning, and the referent-pronoun is the second, because it is the object in meaning. The discussion of omitting this pronoun while it is detached, with the difficulty it involves and the answer, has preceded at His saying: {وَممَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ} [al-Baqara: 3], so let it be consulted.
As for the reading with the short vowel, its meaning is "you came with" and "you did", as in the saying of Zuhayr:
994 - وما كان مِن خيرٍ أَتَوْه فإنَّما ... توارَثَهُ آباءُ آبائِهم قَبْلُ
(Whatever good they have done, it was only inherited by their fathers' fathers before.)
i.e. they did it. The meaning is: when you hand over what you came with and did. Abū ʿAlī said: "The implied form is «ما أتيتم نَقْدَه أو إعطاءه» (what you came to [regarding] its payment or giving); the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place, it being the referent-pronoun of the relative, so it became «آتيتموه» [Translator's note: so in the source, with madd], i.e. «جئتموه»; then the referent-pronoun of the relative was omitted." Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed the implied form to be «ما جِئْتُم به» (what you came with), which was then omitted — he means omitted gradually: the preposition was omitted first, so the pronoun became attached to a verb in the accusative, and then it was omitted.
About «ما» there are two views. The more apparent of them is that it means «الذي» (that which). Abū ʿAlī allowed it to be a particle-relative (mawṣūla ḥarfiyya, i.e. maṣdar-forming), but he mentioned that with the short-vowel reading in particular, the implied form being «إذا سَلَّمتم الإِتيان» (when you hand over the coming/doing); in that case that omitted pronoun is dispensed with. This is not restricted to the short-vowel reading; rather, it may also be maṣdar-forming with the long vowel, the maṣdar standing in the place of the object, its implied form being «إذا سلَّمتم الإِعطاء», i.e. the thing given. What is apparent regarding «ما» is that what is meant by it is the wage given to the wet-nurse, and on this view the address in His saying «سَلَّمتم» and «آتيتم» is to the fathers specifically. They also allowed that what is meant by it is the children; Qatāda and al-Zuhrī said this. This is open to consideration in that it [«ما»] would then refer to rational beings; on this view the address in «سَلَّمتم» is to the fathers and the mothers.
ʿĀṣim read, in the transmission of Shaybān: «أُوتيتم» as passive, its meaning being: what Allah has given you and enabled you to pay of the wage; it is in the sense of His saying, Exalted is He: {وَأَنفِقُواْ مِمَّا جَعَلَكُم مُّسْتَخْلَفِينَ فِيهِ} [al-Ḥadīd: 7]. His saying: {بالمعروف}: there are three views about it. The first: it is attached to «سَلَّمْتم», i.e. with fair words. The second: it is attached to «آتيتم». The third: it is a ḥāl of the agent of «سَلَّمْتم» or «آتيتم», in which case what governs it is omitted, i.e. «ملتبسين بالمعروفِ» (being engaged in what is fair).

semin-durr:265-265.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَمَثَلُ الذين يُنْفِقُونَ}, up to His saying «كَمَثَلِ حَبة» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse reads {كَمَثَلِ جَنَّةٍ}], is like His saying: {مَّثَلُ الذين يُنْفِقُونَ. . . كَمَثَلِ حَبَّةٍ أَنبَتَتْ سَبْعَ} [al-Baqara: 261] in all the construals, so let it be consulted there. Al-Jaḥdarī read «كمثلِ حبةٍ» with the undotted ḥāʾ and the bāʾ.

His saying: {ابتغآء}: there are two aspects regarding it. The first: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and the conditions for the accusative are met. The second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and «تثبيتاً» is conjoined to it under both considerations, i.e. "for the sake of seeking and of making firm", or "seeking and making firm". Ibn ʿAṭiyya disallowed «ابتغاء» being a mafʿūl li-ajlihi. He said: "Because «تثبيتاً» is conjoined to it, and «تثبيتاً» cannot properly be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, because the spending is not for the sake of making firm." He reported from Makkī that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, and said: "It is rejected by what we have explained."

What he rejected requires detailed treatment. That is, His saying «وتثبيتاً» is either taken as a transitive or an intransitive maṣdar (verbal noun). If it is intransitive, or transitive with the object implied thus: "and making firm, on their own part, the reward for that spending", then the making firm and the obtaining of the reward from Allah would be what moves them to spend, and in that case «تثبيتاً» can properly be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi. But if we imply an object other than that, i.e. "and making firm, on their own part, their deeds through sincerity of intention", or we take «مِنْ أنفسهم» to be the object in meaning, with «مِنْ» in the sense of the lām, i.e. "for themselves", as you say «فَعَلْتُه كسراً مِنْ شهوتي» (I did it to break my desire), then its being a mafʿūl li-ajlihi is not clear.

Abū al-Baqāʾ implied the omitted object as "their deeds through sincerity of intention", and he also allowed «مِنْ أنفسهم» to be an object, with «مِنْ» in the sense of the lām. He had first stated that both of them may be mafʿūl li-ajlihi or ḥāl, and this is not clear, as stated above.

In summary, there are two views on «من أنفسهم». The first: it is an object by a figurative use of the particle. The second: it is a naʿt (adjective) of «تثبيتاً», so it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted element. In summary also: «التثبيت» may be transitive — and how its object is to be implied [has been shown] — or it may be intransitive.

If it is said: «تثبيت» is the maṣdar of «ثَبَّت», and «ثَبَّتَ» is transitive, so how can its maṣdar be intransitive? The answer is that «التثبيت» [here stands for] the maṣdar of «تَثَبَّتَ»: it occurs in place of «التثبُّت», and maṣdars substitute for one another. He, Exalted is He, said: {وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلاً} [al-Muzzammil: 8], and the original is «تبتُّلاً». This is supported by the reading of whoever read «وَتَثَبُّتاً». Abū al-Baqāʾ inclined to this. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This view has been rejected on the grounds that this happens only when the verb preceding the maṣdar is stated explicitly, as in the verse; but when the maṣdar is brought without standing in for a mentioned verb, it is not construed as belonging to a verb other than the one that is originally its own." Then he said: "What we say is this: «ثَبَتَ» — meaning with a single (unstressed) bāʾ — is an intransitive verb meaning to be established and to be firmly rooted, and «ثَبَّت» is made transitive by doubling and means to establish and to make real. Ibn Rawāḥa said:
1067 - فَثَبَّتَ اللهُ ما أتاك مِنْ حَسَنٍ ... تثبيتَ عيسى ونصراً كالذي نُصِروا
(May Allah make firm the good that has come to you, as He made ʿĪsā firm, and grant you victory like that which they were granted.)
So if the making firm is attributed to them, «مِنْ» is in the position of the accusative, attached to the maṣdar itself, and is partitive, like it is in «هَزَّ من عِطْفِهِ» (he stirred some of his side) and «حَرَّك مِنْ نشاطِه» (he aroused some of his energy). And if it is attributed in meaning to their souls, «مِنْ» is also in the position of the accusative, as a naʿt of «تثبيتاً»."

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the meaning of the partitive sense? I say: its meaning is that whoever expends his wealth for the sake of Allah has made firm part of his soul, and whoever expends his life and his wealth together has made firm the whole of his soul." The Shaykh said: "What is apparent is that it is his soul that makes him firm and moves him to spend in the way of Allah; he has no mover other than it, because of the faith and the reward it believes in." He means: so it is preponderant that the making firm is attributed in meaning to their souls.

His saying: {بِرَبْوَةٍ} is in the position of the genitive, because it is a naʿt of «جنة». The bāʾ is locative, in the sense of «في», i.e. "a garden that is on a height". «الربوة» is elevated, good land; al-Khalīl said this. It is derived from «رَبَا يَرْبُو», i.e. to rise. Al-Suddī's interpretation of it as low-lying land is worth nothing. One says «رَبْوة» and «رَباوة», with the three vowels on the rāʾ in both; one also says «رابية». The poet said:
1068 - وغيثٍ من الوَسْمِيّ حُوٍّ تِلاعُه ... أَجابَتْ روابيه النَّجاءَ هَواطِلُهُ
(Many a rain of the early autumn season, whose watercourses are dark green, whose heights answered the clouds with their downpours.)
Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim read «رَبْوة» with fatḥa, and the rest with ḍamma. Al-Akhfash said: "We choose the ḍamma, because in the plural scarcely anything is heard but «الرُّبا»." He means that this indicates the singular has ḍamma on its first radical, like «بُرْمَة» and «بُرَم», «صورة» and «صُوَر». Ibn ʿAbbās read «رِبْوَة» with kasra; al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī read «رَياوة», like «رسالة» [Translator's note: so in the source, with yāʾ]; and Abū Jaʿfar read «رَبَاوة», like «كراهة». It has already been stated that these are dialectal usages.

His saying: {أَصَابَهَا وَابِلٌ}: there are four aspects regarding this clause. The first: it is a second naʿt of «جنة». The description here began with the preposition and its genitive noun and then the clause, because that is more frequent in their speech, being closer to a single word; and it began with the established, fixed description, which is its being on a height, and then the accidental one, which is the downpour striking it. In the description of the smooth rock, He described it by His saying {عَلَيْهِ تُرَابٌ} and then conjoined to the description «فأصابه وابلٌ», whereas here He did not conjoin but brought it out as a description.

The second: it is a naʿt of «ربوة». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Because the garden is part of the height", as though he means that describing the height as being struck entails describing the garden by it. The third: it is a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in the preposition phrase, because it occurs as a naʿt. The fourth: it is a ḥāl from «جنة»; this is permissible because the indefinite noun has been particularised by the description, and in that case «قد» must be implied, i.e. "and a downpour had struck it".

His saying: {فَآتَتْ أُكُلَهَا}: there are three aspects regarding it. The first, and it is the soundest: «آتَتْ» takes two objects, the first of which has been omitted, namely "its owner" or "its people". What makes its omission good is that the intent is to report what it yields, not for whom it yields; and because it is implied in His saying «كمثل جنةٍ», i.e. "the planter of a garden" or "the owner of a garden", as stated earlier. «أُكُلَها» is the second object, and «ضِعْفَيْن» is accusative as a ḥāl from «أُكُلَها». The second: «ضِعْفِين» is the second object; this is an oversight and a mistake by whoever said it. The third: «آتَتْ» here means "brought forth", so it takes a single object. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Because the meaning of «آتَتْ» is «أَخْرَجَتْ», and it is from «الإِتاء», which is yield." The Shaykh said: "We do not know this in the language of the Arabs." Attributing the giving to it [the garden] is figurative.

Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «أُكْلها» with ḍamma on the hamza and sukūn on the kāf, and likewise everything of this word annexed to a feminine; except that Abū ʿAmr gives the heavy form to what is annexed to something other than a pronoun or to a masculine pronoun. The rest read with the heavy form everywhere. The clarification of all this will come later. «الأُكُل» with ḍamma is the thing eaten, and with fatḥa it is a maṣdar. It is annexed to the garden because the garden is its place or its cause.

His saying: {فَطَلٌّ}: the fāʾ is that of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and there must be an omission after it to complete the apodosis clause. There is disagreement on this, with three aspects. Al-Mubarrad held that what is omitted is a khabar (predicate), and His saying «فَطَلٌّ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the implied form being "then a drizzle strikes it". Beginning with an indefinite is permitted here because it is in the apodosis of a condition, which is one of the things that permit beginning with an indefinite; among their sayings is: «إنْ ذَهَبَ غَيْرُ فَعَيْرٌ في الرِّباط» (if one donkey has gone, there is another donkey at the tether) [Translator's note: so in the source, «غَيْرُ»; the proverb is usually quoted as «إن ذهب عَيْرٌ فعَيْرٌ في الرباط»]. The second: it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "then what strikes it is a drizzle". The third: it is a fāʿil (agent) of an implied verb, its implied form being "then a drizzle strikes it"; this is the clearest of them.

However, the Shaykh said, after mentioning the three aspects: "The last requires the omission of the clause that is the apodosis while retaining a governed element of part of it, because whenever the fāʾ enters an imperfect verb, it is only on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ, as in His saying: {وَمَنْ عَادَ فَيَنْتَقِمُ الله مِنْهُ} [al-Māʾida: 95], i.e. 'then He takes vengeance'. For that reason this implied form is needed here, i.e. 'then it — the garden — a drizzle strikes it'. In the two previous construals, only one of the two parts of the clause needs to be omitted." What he said is open to consideration, because we do not grant that the imperfect verb after the fāʾ of the apodosis needs an implied mubtadaʾ.

Analogous to the verse is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
1069 - ألا إنْ لا تَكُنْ إبِلٌ فمِعْزَى ... كأنَّ قُرونَ جِلَّتِها العِصِيُّ
(If there are no camels, then goats, as though the horns of their big ones were staffs.)
In his saying «فَمِعْزى» there are the same three construals.

Some claimed that this verse contains a fronting and postponing, the original being: "a downpour struck it — and if no downpour strikes it, then a drizzle — and so it brought forth its produce twofold", so that its bringing forth its produce twofold is made to apply to both conditions, the downpour and the drizzle. There is no need for this, since the meaning is sound without it, and the default is the absence of fronting and postponing, to the point that some restrict it to poetic necessity.

«الطَّلّ» is the finest of rain. Mujāhid said: "It is dew"; this is a loose usage on his part. One says «طَلَّه الندى» and also «أَطَلَّه». The poet said:
1070 - ولَمَّا نَزَلْنَا منزلاً طَلَّه الندى ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And when we alighted at a halting place that the dew had moistened …)
«طَلّ» is pluralised as «طِلال».

His saying: {والله بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ}: the reading of the majority is «تَعْلَمون» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse reads «تَعْمَلُونَ»] in the second person, and it is clear: it is an iltifāt (shift) from the third person to address, which urges the act of spending purely for the sake of Allah and deters from showing off and seeking reputation. Al-Zuhrī read it with yāʾ, in the third person, and it admits two aspects. The first: it refers back to those who spend. The second: it is general and not specific to those who spend, but refers to all people, so that those who spend are included among them with priority.

semin-durr:286-286.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لاَ يُكَلِّفُ الله نَفْساً إِلاَّ وُسْعَهَا}: «وُسْعَها» is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«يُكَلِّفُ» is transitive to two objects, one of which is omitted, its implied form being «عبادةً» 'a worship' or «شيئاً» 'something'." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "If he means that its underlying form is thus, that is correct, because His saying «إلاَّ وُسْعَها» is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh) from the second object. But if he means that it is omitted in terms of technical grammar, that is not so; rather, the second [object] is «وُسْعَها», as in «وما أعطَيْتُ زيداً إلا درهماً» 'I gave Zayd nothing but a dirham' and «ما ضربْتُ إلا زيداً» 'I struck no one but Zayd': this, in technical grammar, is the object, even though its underlying form is «ما أعطيت زيداً شيئاً إلاّ درهماً» 'I did not give Zayd anything except a dirham'." «الوُسْع» is what accommodates a person, does not constrain him, and does not go beyond him.

Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «إلا وَسِعَها», making it a past verb. They have explained this reading as the verb in it being the ṣila (relative clause) of an omitted relative noun, its implied form being «إلاَّ ما وَسِعَها» "except what is within its capacity"; this relative noun is the second object, just as «وُسْعَها» is in the reading of the majority. This [omission of the relative noun] is not permitted by the Basrans, but [it is] by the Kufans; moreover, implying such a relative noun is very weak, since there is nothing indicating it. This is unlike the saying of the other [poet]:

1148 - ما الذي دَأْبُه احتياطٌ وحَزْمٌ ... وهواهُ أَطاعَ يَسْتَوِيان
(The one whose habit is caution and resolve, and [the one who] obeys his desire, are not equal.)

and the saying of Ḥassān as well:

1149 - أَمَنْ يَهْجُو رسولَ الله منكم ... ويَمْدَحُه ويَنْصُرُه سَواءٌ
(Is the one of you who lampoons the Messenger of Allah, and [the one who] praises him and supports him, equal?)

The verification of this has preceded. Does this clause have a grammatical position or not? What is apparent is the second, because it was introduced to give information about that. It has been said: rather, its position is the accusative, conjoined to «سَمِعْنا» and «أَطَعْنَا», i.e. "and they also said: Allah does not burden a soul". This reading has been explained in another way: that you make the second object omitted because the meaning is understood, and make this verbal clause in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of this object, the implied form being: «لا يُكَلِّفُ اللهُ نفساً شيئاً إلاَّ وَسِعَها» "Allah does not burden a soul with anything except what it can bear". Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "In the reading of Ibn Abī ʿAbla there is a liberty of expression (tajawwuz), because it is inverted (maqlūb); the proper form of the wording would have been «إلا وَسِعَتْه» 'except that it encompasses it', as He said: {وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السماوات والأرض} [al-Baqara: 255], {وَسِعَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِلْماً} [Ṭāhā: 98]; but this comes under the category of «أَدْخَلْتُ القَلَنْسُوَةَ في رأسي» 'I put the cap into my head'."

His saying: {لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ}: this clause has no grammatical position because it is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), and it is like an explanation of what precedes it, because its not being held to account for what another earned, and its bearing only what it itself acquired, are part of its not being burdened with what is beyond its capacity. Does a [difference of] meaning appear between the two different forms of the verb of earning, or not? Some said: Yes, and distinguished them by [saying] that «الكسب» is more general, since one says «كَسَب» "he earned" for himself and for others, while «اكتسب» is more specific, since one does not say «اكتسب لغيرِه» "he earned for another". He recited the saying of al-Ḥuṭayʾa:

1150 - أَلْقَيْتَ كاسِبَهم في قَعْرِ مُظْلِمَةٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(You have cast their breadwinner into the depth of a dark [pit]…)

And one says: «هو كاسبُ أهلهِ» "he is his family's earner", but not «مكتسبُ أهلِه».

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: Why did He assign good to «الكَسْب» and evil to «الاكتساب»? I say: In «الاكتساب» there is exertion (iʿtimāl). Since evil is among what the soul craves, and it is drawn to it and commands it, it is more exertive and more earnest in obtaining it, so for that reason it was made «مكتسبة» in it. And since it is not so in the matter of good, it was described with what carries no indication of exertion."

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "He repeated the verb of earning and varied its morphological form, for the beauty of the style of the discourse, as the Exalted said: {فَمَهِّلِ الكافرين أَمْهِلْهُمْ} [al-Ṭāriq: 17]. This is one view. What appears to me in this is that good deeds are among what is earned without strain, since the one who earns them is on the highway of Allah's command and the path of His law; whereas bad deeds are «تكتسب», with the form of intensification, since the one who earns them strains himself in their matter to tear through the veil of Allah the Exalted's prohibition and to go beyond [it] to them. So the coming of the two forms in the verse is fitting, in order to secure this meaning." Some said: "There is no difference; the Quran has used «الكسب» and «الاكتساب» in a single context. The Exalted said: {كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ رَهِينَةٌ} [al-Muddaththir: 38], and the Exalted said: {وَلاَ تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ إِلاَّ عَلَيْهَا} [al-Anʿām: 164], and the Exalted said: {بِغَيْرِ مَا اكتسبوا} [al-Aḥzāb: 58]; so He used both «الكَسْب» and «الاكتساب» for evil."

Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Some people said: There is no difference between them" — and he mentioned something like what has preceded. "Others said: The form iftaʿala indicates intensity of effort, and doing an evil deed is grave because of what it leads to." Al-Wāḥidī said: "What is correct according to the lexicographers is that «الكسب» and «الاكتساب» are one, with no difference between them. Dhū al-Rumma said:

1151 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ألفَى أباه بذاك الكسبِ يَكْتَسِبُ
(… he found his father earning by that [same] earning.)"

I say: He brought the lām with «الكسب» and «على» with «الاكتساب» only because the lām entails possession, and good is loved and rejoiced in, so with it was brought what entails possession; and since evil is something to be wary of, and it is a weight and a burden on the one who bears it, with it was brought «على», which entails its being upon him.

Someone said: "In it there is an intimation that the least act among acts of good is credited to a person as a generosity from Allah toward His servant, so that what his son does for him without his knowledge reaches him, because it is of his earning in general; unlike punishment, for no one is held to account for it except one who strove and exerted himself in it." This is built on the view that there is a difference between the two forms, and it is the more evident [view].

[Translator's note: the source prints «ابنُ من غيرِ علمِه» and «فإنه فا يُؤَاخَذُ»; «ابنُه» "his son" and «لا يُؤاخَذ» "is not held to account" are evidently intended and are translated as such.]

His saying: {لاَ تُؤَاخِذْنَا} is read with the hamza, and it is from «الأخْذ بالذَّنْب» "taking to task for a sin". It is [also] read with the wāw, and this admits two possibilities. The first: that it is also from «الأخْذ», the hamza having been changed into a wāw because it carries fatḥa and what precedes it carries ḍamma, which is a regular lightening (takhfīf qiyāsī). And it may be from «واخذه» with the wāw; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. He used here the form of mutuality (mufāʿala) although it is the act of one party, because the wrongdoer has given [others] power over himself and opened the way to himself by his act; so it is as if he helped the one who punishes him for his sin and holds him to it against himself, and thus the form of mutuality was fitting. It may also be of the category of «سافرت» "I travelled", «عاقبت» "I punished" and «طارقت» "I doubled [the sandal]".

Ubayy read: «ربَّنا ولا تُحَمِّلْ علينا إصْراً» with the mīm doubled.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: What difference is there between this doubled [form] and the one in «ولا تُحَمِّلْنا»? I say: This one is for intensification in «حَمَّل عليه», and that one is for transferring «حَمَلَه» from one object to two objects." End of quotation. He means that the doubling in the first is for intensification, and for that reason it is transitive to only one object; and in the second it is for transitivization, and for that reason it is transitive to two, the first of which is «نا» and the second {مَا لاَ طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ}.

[Translator's note: the source prints «أولُهما «ن»»; the pronoun «نا» "us" is evidently intended.]

«الإِصْر» is in origin weight and hardship. Al-Nābigha said:

1152 - يا مانعَ الضَّيْمِ أَنْ يَغْشَى سَرَاتَهُمُ ... والحاملَ الإِصرِ عنهم بعد ما عَرِقُوا
(O you who prevent injustice from overtaking their nobles, and who carry the burden off them after they have sweated.)

It has been applied to the covenant and the pledge because of their weight, as in His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَخَذْتُمْ على ذلكم إِصْرِي} [Āl ʿImrān: 81], i.e. "My covenant"; {وَيَضَعُ عَنْهُمْ إِصْرَهُمْ} [al-Aʿrāf: 157], i.e. the onerous obligations. Then it is applied to everything that is heavy, so that it is related from one of them that he explained «الإِصر» here as the gloating of enemies, and he recited:

1153 - أَشْمَتَّ بيَ الأعداءَ حينَ هَجَرْتَني ... والموتُ دونَ شماتةِ الأَعْدَاءِ
(You made the enemies gloat over me when you abandoned me — and death is easier than the gloating of enemies.)

It is also said that «الإِصْر» is affection and kinship; one says «ما يَأْصِرُني عليه آصِرَةٌ», i.e. "no kinship or womb-tie inclines me toward him". He recited for al-Ḥuṭayʾa:

1154 - عَطَفُوا عليَّ بغير آ ... صِرَةٍ فقد عَظُمَ الأواصِرْ
(They inclined toward me without any tie of kinship — so great are the ties [of their kindness].)

It has been said: «الإِصر» is the thing by which things are tied, and from it is «الإِصار» for the rope with which loads are bound. One says «أَصَرَ يأصِرُ أَصْراً» with fatḥa on the hamza; with kasra it is a noun. It is also said with ḍamma, and it has been read so as an anomalous reading (shādhdh).

Ubayy read: {وَلاَ تُحَمِّل عَلَيْنَآ} with doubling, as an intensification of the act.

«الطاقَة» is the ability to do a thing. It is in origin a maṣdar that came with the omission of the augment letters; by right it should have been «إطاقة», since it is from «أَطَاق», but it is anomalous, as a few small words are anomalous, such as «أَغار غارةً» and «أَجابَ جابةً»; they said «ساء سمعاً فساءَ جابة» "He heard badly, so he answered badly". It is not analogically extended, so one does not say «طال طالة». A parallel of «أجابَ جابةً» is {أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ الأرض نَبَاتاً} [Nūḥ: 17], and «أعطى عَطاءً» in his saying:

1155 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وبعدَ عطائِك المئةَ الرِّتاعا
(… and after your giving the hundred grazing [camels].)

His saying, the Exalted: {مَوْلاَنَا}: «المَوْلَى» is the mafʿal form from «وَلِي يَلِي». Here it is a maṣdar by which the agent is meant; so it may be on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the One in charge of our protection", i.e. our support — and for that reason He said «فانصُرْنا». «المَوْلَى» may also be a noun of place and a noun of time.

His saying, the Exalted: {فانصرنا}: He brought the fāʾ here to signal causation, because since Allah the Exalted is their Patron, the Owner of their affairs and their Disposer, it followed from that that they called upon Him to give them victory over their enemies; as when you say: «أنت الجوادُ فتكرَّمْ عليَّ وأنت البطلُ فاحْمِ حَرَمَك» "You are the generous one, so be generous to me; and you are the hero, so protect your sanctuary."

This sūra has comprised many kinds of knowledge, most of which have been pointed out; and the intelligent person is spared the need for explicit statement by an allusion.

semin-durr:234-234.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {والذين يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنكُمْ} — the verse: there are several views about it. The first: «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) that has no khabar (predicate); rather, the predication was made about the wives, mention of whom is connected to it, because the discourse concerns them in observing the waiting period; so the khabar came about what is intended, since the meaning is: whoever's husband has died away from her, she waits. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ held this, and al-Farrāʾ cited:
995 - لعَلِّيَ إنْ مَالَتْ بِيَ الريحُ مَيْلَةً ... على ابن أبي ذِبَّانَ أَنْ يتندَّما
(Perhaps I — if the wind sways me once against Ibn Abī Dhibbān — [perhaps] he will come to regret.)
He said «لعلي» (perhaps I), then said «أن يتندم» (that he will regret), making the predication about Ibn Abī Dhibbān and leaving the speaker aside, since the implied form is: perhaps Ibn Abī Dhibbān will regret if the wind sways me once. Another said:
996 - بني أسدٍ إنَّ ابن قَيسٍ وقَتْلَه ... بغيرِ دَمٍ دارُ المَذَلَّةِ حُلَّتِ
(O Banū Asad, Ibn Qays and his killing without blood-guilt — the abode of humiliation has been settled.)
He made the predication about his killing, that it is an abode of humiliation, and left aside predicating about Ibn Qays.
The precise statement of the school of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ is that when a noun is mentioned, and a noun annexed to it is mentioned which carries the sense of the predication, the first is left aside and the predication is made about the second, as in «إنَّ زيداً وأخته منطلقةٌ» (Zayd and his sister — she is departing), the meaning being: Zayd's sister is departing. But the noble verse and the first verse of poetry are not of this type; what he cited by way of likening it to this type is the poet's saying:
997 - فَمَنْ يكُ سائِلاً عني فإني ... وجِرْوَةَ لا تَرُودُ ولا تُعارُ
(Whoever asks about me — I and Jirwa [my mare]: she does not roam and is not lent out.)
The precise statement of this school, its refutation and the interpretation of its proofs belong to a book other than this one.
The second: it has a khabar, namely «يتربَّصْن», and some omission is necessary to make it sound for this clause to be the khabar of the first, since it lacks a linking element (rābiṭ). The implied form is: «وأزواجُ الذين يُتَوفَّوْن يتربَّصْنَ» (and the wives of those who die wait). His saying «ويَذَرون أزواجاً» indicates this omitted element, so the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) put in its place on account of that indication. The third: the khabar is also «يتربَّصْن», but the referent-pronoun (ʿāʾid) was omitted from the speech because something indicates it; the implied form is: «يتربصن بعدهم» (they wait after them) or «بعد موتِهم» (after their death); al-Akhfash said this. The fourth: «يتربَّصْنَ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the implied form being «أزواجُهم يتربَّصْنَ» (their wives wait), and this clause is the khabar of the first; al-Mubarrad said this. The fifth: the khabar is omitted in its entirety before the mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: «فيما يُتْلى عليكم حكمُ الذين يُتَوَفَّوْن» (among what is recited to you is the ruling on those who die), and His saying «يتربَّصْنَ» is a clause clarifying and explaining the ruling, so it has no position in i'rab; this is attributed to Sībawayh. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Al-Mahdawī related from Sībawayh that the meaning is: «وفيما يُتْلَى عليكم الذين يُتَوَفَّون» (and among what is recited to you: those who die). I do not recognise this that he related, because that is only tenable when there is an imperative wording after the mubtadaʾ, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا} [al-Māʾida: 38], {الزانية والزاني فاجلدوا} [al-Nūr: 2]. This verse has the meaning of a command but not its wording, so with this implied form it needs another implied form, which is dispensed with when the imperative wording is present." The sixth: part of the clause stands in the place of something annexed to the referent-pronoun of the mubtadaʾ, the implied form being: «والذين يُتَوفَّون منكم ويذرون أزواجاً يتربصُ أزواجُهم» (and those of you who die and leave wives — their wives wait); «أزواجهُم» was omitted in its entirety, and the nūn, which is the pronoun of the wives, stood in their place with the qualification of their being annexed to the pronoun of the mubtadaʾ.
The reading of the majority is «يُتَوَفَّوْنَ», built for what has not had its agent named (i.e. passive). The Commander of the Faithful [Translator's note: i.e. ʿAlī; the source has «مير المؤمنين», with the initial alif dropped] read it — and al-Mufaḍḍal narrated it from ʿĀṣim — with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, built for the agent (active); its meaning is "they complete (yastawfūn) their terms"; Abū al-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī said this.
What is related — that Abū al-Aswad was behind a funeral bier and a man said to him: "Who is the «متوفِّي»?" with a kasra on the fāʾ [i.e. "the one who takes the soul"], and he said: "Allah"; and that this was one of the causes that moved ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, to order him to compose a book on grammar — [this] is contradicted by this reading.
Possibilities have already been discussed regarding His saying «يَتَرَبَّصْنَ بأنفسِهن ثلاثةَ قُروء»: whether «بأنفسهن» is tawkīd (emphasis) or not, and whether the accusative of «قروء» is as an adverbial or as an object; they apply here.
His saying: {مِنكُمْ} is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the nominative of «يَتَوَفَّوْن», and what governs it is omitted, its implied form being: «حالَ كونِهم منكم» (while they are from among you). «مِنْ» may be partitive or for clarifying the genus.
His saying: {وَعَشْراً}: He only said «عشراً» without the feminine marker in the number for one of several reasons. The first: what is meant is «عَشْر ليال» (ten nights) together with their days; nights were preferred over days in reckoning dates because they come first. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It has been said «عَشْراً» with reference to the nights, the days being included in them. You never see them use the masculine [number form] with reference to days; you say «صُمْت عشراً» (I fasted ten), and if you used the masculine form you would depart from their speech. Among what is clear is His saying, Exalted is He: {إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلاَّ عَشْراً} [Ṭā Hā: 103], {إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلاَّ يَوْماً} [Ṭā Hā: 104]."
The second — and it is the view of al-Mubarrad —: the tāʾ was omitted because the implied form is «عشرُ مُدَدٍ» (ten periods), each period of them being a day and a night. The Arabs say «سِرْنا خمساً» (we travelled five), i.e. between day and night. The poet said:
998 - فطافَتْ ثلاثاً بين يومٍ وليلةٍ ... وكان النكيرُ أَنْ تُضِيفَ وتَجْأرا
(She circled three [periods] between day and night, and her only protest was to take fright and low aloud.)
The third: the counted noun is masculine, namely the days, and the tāʾ was omitted only because when a masculine counted noun is mentioned, the tāʾ must be attached to its number, but when it is omitted in wording, both options are allowed in the number: mentioning the tāʾ and not. Al-Kisāʾī related: «صُمْنَا من الشهرِ خمساً» (we fasted five of the month), and among it is the ḥadīth: «وأتبعَه بستٍّ من شوال» (and follows it with six of Shawwāl). Another said:
999 - وإلاَّ فسيري مثلَ ما سار راكبٌ ... تيمَّمَ خَمْساً ليس في سيره أَمَمْ
(Otherwise, travel as a rider travels who has set out on a five-day journey, with no shortness in his travelling.)
The grammarians stated this explicitly. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "So there is no need to interpret it as nights or as periods, as al-Zamakhsharī and al-Mubarrad respectively gave its implied form." He said: "When this is established, His saying «وعشراً» came according to one of the two permissible forms. The omission of the tāʾ is good here only because it is the end of a section of speech, so it resembles the verse-endings (fawāṣil), just as its being a verse-ending made His saying {إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلاَّ عَشْراً} [Ṭā Hā: 103] good. So his saying 'if you used the masculine form you would depart from their speech' is not as he mentioned; rather, it is the most eloquent. The point of his mentioning «إن لبثتم إلاَّ يوماً» after His saying «إلا عَشْراً» is that, according to his claim, He meant the nights, the days being included with them, and His saying «إلا يوماً» is evidence that the days are meant." The Shaykh said: "This, in our view, indicates that what is meant by the ten is days, because they disagreed about the length of the stay: some of them said 'ten' and some of them said 'a day'; this indicates that what is contrasted with 'a day' is only days, since it would not be good in a contrast for some of them to say 'ten nights' and the others to say 'a day'."
His saying: {بالمعروف}: there are four views about it. The first: it is a ḥāl of the agent of «فَعَلْنَ», i.e. they did [it] being engaged in and accompanied by what is fair. The second: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. the bāʾ is the bāʾ of transitivity. The third: it is the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. «فَعَلْنَ فِعْلاً بالمعروف» (they did a doing [that is] with what is fair), i.e. being so. The school of Sībawayh applies to it: that it is a ḥāl of the definite pronoun of the maṣdar, i.e. «فَعَلْنَه» — i.e. the doing — being engaged in what is fair; this is the fourth view.
«بما تعملون» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «خبيرٌ», and was fronted for the sake of the verse-ending. «ما» may be maṣdar-forming, or mean «الذي» (that which), or be an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, which is weak. On these latter two views there must be an omitted referent-pronoun; on the first it is not needed, except according to a weak opinion.

semin-durr:250-250.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {بَرَزُواْ لِجَالُوتَ}: concerning this lām there are two aspects. The first is that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «برزوا». The second is that it is attached to something omitted, it and its genitive noun being a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «بَرَزوا». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may be a ḥāl, i.e. they went out heading for Jālūt." The meaning of «برزوا» is: they went out to an open stretch (barāz) of land, which is the part of it that is exposed and level; from it is al-mubāraza (single combat) in war, because each opponent comes out into the open to his counterpart. In their calling out with their words «رَبَّنا» ("our Lord") there is an acknowledgement on their part of servitude and a request for their rectification, because the word «الرب» conveys that, unlike other words. They used the word «على» in their saying «أَفْرِغ علينا» ("pour upon us"), requesting that patience be set over them and enveloping them, like a container.

semin-durr:251-251.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَالهَزْمُ}: [Translator's note: so quoted in the source; the verse reads فَهَزَمُوهُم, and the author is discussing the root هزم.] Its original meaning is breaking; from it is «سِقاء مُتَهَزِّم» ("a cracked waterskin") and «قَصَبٌ متهزِّمٌ» ("cracked reeds"), i.e. broken. His words: «بإذنِ الله»: there are in it the two aspects mentioned before, I mean its being a ḥāl (circumstantial) or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). In «مِمَّا يشاء», the fāʿil (agent) of «يشاء» is the pronoun of Allah the Exalted; it is also said: the pronoun of Dāwūd; the first is more evident.

His words: {وَلَوْلاَ دَفْعُ}: Nāfiʿ read here and in [Sūrat] al-Ḥajj «دِفاع», and the rest «دَفْع». As for «دَفْع», it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of the triliteral dafaʿa yadfaʿu. As for «دفاع», it admits two aspects: that it is likewise a maṣdar of the triliteral dafaʿa, like kataba kitāban, or that it is the maṣdar of «دافع», like qātala qitālan. Abū Dhuʾayb said:

1028 - ولقد حَرَصْتُ بأَنْ أدافعَ عنهُم ... فإذا المَنِيَّةُ أَقْبَلَتْ لا تُدْفَعُ
(I strove eagerly to ward [death] off from them, but when fate approaches it is not warded off.)

«فاعَل» here has the meaning of the bare faʿala, so the two readings coincide in meaning.

Whoever read «دفاع» and read in al-Ḥajj {يُدَافِعُ عَنِ الذين آمنوا} [verse 38] — namely Nāfiʿ — or read «دَفْع» and read «يَدْفَع» — namely Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr — has kept to his principle, bringing the maṣdar in agreement with the verb.
