His saying: {ولكن أَكْثَرَ الناس}: this is a rectification (istidrāk) of what is implied by His saying {إِنَّ الله لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى الناس}, because its implied form is: so they ought to give thanks for His favour upon them in bringing [them] into existence and providing, but most of them are not thankful.

semin-durr:244-244.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {وَقَاتِلُواْ}: about this clause there are several views. The first: it is conjoined to His saying «موتوا» (die), and it is a command to those whom Allah brought to life after causing them to die, to wage jihad, i.e. He said to them: die, and fight; this is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk. Al-Ṭabarī said: "There is no sound basis for this view." The second: it is conjoined to His saying {حَافِظُواْ عَلَى الصلوات}, and what lies between them is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ). The third: it is conjoined to something omitted, its implied form being «فَأَطِيعُوا وقاتِلوا» (so obey and fight), or «فلا تَحْذَروا الموتَ كما حَذِرَهُ الذين مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ فلم يَنْفَعهم الحذرُ» (so do not be wary of death as those before you were wary of it, and wariness did not avail them); Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. What is apparent is that this is a command to this Community to wage jihad, after He mentioned that wariness of death did not avail a certain people; so it is an encouragement to them, and it is of the conjoining of clauses, so agreement [between the clauses] in being a command or otherwise is not required.

semin-durr:245-245.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {مَّن ذَا الذي يُقْرِضُ الله قَرْضاً حَسَناً}: «مَنْ» is interrogative, and its position is the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); «ذا» is a demonstrative, its khabar (predicate); and «الذي» with its ṣila (relative clause) is a naʿt (adjective) of the demonstrative or a badal (substitute) of it. It is also possible that «مَنْ ذا» as a whole is in the status of a single noun, the two being compounded, as in your saying «ماذا صَنَعْتَ» (what did you do?), as its explanation has preceded at His saying: {مَاذَآ أَرَادَ الله} [al-Baqara: 26]. Abū al-Baqāʾ disallowed this view, distinguishing between it and your saying «ماذا», where the two are made a single noun, on the ground that «ما» is more vague than «مَنْ», because «مَنْ» is for rational beings. There is no sense in disallowing it for this reason; the grammarians stated explicitly that the ruling of «مَنْ ذا» is the ruling of «ماذا».
It is also possible that «ذا» means «الذي» (who), and there are then two interpretations. The first: the second «الذي» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of it, because it has its meaning, as though it were said: «مَنْ الذي الذي يُقْرِضُ؟» (who is the one, the one who lends?). The second: «الذي» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the ṣila of «ذا», its implied form being «مَنْ الذي هو الذي يُقْرِضُ» (who is the one who is the one who lends?), «ذا» and its ṣila being the khabar of interrogative «مَنْ». Jamāl al-Dīn ibn Mālik allowed these two views; they are weak, and the [right] view is what I gave first.
«قرْضاً» is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) with the augment letters deleted, since the meaning is «إقراضاً» (lending), as in His saying {أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ الأرض نَبَاتاً} [al-Baqara: 26] [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse is Nūḥ: 17]. On this view the second object is omitted, its implied form being «يُقْرِض اللَّهَ مالاً وصدقةً» (lends Allah wealth and charity). A muḍāf must be omitted, its implied form being «يقرضُ عبادَ اللَّهِ المحاويجَ» (lends to Allah's needy servants), since He is exalted above that; or it is by way of figurative usage. It is also possible that it is in the sense of a passive participle, as «الخَلْق» in the sense of «المخلوق» (the created), its accusative then being as a second object of «يُقْرِض».
«حَسَناً» may be an adjective of «قرضاً» on the two meanings mentioned, or it may be the naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, if we make «قَرْضاً» in the sense of a passive participle, i.e. «إقراضاً حسناً» (a goodly lending).
His saying: {فَيُضَاعِفَهُ}: ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read it, here and in al-Ḥadīd, with the fāʾ in the accusative, except that Ibn ʿĀmir doubles the ʿayn without an alif [«فيضعِّفَه»]. The rest read it in the nominative, except that Ibn Kathīr doubles the ʿayn without an alif. The nominative has two explanations. The first: it is conjoined to «يقرضُ», the ṣila. The second: it is nominative as resumptive (istiʾnāf), i.e. «فهو يُضاعِفُهُ» (and He multiplies it). The first is better because there is no implied element.
The accusative has two explanations. The first: it is subjunctive by an implied «أَنْ», conjoined to the maṣdar understood in meaning from «يقرضُ», so it is a maṣdar conjoined to a maṣdar, its implied form being: «مَنْ ذا الذي يكونُ منه إقراضٌ فمضاعفةٌ من اللَّهِ» (who is the one from whom there is lending, and then multiplying from Allah?), as in the poet's saying:
1014 - لَلُبْسُ عباءَةٍ وتَقرَّعيني ... أحبُّ إليَّ مِنْ لُبْسِ الشفوفِ
(Wearing a coarse cloak with my eye at rest is dearer to me than wearing sheer fine garments.)
The second: it is accusative as the answer to the interrogative in meaning, because the interrogative, although in wording it concerns the lender, concerns the lending
in meaning, as though He said: «أيقرضُ اللَّهَ أَحَدٌ فيضاعفَه» (does anyone lend to Allah, so that He multiplies it?).
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may not be the answer to the interrogative according to the wording, because what is asked about in the wording is the lender, i.e. the doer of the lending, not the lending, i.e. that which is the act." Some grammarians disallowed the subjunctive after the fāʾ in answer to an interrogative concerning that to which the predication is attributed rather than the predication itself; this is refuted by this verse and others, such as his ﷺ saying: «مَنْ يستغفرُونِي فأغفرَ له، مَنْ يدعوني فأستجيبَ له» (who will ask My forgiveness, that I may forgive him; who will call upon Me, that I may answer him), with the subjunctive in both.
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "If it is said: why is the verb not conjoined to the maṣdar, namely «قرضاً», just as a verb is conjoined to a maṣdar with an implied «أَنْ», as in the poet's saying:
1015 - لَلُبْسُ عباءةٍ وتَقَرَّعَيْني ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
it is answered: this is not sound for two reasons. The first: «قرضاً» here is an emphasising maṣdar, and the emphasising maṣdar is not interpreted as «أَنْ» plus a verb. The second: conjoining it to it would require that it be governed by «يقرضُ», and this is not sound in meaning, because the multiplying is not lent; it is only an act of Allah the Exalted." His reasoning in the first point implies that he makes it a condition for the subjunctive that it be conjoined to a maṣdar that can be interpreted as «أَنْ» plus a verb. This is not a condition; rather, it is allowed even if the noun conjoined to is not a maṣdar, as in the poet's saying:
1016 - ولولا رجالٌ من رِزامٍ أَعِزَّةٍ ... وآلُ سبيعٍ أو أَسُوءَك عَلْقَما
(Were it not for mighty men of Rizām, and the family of Subayʿ, or my grieving you, O ʿAlqama …)
«أسوءَك» is subjunctive by «أنْ», conjoined to «رجالٌ». So the [right] way of disallowing that is to say: had it been conjoined to «قرضاً», it would share its governor, namely «يُقْرض», and the implied form would become «مَنْ ذا الذي يقرض مضاعفةً» (who is it that lends a multiplying?), which is not sound in meaning.
It has already been stated that it was read «يُضاعِفُ» and «يُضَعِّفُ». It has been said that they have one meaning, the mufāʿala being in the sense of the bare «فَعَل», as in «عاقَبْت». It has also been said that they are different: it has been said that the doubled form is for multiplicity; and it has been said that «يُضَعِّف» is for what is made twofold, and «ضاعَفَه» for what is increased by more than that.
«القَرْض» is cutting; from it is «المِقْراض» (scissors), for what one cuts with. The loan was called «قرض» because it is cutting off a portion of wealth; this is the origin of the derivation. Then the scholars disagreed about «القَرْض»: it has been said that it is a name for everything for which recompense is sought; and it has been said: that you give something so that its like returns to you. Al-Zajjāj said: "It is the trial (al-balāʾ), whether good or bad."
His saying: {أَضْعَافاً}: there are three views about it. The most apparent of them is that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in «يضاعِفُ». Is this ḥāl emphasising or clarifying? What is apparent is that it is clarifying, because, although it is from the root of its governor, it is distinguished by being qualified by something else, so something is understood from it that is not understood from its governor, and this is the nature of the clarifying ḥāl. The second: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), on the basis that «يضاعِفُ» implies the meaning of «يُصَيِّر» (to make become), i.e. He makes it, by multiplying, manifold.
The third: it is accusative as a maṣdar.
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "It has been said: it may be accusative as a maṣdar on the consideration that «الضِّعْف» — which is the multiplied thing — is applied in the sense of multiplying, just as «العَطاء», which is the name of the thing given, was applied in the sense of giving. It was put in the plural because of the different aspects of multiplying, considering the difference of persons, the difference of the lender and the difference of the kinds of recompense." Abū al-Baqāʾ preceded him in this, and this is his wording, and he cited:
1017 - أكفراً بعد ردِّ الموتِ عني ... وبعدَ عطائِكَ المئةَ الرِّتاعا
(Is it ingratitude, after your warding death off from me, and after your giving of the hundred grazing camels?)
«الأَضْعاف» is the plural of «ضِعْف», and «الضِّعْف» is the like of two equal measures. It has been said: the like of a thing in measure. And it is said: «ضِعْفُ الشيء» is its like three times — except that when «ضعفان» is said, it may be applied to the two that are alike in measure, in that each of them doubles the other, just as one says «زَوْجان» (a pair), in that each of them is a mate (zawj) of the other.
Abū ʿAmr [Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, Ḥafṣ and Qunbul] read «وَيَبْسُطُ» with the sīn according to the original, and the rest with the ṣād because of the ṭāʾ. Its verification has preceded at «الصراط».

semin-durr:259-259.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَوْ كالذي مَرَّ}: the majority read the wāw of «أو» quiescent, and here it is for detailing (tafṣīl); it is also said: for choice between marvelling at the affair of either of the two. Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥusayn read «أوَ» with a fatḥa on it, as the conjunctive wāw with the interrogative hamza before it.

Concerning His words {كالذي} there are four aspects. The first is that it is conjoined according to the meaning (ʿaṭf ʿalā al-maʿnā), its implied form according to al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ being: "Have you seen [anyone] like the one who disputed with Ibrāhīm, or like the one who passed by a town?" So said Makkī. As for conjoining according to the meaning, although it exists in their language, as in his words:

1044 - تقيٌّ نقيٌّ لم يُكَثِّرْ غنيمةً ... بِنَهْكَةِ ذي قُرْبى ولا بِحَقَلِّدِ
(God-fearing, pure; he did not increase his spoils by wronging a kinsman, nor is he mean-spirited.)

and the saying of the other:

1045 - أجِدَّكَ لن تَرَى بثُعَيْلِباتٍ ... ولا بَيْدَانَ ناجيةً ذَمُولا
ولا متدارِكٍ والليلُ طَفْلٌ ... ببعضِ نواشغِ الوادي حُمُولا
(Truly, will you not see at Thuʿaylibāt nor at Baydān a swift, ambling she-camel, nor be one overtaking, while the night is young, the departing litters at some of the valley's water-courses?)

— for the meaning of the first is "he is not one who increases", and for that reason he conjoined to it «ولا بِحَقَلَّدِ»; and the meaning of the second is "truly, you are not one who sees", and for that reason he conjoined to it «ولا متداركٍ» — nevertheless they have stated explicitly that it is not to be used as a basis for analogy.

The second is that it is accusative by an implied verb; al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ inclined to this. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«أو كالذي»: its meaning is 'or have you seen the like of the one who…'", and it was omitted because of the indication of «ألم تَرَ», since both are expressions of marvelling. This is good, because omission is established and frequent, unlike conjoining according to the meaning.

The third is that the kāf is redundant (zāʾida), as it is in His words {لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ} [al-Shūrā: 11] and in the saying of the other:

1046 - فَصُيِّروا مثلَ كَعَصْفٍ مأكولْ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(So they were made like straw eaten up.)

The implied form is: "Have you not seen the one who disputed, or the one who passed by a town?" There is weakness in it, because the default is the absence of redundancy.

The fourth is that the kāf is a noun meaning «مِثْل» (like), not a particle. This is the doctrine of al-Akhfash, and it is the correct one in terms of evidence, even though the majority of the Basrans hold otherwise. So the implied form is: "Have you not seen the one who disputed, or the like of the one who passed by?", and this is a good meaning. The view that the kāf is a noun has proofs mentioned in the books of the [grammarians]; we have mentioned the best of them in this book. Among them is its being made equivalent to «مثل» as a fāʿil (agent) in his words:

1047 - وإنّك لم يَفْخَرْ عليك كفاخرٍ ... ضعيفٍ ولم يَغْلِبْكَ مثلُ مُغَلَّبِ
(No one boasts over you like a weak boaster, and none overcomes you like one oft-overcome.)

Among them also are the entry of prepositions upon it and predication of it. The discussion of the derivation of «القرية» has preceded.

His words: {وَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ}: concerning this clause there are five aspects. The first is that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of «مَرَّ»; the wāw here links the ḥāl clause and its possessor, and bringing it is obligatory because the clause lacks a pronoun referring to him. The second is that it is a ḥāl from «قرية»: either by making «على عروشها» a naʿt (adjective) of «قرية» on one of the aspects to come concerning this prepositional phrase, or according to the opinion of whoever permits a ḥāl from an indefinite noun absolutely, which is weak according to Sībawayh. The third is that it is a ḥāl from «عروشها», placed before it, its implied form being: "he passed by a town, by its roofs, while they were fallen in". [Translator's note: so in the source; the order shown places the ḥāl after its possessor.]

The fourth is that it is a ḥāl from the «ها» to which «عروش» is annexed. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The governor is the meaning of annexation, and it is weak though permissible." End quote. What made a ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi easier is that it is a part of the muḍāf, because «العروش» are part of the town; so it is close to His words, the Exalted: {مَا فِي صُدُورِهِم مِّنْ غِلٍّ إِخْوَاناً} [al-Aʿrāf: 43]. [Translator's note: the verse actually reads وَنَزَعْنَا مَا فِي صُدُورِهِم مِّنْ غِلٍّ إِخْوَانًا at al-Ḥijr: 47; al-Aʿrāf: 43 lacks إِخْوَانًا. Quoted as written.] The fifth is that the clause is a naʿt of «قرية»; this is not approved by them, because the wāw does not come between the adjective and what it qualifies — although al-Zamakhsharī permitted it in His words, the Exalted, {وَمَآ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍ إِلاَّ وَلَهَا كِتَابٌ مَّعْلُومٌ} [al-Ḥijr: 4], making «ولَهَا كتابٌ» a naʿt; he said: "The wāw was interposed to signal the close attachment of the adjective to what it qualifies." This is a doctrine in which Abū al-Fatḥ Ibn Jinnī preceded him in some of his works, and there is in it what has preceded. It is as though what made that easier is the likening of the clause occurring as a naʿt to the one occurring as a ḥāl, because the ḥāl is an adjective in meaning. Abū al-Baqāʾ made the treatment of this clause as a naʿt of «قرية» depend on the permissibility of making «على عروشها» a badal (substitute) from «قرية» with repetition of the preposition, and made the treatment of «وهي خاويةٌ» as a ḥāl from «العروش», or from «القرية», or from the «ها» to which it is annexed, depend on making «على عروشها» a naʿt of «القرية». This is his text, which I have cited so that it becomes clear to you; he said: "It is said that it is a badal from «القرية», its implied form being: he passed by a town, by its roofs, i.e. he passed by the roofs of the town, the preposition being repeated with the badal. On this view «على عروشها» may be a naʿt of «القرية», not a badal, its implied form being: by a town fallen upon its roofs. On this, «وهي خاويةٌ» may be a ḥāl from «العروش», or a ḥāl from «القرية» because it has been qualified, or a ḥāl from the «ها» to which [«عروش»] is annexed." In this construction there is an evident difficulty.

His words: {على عُرُوشِهَا}: there are four aspects. The first is that it is a badal from «قرية» with repetition of the governor. The second is that it is a naʿt of «قرية», as its verification has preceded. On the first it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «مَرَّ», because what governs the badal is what governs what it substitutes for; on the second it is attached to something omitted, i.e. "fallen upon its roofs". The third is that it is attached to «خاوية» itself, if we interpret «خاوية» as meaning ruined and fallen. The fourth is that it is attached to something omitted that the meaning indicates, and that omitted thing, they said, is the word «ثابتة» ("standing"), because they interpreted «خاويةٌ» as meaning: empty of its people, standing upon its roofs, its houses upright and not ruined. This is omission without evidence, and the mind does not readily go to it. It is also said: «على» means «مع» ("with"), i.e. "with its roofs"; they said: on this, what is meant by «العروش» is the buildings.

Al-khāwī is the empty. It is said: khawati al-dāru takhwī khawāʾan, with the long vowel, and khuwiyyan; and also khawiyat, with a kasra on the middle radical, takhwā khawan, with the short vowel, and khawyan.

Al-khawā is hunger, because the belly is empty of provision. Al-khawiyy on the pattern faʿīl is the soft, low-lying ground. «خَوَّى البعيرُ»: the camel held its side away from the ground [when kneeling]. He said:

1048 - خَوَّى على مُسْتَوِيات خَمْسِ ... كِرْكِرَةٍ وثَفِناتٍ مُلْسٍ
(He knelt with his flank raised, on five even points: a breast-pad and smooth callused knees.)

Al-ʿurūsh is the plural of ʿarsh, which is the roof of a house, and likewise everything prepared to be shaded by. It is also said: it is the building itself. He said:

1049 - إنْ يَقْتُلوكَ فقد ثَلَلْتُ عروشَهُمْ ... بعُتيبةَ بنِ الحارثِ بِنْ شهابِ
(If they kill you, I have already demolished their edifices by [killing] ʿUtayba ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Shihāb.)

His words: {أنى يُحْيِي هذه الله}: concerning «أنَّى» there are two aspects. The first is that it means «متى» ("when"); Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "On this it is an adverb." The second is that it means «كيف» ("how"); Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Its position is then a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «هذه», and it was put first because of the interrogative sense in it." The apparent view is that it means «كيف». On both views its governor is «يُحْيي», and «بعد» is also governed by it. Giving life and causing death are figurative if what is meant by them is prosperity and ruin, or literal if we posit a muḍāf, i.e. "how will He give life to the people of this town after the death of its people?" It is also possible that «هذه» points to the decayed bones of the town's people and their torn corpses; the context indicates that.

His words: {مِئَةَ عَامٍ}: Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«مئة عام» is an adverb of «أماته» according to the meaning, because the meaning is 'He made him remain a hundred years'. It cannot be an adverb according to the outward wording, because causing death occurs in the smallest span of time. It may also be an adverb of an omitted verb, its implied form being: 'So Allah caused him to die, and he remained a hundred years'; His words «كم لَبِثْتَ» indicate that." There is no need for these two interpretations; rather the meaning is: He made him dead for a hundred years.

«مئة» is a known decade-number of the numerals. Its final radical is elided, and it is a yāʾ; this is indicated by their saying «أَمْأَيْتُ الدراهم», i.e. I made them a hundred. So its pattern is fiʿa. It is pluralized as «مِئات», and «مِئُون» occurs in it anomalously. He said:

1050 - ثلاثُ مئينٍ للملوكِ وَفَى بها ... ردائي وَجَلَّتْ عن وجوه الأهاتِمِ
(Three hundred [camels] for the kings — my cloak [i.e. my pledge] made them good, and cleared the faces of [the clan of] al-Ahtam [of shame].)

It is as though they treated it with this plural because of what was elided from it, as they said sinūn for sana.

Al-ʿām is a known period of time. Its middle radical is wāw, because of their saying in the diminutive ʿuwaym and in the broken plural «أَعْوَام». Al-Naqqāsh said: "It is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) by which time was named, because it is one swim (ʿawma) of the sun in the celestial sphere, and al-ʿawm is swimming. The Exalted said: {وَكُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ} [Yā Sīn: 40]. On this, al-ʿām and al-ʿawm are like al-qawl and al-qāl."

His words: {كَمْ} is accusative as an adverb; its specifier is omitted, its implied form being: "how many days" or "times". What makes it accusative is «لَبِثْتَ», and the clause is in the position of the accusative by the verb of saying. The apparent view is that «أو» in His words {يَوْماً أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ} means «بل» ("rather"), for digression (iḍrāb), and this is an established view; it is also said: it is for doubt. His words {قَالَ بَل لَّبِثْتَ}: «بل» conjoins this clause to an omitted clause, its implied form being: "I did not remain a day or part of a day; rather you remained a hundred years". [Translator's note: so in the source, mixing first and second person.]

Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and Ibn Kathīr read [«لبثت»] with the thāʾ pronounced distinctly throughout the Qurʾān, and the rest with assimilation.

His words: {لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ}: this clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. Some claimed that when the imperfect negated by «لم» occurs as a ḥāl, the preferred practice is that the wāw of the ḥāl enters, and he recited:

1051 - بأَيْدي رجالٍ لم يَشِيْموا سيوفَهُمْ ... ولم تَكْثُر القَتْلى بها حينَ سُلَّتِ
(In the hands of men who did not sheathe their swords [until] the slain were many by them when they were drawn.)

Others claimed that it is better that an imperfect occurring as a ḥāl be negated with «ما» and «لمَّا». Neither claim is correct, because both usages occur in the Qurʾān. The Exalted said: {فانقلبوا بِنِعْمَةٍ مِّنَ الله وَفَضْلٍ لَّمْ يَمْسَسْهُمْ سواء} [Āl ʿImrān: 174] [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse reads لَّمْ يَمْسَسْهُمْ سُوٓءٌ], and the Exalted said: {أَوْ قَالَ أُوْحِيَ إِلَيَّ وَلَمْ يُوحَ إِلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ} [al-Anʿām: 93]. So negation with «لم» came with the wāw and without it.

It has been said: two things preceded, namely «طعامِك وشرابِك», yet He referred back to them only with a singular pronoun. There are three answers to that. The first is that, since the two go together, in the sense that one is not sufficient without the other, they became like a single thing, as though He [said]: "Look at your nourishment." The second is that the pronoun refers to the drink only, because it is the nearest thing mentioned, and there is another clause omitted because this one indicates it, the implied form being: "Look at your food, it has not changed, and at your drink, it has not changed." Or He was silent about the change of the food, pointing by the lesser to the greater: if the drink did not change, despite the soul's inclination toward it, then the food's not changing is all the more so. Abū al-Baqāʾ said something to this effect. The third is that the singular was used in place of the dual; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and recited:

1052 - فكأنَّ في العينين حَبَّ قَرَنْفُلٍ ... أو سُنْبَلٍ كُحِلَتْ به فانْهَلَّتِ
(As though in the two eyes were grains of clove or spikenard, with which it [the eye] was anointed, so it streamed with tears.)

This is worthless.

Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «لم يَتَسَنَّهْ» with the hāʾ in pause and without it in continuous speech, and the rest retained it in both states. As for their reading, the hāʾ in it is the hāʾ of pause (hāʾ al-sakt). As for the reading of the majority, the hāʾ admits two aspects. The first is that it too is for pause, and it was retained in continuous speech only by treating continuous speech like pause; this is frequent in the Qurʾān, and you will come across places of it. On this, the origin of the word is either derived from the word «السَّنة» (year), on our view that its elided final radical is wāw — for that reason it is restored in the diminutive and plural; they said sunayya and sanawāt, and in this dialect they said «سانَيْتُ», the wāw being changed into a yāʾ because it is fourth; and they said «أَسْنَتَ القومُ» ("the people suffered a year of drought"), changing the wāw into a tāʾ, the origin being asnawū, and they changed it as in tujāh and tukhama, as preceded — so its origin is yatasannā, and the alif was elided by the jussive. Or it is from the word «مَسْنون», which is the changed [i.e. putrid], from which is {مِّنْ حَمَإٍ مَّسْنُونٍ} [al-Ḥijr: 26]; the origin is yatasannanu with three nūns, then the succession of identical letters was found heavy, so the last was changed into a yāʾ — as they said in taẓannana: taẓannā, and in qaṣṣaṣtu aẓfārī: qaṣṣaytu — then the yāʾ was changed into an alif because it was vowelled and the letter before it had a fatḥa, then it was elided by the jussive. Abū ʿAmr said this, and al-Zajjāj declared it wrong, saying: "Because al-masnūn is what is poured along the course (sanan) of the road."

It is related of al-Naqqāsh that he said: "It is taken from asina al-māʾu", i.e. the water changed [became stagnant]. Although this is sound in meaning, the grammarians rejected his view because it is corrupt in derivation: had it been derived from «أَسِنَ الماء», then when tafaʿʿala is formed from it, it ought to be said taʾassana.

It can be answered on his behalf that the word may have been metathesized, its first radical — the hamza — being moved to the place of its final radical, leaving yatasannaʾ with the hamza at the end; then the hamza was changed into an alif, as in their saying «قَرَا» for qaraʾa, and in istahzā; then it was elided by the jussive.

The second aspect is that the hāʾ is radical in its own right, and it is also derived from the word «سنة», but in the dialect of those who make its elided final radical a hāʾ, namely the Ḥijāzīs, the origin being sunayha [Translator's note: so in the source, apparently intending sanha]; this is indicated by the diminutive and the broken plural: they said sunayha, sunayhāt and sānahtu. Their poet said:

1053 - وليسَتْ بِسَنْهَاء ولا رُجَّبِيَّةٍ ... ولكنْ عرايا في السنينِ الجوائِحِ
(It [the palm] is neither one that bears only in alternate years nor one needing propping, but one whose fruit is given away in the ruinous years of drought.)

The meaning of «لم يَتَسَنَّهْ», on our view that it is from the word al-sana, is: it did not change through the passing of years over it, but remained in its state. This is better than the statement of Abū al-Baqāʾ in the course of his discussion, "from your saying asnā yusnī, when years have passed over it", because the meaning would become: years have not passed over it — and this contradicts the senses and what actually happened.

Ubayy read «لم يَسَّنَّه», with the tāʾ assimilated into the sīn, the origin being «لم يَتَسَنَّه», as was read {لاَّ يَسَّمَّعُونَ إلى الملإ} [al-Ṣāffāt: 8], the origin being yatasammaʿūna, then assimilated. Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read «لمئة سنة».

His words: {وَلِنَجْعَلَكَ}: there are three aspects. The first is that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb posited after it, its implied form being: "and in order to make you…, We did that". The second is that it is conjoined to something omitted, its implied form being: "We did that so that you know Our power, and in order to make you…". The third is that the wāw is redundant (zāʾida) and the lām is attached to the verb before it, i.e. "and look at your donkey, in order that We make you…" [Translator's note: the source has «لنعجلَكَ», an evident misprint for «لنجعلَكَ».] There is no fronting and postponing in the speech, as some claimed, saying that His words «ولنجعلَكَ» are postponed after His words «وانظُرْ إلى العظامِ», and that the three [commands to] look are conjoined to one another, separated by this prepositional phrase; because the third looking is part of the completion of the second, therefore this statement of reason was not made a separating parenthesis. This lām is the lām of kay (purpose), and the verb after it is accusative by an implied «أَنْ»; it and the verb after it are in the position of the genitive, as has been explained more than once. «آية» is a second object, because «الجَعْل» here means making something become. «للناس» is a naʿt (adjective) of «آية». The «أل» in «الناس» is said to be for prior reference (ʿahd) if what is meant by them is the remainder of his people, and it is said to be generic if what is meant is all the children of Ādam.

His words: {كَيْفَ} is accusative in the manner of ḥāls; its governor is «نُنْشِزُها», and the possessor of the ḥāl is the accusative pronoun in «نُنْشِزُها». «انظُرْ» does not govern this ḥāl, since the interrogative has the head of the speech, so what precedes it does not govern it. This is the [correct] view on this question and its analogues.

Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«كيف نُنْشِزُها» is in the position of a ḥāl from «العظام». The governor of «كيف» is «ننشِزُها», and «انظر» may not govern it, because what precedes an interrogative does not govern it. But «كيف» and «نُنْشِزُها» together are a ḥāl from «العظام», and the governor of it is «انظر», its implied form being: look at the bones being brought to life." This is worthless, because this is an interrogative clause, and an interrogative does not occur as a ḥāl; what occurs as a ḥāl is «كيف» alone, and for that reason a ḥāl may be substituted for it with repetition of the interrogative particle, as in «كيف ضَرَبْتَ زيداً أقائماً أم قاعداً؟» ("How did you strike Zayd — standing or sitting?").

What sound reasoning requires in this question and its like is that the clause «كيف نُنْشِزُها» be a badal (substitute) from «العظام», and so be in the position of the accusative. That is because visual «نظر» is made transitive by «إلى», and suspension (taʿlīq) is permissible with it, as in His words, the Exalted: 
{انظر كَيْفَ فَضَّلْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ على بَعْضٍ} [Hūd: 21] [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse is al-Isrāʾ: 21]. So the clause is in the position of the accusative, because when [a verb] is made transitive by a preposition, what comes after it is in the position of the accusative by it. A muḍāf must be omitted for the substitution to be sound, the implied form being: "to the state of the bones". Analogous to it is their saying: «عَرفْتُ زيداً: أبو مَنْ هو؟» ("I knew Zayd — whose father is he?"), where «أبو مَنْ هو» is a badal from «زيداً», with an omission whose implied form is: "I knew the story of Zayd". The interrogative in the chapter of suspension is not meant in its [interrogative] meaning; rather it has run in their language with the rule of the wording, not of the meaning, attached to it; [it is] analogous to «أيّ» in specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), as in «اللهم اغفر لنا أَيَّتُها العِصابة» ("O Allah, forgive us — O band"), where the wording is like the vocative in all its rules, though its meaning is not that.

Abū ʿAmr and the two Ḥaram readers read «نُنْشِرُها» with a ḍamma on the nūn, a kasra on the shīn, and the undotted rāʾ; the rest likewise, except with the dotted zāy. Ibn ʿAbbās [read] with a fatḥa on the nūn, a ḍamma on the shīn, and also the undotted rāʾ. Al-Nakhaʿī likewise, except with the dotted zāy; it is also reported from him [reading with yāʾ], with a ḍamma and with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, with both the rāʾ and the zāy.

As for the reading of the two Ḥaram readers, it is from «أَنْشَرَ اللَّهُ الموتى» ("Allah resurrected the dead"), meaning He gave them life. As for the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, it is from the triliteral «نَشَر», and there are then two aspects in it. The first is that it has the meaning of afʿala, so the two readings coincide. The second is that it is from «نَشَرَ», the opposite of ṭawā (to fold), i.e. He spreads them out by giving life. «نَشَرَ» is also the reflexive counterpart (muṭāwiʿ) of anshara, as in «أَنْشَرَ الله الميت فَنَشَرَ» ("Allah raised the dead man, and he rose"), so the transitive and intransitive are of the same wording; but its being a reflexive counterpart is inconceivable in this noble verse, because the verb in it is transitive — although there is some vagueness in Abū al-Baqāʾ's wording at this place. An example of «نشر» coming as intransitive is his words:

1054 - حتى يقولَ الناسُ مِمَّا رَأَوا ... يا عجباً للميِّت الناشِرِ
(Until people say, from what they saw: Oh, how wondrous is the dead man who has come back to life!)

So «ناشِر» is from «نَشَر» meaning "came to life".

As for the reading with zāy, it is from al-nashz, which is elevation; from it is «نَشْزُ الأرضِ», the raised part of the ground, and the nushūz of a woman, which is her rising from her [proper] state to another state. So the meaning is: He moves the bones and raises some of them onto others for giving life.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It troubles me that al-nushūz should be the raising of bones onto one another; al-nushūz is only rising little by little." He said: "Look at the usage of the Arabs and you will find it so; from it are «نَشَزَ نابُ البعير» ('the camel's tusk rose [gradually]') and «أَنْشَزُوا فَأَنْشَزوا». So the meaning here is of gradualness in the action." Thus Ibn ʿAṭiyya made al-nushūz a specific kind of rising.

Whoever gave the nūn a ḍamma [took it] from «أَنْشَزَ», and whoever gave it a fatḥa from «نَشَزَ»; one says «نَشَزه» and «أَنْشَزَه» with one meaning. Whoever read with the yāʾ, the pronoun is for Allah the Exalted. Ubayy read «نُنْشِئُها», from al-nashʾa (bringing into being). Some preferred the reading with zāy over the rāʾ, saying: bones are not given life individually, but by joining them to one another, and the zāy is more fitting for this meaning, since it means joining, not giving life; the one described as given life is the man, not the bones, and one does not say "this is a living bone". This is worthless, because of His words: {مَن يُحيِي العظام وَهِيَ رَمِيمٌ} [Yā Sīn: 1] [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse is Yā Sīn: 78].

A pronoun must be omitted from His word «العِظام», i.e. "the bones of it", i.e. of the donkey; or the «أل» stands in place of annexation, i.e. "the bones of your donkey".

His words: {لَحْماً} is the second object of «نَكْسُوها», and it is of the class of «أعطى» (verbs taking two objects). This is metaphor (istiʿāra); similar is the saying of Labīd:

1055 - الحمدُ للَّهِ إذْ لم يَأْتِنِي أَجَلي ... حتى اكتسَيْتُ من الإِسلامِ سِرْبالا
(Praise be to Allah, that my appointed time did not come to me until I had clothed myself with a garment of Islam.)

His words: {فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ}: concerning the fāʿil (agent) of «تبيَّن» there are two views. The first is that it is a latent (mustatir) pronoun explained by the context of the speech, its implied form being: "When the manner of giving life by which he was satisfied became clear to him". Al-Zamakhsharī posited it as: "When what had been problematic to him became clear to him", meaning regarding the matter of giving life to the dead. The first is more fitting, because the force of the speech indicates it, unlike the second. The second — with which al-Zamakhsharī began — is that the question belongs to the chapter of al-iʿmāl (the governing of one of two competing governors), meaning that «تَبَيَّن» requires a fāʿil and «أَعْلَمُ» requires an object, and {أَنَّ الله على كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ} is fit to be the fāʿil of «تبيَّن» and the object of «أعلَمُ», so the question becomes one of contention (tanāzuʿ). This is his text; he said: "The fāʿil of «تبيَّن» is implied (muḍmar), its implied form being: 'When it became clear to him that Allah has power over all things, he said: I know that Allah has power over all things'; the first was omitted because the second indicates it, as in their saying «ضربني وضربتُ زيداً» ('he struck me and I struck Zayd')." So he made it of the chapter of contention, as you see, and made it a case of the second governing, which is the preferred view among the Basrans. When the second was made to govern, he implied a fāʿil in the first. It cannot be a case of the first governing, because a pronoun would then have to be implied in the second as an object pronoun, and it would be said: "When it became clear to him, he said: I know it, that Allah…". Similar to it in the governing of the second are: {آتوني أُفْرِغْ عَلَيْهِ قِطْراً} [al-Kahf: 96] and {هَآؤُمُ اقرؤا كِتَابيَهْ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 19].

However, the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected this on the ground that the condition of iʿmāl, as the grammarians have stipulated, is the association of the two governors, the least of which is by a conjunction — so that the separation is not considered — or that the second governor be governed by the first, as in «جاءني يضحكُ زيدٌ» ("Zayd came to me laughing"), for «يضحك» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) whose governor is «جاءني», so a pronoun is placed in «جاءني» or in «يضحك», so that the verb is not a separator. Their making {آتوني أُفْرِغْ عَلَيْهِ قِطْراً}, {يَسْتَفْتُونَكَ قُلِ الله يُفْتِيكُمْ فِي الكلالة} [al-Nisāʾ: 176], {وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ تَعَالَوْاْ يَسْتَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ رَسُولُ الله} [al-Munāfiqūn: 5] and {هَآؤُمُ اقرؤا كِتَابيَهْ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 19] of the chapter of iʿmāl does not contradict this, because these governors are associated in some way among the ways of association, and association is not restricted to conjunction or governing. So, if it is as they stipulated, the second governor here is not associated with the first by a conjunction or otherwise, nor is it governed by the first; rather it is governed by «قال», and «قال» is the apodosis (jawāb) of «لَمَّا» if we say it is a particle, and the governor of «لَمَّا» if we say it is an adverb, «تبيَّن» on this view being in the genitive by the adverb. The grammarians did not mention contention in cases like «لو جاء قتلتُ زيداً» ("had he come, I would have killed Zayd"), nor «لَمَّا جاء ضربتُ زيداً», nor «حين جاء قتلتُ زيداً», nor «إذا جاء قتلت زيداً». For that reason the grammarians related that the Arabs do not say «أَكْرَمْتُ أهنتُ زيداً» ("I honoured, I insulted Zayd") — meaning because of the lack of association between the two governors. And he contradicted his own statement, in that he made the fāʿil omitted, as preceded in his wording, while omission is incompatible with implication (iḍmār). If by implication in his words "the fāʿil of «تبيَّن» is implied" he meant omission, that is the view of al-Kisāʾī, because he does not permit implying a nominative [pronoun] before its mention, so he claims omission in it, and recites:

1056 - تَعَفَّقَ بالأَرْطى لها وأرادَها ... رجالٌ فَبَذَّت نبلَهم وكَلِيبُ
(Men took shelter by the arṭā shrubs [to ambush] her and sought her, but she outran their arrows — and [their] pack of dogs.)

This has a well-known interpretation. It was refuted against him by attested usage; he said:

1057 - هَوَيْنَنِي وهَوَيْتُ الخُرَّدَ العُرُبا ... أزمانَ كنتُ منوطاً بي هوىً وصِبا
(They loved me, and I loved the shy, affectionate maidens, in the days when love and youthful passion clung to me.)

He said «هَوَيْنَنِي», bringing in the first [verb] the pronoun of the feminine plural without omission. End of what he [Abū Ḥayyān] refuted him with; and there is in it an evident difficulty.

Ibn ʿAbbās read «تُبُيِّن» in the passive, the prepositional phrase after it standing in place of the fāʿil. Ibn al-Samayfaʿ [read] «يُبَيِّن» without tāʾ, in the passive, what stands in its place being the pronoun of the manner of giving life, or the prepositional phrase.

His words: {قَالَ أَعْلَمُ}: the majority read «قال» in the active voice. Concerning its fāʿil on the reading of Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī, «اعْلَمْ» as an imperative from «عَلِمَ», there are two views. The more evident is that it is a pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted or to the angel, i.e. Allah, or the angel, said to that passer-by: "Know!" The second is that it is a pronoun referring to the passer-by himself: he put himself in the position of a stranger and addressed it. From this is:

1058 - وَدِّعْ هُرَيْرَةَ. . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Bid farewell to Hurayra…)

[and his words:]

1059 - ألم تَغْتَمِضْ عيناك. . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Have your eyes not closed…)

[and his words:]

1060 - تطاولَ ليلُك. . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Your night has grown long…)

He means himself. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "As you say to yourself: Know, O ʿAbd Allāh! This is called tajrīd (abstraction)", meaning as though he abstracted from himself someone addressed whom he addresses. As for the reading of the others, «أعلمُ» as an imperfect of the first person, the fāʿil of «قال» is the pronoun of the passer-by, i.e. the passer-by said: "I know."

Al-Aʿmash read «قيل» in the passive. What stands in place of the fāʿil is either the pronoun of the maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb, or the clause after it, according to what preceded at the beginning of the sūra.

Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «اعلمْ» as an imperative, and the rest «أعلمُ» as an imperfect; and al-Juʿfī from Abū Bakr [read] «أَعْلِمُ» [Translator's note: so vowelled in the source; presumably «أَعْلِمْ»] as an imperative from «أَعْلَمَ». The discussion concerning it is like the discussion concerning the reading of Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī with respect to what the fāʿil of «قال» is. «أنَّ الله» is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects, or of the first, the second being omitted, according to the disagreement that has preceded.

semin-durr:274-274.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الذين يُنْفِقُونَ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is the clause in His saying «فلهم أجرُهمْ». The fāʾ has entered because of the sense of condition that the relative noun contains. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The resemblance – meaning between the relative noun and the conditional noun – is found only when the relative noun is connected to a verb, and when no governor that changes its meaning enters upon the relative noun." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "He restricted the resemblance to the case where «الذي» is connected to a verb, and this is imprecise speech. As for his saying «الذي», this is not specific to «الذي»; rather every relative noun other than alif-lām has the same ruling as «الذي», without disagreement, whereas regarding alif-lām there is disagreement, and the position of Sībawayh is that the fāʾ may not enter. Second: his saying «connected to a verb»: he left the verb unqualified and limited himself to it, but that is not so; rather the condition for the verb is that it be fit to be directly joined by a conditional particle. So if you said: «الذي سيأتيني» – or «لمّا يأتيني» – or «ما يأتيني» or «ليس يأتيني» – «فله درهمٌ», none of that would be permissible, because a conditional particle cannot validly enter upon any of these. As for limiting it to the verb, that is not so either; rather the adverbial and the preposition with its genitive noun in the ṣila (relative clause) are the same: whenever either of them is the ṣila of a relative noun, the entry of the fāʾ is permissible. And his saying «and when no governor that changes its meaning enters upon «الذي»» is an unrefined expression, because a governor does not change the meaning of the relative noun; it only changes the meaning of the inceptive position (ibtidāʾ), by making it into a wish, a hope or a supposition, as in: «لعل الذي يأتيني» – or «ليت الذي يأتيني», or «ظننت الذي يأتيني» – «فله درهمٌ»; the entry of the fāʾ is not permitted because the meaning of the inceptive has changed."
He also ought to have said: "and it is a condition that the khabar be deserved by virtue of the ṣila, as in the noble verse, because the reward is consequent only upon the spending."
I say: The Shaykh's saying as well, "rather every relative noun", means the ruling is not limited to every relative noun either; rather every indefinite noun described by something that may be a ṣila, which permits the entry of the fāʾ, or whatever is annexed to that indefinite noun, or to that relative noun, or to what is described by the relative noun, has the same ruling. I have already presented this issue thoroughly.

semin-durr:276-276.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {يَمْحَقُ الله الربا وَيُرْبِي}: The majority read both verbs in the light form, from مَحَقَ and أَرْبى. Ibn al-Zubayr read, and it is also narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: «يُمْحِّق ويُرَبِّي» with shadda (doubling) on both, from «مَحَّق» and «رَبَّى», both with shadda.
And His saying: {سَلَفَ}: سَلَفَ means "passed and elapsed"; hence «سالفُ الدهرِ» (the bygone age), and «له سَلَفٌ صالح» (he has righteous predecessors): forebears who went before. Also from it is {فَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ سَلَفاً}, that is, a nation gone before, from whom those after them take a lesson. سَلَف has the plurals أَسْلاف and سُلوف. «السالِفَةُ» and «السُّلاف» are those who go before in war or travel. «السالفةُ» of the face is so called because it comes foremost. The poet said:
1103 - ومَيَّةُ أحسنُ الثَّقَلَيْنِ جِيداً ... وسالفةً وأَحْسَنْه قَذالا
(Mayya is the most beautiful of the two weighty kinds [jinn and humans] in neck and in the side of the face, and the most beautiful of them in the nape.)
«سُلافة الخمر» (the first run of the wine) is so called because it comes before the pressing. «السُّلْفَةُ» is what is served first of food to a guest. It is said: «سَلِّفوا ضيفكم ولَهِّنوه», that is, hasten to him with something. From it also is «السَّلَفُ في الدَّيْن» (advance payment in debt), because money was given before it.
And His saying: {عَادَ}, that is, "returned". One says: عادَ يعود عَوْداً ومَعاداً. It is reported from some that it may mean "became" (صار), and on that basis:
1104 - وبالمَحْضِ حتى عاد جَعْداً عَنَطْنَطَا ... إذا قام ساوى غاربَ الفَحْلِ غاربُه
(With pure milk, until he became curly-haired and tall; when he stands, his shoulder-top is level with the shoulder-top of the stallion camel.)
And they recited:
1105 - تُعِدُّ لكم جَزْرُ الجَزُورِ رماحُنا ... ويَرْجِعْنَ بالأسيافِ مُنْكَسِرَاتِ
(Our spears prepare for you the slaughtered she-camel's butchering, and they return, with the swords, broken.)
«المَحْقُ» is diminution. One says: مَحَقْتُهُ فانمَحَقَ, and امتَحَقَ. From it comes «المُحاق» of the moon (the waning to disappearance). He said:
1106 - يَزْداد حتى إذا ما تَمَّ أَعقَبهُ ... كَرُّ الجديدَيْنِ نَقْصاً ثم يَنْمَحِقُ
(It grows until, when it is full, the turning of night and day follows it with waning, and then it vanishes.)
And Ibn al-Sikkīt recited:
1107 - وَأَمْصَلْتُ مالي كلَّه بحياتِهِ ... وماسُسْتَ من شيءٍ فَرَبُّكَ ماحِقُهْ
(I wasted all my wealth during his life; and whatever you have managed of anything, your Lord will destroy it.)
One also says: «هَجِيرٌ ماحِقٌ» when its heat diminishes everything.
This verse comprises two types of badīʿ (rhetorical embellishment). One is ṭibāq (antithesis) in His saying «يَمْحَقُ ويُرْبي», for the two are opposites, like {أَضْحَكَ وأبكى} [al-Najm: 43]. The second is tajnīs al-taghāyur (paronomasia of difference) in His saying «الرِّبا ويُرْبى», since one of them is a noun and the other a verb.

semin-durr:281-281.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {تُرْجَعُونَ فِيهِ}: this clause is in the position of an accusative, as a ṣifa (adjective) of the adverbial noun. Abū ʿAmr read «تَرْجِعُون» with fatḥa on the tāʾ, in the active voice, and the others read it in the passive. Al-Ḥasan read «يَرْجِعُون» with the yāʾ of the third person, as an iltifāt (shift of person). Ibn Jinnī said: "It is as though Allah the Exalted showed gentleness to the believers, so as not to address them directly with mention of the return, since it is something at which hearts are rent; so He said to them «واتقوا», then turned, in mentioning the return, to the third person and said «يَرْجِعُون»."
His saying: {وَهُمْ لاَ يُظْلَمُونَ} is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from «كلِّ نفس», and it is in the plural in regard to the meaning. The pronoun referring back to it was first in the singular in «كَسَبَتْ», in regard to the wording. Regard for the wording was put first because it is the basic rule, and because regard for the meaning occurred at the head of a verse-ending (fāṣila), so postponing it was better.
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is possible that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يُرْجَعُون» according to the reading with yāʾ, and it is possible that it is a ḥāl from it also according to the reading with tāʾ, on the basis that it is a departure from the second person to the third person, like His saying, the Exalted: {حتى إِذَا كُنتُمْ فِي الفلك وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِم} [Yūnus: 22]." There is no necessity calling for what he mentioned.

semin-durr:199-199.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {ثُمَّ أَفِيضُواْ مِنْ حَيْثُ}: People found the occurrence of «ثم» here problematic, because the second pouring forth (ifāḍa) is the same as the first: the Quraysh used to stand at Muzdalifa while the rest of the people stood at ʿArafa, so they were commanded to pour forth from ʿArafa like the rest of the people. How then can «ثم», which implies sequence and delay, be used? There are several answers on this. The first: that the sequence is in the mention, not in the time in which the acts occur. What makes this fitting is that the first pouring forth is not commanded; what is commanded is the remembrance of Allah when the pouring forth has been performed. The second: that this clause is conjoined to His saying {واتقوني يا أولي}, so the speech involves fronting and postponing, and this is far-fetched. The third: that «ثم» has the meaning of «و» (wāw); some grammarians have said this, so it joins one statement to a statement that is separate from the first. The fourth: that the second pouring forth is from Jamʿ (Muzdalifa) to Minā, and those addressed by it are all the people. A group, such as al-Ḍaḥḥāk, said this, and al-Ṭabarī preferred it, and it is what the apparent sense of the Qur'an requires; on this view «ثم» is in its proper sense. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how is the position of «ثم»? I say: like its position in your saying «أحْسِنْ إلى الناس ثم لا تُحْسِن إلى غير كريم» ('Be good to people, then do not be good to anyone ungenerous'). You bring «ثم» for the disparity between being good to the generous and being good to others, and the distance between the two. Likewise when He commanded them to remember Allah at the pouring forth from ʿArafāt, He said «ثم أفيضوا» for the disparity between the two pourings forth, one of which is right and the other wrong." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "The verse is not a parallel to the example he gave. The gist of what he mentioned is that «ثم» removes sequence and has another meaning other than it, which he called disparity and distance of what follows it from what precedes it. He did not mention in the verse a pouring forth of error, so that «ثم» might come for the disparity between them, and we know of no one who preceded him in establishing this meaning for «ثم»." And this objection by the Shaykh against al-Zamakhsharī is an attack on him, for by disparity and distance he means the delay occurring between the two ranks. Parallels to it will come, and a man like this is not to be refuted by such things.

And «من حيث» is attached to «أَفيضوا», and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the range (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), and «حيث» here is in its proper sense as an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). Al-Qaffāl said: "Here it refers to the time of the pouring forth." It has already been mentioned that this is the view of al-Akhfash, and its evidence was given. It is as if al-Qaffāl sought by this to distinguish between the two pourings forth so that the answer to the occurrence of «ثم» here would stand, but that does not help, because time necessarily implies the place of the act occurring in it.

And «أفاض الناسُ» is in the position of genitive by the annexation of «حيثُ» to it. The majority read «الناسُ» with ḍamma on the sīn.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read: «الناسي», and there are two interpretations of it. The first: that Ādam, peace be upon him, is meant by it, and they supported it with His saying: {فَنَسِيَ وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُ عَزْماً} [Ṭāhā: 115]. The second: that it means the one who abandons the standing at Muzdalifa, and they are the whole of the people, so what is meant by «الناسي» is the genus of those who forget. [Translator's note: the source prints «حنسَ», evidently a misprint for «جنسَ» (genus).] Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "According to some, dropping the yāʾ is permissible, so one says «الناس», like «القاضِ» and «الهادِ»." He said: "As for its permissibility in Arabic, Sībawayh mentioned it; as for its permissibility as a reading, I do not know of it." The Shaykh said: "Sībawayh did not permit that except in poetry, and al-Farrāʾ permitted it in prose. As for his saying 'I do not know of it,' others have memorized it: al-Mahdawī transmitted it as a reading from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr also."

His saying: {واستغفروا الله}: «استغفر» takes two objects, the first directly, and the second with «مِنْ», as in: «استغفرتُ الله من ذنبي» ("I asked Allah's forgiveness for my sin"). The preposition may be omitted, as in his saying:

890 - أستغفرُ اللهَ ذنباً لستُ مُحْصِيَه ... ربُّ العبادِ إليه الوجهُ والعَمَلُ
(I seek Allah's forgiveness for a sin I cannot count; the Lord of the servants, to Him are the face and the deed.)

This is the view of Sībawayh and the majority of people. Ibn al-Ṭarāwa said: it takes both directly in origin, and it takes «من» only because it includes the meaning of what takes it, so for him «استغفرت الله من كذا» means "I repented to Him of such and such." «استغفر» does not come in the Qur'an taking an object other than the first alone. As for His saying, the Exalted: {واستغفر لِذَنبِكَ} [Ghāfir: 55], {واستغفري لِذَنبِكِ} [Yūsuf: 29], {فاستغفروا لِذُنُوبِهِمْ} [Āl ʿImrān: 135], the apparent sense is that this lām is the lām of cause, not the lām of transitivity, and its genitive noun is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), not a direct object. As for «غَفَر», its object is mentioned in the Qur'an at times: {وَمَن يَغْفِرُ الذنوب إِلاَّ الله} [Āl ʿImrān: 135], and omitted at others: {وَيَغْفِرُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ} [al-Māʾida: 40]. The sīn in «استغفر» is for requesting, in its proper sense. The second object here is omitted because it is known, i.e. "of your sins that have occurred from you."

semin-durr:201-201.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فِي الدنيا حَسَنَةً}: Two analyses are allowed for the preposition and its genitive noun. The first: that it is attached to «آتِنا» like the one before it. The second, which Abū l-Baqāʾ permitted: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «حسنةً», because originally it was an adjective of it, and when it was placed before it, it became accusative as a ḥāl.

His saying: {وَفِي الآخرة حَسَنَةً}: This wāw is a conjunction joining two things to two things that precede. So «في الآخرة» is conjoined to «في الدنيا» by repeating the governing element, and «حسنةً» is conjoined to «حسنةٍ». The wāw joins two or more things to two or more things. You say: «أَعْلَمَ الله زيداً عمراً فاضلاً وبكراً خالداً صالحاً» ("Allah informed Zayd that ʿAmr is virtuous, and Bakr that Khālid is righteous"). The exception is where it stands in for two governing elements: there the grammarians disagree, with much detail that will come in its place, Allah willing. And this is not, as some claimed, a case of separation between the conjunction (which consists of a single letter) and the conjoined word by a preposition and its genitive noun, which he made into evidence against Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī, who forbade that except in necessity; for this is a case of joining two things to two things, as I have told you, not a case of separation. The point of disagreement is only something like: «أكرمت زيداً وعندك عمراً» ("I honoured Zayd, and with you, ʿAmr"). Abū ʿAlī is refuted only by His saying: {إِنَّ الله يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَن تُؤدُّواْ الأمانات إلى أَهْلِهَا وَإِذَا حَكَمْتُمْ بَيْنَ الناس أَن تَحْكُمُواْ [بالعدل]} [al-Nisāʾ: 58] and His saying, the Exalted: {الله الذي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ وَمِنَ الأرض مِثْلَهُنَّ} [al-Ṭalāq: 12].

And His saying: «قِنا» is among the words from which both the first radical (fāʾ) and the last radical (lām) have been dropped, from وقى يقي وقاية. As for the dropping of its fāʾ, it is by analogy with the imperfect, because the wāw falls between a yāʾ and a kasra. As for the dropping of its lām, it is because the imperative follows the course of the jussive imperfect, whose jussive is by dropping the weak letter, so the imperative from it is likewise. So the pattern of «قِنا» is then «عِنا», and the original is «اوْقِنا»; when the fāʾ was dropped, the hamzat al-waṣl was no longer needed and was dropped. And «عذاب» is a second direct object (mafʿūl).

semin-durr:202-202.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أولئك}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «لهم» is a fronted khabar (predicate), and «نصيب» is a mubtadaʾ, and this clause is the khabar of the first. It is also permissible that «لهم» be the khabar of «أولئك», and «نصيب» be a fāʿil (agent) of it, because of the verbal meaning it contains, owing to its reliance on a preceding element. As for what is pointed to by «أولئك», there are two views, the more apparent of them being that it refers to both groups: the one who seeks this world alone and the one who seeks this world and the Hereafter. It was also said: rather, it refers only to the last group, I mean the one who seeks this world and the Hereafter.

His saying: {مِّمَّا كَسَبُواْ} is attached to an omitted element because it is an adjective of «نصيب», so it is in the position of nominative. Regarding «مِنْ» there are three views. The first: that it is partitive (li-l-tabʿīḍ), i.e. a share of the kind of what they earned. The second: that it denotes cause, i.e. on account of what they earned. The third: that it is explicative (li-l-bayān). As for «ما», two analyses are possible. That it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) particle, i.e. "from their earning", in which case it needs no returning pronoun (ʿāʾid). The second: that it means «الذي» (that which), in which case the returning pronoun is omitted because the conditions for omission are complete, i.e. "from that which they earned".

semin-durr:219-219.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {عَنِ الخمر والميسر}: al-khamr is what is pressed from grapes once it has boiled and cast up foam; and, figuratively (majāzan), the name is applied to whatever has boiled and cast up foam from something other than grape juice.

There are four views on why it is called «khamr». The first, which is the well-known one, is that it was so named because it yakhmuru the intellect, that is, covers it; hence the khimār of a woman, because it covers her face; and the saying «خامِري حَضاجِرُ، أتَاك ما تُحَاذِرُ» ("Hide yourself, Ḥaḍājir, what you fear has come to you"), said of a fool (Ḥaḍājir being a proper name for the hyena), that is: hide yourself from people. And «he entered into the khimār of the people and their ghimār» (their throng). And in the ḥadīth: «خَمِّروا آنيتَكم» ("Cover your vessels"). And the poet said:

941 - ألا يا زيدُ والضحاكَ سِيرا ... فَقَدْ جاوَزْتُما خَمَرَ الطرِيقِ
("Zayd and Ḍaḥḥāk, travel on, for you have passed the khamar of the road")

that is, whatever hides you of trees and the like. And al-ʿAjjāj said, describing the march of an army that is plainly visible: 942 - في لامعِ العِقْبَانِ لا يَمْشِي الخَمَرْ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
("In the gleam of the eagles, one does not walk under cover…")

The second: because it is covered (tughaṭṭā) until it matures and becomes strong; hence «خَمِّروا آنيتَكم».

The third, said Ibn al-Anbārī: because it yukhāmiru the intellect, that is, mingles with it; one says "the disease khāmarahu", meaning it mingled with him. The fourth: because it is left until it matures; hence «اختمر العجينُ» ("the dough has fermented"), that is, it has reached its maturity; and «khammara the opinion», that is, he left it until the right course became clear to him in it. These views are close to one another. On all of these views, khamr is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) meant in the sense of the active participle or the passive participle.

And al-maysir is gambling; it is of the pattern mafʿil, from al-yusr, and one says yasara, yaysiru. ʿAlqama said:

943 - لو يَيْسِرون بخيلٍ قد يَسَرْتُ بها ... وكلُّ ما يَسَرَ الأقَوامُ مَغْرومُ
("If they gambled with horses, I would have gambled with them; and everything peoples gamble for is a loss")

and another said:

944 - أقولُ لهم بالشِّعْبِ إذ يَيْسِرونَني ... ألم تَيْئَسوا أني ابنُ فارسِ زَهْدَمِ
("I say to them in the mountain pass as they gamble against me: have you not despaired, for I am the son of the horseman Zahdam?")

There are four views on its derivation. The first: from al-yusr, which is ease, because taking it is easy. The second: from al-yasār, which is wealth, because it strips a man of his wealth. The third: from "yasara lī kadhā", meaning "it became obligatory for me"; al-Ṭabarī related this from Mujāhid, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejected it. The fourth: from yasara when he butchered, the yāsir being the butcher, who divides the slaughtered camel into portions. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «The camel over which lots were cast was called maysir because it is the place of al-yusr; then the arrows were called maysir by proximity.» And al-yasar is the one who enters into the striking with the arrows; its plural is ayṣār; and it was said rather that «yussar» is the plural of yāsir, like ḥāris, ḥurras and aḥrās.

Maysir has a manner of play, and its arrows, which are also called al-qidāḥ and al-azlām, have names that must be mentioned because the meaning depends on them. The manner is that they had ten arrows (and it is said eleven), seven of which carry shares, and each of them bears lines, the line determining the share. Those arrows are: al-fadhdh, which has one share; al-tawʾam, which has two; al-raqīb, which has three; al-ḥils, which has four; al-nāfis, which has five; al-musbil, which has six; and al-muʿallā, which has seven; and three blanks (aghfāl) on which there are no lines, namely al-manīḥ, al-safīḥ and al-waghd; and whoever added a fourth called it al-muḍaʿʿaf. They multiplied the blanks only so that things would be confused for the ḥurḍa, who is the striker, so that he would not lean toward anyone; he is a man of integrity in their eyes. He crouches, wraps himself in a garment and puts his head out, then places those arrows in the rabāba, which is the bag; then he shakes them, puts his hand into it, and draws out an arrow in the name of each man in turn. Whoever has an arrow drawn in his name: if it is one of those with shares, he wins that portion and takes it; and if it is one of the blanks, he is made to pay for the camel. They used to do this in winter and in hardship of life, and they would distribute it to the poor and eat nothing of it themselves, and they boasted of that, and they called whoever did not join them in it al-baram. The camel is divided, according to the majority, by the number of arrows, so it is divided into ten parts; according to al-Aṣmaʿī, by the number of the lines on the arrows, so it is divided into twenty-eight parts.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya declared al-Aṣmaʿī mistaken in this, which is astonishing of him, because it is possible that the Arabs divided it at one time into ten and at another into twenty-eight.

His saying {عَنِ الخمر}: an omitted muḍāf (the first term of a genitive construct) is necessary, since a question about the essences of khamr and maysir is not intended. The implied form is: "about the ruling on khamr and maysir, as to permissibility and prohibition"; and for that reason the answer came in keeping with this implied term.

His saying: {فِيهِمَآ إِثْمٌ كَبِيرٌ}: the preposition and its genitive noun is a fronted khabar (predicate) and «إثمٌ» is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). The fronting of the khabar here is not obligatory even though the mubtadaʾ is indefinite, because there is another justifier here, namely the qualification (the adjective) or the conjunction. An omitted muḍāf is also necessary, that is: "in their practice there is sin", because the sin is not in their essence.

Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «كثيرٌ» with the thā' of three dots, and the rest with the bāʾ of one dot beneath. The reasoning for the reading of the majority is clear: sin is described as kibar (great), and from it is the verse {حُوباً كَبِيراً} [al-Nisāʾ: 2]. And the ruinous acts are called «al-kabāʾir» (the major sins), and from it is His saying, the Exalted: {يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبَائِرَ الإثم} [al-Shūrā: 37]; and drinking khamr and gambling are among the major sins, so describing their sin as great is fitting. The Seven agreed on His saying «وإثْمهما أكبرُ» with the single-dotted bāʾ, and this reading agrees with it in wording.

As for the reasoning for the reading of the two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī): either with regard to the sinners among the drinkers and gamblers, for each one has a sin; or with regard to what follows from their practice, namely the succession and multiplication of punishment; or with regard to what follows from drinking it, namely the evil words and ugly deeds that issue from the one who drinks it; or with regard to whoever deals with it from the time it was grapes until it is drunk, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed khamr and cursed with it ten: its seller and its buyer…, so it was fitting that its sin be described as abundant (kathīr). Moreover, His saying «إثم» is set against «منافع», and «منافع» is a plural, so it was fitting that, by way of correspondence, it be described with the sense of plurality, which is abundance. And this is what a person ought to do with the Qur'an: to give for each reading a justification without exposing the other reading to being declared weak, as some have done; and a good section on this has already preceded, on the two readings «مَلِكَ» and «مالِك».

Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «The better reading is with the bāʾ, because one says "a great sin and a small one", and of the grave indecencies one says "al-kabāʾir" and of what is less than that "al-ṣaghāʾir". It has also been read with the thāʾ, and it is good in meaning, because abundance is greatness (kibar), and the abundant is great, just as the small is paltry and slight.»

semin-durr:168-168.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِمَّا فِي الأرض حَلاَلاً طَيِّباً}: As for «حلالاً», there are five aspects of i'rab. The first: that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «كُلوا». On this view «مِنْ» has two aspects. The first: that it is attached to «كُلوا», its meaning being the beginning of the range (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya). The second: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «حلالاً»; originally it was an adjective of it, but when it was placed before it, it became accusative as a ḥāl, and the meaning of «مِنْ» is partitive (tabʿīḍ). The second: that «حلالاً» is accusative as an naʿt (adjective) of an omitted direct object, its implied form being "something" or "provision, lawful" (شيئاً أو زرقاً حلالاً) — Makkī mentioned it, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya considered it far-fetched without explaining why he thought it far-fetched. What appears to be the reason for its being far-fetched is that «حلالاً» is not an adjective specific to what is eaten; rather what is eaten and other things are described by it, and when an adjective is not specific, omitting the thing described is not permissible. [Translator's note: the source prints «زرقاً»; «رزقاً» (provision) is presumably intended.] The third: that «حلالاً» is accusative as a ḥāl of «ما», in the sense of "that which", i.e. "eat of that which is in the earth while it is lawful". The fourth: that it is accusative as an naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "lawful eating" (أكلاً حلالاً), the direct object of «كُلوا» being omitted and «ما في الأرض» being an adjective of that omitted direct object. Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned it, and it is open to the same objection raised above against Makkī. On this fourth aspect it is also possible that the direct object is not omitted, but rather «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) according to the school of al-Akhfash, the implied form being: "Eat what is in the earth, a lawful eating." The fifth: that it is a ḥāl of the pronoun that refers back to «ما» — Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this, meaning by the pronoun the latent (mustakinn) pronoun in the preposition and its genitive noun that serves as the ṣila (relative clause).

As for «طيباً», it has three aspects. The first: that it is an adjective of «حلالاً». On the view that «مِنْ» denotes the beginning of the range and is attached to «كُلوا», this is clear. But on the view that «مِما في الأرض» is a ḥāl of «حلالاً», Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "But its place is after the preposition and its genitive noun, so that the adjective may not separate the ḥāl from the owner of the ḥāl." What he said is of no substance, for separating the ḥāl from its owner by an adjective is not forbidden; you say: "Zayd the tall came to me riding" (جاءني زيدٌ الطويلُ راكباً); indeed, if you put the ḥāl before the adjective and said "Zayd came to me riding, the tall" (جاءني زيدٌ راكباً الطويلُ), its permissibility would be open to consideration. The second: that it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, or a ḥāl of the omitted definite maṣdar, i.e. "good eating" (أكلاً طيباً). The third: that it is a ḥāl of the pronoun in «كُلوا», its implied form being "finding it good" (مستطيبين) — Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This is faulty in both wording and meaning. As for the wording, «الطيّب» is an active participle, so it ought to be pluralised to agree with its owner, so that one would say «طيبين»; and «طيب» is not a maṣdar, so that it could be said that it was not pluralised for that reason. As for the meaning, «طيباً» differs from «مستطيبين» in meaning, because goodness is among the attributes of what is eaten, while finding good is among the attributes of those who eat. You say: 'The food was good for Zayd' (طاب لزيدٍ الطعامُ), and you do not say 'Zayd was good [with] the food' (طابَ زيدٌ الطعام) in the sense that he found it good."

Al-ḥalāl: what is permitted, the opposite of al-ḥarām, what is prohibited. [It is said:] ḥalla yaḥillu, with kasra on the ʿayn in the imperfect, and that is the regular form because the verb is doubled and intransitive. One says ḥalāl and ḥill, like ḥarām and ḥaram, and it is originally a maṣdar. One also says "ḥillun billun" by way of rhyming echo (ittibāʿ), like "ḥasanun basanun". And ḥalla bi-makān kadhā ("he alighted at such a place") is yaḥullu, with ḍamma or kasra on the ʿayn; and it was read {فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبِي} [Ṭā Hā: 81] in both ways.

His saying: {خُطُواتِ}: Ibn ʿĀmir, al-Kisāʾī, Qunbul and Ḥafṣ read «خُطُوات» with ḍamma on the khāʾ and the ṭāʾ; the rest of the seven read it with sukūn on the ṭāʾ. Abū l-Sammāl read «خُطَوات» with fatḥa on it [the ṭāʾ]; Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others transmitted from him that he read «خَطَوات» with fatḥa on the khāʾ and the ṭāʾ. ʿAlī, Qatāda and al-Aʿmash read it with ḍamma on both and with hamza.

As for the reading of the majority and the first of the two readings of Abū l-Sammāl: when a «فَعْلَة» with sukūn on the ʿayn and sound is a noun, three forms are permissible in forming its sound feminine plural (with alif and tāʾ) — and they are dialects heard from the Arabs: sukūn, which is the original; ittibāʿ (vowel harmony); and fatḥa on the ʿayn for lightness. As for the reading of Abū l-Sammāl that Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmitted, it is the plural of «خَطْوة» with fatḥa on the khāʾ. The difference between «الخُطْوة» with ḍamma and with fatḥa is that the one with fatḥa is a maṣdar indicating a single instance, from khaṭā yakhṭū when one walks, while the one with ḍamma is a noun for what is between the two feet, as though it were a name for the distance, like «الغُرْفة», a name for what is scooped up. It is also said that they are two dialects with one meaning; Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned it.

As for the reading of ʿAlī, it admits two interpretations. The first — al-Akhfash said this — is that the hamza is original and that it comes from «الخطأ» (error), and «خُطُؤات» is the plural of «خِطْأة» if that is heard, otherwise it is by supposition. Mujāhid's explanation of it as "sins/errors" (الخطايا) supports this, though it is possible that Mujāhid explained it by a synonym. The second: that he changed the hamza from wāw because it neighboured the ḍamma before it, so that it was as though it were on it, because the vowel of a letter is in front of it, on the sound view, not on it.

His saying: {إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ}: Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "He put kasra on the hamza only because he meant to inform about its state, and that is more eloquent than fatḥa, because if he put fatḥa on the hamza the implied form would be: 'Do not follow him because he is an enemy to you', and following him is forbidden even if he were not an enemy to us. Similar to it:

810 - لبَّيْكَ إنَّ الحَمْدَ لك ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Here I am at Your service; verily praise is Yours …)

Kasra on the hamza is better because kasra indicates that He deserves praise in every case, and likewise the talbiya." End of his words. He means that the kasra is a resumptive (istiʾnāf), so it is a kind of report of that. But what he said about the reason for the kasra is not conclusive, because it is possible that causation is intended even with kasra on the hamza, for they stated explicitly that kasra-ed «إنّ» also conveys the cause, and he himself mentioned that in this very verse. So it should be said: the kasra reading is preferable because it admits both a pure report of its state and causation, whereas the fatḥa reading is explicit as to causation, because the speech is on the assumption of the lām of cause. [Translator's note: the source prints «المسكروة» for the kasra-ed «إنّ»; «المكسورة» is evidently intended.]

semin-durr:169-169.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَن تَقُولُواْ}: It is conjoined (ʿaṭf) to his saying «بالسوءِ», its implied form being «وبأنْ تقولوا» ("and with your saying"). Its position may be genitive or accusative, according to the two views of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh. «الفحشاءُ» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) from «الفُحْش», like «البأساء» from «البأْس». Al-fuḥsh is ugliness of appearance. Imruʾ al-Qays said:

811 - وجِيدٍ كجيدٍ الرِّئْمِ ليس بفاحِشٍ ... إذا هي نَصَّتْهُ ولا بِمُعَطَّلِ
(And a neck like the neck of the white gazelle, not ugly when she raises it, nor bare of ornament.)

It was then extended in usage until it came to express everything deemed ugly, whether in meaning or in substance.

semin-durr:170-170.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ}: As for the pronoun in «لهم», there are four views. The first: that it refers back to «مَنْ» in His saying {مَن يَتَّخِذُ} [al-Baqara: 165]; this is far-fetched. The second: that it refers to the disbelieving Arabs, because this is their condition. The third: that it refers to the Jews, because they are the people who most closely follow their forebears. The fourth: that it refers to «الناس» in His saying {يَا أَيُّهَا الناس} [al-Baqara: 168] — al-Ṭabarī said this, and it is the apparent view, except that this would be a case of iltifāt (shift) from address to the third person; its wisdom is that they were presented in the form of an absent person whose action is a cause for wonder, since he was called to the law of Allah, to light and guidance, and answered by following the way of his father.

His saying: {بَلْ نَتَّبِعُ}: «بل» here conjoins this clause to an omitted clause before it, its implied form being: "We do not follow what Allah has sent down; rather we follow such-and-such." It is not permissible for it to be conjoined to His saying «اتَّبِعُوا», because that would be invalid. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: «بل» here is for iḍrāb (turning away) from the first, i.e. "We do not follow what Allah has sent down", and it is not a transition from one story to another. He means by that that it is an iḍrāb of invalidation (ibṭāl), not an iḍrāb of transition (intiqāl). On this view it would be said: every iḍrāb in the Qur'an means transition from one story to another except in this verse and except in His saying {أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افتراه بَلْ هُوَ الحق} [al-Sajda: 3], for it admits both possibilities: if you take His saying «أم يقولون افتراه» as a whole, it is an iḍrāb of transition; and if you take «افتراه» alone, it is an iḍrāb of invalidation.

His saying: {أَلْفَيْنَا}: As for «ألفى» here, there are two views. The first: that it is transitive to one object, because it has the meaning of «وَجَدَ» in the sense of "he came upon"; on this view «عليه» is attached to His saying «أَلْفينَا». The second: that it is transitive to two objects, the first being «آباءَنا» and the second «عليه», which was placed before the first. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It admits both, I mean its being transitive to one or to two." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The lām of «أَلْفَيْنَا» is a wāw, because the principle regarding third radicals of unknown origin is that they be wāw" — meaning that it is wider and more frequent, so referring it back to it is preferable.

His saying: {أَوَلَوْ}: The hamza is for denial (inkār). As for the wāw, there are two views. The first — al-Zamakhsharī held it — that it is the wāw of ḥāl. The second — Abū l-Baqāʾ and Ibn ʿAṭiyya held it — that it is for conjunction. The disagreement has already preceded about this hamza occurring before the wāw, the fāʾ and «ثُمَّ»: is there an implied clause after it? That is the opinion of al-Zamakhsharī, and so he implied here: "Do they follow them even if their forefathers understood nothing of the religion and were not guided to what is right?" Or is the intention that it be placed after the conjunction particle? The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] combined the view of al-Zamakhsharī and the view of Ibn ʿAṭiyya and said: "The way to combine them is that the clause accompanied by «لو» in a context like this is a conditional clause. When he says 'Strike Zayd even if he does good to you' the meaning is 'even if he does good to you' (وإنْ أَحسَنَ إليكَ); likewise 'Give to the beggar even if he comes on a horse' and 'Turn the beggar away even with half a date': the meaning in both is «وإنْ» ('even if'). «لو» comes here as a warning that what follows it does not suit what precedes it, but it comes to cover the exhaustive range of circumstances in which the act occurs, and to indicate that what is meant is the occurrence of the act in every circumstance, even in this circumstance which does not suit the act. For this reason it is not permissible to say 'Strike Zayd even if he wronged you' (اضربْ زيداً ولو أساء إليكَ), nor 'Give to the beggar even if he is needy' (أَعْطُوا السائل ولو كان محتاجاً). Once this is established, the wāw in «ولو» in the examples we mentioned is a conjunction upon an implied ḥāl, and what is conjoined to a ḥāl is a ḥāl. So it is valid to say it is for ḥāl insofar as it conjoins a circumstantial clause to an implied ḥāl, and valid to say it is for conjunction insofar as that conjunction goes.
