And the meaning — and Allah knows best — is that it is a denial of their following their forefathers in every circumstance, even in the circumstance in which it would be fitting for them to follow them, namely their being characterised by lack of understanding and guidance. For this reason it is not permissible to drop this wāw that enters «لو» when it is a warning that what follows does not suit what precedes, even if the circumstantial clause contains a pronoun referring back to the owner of the ḥāl, because its appearing bare of this wāw signals restriction of the preceding clause by this circumstance.

That would contradict the inclusion of all circumstances, even this one, so they are two different meanings; hence the difference appears between «أَكْرِمْ زَيْداً لو جَفَاك» ('Honour Zayd were he to wrong you') and «أكْرمْ زيداً ولو جَفَاك» ('Honour Zayd even if he wrongs you')." End of his words. It is fine speech. The apodosis (jawāb) of «لو» is omitted, its implied form being "they would follow them" (لاتَّبعوهم); Abū l-Baqāʾ implied it as «أفكانوا يَتَّبِعونهم» ("would they then follow them?"), which is an explanation of meaning, because «لو» is not answered by the interrogative hamza.

His saying: {شَيْئاً}: There are two aspects. The first: that it is a mafʿūl bihi, so it covers all things that can be understood, because it is indefinite in a negative context; and it is not permissible that what is meant is the negation of oneness, so that the meaning would be "they do not understand one thing but rather several things". The second: that it is accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. "they do not understand anything of understanding" (لا يَعْقِلُون شيئاً من العقلِ). He placed the negation of understanding before the negation of guidance, because all actions issue from it.

semin-durr:278-278.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَذَرُواْ}: The ʿayn (middle radical) of «ذَرْ» takes fatḥa by analogy with «دَعْ», since it has its meaning; and it takes fatḥa in «دَعْ» because it is the imperative of «يَدَعُ»; and in «يَدَعُ» it takes fatḥa, although by analogy it should take kasra because the first radical is a wāw, like «يَعِدُ», because its lām (final radical) is a guttural letter.
The pattern of «ذروا» is «عَلوا», because with the omitted first radical no past tense is used from it except in a minor dialect, and likewise «دَعْ».
Al-Ḥasan read «ما بَقَا», turning the kasra into fatḥa and the yāʾ into alif; this is a dialect of Ṭayyiʾ and of others. From it is the saying of ʿAlqama al-Tamīmī:
1108 - زَهَا الشوقُ حتى ظَلَّ إنسانُ عينِهِ ... يَفِيضُ بمغمورٍ من الدَّمْعِ مُتْأَقِ
(Longing swelled until the pupil of his eye kept overflowing with abundant, brimming tears.)
And another said:
1109 - وما الدُّنيا بباقاةٍ علينا ... وما حَيٌّ على الدنيا بباقِ
(The world is not lasting for us, and no living being on the world is lasting.)
And they say «ناصاةٌ» for «ناصيةٌ» (forelock). Al-Ḥasan also read «بَقِيْ» with the yāʾ quiescent. Al-Mubarrad said: "Making quiescent the yāʾ of a defective noun in the accusative is among the best of poetic licences; this being so although it is declinable, it is better still in the past-tense verb." I say: If they have dropped it from a past-tense verb whose last letter is sound, then all the more so from a weak letter. He said:
1110 - إنما شِعْرِيَ قَيْدٌ ... قد خُلْطَ بجُلْجُلانْ
(My poetry is but a fetter that has been mixed with sesame.)
And Jarīr said, regarding making the yāʾ quiescent:
1111 - هو الخليفةُ فارضُوا ما رَضِيْ لكمُ ... ماضي العزيمةِ ما في حُكْمِهِ جَنَفُ
(He is the caliph, so be content with what he has been content with for you: resolute in purpose, in whose judgement there is no injustice.)
And another said:
1112 - لَعَمْرُكَ لا أخشى التَّصَعْلكَ ما بقِي ... على الأرضِ قَيْسِيٌّ يسوق الأباعرا
(By your life, I do not fear poverty so long as there remains on earth a man of Qays driving camels.)
His saying: {مِنَ الربا} is attached to «بقيَ», as in their saying «بَقِيَتْ منه بقيةٌ» (a remainder remained of it). What appears is that it is attached to an omitted element, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «بقَى», that is, "what remained, being part of the ribā"; so the «مِن» is partitive.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported here that al-ʿAdawī, namely Abū al-Sammāl, read «من الرِّبُو», with rāʾ doubled and kasra, and ḍamma on the bāʾ after which comes a wāw. I say: I have already presented that Abū al-Sammāl read «الربا» only at the beginning of the verse, with a wāw after a fatḥa on the bāʾ, and that Abū Zayd related from some that they put ḍamma on the bāʾ; and I presented the analysis of both, despite its weakness.
Ibn Jinnī said: "This word is anomalous in two respects. One: moving from kasra to ḍamma in a permanent structure. The other: the occurrence of a wāw after a ḍamma at the end of a noun; this occurs only in the verb, such as «يَغْزُو» and «يَدْعُو». As for the Ṭayyiʾī «ذو» meaning «الذي», it is extremely anomalous, and among them are those who change its wāw when it departs from the nominative, saying «رأيتُ ذا قام». The justification of the reading is that when he pronounced the alif with heaviness (tafkhīm), he inclined it toward the wāw of which the alif is a substitute, in the manner of their saying «الصلاةُ والزكاةُ»; and in sum it is an anomalous reading." I say: Others qualify the wording, saying: "There is no declinable noun with a wāw preceded by a ḍamma", so as to exclude «ذو» meaning «الذي» and «هو» among the pronouns. Ibn Jinnī did not mention the qualification; he excepted the Ṭayyiʾī «ذو», yet «هو» is an objection to him, and «ذو» meaning «صاحب» (possessor) is an objection to the wording, since it is declinable and its end is a wāw after a ḍamma.
It has been answered that it changes to alif and yāʾ, so it was paid no regard; moreover the ḍamma of the dāl is incidental, as its origin is fatḥa, and it was given ḍamma only by assimilation, as I have established in the i'rab of the six nouns in the grammar books. His saying "in a permanent structure" is a safeguard against cases of moving from kasra to ḍamma incidentally, such as «الحِبُك», since it arises from blending of forms, and such as «الرِّدُءْ» when one pauses on it; the move from kasra to ḍamma in these two words is not permanent. His saying "among them are those who change its wāw": the well-known usage is its being indeclinable on the wāw in every case, though it may be declined like the one meaning «صاحب», and they recited:
1113 - فإمَّا كِرامٌ مُوسِرُون لَقِيتُهمُ ... فَحَسْبي من ذي عندَهم ما كَفانيا
(Whether I meet generous, well-off men, it suffices me, from those who are with them, what suffices me.)
It is also narrated «مِنْ ذو», in accordance with the original form.
His saying: {إِن كُنْتُمْ} is a conditional, and its apodosis is omitted according to the majority, that is, "so fear [Allah] and give up"; according to a group the apodosis is the earlier clause. It was said: «إنْ» here has the meaning of «إذ»; this is rejected and disfavoured. It was said: what is intended by this condition here is continuity.

semin-durr:206-206.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُ اتق الله}: This conditional clause admits the two aforementioned possibilities that apply to its counterpart, namely that it is resumptive, or conjoined to «يُعْجِبُك». What stands in the place of the agent (here) and the disagreement of the people about it have also been discussed already, at the beginning of the surah, at His saying: {وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لاَ تُفْسِدُواْ}.

His saying «بالإِثمِ»: There are three views on this bāʾ. The first: that it is for transitivization (taʿdiya). This is the view of al-Zamakhsharī, who said: "'I took him with such-and-such' (akhadhtuhu bi-kadhā) when you made him carry it and bound him to it; that is: pride (al-ʿizza) carried him to sin and bound him to committing it." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "The bāʾ of transitivization is chiefly for the intransitive verb, as in {ذَهَبَ الله بِنُورِهِمْ} [al-Baqara: 17] and {[وَلَوْ شَآءَ الله لَذَهَبَ] بِسَمْعِهِمْ} [al-Baqara: 20]; transitivization by the bāʾ with a transitive verb is rare, as in 'ṣakaktu l-ḥajara bi-l-ḥajari' (I struck the stone with the stone), that is: I made one of them strike the other." The second: that it is for causation (sababiyya), meaning that his sin was the cause of pride seizing him, as in the saying (of the poet):

901 - أَخَذَتْهُ عِزَّةٌ مِنْ جَهْلِهِ ... فَتَوَلَّى مُغْضَباً فِعْلَ الضَّجِرْ
(Pride seized him out of his ignorance, so he turned away in anger, as the exasperated do.)

The third: that it is for accompaniment (muṣāḥaba), so that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); and in that case there are two views on it. The first: that it is a ḥāl from «العزَّةُ», i.e. "accompanied by sin". The second: that it is a ḥāl from the object, i.e. "pride seized him while he was accompanied by sin."

In His saying «العزَّةُ بالإِثم» there is tatmīm (completion), which is a type of the science of badīʿ (rhetorical embellishment). It means following a word with another that removes ambiguity from it and brings it closer to understanding. That is because ʿizza (might/pride) may be praiseworthy or blameworthy. Among its occurrences as praiseworthy: {وَلِلَّهِ العزة وَلِرَسُولِهِ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ} [al-Munāfiqūn: 8] and {أَعِزَّةٍ عَلَى الكافرين} [al-Māʾida: 54]. Had it been left unqualified, someone who pays no attention might have thought of the praiseworthy sense in it; so «بالإِثم» was said as a completion of the intended meaning, and the ambiguity was removed by it.

His saying: {فَحَسْبُهُ جَهَنَّمُ}: «حَسْبُهُ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «جهنَّمُ» its khabar (predicate), i.e. "Hell is sufficient for them." It was also said that «جهنَّمُ» is the fāʿil (agent) of «حَسْب». Then those who say this differ about «حَسْب». It was said: it has the sense of an active participle, i.e. "sufficient"; originally it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) intended as an active participle, and the agent, namely Jahannam, takes the place of the khabar; and «حَسْب» is strengthened by its reliance on the connecting fāʾ, which links the clause to what precedes it. All of this is the sense of Abū l-Baqāʾ's words. It was also said: rather «حَسْب» is an ism fiʿl (verbal noun, a noun with the force of a verb), and those who say this differ: it was said that it is an ism fiʿl of the past, i.e. "it sufficed them"; and it was said that it is an imperative, i.e. "let it suffice them". However, its being declined and prepositions entering upon it preclude its being an ism fiʿl. From what has preceded it is summarized whether «حَسْب» has the sense of an active participle and is originally a maṣdar, or is an ism fiʿl of the past, or an imperative verb. It is one of the nouns that obligatorily take a genitive annexation (iḍāfa), and it does not become definite by being annexed to a definite noun: you say "I passed a man ḥasbuka (enough for you)". A tamyīz (specification) may be put in the accusative after it; it may be a mubtadaʾ and then be governed by a redundant bāʾ, or a khabar and then not be governed by it. It is not made dual, plural or feminine, even when it occurs as an adjective of these things.

As for «جهنَّمُ», people have differed about it. It was said: it is non-Arabic and was Arabized, its original being kahnām, so its being a diptote is for being a proper name and non-Arabic. It was said: rather it is Arabic in origin, and those who say so differed about its nūn: is it redundant or original? The sound view is that it is redundant and its pattern is «فَعَنَّل», derived from "rakiyyatun jahnām", i.e. a well of great depth, and it is from al-jahm, which is aversion. It was also said: rather its nūn is original and its pattern is faʿallal, like ʿadabbas. He said (the proponent): because «فعنَّلاً» is lacking in their speech; and he made «زَوْنَكاً» also faʿallal, since the wāw is original in quadriliteral words such as waranṭal. But the sound view is to affirm this pattern, and some words came from it. They said «ḍaghanṭ» from ḍaghāṭa, which is bigness, and «safanjaj» and «hajanfaf» for the male ostrich; and the zawnak is the short man, so named because he strides with a swagger in his walk, i.e. struts. Ḥassān said:

902 - أَجْمَعْتَ أَنَّك أنتَ أَلأَمُ مَنْ مَشَى ... في فُحْشِ زانيةٍ وَزْوكِ غُرابِ
(You are convinced that you are the vilest of all who walked, in the obscenity of an adulteress and the strut of a crow.)

All this indicates that the nūn is redundant in «زَوْنَك», and on this basis its being a diptote is due to feminine gender and being a proper name.

«ولَبِئْسَ المِهادُ»: The one specified for blame is omitted, i.e. "wa-labiʾsa l-mihādu jahannamu"; and what made its omission here good is that «المِهاد» occurs as a verse-ending (fāṣila). The discussion of «بئس» and the people's disagreement about it has already preceded. This specified noun is omitted on the view that it is a mubtadaʾ and the clause of niʿma and biʾsa is its khabar, whether it precedes or follows; for if we made it the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or a mubtadaʾ with omitted khabar, and then omitted it, we would have omitted the whole clause without anything standing in its place. Also, it would follow from that that the clause is detached from what precedes it, since it would have no position in grammatical analysis, and it is neither parenthetical, nor explicative, nor a ṣila, nor resumptive.

As for «المِهَادُ» there are two views on it. The first: that it is the plural of «مَهْد» (cradle), which is what is levelled for sleeping. The second: that it is a singular noun, by which the bedding laid out for sleeping is named. This is of the category of mockery and derision, i.e. Jahannam is made for them in place of a bed that they spread out, like his saying:

903 - وخيلٍ قد دَلَفْتُ لها بِخَيْلٍ ... تحيةُ بينِهم ضَرْبٌ وَجِيعُ
(Many a cavalry I advanced upon with cavalry, whose greeting among them is a painful blow.)

that is: what stands for them in the place of greeting is the painful blow.

semin-durr:207-207.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَن يَشْرِي}: In «مَنْ» are the two aforementioned views that apply to the first «مَنْ». The meaning of yashrī is "sells". The Exalted said: {وَشَرَوْهُ بِثَمَنٍ بَخْسٍ} [Yūsuf: 20], if we return the nominative pronoun to the Hereafter (al-ākhira)... and the poet said:

904 - وَشَرَيْتُ بُرْداً ليتني ... من بعدِ بُرْدٍ كنتُ هامَهْ
(I sold Burd — would that after Burd I had been an owl/skull!)

So the meaning is: he gives up his own self for Allah. It was also said: rather it is in its original sense of buying (shirāʾ), because Ṣuhayb bought his own self from Quraysh when he emigrated, and the verse was revealed concerning him.

His saying: {ابتغآء} is accusative as a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose). The conditions requiring the accusative are present. The sound view is that the annexation of the mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose) is a true (maḥḍa) annexation, contrary to al-Jarmī, al-Mubarrad, al-Riyāshī and a group of the later scholars. «مرضاة» is a maṣdar built with the tāʾ of feminization, like madʿāh; the analogical form is without it, like maghzā and marmā.

Ḥamza paused on it with the tāʾ, for two reasons. The first: some of the Arabs pause on the feminine tāʾ with the tāʾ as it is. They recited:

905 - دارٌ لسَلْمَى بعد حولٍ قد عَفَتْ ... بل جَوْزِ تيهاءَ كظهْرِ الجَحَفَتْ
(An abode of Salmā that has effaced after a year — rather the expanse of a desert, like the back of the shield.)

Sībawayh related this dialect. The second: that he paused with the intention of annexation, as if he intended the wording of the following genitive noun, because of the strength of the connection between the two annexed words, so he kept the tāʾ as it is to alert to that. This is like their giving a hint of the ḍamma (ishmām) to the letter, to let it be known that the ḍamma is as if pronounced. Al-Kisāʾī and Warsh pronounced «مَرْضات» with imāla.

In His saying: {بالعباد} there is a shift from the pronoun of the absent person to the overt noun, since the original would be "raʾūfun bihi" or "bihim"; and the benefit of this shift is that the word «العباد» conveys honour, or because it is a verse-ending (fāṣila), so it was chosen for that.

semin-durr:208-208.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {السلم}: Nāfiʿ, al-Kisāʾī and Ibn Kathīr read here «السَّلْم» with fatḥa, and the rest with kasra. As for the one in al-Anfāl, none read it with kasra except Abū Bakr alone, from ʿĀṣim; and the one in (Sūrat) al-Qitāl (Muḥammad) none read with kasra except Ḥamza and Abū Bakr alone, from ʿĀṣim; and the one in al-Qitāl none read with kasra except Ḥamza and Abū Bakr also, and it will come. [Translator's note: the source repeats the sentence on al-Qitāl twice.] It was said: both have the same meaning, which is peace (ṣulḥ), and it is treated as masculine and feminine. The Exalted said: {وَإِن جَنَحُواْ لِلسَّلْمِ فاجنح لَهَا}. They related: "Banū so-and-so are silm and salm." Its origin is from istislām, which is submission, and it is applied to Islam; al-Kisāʾī and a group said this. They recited:

906 - دَعَوْتُ عشيرتي للسِّلْمِ لَمَّا ... رأيُتُهمُ تَوَلَّوا مُدْبِرِينا
(I called my clan to peace when I saw them turning away, retreating.)

This is recited with kasra. Another said, with the fatḥa:

907 - شرائِعُ السَّلْم قد بانَتْ معالِمُها ... فما يَرى الكفرَ إلا مَنْ بِه خَبَلُ
(The laws of Islam/peace have become clear in their landmarks, and none sees unbelief but one afflicted with madness.)

So al-silm and al-salm in these two verses have the meaning of Islam, except that the fatḥa is rare for the sense of Islam. «السَّلَم» was also read with fatḥa on both letters. And it was said: rather the two differ in meaning: with kasra it is Islam, and with fatḥa it is peace.

His saying: {كَآفَّةً} is accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial), and there are three views concerning its ṣāḥib (the one it describes). The first, which is the most apparent: that it is the agent in «ادخُلوا», and the meaning is: "enter into al-silm all together." This ḥāl corroborates the meaning of generality, for your saying "qāma l-qawmu kāffatan" (the people stood, all) is equivalent to "they stood, all of them." The second: that it is «السِّلْم». Al-Zamakhsharī and Abū l-Baqāʾ said this. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is possible that «كافةً» is a ḥāl from «السِّلْمِ», because it is feminine just as al-ḥarb (war) is feminine. The poet said:

908 - السِّلْمُ تأخذُ منها ما رَضِيتَ به ... والحربُ يَكْفيكَ من أَنْفَاسِها جُرَعُ
(Peace — take from it what you are content with; and war — gulps of its breaths suffice you.)

on the grounds that the believers were commanded to enter into all acts of obedience and not to enter into one obedience and not another." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "His justification of «كافةً» being a ḥāl from «السِّلم» by his saying 'because it is feminine just as war is feminine' is worthless, because the tāʾ in «كافة» is not for the feminine, even though its original is to indicate it. Rather this has become a pure transfer to the meaning of 'all' (jamīʿ) and 'every' (kull), as qāṭibatan and ʿāmmatan have become a pure transfer when they are ḥāl. So when you say 'qāma n-nāsu kāffatan wa-qāṭibatan', none of that indicates the feminine, just as kull and jamīʿ do not indicate it."

The third: that the ṣāḥib al-ḥāl is both of them, I mean the agent of «ادخُلُوا» and «السِّلْم», so that it is a ḥāl from two things. Ibn ʿAṭiyya permitted this, for he said: "And «كافة» then encompasses the believers and all parts of the law, so the ḥāl is from two things, and that is permissible, like His saying: {فَأَتَتْ بِهِ قَوْمَهَا تَحْمِلُهُ} [Maryam: 37]." Then he said after some discussion: "«كافةً» means 'all'; what is meant by kāffa is the group that restrains (takuffu) those who oppose it."

His saying "like His saying: taḥmiluhu" means that «تَحْمِلُهُ» is a ḥāl from the agent of «أَتَتْ» and from the hāʾ in «بِهِ». The Shaykh said: "This example does not conform to a ḥāl from two things, because the wording «تَحْمِلُهُ» does not admit two things, and a ḥāl does not come from two things unless the wording admits them. The test of that is to make the two ṣāḥib al-ḥāl a mubtadaʾ and make that ḥāl a khabar about them. Whenever that is sound, the ḥāl is sound, like:

909 - وَعُلِّقْتُ سلمى وَهْيَ ذاتُ مُوَصَّدٍ ... ولم يَبْدُ للأتْرابِ من ثَدْيِها حَجْمُ
(I was attached to Salmā when she was one with a closed-off veil, and for her peers no size of her breast had yet appeared.)

صَغِيرَيْنِ نَرْعى البَهْم يا ليت أنَّنا ... إلى اليومِ لم نَكْبَر ولم تكْبَرِ البُهْمُ
(Two little ones, we pastured the lambs — would that we had not grown up to this day, nor the lambs grown!)

Here «صغيرَيْنِ» is a ḥāl from the agent of «عُلِّقْتُ» and from «سلمى», because if you said 'I and Salmā are two little ones' it would be sound. Similar is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:

910 - خَرَجْتُ بها نمشي تَجُرُّ وراءَنا ... على أَثَرَيْنَا ذَيْلَ مِرْطٍ مُرَحَّلِ
(I went out with her, walking, she trailing behind us, over our two tracks, the hem of a patterned mantle.)

Here «نمشي» is a ḥāl from the agent of «خَرَجْتُ» and from the «ها» in «بها», because if you said 'I and she are walking' it would be sound; therefore the grammarians analysed «نَمْشِي» as a ḥāl from both, as has preceded; and «تَجُرُّ» is a ḥāl from the «ها» in «بها» only, because «تَجُرُّ» cannot be made a khabar about the two: if you said 'I and she trails' it would not be sound. So likewise it is taken to be a singular, namely «جارَّة» (trailing), and if you predicated it of two it would not be sound. Likewise «تحمله» cannot be a khabar about two, so it cannot be a ḥāl from the two. As for «كافة», it has the meaning of «جميع», and for «جميع» that is sound. It may not be said: 'kāffa cannot occur as a khabar; if you said "al-Zaydūn wa-l-ʿAmrūn kāffa" it would not be permitted; therefore it does not occur as a ḥāl on what I established.' For that is only because of the obligatory fixing of «كافةً» in the accusative as ḥāl, and its not being declined freely, not because of a semantic obstacle; the proof being that its synonyms «جميع» and «كل» can be used as khabar. So the accidental obstacle preventing «كافّة» from free usage does no harm. As for his saying 'the group that restrains those who oppose it', he means that it is originally so, and then its usage became the sense of 'all' (jamīʿ) and 'every' (kull)."

Know that the origin of «كافة» is an active participle from kaffa yakuffu, i.e. "prevented", and from it "kaff al-insān" (the human hand), because it prevents what it requires; and "kiffat al-mīzān" (the pan of the scale), for gathering what is weighed; and al-kuffa with ḍamma is for anything elongated, and with kasra for anything round. It was said: «كافة» is a maṣdar like ʿāqiba and ʿāfiya. Kāffa and qāṭiba are among what must be put in the accusative as ḥāl, so taking them out of that is a solecism (laḥn).

semin-durr:209-209.t: The majority read {زَلَلْتُمْ} with fatḥa on the ʿayn (the middle radical); Abū l-Sammāl read it with kasra, and they are two dialects, like ḍalaltu and ḍalliltu. The «ما» in «مِنْ بعدِما» is maṣdarī (forming a verbal noun), and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent, and it is attached to «زَللْتُم».

semin-durr:198-198.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَن تَبْتَغُواْ}: «أَنْ» is in the position of accusative according to Sībawayh and al-Farrāʾ, and of genitive according to their two teachers and al-Akhfash, because it is on the implication of a preposition, i.e. «في أَنْ» ("in [seeking]"). This preposition is attached either to «جُناحِ» because of the verbal sense it contains, namely inclination and sin, and whatever is in their sense; or to an omitted element, because it is an adjective of «جُناح», in which case it is nominative in position, i.e. "a sin existing in such and such". Abū l-Baqāʾ transmitted from some that it is attached to «ليس», and he considered that weak; but it should not be so described: rather it is to be judged an outright error.

His saying: {مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ}: It may be attached to «تبتغوا», or it may be an adjective of «فضلاً», in which case it is accusative in position, attached to an omitted element. «مِنْ» in both analyses is for the beginning of the range (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), but in the second analysis it requires the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "a bounty coming from among the bounties of your Lord".

His saying: {فَإِذَآ أَفَضْتُم}: The element governing «إذا» is its apodosis, namely «فاذكروا». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The fāʾ does not prevent what follows it from governing what precedes it, because it is a conditional." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) objected to this, in substance because the place where the pouring forth (ifāḍa) begins is not the place of the remembrance: that is ʿArafāt, and this is al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām, and when the place differs the time necessarily differs, so it is not permissible that the remembrance at al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām occur at the beginning of the pouring forth.

His saying: {مِّنْ عَرَفَاتٍ} is attached to «أَفَضْتُم». Ifāḍa originally means pouring: one says «فاضَ الماء وأَفَضْتُه» ("the water overflowed and I poured it out"), then it is used figuratively for entering the state of iḥrām [Translator's note: the source reads «الإحرام» (iḥrām); the sense here appears to concern the pilgrims' departure, but I translate what is written]. The hamza in «أَفَضْتُم» has two analyses. The first: that it is for transitivity, so its object is omitted, its implied form being "you poured yourselves forth". This is the view of al-Zajjāj, and al-Zamakhsharī followed him. Al-Zajjāj gave the implied form, saying: "Its meaning is: some of you pushed others." The second: that «أَفْعَلَ» here has the meaning of the bare «فَعَلَ», so there is no direct object. The Shaykh said: "Because «أَفَضْتُ زيداً» in this sense which we explained is not recorded," and he had explained it as rushing forth, surging, and leaving a place in great numbers.

The original of «أَفَضْتُم» is «أَفْيَضْتُم», and it underwent weakening-change like its parallels: the vowel of the weak letter was moved to the sākin letter before it, so the weak letter, which originally had a vowel and had a fatḥa before it, was turned into an alif. It is from the roots with yāʾ, from «الفَيْض», as I told you, and it is not from the roots with wāw, from their saying «فَوْضى الناسِ», meaning people in a mixed crowd without a leader.

And «عَرَفات» is the name of a specific place. Is it derived or ad hoc (murtajal)? There are two views. The first: that it is murtajal, and al-Zamakhsharī took this view. He said: "Because «العَرَفة» is not known among generic nouns, unless it is the plural of «عارف»." The second: that it is derived, and its derivation is disputed. It was said: from «المعرفة» (knowing), because when Jibrīl made Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, acquainted with this spot, he said: "I knew, I knew"; or because he made Hājar and Ismāʿīl acquainted with it when Sāra drove them out in his absence and he found them there; or because Ādam came to know Ḥawwāʾ there. It was also said: derived from «العَرْف», which is a pleasant scent; and it was said: from «العُرْف», which is elevation, from which comes «عُرْفُ الديك» (the cock's comb). «عرفات» was originally the plural of «عَرَفة», then this place was named with it. The well-known view is that «عرفات» and «عَرَفة» are the same. It was also said: «عَرَفة» is the name of the day and «عرفات» is the name of the place. As for the tanwīn in «عَرَفات» and its like, there are three views, the most apparent being that it is the tanwīn of correspondence (tanwīn muqābala). They mean that the tanwīn of this plural corresponds to the nūn of the masculine plural; so the tanwīn of «مسلمات» corresponds to the nūn of «مسلمين», and then every tanwīn in the feminine plural was made so, even where it has no masculine plural, to keep the chapter regular. The second: that it is the tanwīn of inflection (ṣarf), which is the apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's statement, for he said: "If you say: why is it not made diptote, when it has the two causes, definiteness and feminine? I say: the feminine marking cannot fail to be either by the tāʾ in its wording or by an implied tāʾ as in «سعاد». The one in its wording is not for the feminine; rather it, together with the alif before it, is the marker of the feminine plural. And an implied tāʾ is not valid in it, because [this] tāʾ, by being specific to the feminine plural, prevents its being implied, just as the feminine tāʾ is not implied in «بنت», because the tāʾ that replaces the wāw is, by its specificity to the feminine, like the feminine tāʾ and refuses to be implied." So al-Zamakhsharī denied that the feminine is a cause in it, and the tanwīn for him is that of ṣarf. The third: that if the feminine plural has a masculine plural, like «مسلمات» and «مسلمين», the tanwīn is for correspondence, and otherwise it is for ṣarf, as in «عرفات».

The well-known practice, when naming with it, is that it takes tanwīn and is inflected with the two vowels, ḍamma and kasra, as if it were a plural. A second dialectal form: dropping the tanwīn for lightness and inflecting it with kasra in the accusative. A third: inflecting it as a diptote with fatḥa in the genitive. The Kufans and al-Akhfash reported it, and he cited the verse of Imruʾ al-Qays:

887 - تَنَوَّرْتُها مِنْ أَذْرِعاتَ وأهلُها ... بيثربَ أدنى دارِها نظرٌ عالي
(I made out her fire from Adhriʿāt, while her people were in Yathrib, and the nearest of her abode was a lofty gaze away.)

with fatḥa [on «أَذْرِعاتَ»].

His saying: {عِندَ المشعر الحرام}: There are two analyses of it. The first: that it is attached to «اذكروا». The second: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from the agent of «اذكروا», i.e. "remember Him while being at al-Mashʿar".

His saying: {كَمَا هَدَاكُمْ}: There are five views on it. The first: that it is in the position of accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a good remembrance, as He guided you with a good guidance". This is al-Zamakhsharī's implied form. The second: that it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun of the implied maṣdar, and this is the view of Sībawayh. The third: that it is for cause, with the meaning of the lām, i.e. "remember Him for the sake of His guiding you". Sībawayh related: «كما أنه لا يَعْلَمُ فتجاوزَ الله عنه» ("since he did not know, Allah overlooked him"). Among those who said it is causal are al-Akhfash and a group.

As for «ما» in «كما», two analyses are possible. The first: that it is a maṣdar particle, so it with what follows is in the position of genitive through the kāf, i.e. "like His guiding". The second, which al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya held: that it is a restraining particle (kāffa) that holds the kāf back from governing, so the clause after it has no grammatical position; rather, if a noun comes after it, it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, as in his saying:

888 - ونَنْصُرُ مولانا ونعلُم أنَّه ... كما الناسُ مجرومٌ عليه وجَارِمُ
(We support our patron and know that, as people are, he is one wronged and one who wrongs.)

and another said:

889 - لعمرك إنني وأبا حميدٍ ... كما النشوانُ والرجلُ الحليمُ
أريد هجاءَه وأخاف ربي ... وأعلم أنه عبدٌ لئيم
(By your life, I and Abū Ḥumayd are like the drunk and the forbearing man: I want to lampoon him yet fear my Lord, and I know he is a base servant.)

The author of «al-Mustawfā» denied that «ما» can be a kāffa for the kāf, but he is refuted by what has preceded.

The fourth: that it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «اذكروا», its implied form being "resembling yourselves when He guided you". Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "A muḍāf must be omitted, because a body does not resemble an event." The fifth: that the kāf means «على», as in His saying: {وَلِتُكَبِّرُواْ الله على مَا هَدَاكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 185].

His saying: {وَإِن كُنْتُمْ مِّن قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ الضآلين}: This «إنْ» is the lightened form of the heavy «إنَّ», and the lām after it is to distinguish it from the negative «إنْ». It is allowed for «إنْ» to enter a verb because the verb is a nāsikh (one that abrogates the nominal sentence). Is this lām the lām of ibtidāʾ that used to accompany «إنَّ», or another lām brought in to distinguish? There are two views; this is the opinion of the Basrans. As for the Kufans, there is disagreement among them: al-Farrāʾ claims it has the meaning of the negative «إنْ» and the lām the meaning of «إلا», i.e. "You were not, before it, anything but among the astray". The view of al-Kisāʾī is a distinction: if it enters a verbal sentence, «إنْ» means «قد» and the lām is redundant for emphasis; and if it enters a nominal sentence, it is as al-Farrāʾ said. Some of these views have already been given.

And «من قبله» is attached to an omitted element indicated by «لمن الضالين», its implied form being: "you were astray before it, among the astray". It is not attached to «الضالين» after it, because what comes after the relative «أل» does not govern what precedes it, except in the opinion of those who are lenient with adverbials, as has already been verified. The hāʾ in «قبله» refers to «الهدى» understood from His saying «كما هداكم».

semin-durr:220-220.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فِي الدنيا}: there are five possibilities here, the most evident of which is that it is attached to «يتفكرون», in the sense "they reflect upon their affair, and so take what is most beneficial and prefer what has the more lasting benefit". The second: that it is attached to «يبيِّن»; its meaning is reported from al-Ḥasan, and in that case it is possible that a muḍāf be implied, that is, "in the affair of this world and the Hereafter", and it is possible that none be implied, because the clarification of the signs, which are the indications, becomes manifest in them. Some made al-Ḥasan's statement a case of fronting and postponing (taqdīm and taʾkhīr), then said: «There is no need for that, since the speech is to be taken at its apparent sense», meaning that «في الدنيا» is attached to «تتفكرون». But this is not a case of fronting and postponing at all, because the clause of hope runs in the manner of a reason and so is attached to the verb in meaning, and putting one of the dependents before another is not called fronting and postponing; and it is possible that it is parenthetical, in which case there is neither fronting nor postponing.

The third: that it is attached to «الآيات» itself, because of the sense of the verb in it; and this is the apparent meaning of the statement of Makkī as Ibn ʿAṭiyya understood it from him. Makkī said: «The meaning of the verse is that He makes clear to the believers signs in this world and the Hereafter, which point to them and to their rank, so that perhaps they will reflect on those signs.» Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «So His saying "في الدنيا" is attached, on this interpretation, to "الآيات".» But what he said on his authority is not evident, because Makkī's explanation of the verse does not require the preposition and its genitive noun to be attached to «الآيات». Then, if Ibn ʿAṭiyya meant by attachment the technical attachment, then the Shaykh said: «It is invalid, because "الآيات" does not govern anything at all, and no adverb or prepositional phrase is attached to it.» But in this statement of the Shaykh there is room for consideration, for adverbials are attached to the scents of verbs (the faint sense of a verb), and there is no doubt that the meaning of «الآيات» is the evident signs, so the adverbial is attached to it on this basis. And if he meant the attachment in meaning, which is that the prepositional phrase be part of the completion of the meaning of «الآيات», then that cannot be unless we make the prepositional phrase a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الآيات»; and for that reason Makkī gave it as indefinite, saying: «He makes clear to them signs in this world», to let it be known that it stands in the position of an adjective to «آيات»; and there is no difference in meaning between the adjective and the ḥāl in what we are concerned with. On this basis it is attached to an omitted word because it stands as an adjective.

The fourth: that it is a ḥāl from «الآيات», as its exposition has just preceded. The fifth: that it is a ṣila (relative clause) for «الآيات», so that it is attached to an omitted word as well; and that is the position of the Kufans, for they count among the relative nouns the noun defined by the article «al», and they recited as evidence:

946 - لَعَمْرِي لأنت البيتُ أُكْرِمُ أَهْلَهُ ... وَأَقْعُدُ في أَفْيَائِهِ بالأصائِلِ
("By my life, you are the house whose people I honour, and I sit in its shade in the late afternoons")

so «البيت» is, in their view, a relative noun; and the establishing of their position and the refutation of it have a more fitting place.

Al-tafakkur is of the pattern tafaʿʿul, from al-fikr; and al-fikr is the mind; so the meaning of "he reflected on such and such" is: he turned his mind over it and went back over it.

His saying: {إِصْلاَحٌ لَّهُمْ خَيْرٌ}: «إصلاحٌ» is a mubtadaʾ, and one of two things justified the beginning with it: either its being qualified by His saying «لهم», or its being specified by its governing something in it; and «خيرٌ» is its khabar.

And «إصلاحٌ» is a maṣdar whose agent is omitted, its implied form being "your putting them right (iṣlāḥukum lahu)", so the goodness is for both sides, I mean the side of the one who sets right and the side of the one who is set right; and this is preferable to restricting the iṣlāḥ to one of the two sides, as some have done. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «It is permissible that the implied form be "khayrun lakum" and permissible that it be "khayrun lahum", that is, putting them right is beneficial to you.»

And «لهم» is either in the position of the nominative as an adjective of «خير», or in the accusative as attached to it, being governed by it, as has preceded. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed that it be a ḥāl from «خير» put before it: its origin was an adjective, and when it was put before, it became accusative as a ḥāl from it; and he excused the beginning with an indefinite in that case by one of two explanations: either because the indefinite is in the sense of a verb, its implied form being "aṣliḥūhum" (set them right), or because the indefinite and the definite are the same here since it is a genus.

His saying: {فَإِخْوَانُكُمْ}: the fāʾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and «إخوانُكم» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: "fa-hum ikhwānukum" (they are your brothers). The clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of the condition. The majority read it in the nominative; Abū Mijlaz read «فإخوانَكم» in the accusative by an implied verb, that is: "you have mingled with your brothers"; and the verbal clause is likewise in the position of the jussive. It seems this reading did not reach Abū al-Baqāʾ, for he said: «The accusative is permissible in speech, that is: "you have mingled with your brothers".»

And His saying: {يَعْلَمُ المفسد مِنَ المصلح}: discussion of it has preceded in His saying: {إِلاَّ لِنَعْلَمَ مَن يَتَّبِعُ الرسول مِمَّن يَنقَلِبُ} [al-Baqara: 143]. Al-mufsid and al-muṣliḥ are two classes here; the article is not for defining a previously mentioned referent, and this is the apparent view; it is also possible that it be for a previously known referent as well.

And in His saying: {تُخَالِطُوهُمْ} there is an iltifāt (shift of person) from the third-person pronoun in His saying «ويسألونك» to the second person, in order to alert the hearer to what is being conveyed to him. The answer to the question came in two clauses: one of mubtadaʾ and khabar, brought out as affirmative (nominal) with an indefinite mubtadaʾ to show that it covers every setting right by way of substitution; had it been made a construct, it would have been general, or it would have been a known referent in a particular setting right, and neither is intended: generality is not possible, and a known referent would not cover anything else; therefore the indefinite, which denotes the generality of substitution, was preferred, and it was predicated with «خير», which denotes obtaining reward, so that the Muslim would hasten to it. The other is of condition and consequence, indicating the permissibility of the occurrence, not its being sought or recommended.

His saying: {وَلَوْ شَآءَ الله}: the object of «شاءَ» is omitted, that is: "your being distressed". The jawāb of «لو» is «لأعنَتَكم», and that is the frequent form, I mean the presence of the lām in the affirmative verb.

The well-known reading has the hamza of «لأعنتكم» pronounced fully, because it is a hamzat qaṭʿ. Al-Bazzī, from Ibn Kathīr, in the well-known report, read it with its softening, between the two (bayna bayna), although that is not his principle; and it is reported that it is dropped altogether, and this is like the reading {فلا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ} [al-Baqara: 173] in its irregularity and its justification. Some ascribed this reading to a slip of the transmitter, in that he took the softening in what he heard to be a dropping; but what is sound is that it is established as an irregular (shādhdha) reading.

Al-mukhālaṭa is mingling. And al-ʿanat is hardship, and from it «ʿaqabatun ʿanawtun», that is, a hard-to-climb slope.

semin-durr:185-185.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ}: There are two readings of it. The well-known one is the nominative, and it admits several analyses. The first: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject). Its khabar (predicate) is then one of two things. The first: His saying {الذي أُنْزِلَ فِيهِ القرآن}, in which case He mentioned this clause to draw attention to the month's merit and standing, meaning: this month in which the Qur'an was revealed is the one whose fasting has been made obligatory upon you. The second: His saying {فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ الشَّهْرَ فَلْيَصُمْهُ}, with the fāʾ being redundant (zāʾida), and that is according to the opinion of al-Akhfash. [Translator's note: the source reads "وليست هذه الفاء لا تزاد في الخبر لشبه المبتدأ بالشرط", which is grammatically confused as printed; the sense appears to be that this fāʾ is not of the kind that is added to a khabar because the mubtadaʾ resembles a conditional.] Some have claimed that it is like His saying: {قُلْ إِنَّ الموت الذي تَفِرُّونَ مِنْهُ فَإِنَّهُ مُلاَقِيكُمْ} [al-Jumuʿa: 8], but that is not so, because in {الموت الذي تَفِرُّونَ} a generality is imagined, unlike "the month of Ramaḍān". If it is asked: where is the link (rābiṭ) between this clause and the mubtadaʾ? It is said: the repetition of the mubtadaʾ in its very wording, as in the verse:
843 - لا أَرى الموتَ يَسْبِقُ الموتَ شيءٌ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I do not see anything outrunning death ...) [the verse is incomplete in the source]
This analysis, namely that "شهر رمضان" is a mubtadaʾ, rests on our view that the "counted days" are other than Ramaḍān. But if we say that they are Ramaḍān itself, then the two remaining analyses apply.
The first: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. Al-Farrāʾ implied it as: "that is the month of Ramaḍān", and al-Akhfash implied it as: "what is prescribed is the month of". The second: that it is a badal (substitute) for His saying "الصيام", i.e. "the month of Ramaḍān has been prescribed for you". Although al-Kisāʾī held this view, it is very remote, for two reasons. The first: the great separation between the substitute and what it substitutes for. The second: that in that case it could only be a badal al-ishmāl, which is the reverse of badal al-ishtimāl (inclusion substitute), because badal al-ishtimāl is generally with verbal nouns, as in His saying {عَنِ الشهر الحرام قِتَالٍ فِيهِ} [al-Baqara: 217], and al-Aʿshā's verse:
844 - لقد كانَ في حَوْلٍ ثَواءٍ ثَوَيْتُه ... تَقَضِّي لُباناتٍ وَيَسْأَمُ سائِمُ
(Surely in a year there was a stay I stayed ... the fulfilling of needs, while the weary grows weary)
Here the adverbial noun (ẓarf) has been substituted for the verbal noun. [Translator's note: "بدل الإشمال" is as printed in the source; it appears to be a slip for "بدل الاشتمال", though the author's point is that this would be the reverse of that type.] His view can be supported by saying that the sentence involves an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being "the fasting of the month of Ramaḍān"; it would then be a case of badal of a thing from the thing, both being one and the same entity. It is also possible that the nominative is a badal for His saying "أياماً معدوداتٍ" in the reading of those who read "أياماً" in the nominative, which is the reading of ʿAbdullāh [Ibn Masʿūd]; but this too is remote.
As for the less well-known reading, it is the accusative, and it has several analyses. The best of them: it is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "fast the month of Ramaḍān". The second, mentioned by al-Akhfash and al-Rummānī: that it is a badal for His saying "أياماً معدوداتٍ", and this strengthens the view that the counted days are Ramaḍān, except that it is remote because of the great separation. The third: accusative as a word of urging (ighrāʾ), mentioned by Abū ʿUbayda and al-Ḥūfī. The fourth: that it is made accusative by His saying "وَأَنْ تصوموا", reported by Ibn ʿAṭiyya and permitted by al-Zamakhsharī; but the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] declared both mistaken, saying: "It necessarily involves separation between the relative (mawṣūl) and its ṣila (relative clause) by an alien element, because the khabar, namely «خير», is alien to the mawṣūl, and it has already been stated that the mawṣūl is not predicated of until its ṣila is complete; and «شهر», on their view, is part of the completion of the ṣila of «أَنْ», so what they said is ruled out."
And no one may say that this can be accounted for on the basis of the disagreement concerning the adverbial and the preposition, in that such separation is tolerated in them according to some, since the apparent sense of its being accusative here is that it is a direct object, not an adverbial. The fifth: that it is accusative by «تَعْملون» [Translator's note: so printed; elsewhere in the passage the verb is given as "تعلمون"] with an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being: "you know the nobility of the month of Ramaḍān"; the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi was put in its place in respect of i'rab.
Abū ʿAmr assimilated the rāʾ of «شهر» into the rāʾ of «رمضان». No attention is paid to whoever considered it weak on the ground that it joins two silent letters not within their proper limits; and Ibn ʿAṭiyya's saying "the principles do not require that" is not acceptable from him, for when the transmission is sound it is not opposed by analogy.
As for al-shahr (the month), the lexicographers have two views about it. The better known of the two: that it is a name for the span of time whose beginning is the crescent hidden until it becomes concealed [again]; it was so called because of its renown (shuhra), given people's need of it for the things known [by it]. The second, stated by al-Zajjāj: that it is a name for the crescent itself. He said:
845 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... والشهرُ مثلُ قُلاَمَةِ الظُّفْرِ
(... and the month is like a fingernail paring)
It was so called because of its being manifest. Dhū l-Rumma said:
846 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... يَرى الشهرَ قبلَ الناسِ وهو نَحِيلُ
(... he sees the month before the people, while it is thin)
They say "I saw the month", meaning its crescent; then it was applied to the period of time because of the crescent's appearing in it. One says "أَشْهَرْنا", meaning that a month came upon us. Al-Farrāʾ said: "I have not heard a verb [of this kind] other than this one." Al-Thaʿlabī said: "One says «شَهَرَ الهِلالُ» when it has appeared." In the plural of paucity it is «أَشْهُر», and in the plural of multitude «شُهور»; both are regular.
"Ramaḍān" is a proper name (ʿalam) for this particular month, and it is a ʿalam jins (name of a genus). There are several views on why it was called Ramaḍān. One: that its coming coincided with the ramḍāʾ, which is intense heat, so it was named for that, like Rabīʿ for coinciding with the spring (rabīʿ), and Jumādā for coinciding with the freezing (jumūd) of water. It was also said: because it burns away (yarmaḍu) sins, i.e. it burns them, meaning it wipes them out. It was also said: because hearts are burned in it by admonition. It was also said: from «رَمَضْتُ النَّصْلَ», "I pounded the blade between two stones to make it thin"; one says «نَصْلٌ رَميض ومَرْموض». Its name in the pre-Islamic period was Nātiq. Al-Mufaḍḍal recited:
847 - وفي ناتِقٍ أَجْلَتْ لدى حَوْمةِ الوَغى ... وولَّتْ على الأدبارِ فُرْسانُ خَثْعَمَا
(And in Nātiq, at the thick of battle, they were driven off ... and the horsemen of Khathʿam turned their backs)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«الرَّمَضانُ» is the verbal noun of «رَمِضَ», when something burned from the heat of the ground." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "To establish that it is a verbal noun requires a sound report, since fa'alān is not the verbal noun of the intransitive fa'ila; if any such form comes, it is irregular." It was also said: it is derived from al-ramaḍī, which is a rain that comes before the autumn and cleanses the earth of dust; likewise this month cleanses hearts of sins.
Al-Qur'ān was originally a verbal noun of «قَرَأْتُ», then became the proper name for what lies between the two covers. That it was originally a verbal noun is indicated by Ḥassān's verse about ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him:
848 - ضَحُّوا بأَشْمَطَ عنوانُ السجودِ به ... يُقَطِّعُ الليلَ تسبيحاً وقُرْآنا
(They sacrificed a grey-haired man, the mark of prostration on him ... who spent the night in glorification and recitation)
It comes from «قَرَأَ» with hamza, meaning "he gathered", because it gathers the sūras, verses, wisdom and admonitions. The majority read it with the hamza; Ibn Kathīr read it without hamza.
There is disagreement about how his reading is to be accounted for, in two ways. The more apparent: that it is a case of transfer (naql), as Warsh transfers the vowel of the hamza to the silent letter before it and then drops it, in such cases as {قَدْ أَفْلَحَ} [al-Muʾminūn: 1]. Although transfer is not its original basis, it was transferred here because of its frequent recurrence and to combine the two dialects.
The second: that according to him it is derived from «قَرَنْتُ» "I joined two things together", so its pattern on this view is fuʿāl, and on the first view fuʿlān; for in it the sūras, verses, wisdom and admonitions are joined together.
As for the saying of whoever said that it is derived from «قَرَيْتُ الماءَ في الحَوْضِ», "I gathered the water in the trough", that is a mistake, because they are two different roots. And «القرآن» is a passive-voice object (mafʿūl lam yusamma fāʿiluhu); the meaning of {أُنْزِلَ فِيهِ القرآن} is that the Qur'an was sent down in it, so it is the time-frame of its revelation; it was said: on the twenty-fourth of it. It was also said: it was revealed concerning its status and merit, as you say "a Qur'an [passage] was revealed about so-and-so".
His saying: {هُدًى}: in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «القرآن», the operator in it being «أُنْزِلَ». «هُدًى» is a verbal noun, and so either there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "possessing guidance"; or it stands in the place of the active participle, i.e. "guiding"; or it is made guidance itself, for emphasis.
His saying: {لِّلنَّاسِ}: two analyses are possible. The first: that it is attached to «هُدًى», on our view that it takes the place of «هادٍ», i.e. "guiding the people". The second: that it is attached to an omitted element because it is an adjective of the indefinite noun before it, its position being accusative as an adjective. It is not permissible that «هُدًى» be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "it is guidance", because an overtly accusative word is conjoined to it, namely «بَيِّنات»; «بَيِّنات» is conjoined to the ḥāl and is therefore also a ḥāl; and both ḥāls are inherent (lāzima), for the Qur'an is nothing but guidance and clear proofs. This is an instance of conjoining the specific to the general, because guidance may be through hidden things and manifest things, while clear proofs are among manifest things.
His saying: {مِّنَ الهدى والفرقان}: this preposition and its genitive noun is an adjective of His saying «هدىً وبَيِّناتٍ», so its position is accusative, and it is attached to an omitted element, i.e. "the Qur'an's being guidance and clear proofs is part of Allah's guidance and His clear proofs". He expressed the clear proofs as al-Furqān, and did not say "من الهدى والبينات" so that the end would match the beginning, because there is in it an added meaning inherent in clear proofs, namely that it distinguishes (yufarriqu) between truth and falsehood, and whenever a thing is evident and plain, distinction results from it; and because the word al-Furqān harmonises with the verse endings before it. For that reason he expressed the clear proofs as al-Furqān. Some said: "What is meant by the first «الهدى» is the fundamentals of the religions, and by the second their branches." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The lām in «الهدى» is the lām of previous mention (ʿahd), and what is meant is the first," meaning that an indefinite noun came first and then its wording was repeated made definite with «ال»; and whatever is like that, the second in it is the first, as in His saying: {إلى فِرْعَوْنَ رَسُولاً فعصى فِرْعَوْنُ الرسول} [al-Muzzammil: 15-16]. From here Ibn ʿAbbās said: "One hardship will never overcome two eases." The rule for this is that the pronoun of the first indefinite noun could take the place of the second; do you not see that if it were said «فعصاه» ("so he disobeyed him") it would be sound speech?
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "What Ibn ʿAṭiyya said does not work out here, because he and the other iʿrāb scholars stated that «هدى» is accusative as a ḥāl, and the ḥāl is a description of the one it qualifies, and «وَبيِّنات» is conjoined to it. So His saying «من الهدى», by which the first guidance is meant, cannot avoid being either an adjective of «هُدًى», or of «وبيناتٍ», or of both, or attached to the word «بينات». It cannot be an adjective of «هدى», because as an adjective it must be a part, and as the first it must be identical with it, and one and the same thing cannot be both a part and the whole in relation to its essence. Nor can it be an adjective of «بينات» alone, because «وبينات» is conjoined to «هُدَى», and «هُدَى» is a ḥāl, and what is conjoined to a ḥāl is a ḥāl, and the two ḥāls are descriptions of the one they qualify; so insofar as they are two ḥāls, the possessor of the ḥāl is specified by them, since they are two descriptions, and insofar as «بَيِّنات» is described by «مِنَ الهدى», we have specified it by it. Thus the specification of the Qur'an depends on His saying «هُدَىً وَبَيَّنات» together, and insofar as you make «مِنَ الهدى» an adjective of «بيِّنات», the specification of «بيِّنات» depends on «هُدَى», and so it follows that a thing is specified by itself, which is impossible. Nor can it be an adjective of both, because that fails for the two reasons mentioned, namely that it describes only «الهدى», or only «بينات». Nor can it be attached to the word «بينات», because the thing attached is a qualifier of that to which it is attached, so it is like the adjective and is excluded where the adjective is excluded. Moreover, if you put a pronoun here in place of «الهدى» and said «منه», meaning 'from that guidance', it would not be sound. For that reason we prefer that al-hudā and al-furqān be general, so that «هُدَى وبينات» are parts of them."
His saying: {فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ الشَّهْرَ}: «مَنْ» admits both analyses, namely that it is a relative or a conditional, and the latter is the more apparent. «منكم» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «شَهِدَ», and so it is attached to an omitted element, i.e. "being among you". Abū l-Baqāʾ said: «منكم» is a ḥāl from the agent, and it is attached to «شَهِدَ». The Shaykh said: "He contradicted himself, because making it a ḥāl requires that its operator be omitted, while making it attached to «شَهِدَ» requires that it not be a ḥāl." It can be answered against the Shaykh's objection that what he meant is attachment in meaning: "being", which is the operator in «منكم», is attached to «شَهِدَ», and it is in reality the ḥāl.
There are two views on the accusative of «الشهر». The first: that it is accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), what is meant by «شَهِدَ» being "he was present", and the object of «شَهِدَ» is omitted, its implied form being: "whoever of you is present in the town or city during the month".
The second: that it is accusative as a direct object, with an omitted muḍāf. Then they disagreed on the implied form of that muḍāf: the sound view is that it is "the entering of the month". Some said "the crescent of the month", but this is weak for two reasons. The first: that you do not say «شَهِدْتُ الهلالَ», you say «شاهَدْتُ الهِلالَ». The second: that fasting would then be obligatory for everyone who saw the crescent, which is not so. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«الشهرَ» is accusative as an adverbial, and so is the hā in «فَلْيَصُمْه»; it is not a direct object as in your saying «شَهِدْتُ الجمعة», because the resident and the traveller are both witnesses of the month." As for his saying "the hā is accusative as an adverbial", there is something in it that is not hidden, because the verb does not govern the pronoun of an adverbial except with «في», unless latitude is allowed in it so that it is put in the accusative like a direct object; yet he explicitly stated that the accusative of the hā is also as an adverbial.
The fāʾ in His saying «فَلْيَصُمْهُ» is either the fāʾ of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) [Translator's note: the source prints "جوب الشرط", an evident misprint for "جواب الشرط"], or redundant in the khabar, according to what preceded regarding «مَنْ». The lām is the lām of command. The majority read it with sukūn though its original is kasra; they made it sukūn by likening it, when it comes after wāw and fāʾ, to «كَتِف», treating the separate as the attached. Al-Sulamī, Abū Ḥaywa and others read it with the original, namely kasra of the command lām throughout the Qur'an. Fatḥa on this lām is the dialect of Sulaym, as al-Farrāʾ reported; some restricted this on al-Farrāʾ's authority, saying: "Among the Arabs are those who give this lām fatḥa because of the fatḥa of the yāʾ after it", and he said: "So there is no fatḥa on this account if what follows it has kasra or ḍamma, such as «لِيُنْذِرُ» and «لِتُكْرِمْ أنتَ خالداً»."
The alif and lām in His saying {فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ الشَّهْرَ} is for previous mention (ʿahd), since had a pronoun come in its place, saying «فَمَنْ شَهِدَه منكم», it would have been sound; but He made it overt in order to exalt it.
His saying: {يُرِيدُ الله بِكُمُ اليسر}: the meaning of irāda (willing) and its derivation were covered at His saying, the Exalted: {مَاذَآ أَرَادَ الله بهذا} [al-Baqara: 26]. «أراد» for the most part is transitive to persons by «بـ» and to verbal nouns directly, as in the noble verse, and sometimes the matter is reversed. The poet said:
849 - أرادَتْ عَراراً بالهَوانِ ومَنْ يُرِدْ ... عَراراً لعَمْرِي بالهَوانِ فَقَدْ ظَلَمْ
(She wanted ʿArār with humiliation, and whoever wants ʿArār, by my life, with humiliation has done wrong)
The bāʾ in «بكم»: Abū l-Baqāʾ said, "is for attachment (ilṣāq), i.e. 'He attaches ease to you'; this is figurative speech, i.e. Allah wants ease for you in your breaking the fast when there is an excuse." In His saying: {وَلاَ يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ العسر} there is emphasis, because before it is {يُرِيدُ الله بِكُمُ اليسر}, which would have sufficed. Abū Jaʿfar, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and Ibn Hurmuz read «اليُسُر والعُسُر» with ḍamma on the sīn. The grammarians disagreed: is the ḍamma the original and the sukūn a lightening, or is the original the sukūn and the ḍamma for harmony (ittibāʿ)? The first is more apparent, because it is what is familiar in their speech.
His saying: {وَلِتُكْمِلُواْ}: there are three views on this lām. The first: that it is redundant in the direct object, like the one in your saying «ضَرَبْتُ لزيدٍ», with «أَنْ» implied after it, its implied form being "and He wants that you complete the number", i.e. the completion, so it is conjoined to «اليُسْر». Similar is Abū Ṣakhr's verse:
850 - أريدُ لأَنْسَى حُبَّها فكأنَّما ... تَمَثَّلُ لي ليلى بكلِّ طريقِ
(I want to forget her love, yet it is as if Laylā appears to me on every road)
This is the view of Ibn ʿAṭiyya, al-Zamakhsharī and Abū l-Baqāʾ. The redundancy of this lām in the object was made good, even though that is normally only when the operator is derivative or the object is fronted, in that when the separation between the verb and what is conjoined to its object became long, its transitivity to it was weakened, so it was made transitive by the added lām, by analogy of its weakness through long separation with its weakness through fronting.
The second: that it is the lām of cause (taʿlīl) and not redundant. Those who hold this disagreed on six analyses. The first: that after the wāw there is an omitted verb, which is the thing caused, its implied form being "and in order that you complete the number He did this"; this is al-Farrāʾ's view. The second, the view of al-Zajjāj: that it is conjoined to an omitted cause whose effect is also omitted, the implied form being: "Allah did that to make it easy for you and so that you complete." The third: that the verb whose cause is stated is implied after this cause, the implied form being "and so that you complete the number, He granted you a concession in that"; Ibn ʿAṭiyya attributed it to some of the Kufans. The fourth: that the wāw is redundant, the implied form being "Allah wants such-and-such for you so that you complete", and this is very weak. The fifth: that the verb whose cause is stated is implied after His saying «ولَعَلَّكم تَشْكُرون», its implied form being "He legislated that", said al-Zamakhsharī, and this is the text of his words. He said: "He legislated that", meaning the sum of what was mentioned: the command to the one present to fast the month, the command to the one given a concession to observe the number of days he broke the fast in, and the concession in permitting the breaking of the fast. So His saying «ولِتُكْمِلوا» is the reason for the command to observe the number; «لِتُكَبِّروا» is the reason for what is known about how to make up the days and to be released from the obligation of the fast-breaking; and «لعلَّكم تَشْكرون» is the reason for the concession and the facilitation. This is a kind of laff (interwoven list), subtle in approach, which only the keen-sighted among the scholars of bayān can discern." The sixth: that the wāw conjoins to an omitted cause, the implied form being: "so that you do what you know and so that you complete", said al-Zamakhsharī; and on this the thing caused is the wish for facilitation. The summary of these analyses is that this lām is a cause for an omitted element, either before it or after it, or a cause for the verb mentioned before it, namely «يُريد».
The third: that it is the lām of command, the wāw having conjoined an imperative clause to a declarative clause. On this it is a case of conjoining clauses, whereas on the previous view it is a case of conjoining single words, as set out earlier. This is the view of Ibn ʿAṭiyya, and the Shaykh weakened it for two reasons. The first: that commanding the addressee with the imperfect and its lām is a rare dialect, as in «لِتَقُمْ يا زيد», and «فَبِذَلِكَ فَلْيَفْرَحُواْ» [Yūnus: 58] has been read irregularly with the tāʾ of address. The second: that the readers agreed on kasra for this lām, and had it been for command, both kasra and sukūn would have been allowed in it like its sisters.
The majority read «ولِتُكْمِلوا» lightened, from «أَكْمل», the hamza in it being for transitivity. Abū Bakr read it with shadda on the mīm, the doubling also being for transitivity, because hamza and doubling alternate in transitivity for the most part. The alif and lām in «العِدَّة» admit two analyses. The first: that it is for previous mention (ʿahd), so that it refers back to His saying, the Exalted: {فَعِدَّةٌ مِّنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ}, and this is the apparent one. The second: that it is generic, so that it refers back to the month of Ramaḍān that is commanded to be fasted, and the meaning is that you bring a substitute for Ramaḍān complete in its number, whether thirty or twenty-nine. The lām in «وَلِتُكَبِّروا» is like the one in «ولِتُكْمِلوا», so what is said of it is like what is said of that, except that the fourth view [Translator's note: the source prints "القول الربع", evidently a slip for "الرابع"] does not work here.
His saying: {على مَا هَدَاكُمْ}: this preposition and its genitive noun is attached to «تُكَبِّروا». As to «على» there are two views. The first: that it has its basic sense of elevation, and the verb of takbīr (magnifying) is made transitive by it because it is understood to contain the meaning of praising. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is as though it said: 'and so that you magnify Allah, praising Him for having guided you'." The Shaykh said: "This is an explanation of meaning, not of i'rab, for if it were so, «على» would be attached to «حامدين», which he implied, not to «تُكَبِّروا»; and the i'rab implication in this is: 'so that you praise Allah by magnifying Him for having guided you', as people have implied in His saying:
851 - قد قَتَلَ اللهُ زياداً عَنِّي
(Allah has killed Ziyād on my behalf)
i.e. He turned him away from me by killing, and in his saying:
852 - ويَرْكَبُ يومَ الرَّوْع مِنَّا فوارِسٌ ... بصيرونَ في طَعْن الكُلى والأباهِرِ
(And on the day of terror horsemen of ours ride out ... skilled in piercing kidneys and aortas)
i.e. in control through insight in piercing the kidneys." The second: that it has the meaning of the lām of cause; the first is preferable, because figurative usage in a particle is weak.
«ما» in {على مَا هَدَاكُمْ} admits two analyses; the more apparent: that it is maṣdarī (verbal-noun-forming), i.e. "for His guiding you". The second: that it means "the one who" (alladhī). The Shaykh said: "This is remote for two reasons. The first: omission of the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid), its implied form being «هداكُموه»", and he implied it as accusative, not genitive with a lām or «إلى», because omitting an accusative is easier. The second: omission of a muḍāf by which the meaning of the sentence is made sound, its implied form being 'for following that which guided you' or the like."
This verse is closed with the hope of gratitude, because before it are facilitation and concession, so closing it with that is fitting. The two verses before it were closed with the hope of piety (taqwā), namely His saying: {وَلَكُمْ فِي القصاص حَيَاةٌ} [al-Baqara: 179] and His saying: {كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصيام} [al-Baqara: 178], because retaliation and fasting are among the hardest obligations, so closing them with that was fitting. This is a consistent manner: wherever a concession occurs, it is generally followed by the hope of gratitude, and wherever no concession occurs, it is followed by the hope of piety and the like. This is among the fine points of the science of bayān.

semin-durr:279-279.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَأْذَنُواْ}: Ḥamza and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «فآذِنوا» with an alif after the hamza; the others read it without alif, with the hamza quiescent.
The first is from «آذَنَه بكذا», that is, "he informed him of such-and-such", as in His saying: {فَقُلْ آذَنتُكُمْ على سَوَآءٍ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 109]. The meaning is: "inform others." Those addressed are commanded, having abandoned ribā, to inform others who are in the same state as themselves, persisting in ribā, of the war from Allah and His Messenger. So the object here is omitted; the poet made it explicit in his saying:
1114 - آذَنَتْنَا بِبَيْنِها أسماءُ ... رُبَّ ثاوٍ يُمَلُّ منه الثَّواءُ
(Asmāʾ informed us of her departure; many a one who stays is wearied of for his staying.)
and in His saying, the Exalted: {آذَنتُكُمْ}. It was said: the hamza in «فَأْذَنُوا» is for becoming (ṣayrūra), not for transitivity, and the meaning is: "become knowers of the war"; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and there is great remoteness in it.
The reading of the others is an imperative from «أَذِنَ يَأْذَنُ», that is, «عَلِمَ يَعْلَمُ» (he knew): "so know." It is said: «أَذِن به فهو أَذِين», that is, he knew it, so he is knowing (ʿalīm).
A group preferred Ḥamza's reading. Makkī said: "Were it not that the community of readers is on the short form, the preferred one would be the long." He justified this by saying that «آذَنَ» with the long vowel is more general than «أَذِنَ» with the short, because if they inform others they themselves necessarily know, but not the reverse; or they know by themselves while others do not know." He said: "ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and a group read with the short form."
Abū Ḥātim reversed this and preferred the short reading, and found the long reading remote. He said: "Because the command in it, to make war, is directed to others, while the intended are they themselves, since they are the ones addressed with abandoning ribā." But what he said is not necessary; for if you were in a state and I said to you, "O so-and-so, inform so-and-so that he is committing something ugly," and it is something like what you are in, you would know certainly that you too are commanded by it; indeed it is more forceful than my commanding you directly. Thus also said Thaʿlab, who said: "The preferred is the reading of the common people, from «الإذن», because it explains «be of knowledge and awareness»; and because the discourse proceeds by it on one track, and it is more indicative of the intended meaning and closer to understanding." Abū ʿUbayda said: "One says: «أَذِنْتُه بالشيء فَأَذِنَ به», that is, he knew, like «أَنْذَرْتُهُ بالشيء فَنَذِرَ به»", making it the intransitive-passive correlate (muṭāwiʿ) of «أَفْعَلَ».
Abū ʿAlī said: "When they are commanded to inform others, they themselves undoubtedly know; so in their informing is their knowing, whereas in their knowing there is no informing of others. Hence the long reading is preferable, since it is more forceful and more emphatic."
Al-Ṭabarī said: "The short reading is preferable because it is specific to them; on the long reading they were commanded only to inform others."
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It was also read «فآذِنُوا»: 'inform others of it'; it is from «الإذن», which is making hear, for it is one of the ways of knowledge. Al-Ḥasan read «فَأَيْقِنُوا»", and this is evidence for the reading of the common people, meaning the short form, because it is explicit in knowing, not in informing.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The two readings are equal in my view, because the addressee is delimited, being everyone who does not abandon what remains of ribā. If «فَأْذَنوا» is said, the command includes them all; and if «فآذِنُوا» with the long vowel is said, the meaning is: 'inform yourselves, or some of you the others', and this reading as though requires leaving them room for reflection and deliberation, that is: 'inform yourselves of this, then consider what is better for you: abandoning ribā or war.'"
His saying: {بِحَرْبٍ}: the bāʾ, on the short reading, is, the Shaykh said, "for attachment (ilṣāq); you say «أَذِنَ بكذا», meaning he knew such-and-such, and therefore Ibn ʿAbbās and others said: the meaning is 'be certain of a war from Allah'." I say: I have established that a verb of knowing, although originally transitive by itself, is made transitive by the bāʾ because of the sense of comprehension it contains, and so it is here. It appears from Ibn ʿAṭiyya's words that this bāʾ is locative (ẓarfiyya), for he said: "It is in my view from «الإذن», and when a person gives consent (idhn) to something he has settled it and built on it within himself; so it is as though it were said to them: 'settle the war between you and Allah and His Messenger.'" His saying "when a person gives consent in something" requires the implied reading «فَأْذنوا في حربٍ» (consent to a war), and this works only on the short reading; as for the bāʾ with the long reading, it makes «الإعلام» transitive in the manner I stated.
His saying: {مِّنَ الله} is attached to an omitted element, because it is a ṣifa (adjective) of the indefinite noun before it. «مِنْ» has two aspects, the more apparent being that it is for the beginning of the extent, figuratively, and in it is a sense of awe and magnification of the war, since it comes from Allah the Exalted. The second is that it is partitive, that is, "of the wars of Allah", with an omitted muḍāf. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was it not said «بحربِ اللَّهِ ورسولهِ»? I say: this is more forceful, for the meaning is: 'be informed of a mighty kind of war from Allah and His Messenger.'" End. It is more forceful because, had it been annexed, it could have been taken as the annexation of the maṣdar to its agent, which is what is intended, and could also have been taken as annexation to its object, meaning that you are making war on Allah and His Messenger; and the first meaning is more forceful. So he left what is ambiguous for what is explicit in the intended meaning.
His saying: {وَلاَ تُظْلَمُونَ} has two aspects. The more apparent is that it has no position, being resumptive; the Exalted informs them of that, that is: you do not wrong others by taking an increase from them, and you are not wronged either, by the loss of your capital sums. The second is that it is in the position of an accusative as ḥāl from the pronoun in «لكم», the governor being the sense of being-established contained in the preposition and its genitive noun, since it occurs as a khabar, in the opinion of al-Akhfash.
The majority read the first verb in the active and the second in the passive. Abān and al-Mufaḍḍal related from ʿĀṣim the reverse. Al-Fārisī preferred the reading of the common people because it suits His saying {وَإِنْ تُبْتُمْ} in assigning both verbs to the agent; thus «تَظْلِمُون» in the active is closer to what precedes it. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «أَشْكَلُ بما قبله», literally "more similar to what precedes it"; rendered accordingly.] Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is read with the agent named in the first and not named in the second. Its justification is that preventing them from wronging is more important, so it was begun with; and it is read in reverse, the justification being that He put first what reassures their souls, the denial of wrong to them, then forbade them wronging. It is also possible that the two readings have one meaning, because the wāw does not impose order."

semin-durr:200-200.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَّنَاسِكَكُمْ}: the plural of «مَنْسَك», with fatḥa or kasra on the sīn; their verification will come, and their derivation was given a little earlier. The readers read it with the two kāfs clearly separated, but assimilation (idghām) is reported from Abū ʿAmr. They said: he likened the case-vowel to the vowel of an indeclinable form, and dropped it for the sake of assimilation. He also assimilated «مناسككم», but did not assimilate what resembles it, such as {جِبَاهُهُمْ} [al-Tawba: 35] and {وُجُوهُهُمْ} [Āl ʿImrān: 106].

His saying: {كَذِكْرِكُمْ آبَآءَكُمْ}: The kāf is like the kāf in His saying {كَمَا هَدَاكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 198], except for its meaning «على» or the lām, so one should look into that. The majority read «آباءكم» accusative as a direct object (mafʿūl bihi), the maṣdar (verbal noun) being annexed to its agent, as in the original. Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb read «آباؤكم» nominative, the maṣdar being annexed to its object, and the meaning is: as the son is devoted to mentioning his father. It is also reported from him: «أباكم» in the singular, intending the genus, and it agrees with the reading of the majority in that the maṣdar is annexed to its agent. It is unlikely to say that it is nominative on the dialect of those who treat «أباك» and its like as an indeclinable-ending (maqṣūr) noun.

His saying: {أَوْ أَشَدَّ ذِكْراً}: «أشد» may be genitive or accusative. As for its being genitive, they mentioned two analyses. The first: that it is genitive by being conjoined to «ذِكركم», which is genitive through the kāf of comparison, its implied form being: "or like a remembrance more intense in remembrance", whereby the remembrance is given a remembrance, figuratively. Al-Zajjāj took this view, and Abū l-Baqāʾ and Ibn ʿAṭiyya followed him.

The second: that it is genitive by being conjoined to the genitive term by virtue of the annexation of the maṣdar to it, which is the pronoun of those addressed. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«أو أشدَّ ذكراً» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to what the remembrance was annexed to in «كذكركم», as you say: «كذكرِ قريشٍ آباءَهم أو قومٍ أشدَّ منهم ذِكْراً» ('like the Quraysh's mention of their fathers, or of a people more intense than them in mention')." What al-Zamakhsharī said has a good meaning, with no figurative usage in giving the remembrance a remembrance, because he made «أشد» one of the attributes of those who remember. But it involves conjoining to a genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition, which is forbidden according to the Basrans and is a place of necessity.

As for its being accusative, it has several analyses. The first: that it is conjoined to «آباءكم». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning is: or more intense in remembrance than your fathers, in that «ذِكْراً» is the act of the one mentioned." This statement needs explanation. His saying "it is conjoined to «آباءكم»" means that when you conjoin «أشد» to «آباءكم» the implied form is: "or a people more intense in remembrance than your fathers", so the people are mentioned, and the remembrance, which is the tamyīz (specification) after «أشدَّ», is their act, i.e. the act of the people mentioned, because it comes after «أَفْعَلَ», which is an adjective of the people; and the meaning of «من آبائِكم» is "than your remembrance of your fathers". This too involves no figurative usage whereby remembrance is made a rememberer.

The second: that it is conjoined to the position of the kāf in «كذكركم», because according to them it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being: "a remembrance like your remembrance of your fathers, or more intense", and they made the remembrance a rememberer, figuratively, like their saying «شعرٌ شاعِرٌ» ("poetry that is poetic"). This is the analysis of Abū ʿAlī and Ibn Jinnī.

The third: Makkī said: that it is accusative by an implied verb. He said: "Its implied form is: «فاذكروه ذكراً أشد من ذكركم لآبائكم» ('Remember Him with a remembrance more intense than your remembrance of your fathers'), so it is an adjective of a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. remember Him reaching the utmost in remembrance."

The fourth: that it is accusative by an implied verb of being (kāna). Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "In my view the speech is carried on the meaning, and the implied form is: «أو كونوا أشدَّ لله ذِكْراً منكم لآبائكم» ('or be more intense in remembrance of Allah than you are of your fathers'), and this meaning is indicated by His saying «فاذكروا الله», i.e. be rememberers of Him. This is easier than carrying it on the figurative usage," meaning the figurative usage mentioned earlier from al-Fārisī and his student.

The fifth: that «أشدَّ» is accusative as a ḥāl from «ذِكْراً», because if it came after it, it would be an adjective of it, as in his saying:

891 - لميَّةَ موحشاًَ طَلَلٌ ... يَلُوح كأنه خِلَلُ
(Mayya has a ruin, desolate, that gleams as if it were sword-sheaths.)
