«موحشاً» is a ḥāl from «طلل», because originally it is an adjective, and when it was fronted its remaining an adjective became impossible, so it was made a ḥāl. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said this. After mentioning three analyses for its being accusative and two for its being genitive, he said: "These are five analyses, all weak. What comes first to the mind in the verse is that they were commanded to remember Allah with a remembrance that equals the remembrance of their fathers or is more intense, and it is possible for us to carry this verse on that in a way they overlooked." Then he mentioned what preceded. Then he allowed two analyses for «ذِكْراً» in this case. One: that it is conjoined to the position of the kāf in «كذكركم». Then he objected to himself on this analysis, since it requires separation between the conjunction «أو» and the conjoined «ذِكْراً» by the ḥāl, namely «أشدَّ», while the grammarians have stated that separation between them is not permissible except under two conditions: one, that the conjunction be more than one letter; the other, that the separating element be an oath, an adverbial, or a preposition with its genitive. One of the two conditions is present, namely that it exceeds one letter, and the other is missing, namely that the separator is not one of the three mentioned. Then he replied that the ḥāl is implicitly governed by a preposition, and likened it to the adverbial, so it was treated like them.

The second of the two analyses of «ذِكْراً»: that it is a maṣdar for His saying «فاذكروا», and His saying «كذكركم» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from «ذِكْراً», because originally it is an adjective of it, and when it was fronted it became a ḥāl; and «أشدَّ» is conjoined to this ḥāl. The implied form of the speech is: "Remember Allah with a remembrance like your remembrance, i.e. resembling your remembrance or more intense." So it becomes parallel to: «اضربْ مثل ضربِ فلانٍ ضرباً أو أشد» ("Strike like so-and-so's striking, a striking, or more intense"), the original being: «اضرب ضرباً مثلَ ضَرْبِ فلانٍ أو أشدَّ».

And «ذِكْراً» is a tamyīz according to others than the Shaykh, as mentioned. They found it problematic that it be an accusative tamyīz, because the elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl) must be annexed to what follows it when that is of the same kind as what precedes, as in «وجهُ زيدٍ أحسنُ وجهٍ» ("Zayd's face is the best face") and «وعِلْمُهُ أكثرُ علم» ("his knowledge is the most knowledge"); and if it is not of the same kind as what precedes it, accusative is required, as in «زيد أحسنُ وجهاً وخالدٌ أكثرُ علماً» ("Zayd is better in face and Khālid greater in knowledge").

Once that is established: his saying «ذِكْراً» is of the same kind as what precedes it, so on what was laid down it would require genitive, for it is parallel to: «اضربْ بكراً كضربِ عمرو زيداً أو أشدَّ ضربٍ» ("Strike Bakr like ʿAmr's striking of Zayd, or the most intense striking"), with genitive only. The answer to this difficulty is taken from the analyses given above for the accusative and the genitive mentioned for «أشدَّ»: either by making the remembrance a rememberer figuratively, like their saying «شِعْرٌ شاعرٌ», as al-Fārisī and his companion said; or by making «أشدَّ» one of the attributes of persons, not of the acts of remembering, as al-Zamakhsharī said; or by making «أشدَّ» a ḥāl from «ذِكْراً»; or by making it accusative by a verb. All this, although understood from what preceded, I have stated explicitly, to ease the matter, for it is a place that needs consideration and reflection. This is the end of the discussion of this question as far as this book is concerned. As for «أو» here, it was said to be for permission (ibāḥa), and it was said to be for choice (takhyīr), and it was said to mean «بل» ("rather").

His saying: {مَن يَقُولُ رَبَّنَآ آتِنَا}: «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is in the preposition and its genitive noun before it; it may also be an agent according to al-Akhfash, and it may be an indefinite noun with an adjective. In this speech there is an iltifāt (shift of person), for had it followed the first pattern it would have been said «فمنكم» ("so among you"); and it was carried on the meaning of «مَنْ», since the pronoun came in the plural in «ربَّنا آتِنا»; had it been carried on its form, it would have said «ربِّ آتني» ("My Lord, give me").

Regarding the second object of «آتِنا», because it takes two objects, the second being other than the first, there are three views. The most apparent: that it is omitted for brevity or restriction, since it is of the type of «أعطى» ("gave"), i.e. "give us what we want", or "what we ask for". The second: that «في» means «مِنْ», i.e. "from this world". The third: that it is redundant, i.e. "give us this world". The last two are nothing.

semin-durr:221-221.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلاَ تَنْكِحُواْ}: the majority read with fatḥa on the tāʾ of the imperfect; al-Aʿmash read it with ḍamma, from the quadriliteral verb ankaḥa, in which the hamza is for transitivity; on this basis one of the two objects is omitted, namely the first object, because it is an agent in meaning, its implied form being: "and do not marry yourselves (lā tunkiḥū anfusakum) to the idolatresses".

Al-nikāḥ, originally among the Arabs, is clinging to a thing and bending over it, and from it "the rain nakaḥa the earth"; Thaʿlab reported this from Abū Zayd and Ibn al-Aʿrābī. It was said that its origin is interpenetration, and from it "the trees tanākaḥat", that is, their branches intertwined. Nikāḥ is also applied to the contract, as in his saying:

947 - ولا تَقْرَبَنَّ جارةً إنَّ سِرَّها ... حرامٌ عليك فانِكحَنْ أو تأبَّدا
("Do not go near a neighbour woman, for her secret is forbidden to you; so marry, or live wild")

that is: so contract (a marriage), or live wild and avoid women. It is also applied to intercourse, as in his saying:

948 - البارِكينَ على ظهورِ نِسْوَتِهِمْ ... والناكحينَ بِشَطْءِ دجلةَ البَقَرَا
("Those who crouch on the backs of their women, and who copulate with the cows on the bank of the Tigris")

Al-Farrāʾ reported «nukḥ al-marʾa», with ḍamma on the nūn, on the pattern of «al-qubul» and «al-dubur», meaning her private part (buḍʿ); so the meaning of their saying «nakaḥahā» is that he reached that place, like «kabadahu», that is, he struck his liver. It is seldom said «nākaḥahā», as one says «bāḍaʿahā».

Abū ʿAlī said: «The Arabs distinguished between the contract and intercourse by a subtle distinction: when they say "Fulān nakaḥa Fulāna" or "the daughter of so-and-so", they mean he contracted a marriage with her; and when they say "he nakaḥa his wife (imraʾatahu) or his spouse (zawjatahu)", they mean nothing but sexual intercourse. Is its application to both by way of literal meaning, so that it is a case of homonymy (ishtirāk), or by way of literal and figurative meaning? The apparent view is the second, for the figurative is better than homonymy; and if it is said to be literal and figurative, then there are two views as to which is literal: a group held that it is literal for intercourse, and a group held the opposite. Al-Rāghib said: «The origin of nikāḥ is for the contract, then it was borrowed for intercourse; and it is impossible that it be originally for intercourse and then borrowed for the contract, because all the names of intercourse are euphemisms, owing to their finding its mention as repugnant as they find its practice; and it is impossible that one who does not intend obscenity should borrow the name of what they find abhorrent for what they find agreeable. The Exalted said: {فانكحوا مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ النسآء} [al-Nisāʾ: 3].»

His saying: {حتى يُؤْمِنَّ}: «ḥattā» here means only «ilā» (until), and the verb after it is accusative by an implied «an», that is: "until they believe"; it is indeclinable (mabnī) according to the well-known view because of its attachment to the feminine plural nūn, and the origin is «yuʾminnana» (يُؤْمِنْنَ), so the lām of the verb was assimilated into the feminine nūn.

His saying: {وَلأَمَةٌ مُّؤْمِنَةٌ خَيْرٌ}: two things justified the beginning with «أَمَة»: the lām of inceptive emphasis (lām al-ibtidāʾ) and the qualification (adjective). The origin of «أمة» is «amawun», and its lām was dropped irregularly (ʿalā ghayri qiyās), and the tāʾ of the feminine was given in compensation for it, like «qulla» and «thuba»; what shows that its lām is a wāw is its reappearance in the plural. Al-Kilābī said:

949 - أمَّا الإِماءُ فلا يَدْعُونني ولداً ... إذا تداعى بنون الإِمْوانِ بالعارِ
("As for the slave-women, they do not call me a son, when the sons of the female slaves call one another by disgrace")

and also because of its appearing in the maṣdar: they said «a clear amatun (slave woman) of slavehood (umūwa)» and «she acknowledged to him her slavehood (umūwa)». Is its pattern «faʿala» with the ʿayn vowelled, or «faʿla» with the ʿayn unvowelled? Two views, the first being the more evident. On this basis its analogical form would have been for its lām to be turned into an alif because of its vowelling and the fatḥa before it, like «fatāt» and «qanāt», but it was dropped irregularly.

The second view was held by Abū al-Haytham, who claimed that the plural of «ama» is «amw», and that its pattern is «faʿla» with unvowelled ʿayn, so it would be like «nakhl» and «nakhla», and its origin «amwa»; so they dropped its lām since it was a weak letter; then when they pluralised it on the model of «nakhla» and «nakhl», it would have been necessary for them to say «ama» and «am», but they disliked making it two letters and disliked restoring the dropped wāw because it was at the end of the noun, so they put the wāw first and made an alif between the hamza and the mīm, and said «ām». And what he claimed is nothing, for it would have been necessary for the iʿrāb to be on the mīm, as it was on the lām of «nakhl» and the rāʾ of «tamr», but it is on the dropped tāʾ (sic), implied, as its explanation will come. [Translator's note: the source reads «ولكنه على التاءِ المحذوفَةِ مقدَّرٌ», translated as written; it presumably means that the iʿrāb is implied on the dropped letter.] It was pluralised as «imwān», as has preceded, and as «imāʾ», the origin being «imāwun», like «raqaba» and «riqāb», and the wāw was turned into hamza because it came at the end after an extra alif, like «kisāʾ». And in the ḥadīth: «لا تَمْنَعُوا إماءَ اللَّهِ مساجدَ الله» ("Do not prevent the female servants of Allah from the mosques of Allah"). And as «āmin», the poet said:

950 - تَمْشِي بها رُبْدُ النَّعا ... مِ تَماشِيَ الآمِ الزوافِرْ
("Dusky ostriches walk in it, walking like the female slaves who carry water-skins…")

[Translator's note: the gloss of this half-verse is tentative; the second half of the verse is incomplete in the source's rendering.]

The origin is «aʾmuwun» with two hamzas, the first vowelled with fatḥa and extra, the second unvowelled and being the fāʾ of the word, like «akama» and «aʾkum»; so the wāw fell at the end with ḍamma before it, in a declinable noun, and it has no parallel; so the wāw was turned into yāʾ and the ḍamma into kasra so that the yāʾ would be sound, and the noun became of the class of the defective noun (manqūṣ), like «ghāzin» and «qāḍin». Then the second hamza was turned into an alif because it is unvowelled after another with fatḥa; so you say «jāʾa āmin», «marartu bi-āmin» and «raʾaytu āmiyan», implying the ḍamma and the kasra and showing the fatḥa; and its parallel in this reversal in plurals is «adlin» and «ajrin», plurals of «dalw» and «jarw». And this morphological analysis we have given refutes Abū al-Haytham's earlier statement, I mean his claim that «āmiyan» is the plural of «amwa» with unvowelled ʿayn and that it was reversed, for if it were so, it would have been right to say «jāʾa āmun», «marartu bi-āmin» and «raʾaytu āman», and «jāʾa al-āmu», «marartu bi-l-āmi», with the iʿrāb shown by overt vowels.

The comparative in His saying: {خَيْرٌ مِّن مُّشْرِكةٍ} is either by way of belief, not by way of actual existence, or because marrying a believing woman comprises benefits of the Hereafter, whereas marrying a free idolatress comprises worldly benefits; this holds if we commit to the view that «afʿal» must indicate some excess; otherwise there is no need for this interpretation, as is the view of al-Farrāʾ and a group.

And His saying: {مِّن مُّشْرِكَةٍ}: it is possible that «مشركةٍ» is an adjective of an omitted noun indicated by its counterpart, that is, "than a free idolatress", or indicated by its own wording, that is, "than a slave woman who is an idolatress", according to the disagreement over His saying «ولأمةٌ»: is what is meant the woman owned by human beings, or women in general because they are the property of Allah the Exalted? And likewise the disagreement over His saying: {وَلَعَبْدٌ مُّؤْمِنٌ خَيْرٌ مِّن مُّشْرِكٍ}; and the discussion of it is like the discussion of this.

His saying: {وَلَوْ أَعْجَبَتْكُمْ} and His saying «ولو أَعْجَبَكم»: this clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. It has already preceded that this «law» in a construction like this is conditional in the sense of «in» (if), as in "Turn away the beggar, even with a burnt hoof"; and that the wāw is a conjunction upon an omitted ḥāl, the implied form being: "better than an idolatress in every state, even in this state"; and that this is to cover all states exhaustively; and that what follows this «law» comes only as something somehow contrary to what precedes it: so admiration is contrary to the ruling of goodness, and it requires the permissibility of marriage owing to the desire of the one who marries for her.

Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «"Law" here is in the sense of "in", and likewise at every place where the past verb occurs after "law" and its jawāb precedes it»; and its being in the sense of «in» does not require that its jawāb precede. Do you not see that they said of His saying, the Exalted: {لَوْ تَرَكُواْ مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّةً ضِعَافاً خَافُواْ عَلَيْهِمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 9] that it is in the sense of «in», though its jawāb, «خافوا», comes after it? He himself stated that in the verse of al-Nisāʾ, saying of «خافوا»: «It is the jawāb of "law", and its meaning is "in".»

His saying: {والمغفرة}: the majority read «المغفرة» in the genitive, conjoined to «الجنة», and «بإذنه» is attached to «يدعو», that is, by His facilitating it.

In other than this verse «المغفرة» precedes «الجنة»: {سابقوا إلى مَغْفِرَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ وَجَنَّةٍ} [al-Ḥadīd: 21], {وسارعوا إلى مَغْفِرَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ وَجَنَّةٍ} [Āl ʿImrān: 133]; and this is the original order, because forgiveness is a cause of entering Paradise. It was put later here only for correspondence, for before it is «يدعو إلى النار», so He put Paradise first to set it against the Fire in wording, and because souls yearn for it when He mentions Allah's calling to it, so He brought the more noble. Al-Ḥasan read «والمغفرةُ بإذنِهِ» as mubtadaʾ and khabar, that is: "attained by His permission".

semin-durr:280-280.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِن كَانَ ذُو عُسْرَةٍ}: Regarding this «كان» there are two aspects. The first, and the more apparent, is that it is complete (tāmma), meaning "occurred and existed", that is, "if one in hardship occurs", so it is content with its agent like all other verbs. It is said that it is most often thus when its nominative is indefinite, such as «قد كان مِنْ مَطَرٍ» (there has been some rain). The second is that it is the incomplete (nāqiṣa) and the khabar is omitted. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Its implied form is: «وإنْ كان ذو عسرة لكم عليه حَقٌّ» (if one in hardship, to whom you have a right, ...), or the like." This is the position of some of the Kufans on the verse, and the khabar was implied as: «وإنْ كان من غُرمائِكُمْ ذو عُسْرَةٍ» (if among your debtors there is one in hardship). Some implied it as: «وإنْ كان ذو عسرةٍ غريماً» (if the one in hardship is a debtor).
The Shaykh said: "Omitting the khabar of «كان» is not permitted by our colleagues, neither for brevity nor for limitation, for a reason they mentioned in grammar. If it is said: did not the Basrans, when the Kufans argued against them that «ليس» can be a conjunction by the verse:
1115 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... إنما يَجْزِي الفتى ليسَ الجَمَلْ
(... the young man is requited, not the camel)
interpret it as an omission of the khabar? And they recited as evidence for omission of the khabar his saying:
1116 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... يبغى جِوارَك حين ليسَ مُجِيرُ
(He seeks your protection when there is no protector.)
And if this is established, it is established for the rest of the chapter." The answer is that this is specific to «ليس», because it resembles the negative «لا», and the khabar of «لا» may be omitted, so also what resembles it. The reason to which the Shaykh alluded is that the demand for the khabar is doubly reinforced: first, it is a predicate about a subject; second, it is governed by the verb before it. Since its being required is reinforced, its omission is barred.
The Kufans were strengthened by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, Ubayy and ʿUthmān: «وإن كان ذا عُسْرةٍ», that is, "if the debtor is one in hardship." Abū ʿAlī said: "In «كان» its subject is a pronoun, implied as «هو», that is, the debtor; what has preceded of the discourse indicates its being implied, because the one who practises ribā must have someone with whom he does ribā."
Al-Aʿmash read: «وإنْ كان مُعْسِراً». Al-Dānī related from Aḥmad ibn Mūsā: "It is thus in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh."
But the majority favour the reading of the common people and analyse the well-known reading. Makkī said: "«وإنْ وقع ذو عسرةٍ» (if one in hardship occurs), and this is permissible for all people; whereas if you made «ذا» accusative as the khabar of «كان», it would become specific to particular people; for this reason the well-known readers agreed on the nominative of «ذو»." Al-Wāḥidī made this clear, saying: "that is, if one in hardship occurs; the meaning on this basis is sound. For if it were put in the accusative, so that «وإنْ كان ذا عسرةٍ» were said, the meaning would be 'if the purchaser is one in hardship, then a respite', and the respite would be limited to him, and the matter is not so, because the purchaser and others, if in hardship, have the respite until ease." The Shaykh said: "Whoever puts «ذا عسرة» in the accusative or reads «مُعْسِراً» is said to restrict it to people of ribā, and whoever puts it in the nominative, it is general for everyone who has a debt." He said: "This is not necessary, because the verse was brought only about people of ribā and was revealed about them." I say: This answer is of no avail, for although the context is so, the ruling is not specific to them.
«العُسْرَةُ» has the meaning of «العُسْر» (hardship).
His saying: {فَنَظِرَةٌ}: the fāʾ is the apodosis of the condition, and «نَظِرةٌ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, «فالأمرُ» (the matter) or «فالواجِبُ» (the obligation); or it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, that is, «فعليكم نظرةٌ» (upon you is a respite); or it is an agent of an implied verb, that is, «فتجِبُ نظرةٌ» (a respite is obligatory).
The common people read «نَظِرة» on the pattern of «نَبِقَة». Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and Abū Rajāʾ read «فَنَظْرة» with the ʿayn quiescent; this is a Tamīmī dialect: they say «كَبْد» for «كَبِد» and «كَتْف» for «كَتِف». ʿAṭāʾ read «فناظِرَة» on the pattern of «فاعِلَة»; Abū Isḥāq analysed it as a maṣdar, like {لَيْسَ لِوَقْعَتِهَا كَاذِبَةً} [al-Wāqiʿa: 2], {يَعْلَمُ خَآئِنَةَ الأعين} [Ghāfir: 19], {أَن يُفْعَلَ بِهَا فَاقِرَةٌ} [al-Qiyāma: 25]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «فناظِرُهُ» – that is, the owner of the right is the one who waits for him (nāẓiruhu), meaning the one who awaits him; or the possessor of his respite, in the manner of relation (nisba), as they say «مكان عاشِب وباقل» meaning possessing herbage and possessing vegetables; and from him [also]: «فناظِرْهُ» as an imperative, meaning: 'be lenient with him by respite and attend to him with it.'" His transmitting the first reading from him requires that his reading was «ناظِر», an active participle annexed to the pronoun of the one in hardship, unlike the reading I presented from ʿAṭāʾ, which is «ناظرةٌ» with the tāʾ of the feminine, and for that reason al-Zajjāj analysed it as a maṣdar. ʿAbd Allāh read «فناظِرُوه», an imperative to the group to grant respite. These are six readings, of which one is well known. [Translator's note: the printed text mentions "the Kufans" as «الكفيون» earlier; this is a misprint for «الكوفيون».]
This clause is a statement in wording and a command in meaning, like His saying: {والوالدات يُرْضِعْنَ} [al-Baqara: 233], which has been dealt with. «النظرةُ» comes from «الانتظار», which is patience and giving time.
His saying: {إلى مَيْسَرَةٍ}: Nāfiʿ alone read «مَيْسُرَة» with ḍamma on the sīn, and the others with fatḥa. The fatḥa is the well-known one, since «مَفْعَل» and «مَفْعَلَة» with fatḥa are many, while «مَفْعُل» with ḍamma is nonexistent except for al-Kisāʾī; and I shall adduce some words of it. As for «مَفْعُلة», they said it is very rare and is the dialect of the Hijaz, and some words have come in it, such as: «المَسْرُقَة» والمَقْبُرَةِ والمَشْرُبة، والمَسْرُبة والمَقْدُرَة والمَأْدُبَة والمَفْخُرَة والمَزْرُعة ومَعْوُلَة ومَكْرُمَة ومَأْلُكة.
Al-Naḥḥās rejected the ḍamma, out of boldness on his part, and said: "«مَفْعُلة» has come only in a few counted words, of which this is not one; moreover the hāʾ is extra, and «مَفْعُل» has never come in its speech at all." End. Sībawayh said: "There is no «مَفْعُل» in the language." Abū ʿAlī said: "He means in singulars." It has been related from Sībawayh «مَهْلَك» with the lām in three vowels. Al-Kisāʾī said: «مَفْعُل» exists in singulars, and he adduced from it «مَكْرُماً» in the poet's saying:
1117 - ليومِ رَوْعٍ أو فَعالِ مَكْرُمِ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(for a day of terror, or a deed of noble character...)
and «مَعْوُن» in the saying of another, namely Jamīl:
1118 - بُثَيْنُ الزمي «لا» إنَّ لا إنْ لَزِمْتِهِ ... على كثرةِ الواشين أيُّ مَعْونِ
(Buthayna, hold to "no"; for "no", if you hold to it, despite the multitude of slanderers, is a great help.)
and «مَأْلُكاً» in the saying of ʿAdī:
1119 - أَبْلِغِ النعمانَ عني مَأْلُكاً ... أنه قد طالَ حَبْسي وانتظاري
(Carry to al-Nuʿmān from me a message: that my imprisonment and my waiting have grown long.)
This is no objection to Sībawayh for two reasons. One: these are plurals of «مَكْرُمَة» and «مَعُونَة» and «مَأْلُكَة»; to this the Basrans and Kufans went, except al-Kisāʾī, and it is also transmitted from al-Farrāʾ. The other: Sībawayh does not take account of the rare, so he says "it has not occurred" even if a word or two have occurred of it, since he does not count the rare and odd.
This being established, the grammarians have declared mistaken Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ in their reading «إلى مَيْسُرِهِ», annexing «مَيْسُر» with ḍamma on the sīn to the pronoun of the debtor, because they built on the premise that there is no «مَفْعُل» among singulars. This should not be a mistake, because, even granting that «مَفْعُل» is not among singulars, «مَيْسُر» here is not a singular; it is the plural of «مَيْسُرَة», as you yourselves said that «مَكْرُماً» is the plural of «مَكْرُمَة» and the like; or the tāʾ of the feminine has been dropped for the annexation, as in:
1120 - إنَّ الخليطَ أَجَدُّوا البَّيْنَ فانجردوا ... وأَخْلَفوك عِدَ الأمرِ الذي وَعَدوا
(The companions resolved on parting and set off, and failed you in the promise of the matter they promised.)
that is, «عِدَة الأمر». What indicates this is that they reported of the two that they also read «إلى مَيْسَرِهِ» with fatḥa on the sīn annexed to the pronoun of the debtor; this reading is explicit in what I told you of the dropping of the tāʾ of the feminine for the annexation, so as to agree with the reading of the common people «إلى مَيْسَرَة» with the feminine tāʾ.
Abū al-Baqāʾ analysed it in another way, namely that the origin is «ميسورِه», lightened by dropping the wāw, contenting oneself with the ḍamma as indication of it. What he mentioned, despite its weakness, may be supported by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, who read «إلى مَيْسُوره», annexing «ميْسُور» to the pronoun; it is a maṣdar on the pattern «مَفْعُول», like «المَجْلود» and «المَعْقُول». This works only on the opinion of al-Akhfash, who affirmed among maṣdars the pattern «مَفْعُول», which Sībawayh did not affirm.
His saying: {وَأَن تَصَدَّقُواْ}: ʿĀṣim read it with the ṣād light, and the others with it doubled. The origin of both readings is one, for the origin is «تَتَصَدَّقُوا»; ʿĀṣim dropped one of the two tāʾs, either the first or the second (the disagreement on this was presented earlier), and the others assimilated the tāʾ into the ṣād. ʿAbd Allāh read according to this origin: «تَتَصَدَّقوا». The object of «التصدُّق» is omitted because it is known, that is, by granting respite. It was said: by the capital sum, in favour of the debtor. {إِن كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ}: its apodosis is omitted. «أَنْ تَصَدَّقُوا», interpreted as a maṣdar, is a mubtadaʾ, and «خيرٌ لكم» is its khabar.

semin-durr:210-210.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {هَلْ يَنظُرُونَ}: The wording of «هل» is interrogative, but what is meant by it is negation, as in his saying:

911 - وهلْ أنا إلا مِنْ غُزَيَّةَ إنْ غَوَتْ ... غَوَيْتُ وإنْ تَرْشُدْ غُزَيَّةُ أَرْشُدِ
(Am I anything but one of Ghuzayya? If she errs I err, and if Ghuzayya is rightly guided I am rightly guided.)

that is: "they do not wait" and "I am not"; for that reason «إلاَّ» occurs after it as it occurs after «ما».

«يَنْظُرون» here has the sense of yantaẓirūna (they wait), and it is made transitive by itself. Imruʾ al-Qays said:

912 - فإنَّكما إنْ تَنْظُراني ساعةً ... من الدَّهْرَ يَنْفَعْني لدى أُمِّ جُنْدَبِ
(If you two wait for me an hour of time, it will profit me with Umm Jundab.)

What is meant by naẓar here is not the turning of the eye, because the meaning does not call for that. Some argued for this by saying that naẓar in the sense of sight is made transitive by ilā and is annexed to the face, whereas in the noble verse it is transitive by itself and is not annexed to the face. By its annexation to the face he means the saying of the Exalted: {وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَّاضِرَةٌ إلى رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٌ} [al-Qiyāma: 23]; so (here) it would have the sense of waiting (intiẓār). But this is worthless. As for his saying that naẓar in the sense of sight is made transitive by ilā, it is conceded; but his saying "and here it is transitive by itself" is disputed, since it is possible that the preposition, namely «إلى», is omitted, because its omission is regular with «أَنْ» when there is no ambiguity. As for his saying "it is annexed to the face", this too is disputed, since it has come annexed to the person itself. The Exalted said: {أرني أَنظُرْ إِلَيْكَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 143] and {أَفَلاَ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَى الإبل} [al-Ghāshiya: 17]. The pronoun in «ينظرون» returns to those addressed by His saying «زَلَلْتُم», so it is an iltifāt (shift of person).

His saying: {إِلاَّ أَن يَأْتِيَهُمُ}: this is the object of «ينظرون» and it is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh), i.e. "they wait for nothing but the coming of Allah."

His saying: {فِي ظُلَلٍ}: There are four views on it. The first: that it is attached to «يأتِيَهم»; and the meaning is: His command, or His power, or His punishment, or the like comes to them; or it is a figure (kināya) for vengeance, since the ascription of coming to Allah the Exalted in the literal sense is impossible. The second: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl, and about its ṣāḥib there are two views. The first: it is the object of «يأتيهم», i.e. "while they are settled in canopies (ẓulal)", and this is literal. The second: that it is Allah the Exalted, by the aforementioned figurative sense, i.e. "the command of Allah while it is settled in canopies." The third: that «في» has the sense of «الباء», and it is attached to the coming, i.e. "unless He brings to them with canopies." Among the occurrences of «في» in the sense of «الباء» is the saying:

913 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... خَبيرون في طَعْنِ الكُلى والأباهِرِ
(... experts in piercing the kidneys and the aortas)

because «خبيرين» is made transitive only by «الباء», as in his saying:

914 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... خبيرٌ بأَدْواءِ النِّساء طَبيبُ
(... one well-versed in women's ailments, a physician)

The fourth: that it is a ḥāl from «الملائكة», placed before it, the original being: "unless Allah and the angels come to them in canopies." This is supported by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd) of it thus. By this also the figurative usage is reduced, since in this case nothing is ascribed to Allah the Exalted but the coming only, by the aforementioned figurative sense.

Ubayy, Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read: «في ظلالٍ», and there are two views on it. The first: that it is the plural of ẓill (shade), like ṣill (viper) and ṣilāl. The second: that it is the plural of ẓulla (canopy), like qulla and qilāl, khulla and khilāl; except that the form fiʿāl is not regular for fuʿla.

His saying: {مِّنَ الغمام}: there are two views on it. The first: that it is attached to an omitted element, because it is an adjective of «ظُلَل», the implied form being: "canopies that are of the cloud"; and «مِنْ» on this view is partitive. The second: that it is attached to «يأتيهم», and on this view it is for the beginning of the extent, i.e. "from the direction of the cloud".

The majority read «الملائكةُ» nominative, conjoined to the noun «الله». Al-Ḥasan and Abū Jaʿfar read «والملائكةِ» genitive, and there are two views on it. The first: genitive, conjoined to «ظُلَلٍ», i.e. "unless He comes to them in canopies and in the angels"; the second: genitive, conjoined to «الغمام», i.e. "from the cloud and from the angels", so the angels are described as being canopies by way of simile.

His saying: {وَقُضِيَ الأمور}: the majority read «قُضِيَ» as a passive past verb, and there are two views on it. The first: that it is conjoined to «يَأْتِيهم» and it enters the scope of the waiting, and that is by putting the past in the place of the future, the original being "wa-yuqḍā l-amru" (and the matter will be decreed); it was brought thus only because it is certain, as in His saying: {أتى أَمْرُ الله} [al-Naḥl: 1]. The second: that it is a resumptive clause in its own right, in which Allah the Exalted informs that He has finished with their affair; so it is a conjunction of clauses and does not enter the scope of the waiting. Muʿādh ibn Jabal read «وقضاء الأمر». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "as a nominative maṣdar conjoined to the angels." Another said: with the long vowel and genitive, conjoined to «الملائكة»; it was said: "on this view «في» has the sense of «الباء»", i.e. "with canopies, and with the angels, and with the decree of the matter." So two readings are reported from Muʿādh for the angels, nominative and genitive, and from them arose two readings of his for the saying «وقُضي الأمر».

His saying: {وَإِلَى الله تُرْجَعُ الامور}: this preposition and its genitive noun is attached to what follows it; it was put first only for restriction, i.e. "they return to none but Him, to the exclusion of any other." The majority read «تُرْجَعُ» with the feminine, because a broken plural is treated as feminine. However, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī and Nāfiʿ read it as active (tarjiʿu), and the rest read it as passive; and rajaʿa is used both as transitive at times and intransitive at others. The Exalted said: {فَإِن رَّجَعَكَ الله} [al-Tawba: 83]; the two readings came accordingly. In the transitive, arjaʿa, a quadriliteral, has been heard, and it is a weak dialect; therefore the scholars refused to make the reading of those who put it in the passive derived from it. Khārija read from Nāfiʿ: «يُرْجَعُ» in the masculine and passive, because its feminine is figurative (not literal). The omitted agent in the reading of those who put it in the passive is either Allah the Exalted, i.e. He returns them to Himself by annihilating this world; or the possessors of the affairs, because when their own selves and states bore witness against them that they are owned (by a Lord) and recompensed for their deeds, they were returning their affairs to their Creator.

semin-durr:211-211.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {سَلْ}: The majority read «سَلْ», and it admits two views. The first: that it is from the dialect "sāla yasālu", like "khāfa yakhāfu"; and whether this alif is converted from a hamza, a wāw or a yāʾ is a disagreement that preceded at His saying {فَإِنَّ لَكُمْ مَّا سَأَلْتُمْ}. In that case the imperative from it is «سَلْ», like «خَفْ»: when the lām was made quiescent, carrying the imperative on the jussive, two quiescent letters met, so the ʿayn (middle radical) was dropped for that reason, and its pattern on this view is «فَلْ». The second: that it is from saʾala with hamza, the original being «اسْأَلْ»; then the vowel of the hamza was cast onto the sīn for lightening, we counted the vowel of transfer, so we did without the hamzat al-waṣl and dropped it; its pattern is also «فُلْ» with the ʿayn dropped, though the derivation differs. ʿAbbās related from Abū ʿAmr: «اسأَلْ» in the original form without transfer. A group read «اسَلْ» with transfer and the hamzat al-waṣl, as if they did not count the transferred vowel, like their saying «الحْمَر» with the hamza. More explanation of these questions will come in their places, as you will see, if Allah wills. «بنى» is the first object according to the majority.

His saying: {كَمْ آتَيْنَاهُم}: In «كَمْ» there are two views. The first: that it is in the position of the accusative. There is disagreement on that. It was said: its being accusative is as the second object of «آتيناهم» according to the school of the majority, and the first (object) according to the school of al-Suhaylī, as its establishment has preceded. It was also said: it may be accusative by an implied verb which the verb after it explains, its implied form being "kam ātaynā ātaynāhum"; and we imply its governor after it only because the interrogative has the right of the head of the sentence and what is before it does not govern it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this, meaning that for him it belongs to the chapter of ishtighāl (preoccupation). The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "This is not permissible if «من آية» is a tamyīz (specification), because the explaining verb did not govern the pronoun of «كم» nor anything connected with it; and if that is not so, it cannot be of the chapter of ishtighāl, since it is a condition of ishtighāl that the explainer govern the pronoun of the first or something connected with it. The like of what he permitted would be your saying 'Zaydan ḍarabtu' (Zayd — I struck) as ishtighāl, and no one permits that. But if we say that its specifier is omitted and «كم» is applied to the people, that is permissible, because in the ishtighāl clause there is the pronoun of the first, the implied form being 'kam min qawmin ātaynāhum'." I say: What the Shaykh said, that it does not proceed if «من آية» is a tamyīz, was stated explicitly by Ibn ʿAṭiyya, for he said: "His saying «مِن آية» is on the first reading a second object of «آتيناهم», and on the second in the position of the tamyīz", meaning by the first its accusative by ishtighāl and by the second its accusative by what is after it.

The second of the two views on «كم»: that it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the clause after it is in the position of the nominative as its khabar, the returning pronoun being omitted, its implied form being "kam ātaynāhumūhā" or "ātaynāhum iyyāhā". Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū l-Baqāʾ permitted that, and the Shaykh found it weak, because omitting the returning pronoun in the accusative is not permitted except of necessity, as in his saying:

915 - وخالدٌ يَحْمَدُ ساداتُنا ... بالحقِّ لا يُحْمَدُ بالباطِل
(And Khālid — our chiefs praise him for what is right; he is not praised for falsehood.)

that is, "wa-Khālidun yaḥmaduhu". This is the report of some of them. As for Ibn Mālik, he reported that when the mubtadaʾ is the word «كُل» or what resembles it in indefiniteness and generality, omitting its accusative returning pronoun is permitted by agreement of the Basrans and the Kufans, and from this is {وَكُلاًّ وَعَدَ الله الحسنى} [al-Nisāʾ: 95] in the reading of Nāfiʿ; and when the mubtadaʾ is other than that, the Kufans forbid it except in broad usage, and the Basrans permit it with weakness, and from this is {أَفَحُكْمَ الجاهلية يَبْغُونَ} [al-Māʾida: 50] with «حكم» in the nominative. So the result is that what Ibn ʿAṭiyya permitted is forbidden to the Kufans and weak to the Basrans.

Is this «كَمْ» interrogative or declarative (khabariyya)? The apparent view is the first. Al-Zamakhsharī permitted both views, and the Shaykh forbade it on the ground that "the declarative «كم» stands independently, not attached to the question, so it would be detached from what precedes it, whereas the meaning leads to the question being directed at it; also it would need the omission of the second object of the asking, its implied form being: ask the Children of Israel about the signs We gave them; then He said: many of the signs We gave them; whereas the interrogative does not need that."

As for «من آيةٍ», there are two views on it. The first: that it is a second object on the view that «كم» is accusative by ishtighāl as its verification has preceded, and the specifier of «كم» is omitted, and «مِن» is redundant in the object, because the sentence is not affirmative, since it is an interrogative. This is if we say that «كم» is interrogative, not declarative, since the sentence with the declarative is affirmative, and «مِنْ» is not added in the affirmative except by the opinion of al-Akhfash and the Kufans, unlike when it is interrogative. The Shaykh said: "It may be possible to permit that in it because the interrogative extends to what is after it; but it is remote, because what the interrogative is attached to is the first object, not the second; for if you said 'kam min dirhamin aʿṭaytuhu min rajulin' with «من» redundant in «رجل», there would be something to consider in it." End.

The second: that it is a tamyīz, and «مِنْ» may enter upon the specifier of «كم», whether interrogative or declarative, absolutely, i.e. whether its specifier follows it directly or they are separated by a clause, an adverb, or a preposition and its genitive noun, according to what the grammarians have established. «كم» and what is in its scope are in the position of the accusative or the genitive, because it is in the position of the second object of the asking, which is transitive to two: to the first by itself and to the second by a preposition, either «عن» or the «باء», as in "I asked him about such-and-such" (saʾaltuhu ʿan kadhā / bi-kadhā). The Exalted said: {فَسْئَلْ بِهِ خَبِيراً} [al-Furqān: 59], and the two have been combined in his saying:

916 - فَأَصْبَحْنَ لا يَسْأَلْنني عن بما بِه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(They (the women) came to be such that they no longer ask me about what ails him...)

The preposition may be omitted; hence in the position of «كم» the accusative and the genitive are both possible, according to the two implied forms. «كم» here suspends (muʿallaqa) the asking, and asking is suspended only by an interrogative, like this verse and the saying of the Exalted: {سَلْهُمْ: أَيُّهُم بِذَلِكَ زَعِيمٌ} [al-Qalam: 40], and his saying:

917 - يا أيُّها الراكبُ المُزْجِي مَطِيَّتَه ... سائلْ بني أسدٍ ما هذه الصَّوْتُ
(O rider driving on his mount, ask the Banū Asad what is this noise.)

And another said:

918 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... واسألْ بمَصْقَلَةَ البَكْرِيِّ ما فَعَلا
(... and ask about Maṣqala al-Bakrī what he did.)

They suspended the asking even though it is not among the verbs of the heart, for they said that it is a cause of knowledge and knowledge is suspended, so likewise its cause; and since they have treated its opposite as it in suspension, in his saying:

919 - وَمَنْ أنتُمُ إنَّا نسِينا مَنَ أَنْتُمُ ... وريحُكمُ من أيِّ ريحِ الأَعاصِرِ
(And who are you? We have forgotten who you are, and your wind is from which of the whirlwinds' winds?)

then treating its cause as it is more fitting.

The grammarians differed about «كم»: is it simple or compounded of the kāf of simile and the interrogative «ما», whose alif was dropped because of its being governed by the preposition, then its mīm was made quiescent, as the mīm of «لِمْ» in «لِمْ فَعَلْتَ كذا» is made quiescent in some dialects, so they were compounded in an obligatory compounding? The sound view is the first. Most often it occurs in the Qur'an as declarative, meaning multiplicity, and its specifier has not occurred in the Qur'an except genitive by «مِنْ».

His saying: {وَمَن يُبَدِّلْ نِعْمَةَ الله}: «مَنْ» is conditional, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ. The disagreement about what the khabar of the conditional noun is has already preceded. Substitution (tabdīl) requires two objects, the mubaddal (the thing replaced) and the badal (the replacement), and he mentioned here only one, the mubaddal, and omitted the badal, which is the second object, because the meaning is understood. He stated it explicitly in His saying: {بَدَّلُواْ نِعْمَةَ الله كُفْراً} [Ibrāhīm: 28], so «كفراً» is what is omitted here. It had preceded, at the saying of the Exalted {فَبَدَّلَ الذين ظَلَمُواْ} [al-Baqara: 59], that «بَدَّل» is transitive to two: one by itself, which is the badal, the one that is present, and to the other by a preposition, which is the mubaddal, the one that is left; and the preposition may be omitted for the sake of understanding the meaning. So the implied form here is: "wa-man yubaddil bi-niʿmatihi kufran", and the preposition and the badal were omitted for the sake of understanding the meaning. It is not permissible to imply the preposition entering upon «كفراً», so that the implied form would be "wa-man yubaddil bi-l-kufri niʿmata llāhi", because the threat in His saying {فَإِنَّ الله شَدِيدُ العقاب} would not follow from that. Likewise His saying {فأولئك يُبَدِّلُ الله سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ حَسَنَاتٍ} [al-Furqān: 70] has the implied form "bi-sayyiʾātihim ḥasanāt", and its implied form "sayyiʾātihim bi-ḥasanāt" is not permissible, because it would not follow from His saying {إِلاَّ مَن تَابَ}.

It was read «يُبْدِل» with lightening, and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent. «ما» is maṣdarī, and the returning pronoun from the apodosis clause to the conditional noun is omitted for the understanding of the meaning, i.e. "the punishment is for him", or because «أَلْ» takes its place according to the Kufans.

semin-durr:212-212.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {زُيِّنَ}: No sign of feminine was attached to the verb only because it is figuratively feminine, and the separation made that good. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «زُيِّنَتْ» with the feminine, observing the wording. Mujāhid and Abū Ḥaywa read «زَيَّنَ» as active, with «الحياة» as the object and the agent being Allah the Exalted; the Muʿtazila say that it is Satan.

His saying: {وَيَسْخَرُونَ}: It may be of the chapter of conjoining a verbal clause to a verbal clause, not of the chapter of conjoining a verb alone to another verb, which would be a conjunction of single words, because of the lack of unity of tense. It may also be that «يَسْخَرُون» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "wa-hum yaskharūna" (and they mock), so it is resumptive, and it is of the chapter of conjoining a nominal clause to a verbal clause. «زُيِّن» was brought in the past, indicating that it has occurred and been finished, and «وَيَسْخَرُون» in the imperfect, indicating renewal and occurrence.

His saying: {والذين اتقوا فَوْقَهُمْ}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar. «فوق» here admits two views. The first: that it is an adverb of place in its literal sense, because the God-fearing are in the highest of ʿilliyyīn and the unbelievers in the lowest of sijjīn. The second: that the superiority is figurative, either in relation to the bliss of the believers in the Hereafter and the bliss of the unbelievers in this world. «يوم» is accusative by the settledness (istiqrār) to which «فوقهم» is attached.

His saying: {مَن يَشَآءُ}: the object of «يشاء» is omitted, i.e. "whom He wills to provide for". «بغيرِ حساب»: in this preposition and its genitive noun there are two views. The first: that it is redundant. The second: that it is not redundant. On the first it has no attachment to anything, and on the second it is attached to an omitted element. As for the view of redundancy: three things precede it in His saying {والله يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُ}: the verb, the agent and the object, and it is suitable, in terms of meaning, to be attached to each one of them. If it is attached to the verb, it is among the attributes of actions, the implied form being: "Allah provides provision without reckoning (ghayra ḥisāb)", i.e. not subject to reckoning, meaning that it is not counted or enumerated because of its abundance; so it is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, and the bāʾ is redundant.

If it is attached to the agent, it is among the attributes of agents, and the implied form is: "Allah provides without calling to account (ghayra muḥāsib), rather out of grace," or "without counting (ghayra ḥāsib)", i.e. one who enumerates; so «حساب» occurs in the place of an active participle of ḥāsaba or of ḥasaba. It is also possible that the maṣdar occurs in the place of a passive participle of ḥāsaba, i.e. Allah provides one who is not called to account, that is, no one holds him to account for what he is given; so the maṣdar is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the agent, and the bāʾ is redundant in it.

If it is attached to the object, it is among its attributes too, and the implied form is: "Allah provides whomever He wills without his being called to account, or without being counted against him", i.e. enumerated against him, meaning that no one calls the provided one to account, or no one counts against him, i.e. enumerates. So the maṣdar here too occurs in the place of a passive participle of ḥāsaba or ḥasaba; or it is on the omission of an annexed word, i.e. "ghayra dhī ḥisāb", i.e. muḥāsaba (accounting); so the maṣdar occurs in the place of the ḥāl, and the bāʾ is redundant in it too. In this view it is also possible that the meaning is that he is provided from where he does not reckon (min ḥaythu lā yaḥtasibu), i.e. from where he does not expect the provision to come to him, and the implied form is: "He provides him without his reckoning that", i.e. not expecting it; so it is also a ḥāl.

Similar to it in meaning is {وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لاَ يَحْتَسِبُ} [al-Ṭalāq: 3]. As for the bāʾ being added in the ḥāl, they stated a condition for that, with disagreement over the permissibility of it in the first place, namely that the ḥāl be negated, as in his saying:

920 - فما رَجَعَتْ بخائبةٍ رِكابٌ ... حكيمُ بن المُسَيَّب مُنْتَهَاها
(No riding-camels have returned disappointed, those whose destination was Ḥakīm ibn al-Musayyab.)

And this ḥāl, as you see, is not negated, so forbidding the redundancy in it is more fitting.

As for the view of non-redundancy, it is to make the bāʾ for the ḥāl and accompaniment. The suitability of describing the three things, I mean the verb, the agent and the object, by His saying «بغير حساب» remains as well, as preceded in the view of its being redundant. What is meant by the maṣdar is muḥāsaba (calling to account) or counting and enumeration, i.e. "He provides whom He wills, and there is no reckoning for the provision," or "no reckoning for the Provider," or "no reckoning against the provided one." This is more fitting because it involves no redundancy, whose original is absence; because it keeps the maṣdar in its own state, not occurring in the place of an active or passive participle; and because it involves no implying of an annexed word after «غير», i.e. "ghayra dhī ḥisāb". So this preposition and its genitive noun is attached to an omitted element, since it occurs as a ḥāl from whichever of the three preceding you wish, as its establishment has preceded, i.e. "accompanied by lack of reckoning".

semin-durr:222-222.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {عَنِ المحيض}: it is of the pattern mafʿil, from al-ḥayḍ, and by it the maṣdar, the time and the place are meant. You say: "ḥāḍat the woman, taḥīḍu, ḥayḍan, maḥīḍan and maḥāḍan", so they built it on mafʿil and mafʿal, with kasra and with fatḥa.

Know that, regarding the mafʿal from yafʿilu with kasra on the ʿayn when the verb is defective-medial with yāʾ, there are three positions. The first: that it is like the sound verb, so its ʿayn takes fatḥa when the maṣdar is meant, and kasra when the time and place are meant. The second: that one may choose between fatḥa and kasra for the maṣdar specifically, as it came here: al-maḥīḍ and al-maḥāḍ; the reasoning for this view is that these two forms, I mean kasra and fatḥa, became frequent, and so they were made analogical. The third: that it be restricted to what is heard, so what has been heard with kasra or fatḥa is not extended. So al-maḥīḍ, by which the maṣdar is meant, is not analogical according to the first and third positions, and is analogical according to the second. One says "imraʾa ḥāʾiḍ" and not "ḥāʾiḍa" except rarely; al-Farrāʾ recited:

951 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كحائِضَةٍ يُزْنَى بها غيرِ طاهرِ
("… like a menstruating woman with whom adultery is committed, not pure")

What is well known is that the grammarians distinguished between ḥāʾiḍ and ḥāʾiḍa: the one free of the tāʾ of the feminine is in the sense of relation (nisba), that is, "possessor of menstruation", even if she is not menstruating; while the one with the tāʾ is for her who is menstruating at the time; so it is possible that this is what the poet meant. And so it is with every adjective specific to the feminine, such as ṭāmith, murḍiʿ and their like.

The origin of al-ḥayḍ is flowing and bursting forth; one says "ḥāḍa the torrent and fāḍa". Al-Farrāʾ said: «"ḥāḍat the tree", that is, its gum flowed.» Al-Azharī said: «From this the cistern (ḥawḍ) is called ḥayḍ, because the water flows into it.» The Arabs bring the wāw into the yāʾ and the yāʾ into the wāw, because both are from one domain, which is the air. The apparent view is that al-maḥīḍ in this verse means the maṣdar, and to this al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya went. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «Al-maḥīḍ is a maṣdar like al-ḥayḍ, and the like of it is "al-maqīl" from "qāla yaqīlu" (to take a midday rest).» Al-Rāʿī said:

952 - بُنِيَتْ مَرافِقُهُنَّ فوقَ مَزَلَّة ... لا يَسْتَطِيعُ بها القُرادُ مَقيلا
("Their elbows were built upon a slippery place where the tick cannot take a midday rest")

And likewise al-Ṭabarī said: «Al-maḥīḍ is a noun, like al-maʿīsh, a noun for al-ʿaysh (life)»; and he recited for Ruʾba:

953 - إليك أشكو شدَّة المعيشِ ... ومَرَّ أعوامٍ نَتَفْنَ ريشي
("To You I complain of the hardness of livelihood and the passing of years that have plucked my feathers")

And it was said that what is meant by al-maḥīḍ in the verse is the noun of the place of the blood; on this basis it is analogical by agreement. The first view is supported by His saying: {قُلْ هُوَ أَذًى}; it may be answered that an omitted muḍāf is there, that is: "it is a cause of harm"; and the second is supported by His saying: {فاعتزلوا النسآء فِي المحيض}. And whoever took it as the maṣdar implied an omitted muḍāf here, that is: "so keep away from having intercourse with women during the time of menstruation"; and it is possible that the first maḥīḍ be a maṣdar and the second a place.

And His saying: {هُوَ أَذَى}: there are two possibilities. One, said by Abū al-Baqāʾ: «that it is the pronoun of the forbidden intercourse», as if he is saying that the context indicates it though no mention of it has gone before. The second: that it refers back to al-maḥīḍ; Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «and the implied form would be "it is a cause of harm"», and there is room for consideration in this, for they explained al-adhā here as a filthy thing, so if by al-maḥīḍ we mean the blood itself, it is something repugnant, and there is no need to imply an omitted muḍāf.

«وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ» came three times with the conjunction after His saying: {يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الخمر} [al-Baqara: 21], and they are: {وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَا يُنفِقُونَ} [al-Baqara: 219], {وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ اليتامى} [al-Baqara: 320] and {وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ المحيض} [al-Baqara: 222]. [Translator's note: the verse numbers 21 and 320 are as printed in the source; they are evidently misprints for 219 and 220.] And «يَسْأَلُونك» came four times without conjunction: {يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الأهلة} [al-Baqara: 189], {يَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَا يُنْفِقُونَ} [al-Baqara: 215], {يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الشهر الحرام} [al-Baqara: 217], {يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الخمر} [al-Baqara: 219]. What is the difference? The answer: the later questions occurred at one time, so they were joined by the particle of joining, which is the wāw; as for the earlier questions, they occurred at separate times, so each clause was begun anew and brought alone.

His saying: {حتى يَطْهُرْنَ}: «ḥattā» here is in the sense of «ilā» (until), and the verb after it is accusative by an implied «an», and it is indeclinable because of its attachment to the feminine plural nūn.

Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī and Abū Bakr read with shadda on the ṭāʾ and the hāʾ; the origin is «yataṭahharna», and it was assimilated. The rest read «yaṭhurna», imperfect of ṭahura. They said: the reading with shadda means "they wash themselves (yaghtasilna)", and the reading without it means "their blood ceases". Al-Ṭabarī preferred the reading with shadda and said: «It is in the sense of "yaghtasilna", because all agree on the prohibition of a man's approaching his wife after the cessation of the blood until she is pure; the disagreement is only about what purity is: is it the full bath, or the ablution, or washing the private part only?» Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «Each of the two readings can be taken to mean washing with water, and can be taken to mean the cessation of the blood and the going of its harm.» He said: «And what al-Ṭabarī held, that the reading with shadda comprises the washing and the reading without it comprises the cessation of the blood, is not necessarily so, and likewise his claiming of consensus.» And in Ibn ʿAṭiyya's refutation of him there is room for consideration; for if we take the two readings to one meaning, repetition would follow. Al-Fārisī preferred the reading without shadda because it is from the triliteral verb opposed to ṭamitha, which is triliteral.

His saying: {مِنْ حَيْثُ}: regarding «min» there are two views. One: that it is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), that is, from the direction that ends at the place of menstruation. The second: that it is [in the sense of] «fī» (in), that is, in the place that you were forbidden during menstruation. Some preferred this on the ground that it is suited to His saying: {فاعتزلوا النسآء فِي المحيض}, and some compared this verse to His saying: {لِلصَّلاَةِ مِن يَوْمِ الجمعة} [al-Jumuʿa: 9] and {مَاذَا خَلَقُواْ مِنَ الأرض} [Fāṭir: 40], that is, on the day of Friday and in the earth. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «There is an omission in the speech, its implied form being: "Allah has commanded you to come to them from it"», meaning that the second object was omitted because of an indication of it. And He repeated His saying «يحب» as an indication of the difference in what calls for the love, so that the love differs.

semin-durr:197-197.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الحج أَشْهُرٌ}: «الحَجُّ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «أشهرٌ» is its khabar (predicate). The mubtadaʾ and khabar must apply to one and the same entity, but «الحَجُّ» is an act among acts and «أشهرٌ» is a period of time, so the two are different; hence an interpretation is necessary, and there are three possibilities. The first: that it rests on the omission of a muḍāf (annexed term) from the first, the implied form being: "the months of the Ḥajj are known months". The second: omission from the second, the implied form being: "the Ḥajj is the Ḥajj of months", so that from each one is omitted what is retained in its counterpart. The third: that the event is made the very time itself, for emphasis; the ground of the figure is that it takes place within it, and when the adverbial was treated expansively it was made the very event. A parallel is {وَحَمْلُهُ وَفِصَالُهُ ثَلاَثُونَ شَهْراً} [al-Aḥqāf: 15].

And when a noun of time, indefinite, is used as the predicate of an event, both nominative and accusative are permissible, without restriction, that is, whether the event covers the whole of the time or not. This is the view of the Basrans.

As for the Kufans, they said: if the event covers the whole, then nominative only, as in «الصومُ يومٌ» ("the fast is a day"); and if it does not cover the whole, Hishām also insists on nominative, as in «ميعادُك يومُ» ("your appointment is a day"), whereas al-Farrāʾ allows its accusative like the Basrans. It has also been transmitted from him that he forbade the accusative of «أشهر», meaning in the verse, because it is indefinite, so he would have two views on the question. This question has far-reaching branches that the books of the grammarians contain. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Whoever takes the speech to imply «[الحج] في أشهر» ('[the Ḥajj] is in months') is bound, once the preposition is dropped, to make «الأشهر» accusative, and no one read it so." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "That is not binding, because the nominative is by way of extension, even though its origin is the genitive with «في»."

His saying: {فَمَنْ}: «مَنْ» may be conditional (shartiyya) or relative (mawṣūla), as has been said for its parallels. And «فيهن» is attached to «فَرَضَ», and the pronoun in «فيهن» refers to «أشهر». It was brought in the form of the feminine pronoun because, as has preceded, the plural of non-rational beings, in the paucal, is treated like the feminine plural according to the most eloquent usage; hence «فيهنَّ» came rather than «فيها». This differs from His saying {مِنْهَآ أَرْبَعَةٌ حُرُمٌ} [al-Tawba: 36], because there it is a plural of multitude.

His saying: {فَلاَ رَفَثَ}: The fāʾ is either the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) or redundant in the khabar, according to the earlier grammarians. Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read «رفث» and «فُسوق» with tanwīn and nominative, and «جدال» with fatḥa; the rest read all three with fatḥa; Abū Jaʿfar, and it is also reported from ʿĀṣim, read all three nominative with tanwīn; and al-ʿUṭāridī read all three accusative with tanwīn.

As for the nominative reading, it has two analyses, the more apparent being that «لا» is disregarded (mulghāt) and what follows it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and what made it permissible to begin with an indefinite noun is the negation preceding it. «في الحجّ» is the khabar of the third mubtadaʾ, and the khabar of the first and second is omitted because the khabar of the third indicates them; or «في الحج» is the khabar of the first, and the khabar of the second and third is omitted because the khabar of the first indicates them; and it is permissible that «في الحج» be the khabar of all three.

It is not permissible that «في الحج» be the khabar of the second, with the khabar of the first and third omitted, because of the ugliness of such a construction and because it leads to separation.

The second: that «لا» operates the operation of «ليس», and its so operating has conditions: that the noun be indefinite, that the khabar not precede, and that the negation not be broken. So «رفث» is its ism (subject) and what follows it is conjoined to it, and «وفي الحجِّ» is the khabar according to the implied forms mentioned for the preceding analysis. Ibn ʿAṭiyya was categorical about this analysis, but it is weak, because there is no explicit evidence that «لا» operates the operation of «ليس»; they only cited things that are open to other interpretation. Sībawayh cited:

880 - مَنْ صَدَّ عن نيرانِها ... فأنا ابنُ قيسٍ لا براحُ
(Whoever turns away from her fires, I am the son of Qays, there is no leaving.)

and another cited:

881 - تَعَزَّ فلا شيءٌ على الأرضِ باقيا ... ولا وَزَرٌ مِمَّا قَضَى اللَّهُ واقِيَا
(Console yourself: nothing on earth abides, nor is any refuge a protection from what Allah has decreed.)

and the saying of another:

882 - أَنْكَرْتُها بعد أعوامٍ مَضَيْنَ لها ... لا الدارُ داراً ولا الجيرانُ جيرانا
(I did not recognise it after years had passed for it: the abode is no abode, and the neighbours are no neighbours.)

and Ibn al-Shajarī cited:

883 - وحَلَّتْ سوادَ القلبِ لا أنا باغياً ... سِواها ولا في حُبِّها متراخِيا
(She settled in the blackness of my heart; I seek none but her, nor am I slack in loving her.)

The discussion of these verses has a place other than this.

As for the one who read all three accusative with tanwīn, his analysis is that they are accusative as maṣdars of implied verbs from their own wording, the implied form being: «فلا يَرْفُثُ رَفَثَاً ولا يَفْسُقُ فُسوقاً ولا يجدال جِدالاً» [Translator's note: the source prints «ولا يجدال» with the yāʾ; the evident intent is «ولا يُجادِلُ» ("nor dispute")], and in that case «لا» has no operation on what follows it; it merely negates the implied clauses. And «في الحجِّ» is attached to whichever of the three maṣdars you wish, on the ground that the question is one of conflict of governors (tanāzuʿ), and this would be evidence for conflict among more than two governors. It may also be said that this «لا» is the «لا» of absolute negation (li-l-tabriʾa), according to the view of those who hold that its ism is inflected and accusative, and that its tanwīn was dropped only for lightness, and in this irregular reading the original was restored, as it was restored in his saying:

884 - ألا رجلاً جَزاه اللهُ خيراً ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Is there not a man whom Allah may reward with good...)

The verification of this view has already been given.

As for the reading with fatḥa for all three, it is the «لا» of absolute negation. Is the fatḥa of the noun a fatḥa of inflection or of indeclinability (bināʾ)? Two views; the second is the view of the majority. And when it is built with it, is the compound of it and its ism in the position of nominative by the mubtadaʾ, even though «لا» operates accusative on the position in the noun, with no khabar for it? Or is the compound not in the position of a mubtadaʾ, but «لا» operates accusative on the position in the noun, and what follows it is the khabar of «لا», because it was treated like «أنَّ» in making the noun accusative and the khabar nominative? Two views: the first is the view of Sībawayh, and the second the view of al-Akhfash. On these two views the disagreement over His saying «في الحج» is based: on Sībawayh's view it is in the position of the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and on al-Akhfash's opinion it is in the position of the khabar of «لا». This was given at the beginning of the book, and I repeat some of it only to draw attention to it.

As for the one who read the first two nominative and the third with fatḥa: the nominative is as already said, and likewise the fatḥa, except that one should be alert to something. When we adopt Sībawayh's view, that «لا» and what is built with it is in the position of a mubtadaʾ, «في الحج» is a khabar for all, since it involves only conjoining a mubtadaʾ to a mubtadaʾ. But on al-Akhfash's view, «في الحج» can only be the khabar of the two mubtadaʾs or the khabar of «لا». It cannot be a khabar for all, because of the difference in what seeks it: the mubtadaʾ seeks it as its khabar, while «لا» does not seek it as its khabar [Translator's note: the source text is as written; the sense seems to be that the mubtadaʾ and «لا» each seek a khabar in a different construction].

It was read this way, al-Zamakhsharī said, "because they took the first two in the sense of prohibition, as if it were said: «فلا يكونَنَّ رفثٌ ولا فسوقٌ» ('so let there be no obscenity and no wickedness'), and the third in the sense of informing of the absence of disputation, as if it were said: no doubt and no disagreement in the Ḥajj." He inferred that what is prohibited is obscenity and wickedness, not disputation, from the Prophet's saying, peace be upon him: «مَنْ حَجَّ فلم يَرْفُثْ ولم يَفْسُقْ» ("Whoever performed the Ḥajj and did not commit obscenity and did not commit wickedness"), where disputation is not mentioned. What al-Zamakhsharī mentioned was anticipated by the author of this reading, though he made his intention clearer. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, one of its two readers, said: the nominative is in the sense «فلا يكونُ رفثٌ ولا فسوقٌ» ("so there is no obscenity and no wickedness"), i.e. anything that takes one out of the Ḥajj; then he began the negation and said «ولا جدالَ». So Abū ʿAmr did not make the first two negations a prohibition, but left them as real negation; hence his saying is open to question, for the sentence of negation with the «لا» of absolute negation may also be intended as a prohibition, and that was said about His saying {لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ} [al-Baqara: 2]. What seems to be the answer to that is what Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Fāsī transmitted from some, saying: "It was said: the argument for the one who read them nominative is that the negation in them is not general, since obscenity and wickedness do occur in the Ḥajj from some people, unlike the negation of disputation in the matter of the Ḥajj, which is general..." This fits the usage of the grammarians, for they say: the «لا» that operates as «ليس» is for negating oneness, and the one that operates as «إنَّ» is for negating the genus. They said: for that reason one may say «لا رجلَ فيها بل رجلان أو رجال» ("there is no one man in it, rather two men or men") when you use the nominative, and that is not good when you build its ism or make it accusative with it. Some took a middle position, saying: the «لا» of absolute negation is explicit (naṣṣ) in generality, while the other is not explicit, and the apparent sense is that an indefinite noun in the context of negation is general in every case.

The meaning of «الرَّفَث» and «الفِسْق» has already been given. ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read «الرَّفُوث», a maṣdar with the meaning of «الرَّفث».

And His saying: {فَلاَ رَفَثَ} and what is within its scope is in the position of jussive if «مَنْ» is conditional, and of nominative if it is relative. On both assumptions there must be a link (rābiṭ) referring back to «مَنْ», because if it is conditional, it has already been said that a pronoun referring to the conditional noun is required; and if it is relative, it is a mubtadaʾ and the clause is its khabar, with no link in the wording, so it must be supplied, and there are two possibilities. The first: that you supply it after «جدال», the implied form being «ولا جدالَ منه» ("and no disputation from him"), with «منه» an adjective of «جدال», so attached to an omitted element, and this becomes parallel to their saying «السَّمْنُ مَنَوانِ بدرهم» ("the clarified butter, two manns for a dirham"), whose implied form is «مَنَوانِ منه» ("two manns of it").

The second: that it be supplied after «الحج»: «ولا جدالَ في الحجِّ منه» or «له» ("and no disputation in the Ḥajj from him" or "for him"), and this preposition and its genitive noun would be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from «الحج». The Kufans have another interpretation of this: that the alif and lām stand in for the pronoun, the original being «في حَجِّه» ("in his Ḥajj"), like {وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ} [al-Nāziʿāt: 40] then {فَإِنَّ الجنة هِيَ المأوى} [al-Nāziʿāt: 41], i.e. his refuge.

He repeated «الحج» by putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun for emphasis of grandeur, as in his saying:

885 - لا أرى الموتَ يَسْبِقُ الموتَ شيءٌ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I do not see that anything outstrips death...)

The structure of the speech would seem to require: «فَمَنْ فرض فيهنَّ الحجَّ فلا رَفَث فيه» ("whoever makes the Ḥajj obligatory on himself in them, then no obscenity in it"); what makes this fitting in the verse is the separation, unlike the verse of poetry.

«الجِدال» is a maṣdar of «جادَلَ». «الجدالُ» is the most intense quarrel, derived from «الجَدالة», which is the earth, as if each of two disputants throws his opponent to the ground. The poet said:

886 - قد أَرْكَبُ الآلَةَ بعدَ الآلَهْ ... وأترُكُ العاجِزَ بالجَدَالَهْ
(I may mount the device after the device, and leave the incapable one on the ground.)

From it too comes «الأجْدل», the falcon, for its strength. «الجَدْل» is the twisting of a rope, from which comes «زِمامٌ مجدولٌ», i.e. a tightly twisted rein.

His saying: {وَمَا تَفْعَلُواْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ}: The discussion of its parallel, {مَا نَنسَخْ}, has preceded, so everything said there is said here. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "We add here another analysis: that «من خير» is in the position of accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, the implied form being: «وما تفعلوا فعلاً كائناً مِنْ خيرٍ» ('whatever act, being of good, you do')."

«يَعْلَمْه» is jussive as the apodosis of the condition, and figurative usage is necessary in the speech: either He expressed by knowledge the recompense for doing good, as if it were said «يُجازِكم» ("He will recompense you"), or you supply the recompense after the knowledge, i.e. «فيثيبه عليه» ("so He will reward him for it").

In His saying {وَمَا تَفْعَلُواْ} there is an iltifāt (shift of person), for it is a departure from the third person in His saying «فَمَنْ فَرَض». It was carried on the meaning of «مَنْ», since the pronoun was made plural and not singular.

Some of the iʿrāb-writers blundered, saying: «مِنْ خير» is attached to «تَفْعلوا», and it is in the position of accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being «وما تفعلوه فعلاً مِنْ خير» ("whatever you do of an act of good"), and the hāʾ in «يَعْلَمْه» refers back to «خير». This is a gross error. For since he attached it to the verb before it, how can he make it the adjective of an omitted maṣdar? And since he made the hāʾ refer to «خير», it follows that the apodosis clause lacks a pronoun referring to the conditional noun, and that is not permissible (whereas if the conditional particle were a particle, this would not be required). The correct view is what preceded. I mention this only so that you do not see it and imagine it sound. The hāʾ refers to «ما», which is the conditional noun. And the alif of «الزاد» is changed from wāw, because they say «تَزَوَّدَ» ("he took provisions").

semin-durr:283-283.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلَمْ تَجِدُواْ كَاتِباً}: The common people read «كاتباً», an active participle. Ubayy, Mujāhid and Abū al-ʿĀliya read «كِتاباً», which has two aspects. One: that it is a maṣdar, i.e. "possessing writing". The other: that it is the plural of «كاتب», like «صاحب» and «صِحاب». Al-Zamakhsharī reported this reading only from Ubayy and Ibn ʿAbbās, and said: "Ibn ʿAbbās said: 'Do you think that if you find the scribe but do not find the sheet and the inkwell...?'" Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «كُتَّاباً» in the plural, considering that every occurrence has a scribe. Abū al-ʿĀliya read «كُتُباً», the plural of «كتاب», considering the occurrences. I say: Ibn ʿAbbās's saying "Do you think that if you find the scribe, etc." is a preference for the reading narrated from him and a finding remote of the reading of others, «كاتباً»; he means that what is intended is the writing, not the scribe.
His saying: {فَرِهَانٌ} has three aspects. First: that it is nominative by an omitted verb, i.e. "so there suffices in place of that pledges taken into possession." Second: that it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is omitted, i.e. "pledges taken into possession suffice." Third: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ whose implied form is "the security, or what stands in place of that, is pledges taken into possession."
Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «فَرُهُنٌّ» with ḍamma on the rāʾ and the hāʾ, and the others «فَرِهَانٌ» with kasra on the rāʾ and an alif after the hāʾ. It is narrated from Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr, in one transmission, that the hāʾ is quiescent.
As for the reading of Ibn Kathīr, it is the plural of «رَهْن», and «فَعْل» takes the plural «فُعُل», like «سَقْف» and «سُقُف». In Abū al-Baqāʾ, after his saying "سَقْف and سُقُف, أَسَد and أُسُد", there occurs [the word "and it is a slip"] [Translator's note: the printed text here reads «وهو [وهم]», i.e. "and it is [an error]", apparently an editor's bracket, and the sentence is incomplete]. But they said that «فُعُل» as the plural of «فَعْل» is rare, and al-Akhfash adduced words of it, among them: «رَهْن» and «رُهُن»; «لَحْد» of the grave and «لُحُد»; «قَلْب» of the palm and «قُلُب»; «رجلٌ ثَطٌّ» (a man with scanty beard) and «قومٌ ثُطٌّ»; «فرس وَرْدٌ» (a reddish horse) and «خيلٌ وُرُدٌ»; «سهم حَشْر» (a slender arrow) and «سهام حُشُر». Abū ʿAmr recited, as proof for his reading, the saying of Qaʿnab:
1135 - بانَتْ سعادُ وأمسى دونَها عدنُ ... وَغلَّقَتْ عندَها مِنْ قبلِك الرُّهُنُ
(Suʿād has departed, and ʿAdan has come to lie between us; and before you, pledges have been locked up with her.)
Abū ʿAmr said: "I read «فَرُهُن» only to distinguish between «الرهان» in horse-racing and the plural of «رَهْن» in other things." The meaning of this speech is that he chose this reading over the reading «رهان», since it would not be permitted him to do that as he said without following a transmission.
Al-Zajjāj chose this reading of his, saying: "This reading agrees with the codex, and whatever agrees with the codex, is sound in meaning, and the readers have read it, is the chosen one." I say: the noble orthography is «فرهن» without alif after the hāʾ, although al-Zajjāj says "«فُعُل» as the plural of «فَعْل» is rare." It is related of Abū ʿAmr that he said: "I know «الرِّهان» only in horses, nothing else." Yūnus said: "«الرَّهْن» and «الرِّهان» are both Arabic; «الرُّهُن» is more frequent for «الرَّهْن», and «الرِّهان» is more frequent for horses." They also recited, for «رَهْن» and «رُهُن», his saying – the verse:
1136 - آلَيْتُ لا نُعْطِيه من أَبْنائِنا ... رُهُناً فيُفْسِدَهم كَرَهْنٍ أَفْسدا
(I swore we would not give him, from among our sons, pledges, lest he corrupt them as the pledge corrupted [others].)
It is said that «رُهُن» is the plural of «رِهان», and «رِهان» the plural of «رَهْن», so it is a plural of a plural, as they said of «ثِمار» the plural of «ثَمَر», and «ثُمُر» the plural of «ثِمار»; to this al-Farrāʾ and his shaykh went, but the plural of a plural is not regular according to Sībawayh and the majority of his followers.
As for the reading of the others, «رِهان»: «رِهان» is the plural of «رَهْن», and «فَعْل» with «فِعال» is regular and frequent, such as «كَعْب» and «كِعَاب», «كَلْب» and «كِلاب». Whoever makes the ḍamma of the hāʾ quiescent in «رُهُن» does so for lightness, and it is a dialect; they say «سُقْف» for «سُقُف», the plural of «سَقْف».
«الرَّهْن» is originally the maṣdar of «رَهَنْتُ». One says: «رَهنْتُ زيداً ثوباً أَرْهَنُه رَهْناً», i.e. I handed it to him as a pledge with him. He said:
1137 - يراهِنُني فَيَرْهَنُنِي بَنِيه ... وأَرْهَنُه بَنِيَّ بما أَقولُ
(He wagers with me, so he pledges his sons to me, and I pledge my sons to him for what I say.)
And «أرهنْتُ زيداً ثوباً», i.e. I handed it to him for him to pledge it; so they distinguished between «فَعَل» and «أَفْعَل». According to al-Farrāʾ, «رَهَنْتُه» and «أَرْهَنْتُه» have the same meaning, and he argued with the saying of Hammām al-Salūlī:
1138 - فَلَمَّا خَشِيْتُ أظافيرَهُمْ ... نَجَوْتُ وأَرْهَنْتُهُمْ مالِكا
(When I feared their talons, I escaped, and I left Mālik as a pledge with them.)
Al-Aṣmaʿī denied this transmission and said: "The transmission is only: «وأَرْهنُهُم مالكا»", the wāw being circumstantial, as in their saying «قَمْتُ وأصُكُّ عينَه», and it is on the implication of a mubtadaʾ.
It is said: «أُرْهِنَ في السِّلعة» when one overbid for the commodity until he took it at a high price; and from it his saying:
1139 - يَطْوي ابنُ سلمى بها من راكبٍ بَعُداً ... عِيدِيَّةٌ أُرْهِنَتْ فيها الدَّنانيرُ
(Ibn Salmā, riding it, covers great distances on a ʿĪdī she-camel for which dinars were paid dear.)
It is said «رَهَنْتُ لساني بكذا», and «أَرْهَنْتُ» is not said of it. And they recited:
. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
[Translator's note: the verse is absent in the source text, which shows only dots.]
Then «الرَّهْن» was applied to the thing pledged, in the way of applying the maṣdar to the passive participle, like His saying, the Exalted: {هذا خَلْقُ الله} [Luqmān: 11], and «درهَمٌ ضَرْبُ الأمير» (a dirham struck by the emir). So if you say «رَهَنْتُ زيداً ثوباً رَهْناً», «رَهْناً» here is only a maṣdar; and if you say «رهنْتُ زيداً رَهْناً», it is here a mafʿūl bihi, because what is meant by it is the pledged thing. It is possible that «رَهْناً» here is also a maṣdar of emphasis, and the second object is not mentioned, for limitation, like His saying: {وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ} [al-Ḍuḥā: 4].
«رَهْن» is one of those for which the plural of abundance suffices in place of the plural of paucity, because by analogy its plural of paucity is «أَفْعُل», like «فَلْس» and «أفلُس», but «رَهْن» and «رِهان» sufficed in place of «أَرْهُن».
The origin of «الرَّهْن» is permanence and stability. One says: «رَهَنَ الشيءُ, فهو راهنٌ» when it lasts and is stable, and «نِعمة راهنة», i.e. a lasting, firm blessing. Ibn al-Sikkīt recited:
1140 - لا يَسْتَفيقون منها وَهْي راهِنةٌ ... إلا بهاتِ وإنْ عَلُّوا وإنْ نَهِلوا
(They do not recover from it while it persists, except with "Give!", even when they have drunk a second and a first draught.)
One says «طعام راهن», i.e. abiding, lasting. He said:
1141 - الخبزُ واللحمُ لهم راهِن ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Bread and meat are ever-present for them...)
that is, lasting and stable; from it the pledged thing is called «رَهْن», for its lasting and staying with the pledgee.
His saying: {وَلَمْ تَجِدُواْ كَاتِباً}: this clause has three aspects. One: that it is conjoined to the protasis verb, i.e. «وإنْ كنتم ولم تَجِدوا», so it is in the position of jussive, by being conjoined to what is jussive in implied form. The second: that it is conjoined to the khabar of «كان», i.e. «وإنْ كنتم لم تَجِدُوا كاتباً». The third: that the wāw is circumstantial and the clause after it is accusative as ḥāl; so on these last two aspects it is in the position of an accusative.
His saying: {فَإِنْ أَمِنَ}: Ubayy read, in what al-Zamakhsharī transmitted from him, «أُومِنَ» in the passive. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "that is, people trusted him and described the debtor with trustworthiness and fulfilment." I say: and by what is «بعضاً» put in the accusative? The apparent is that it is accusative by removal of the preposition, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. «فإن أومِنَ بعضُكم على متاعِ بعضٍ أو على دَيْنِ بعض».
His saying: {فَلْيُؤَدِّ الذي اؤتمن}: when one pauses on «الذي» and begins with what follows it, one says «اوتُمِنَ» with a ḍammated hamza followed by a quiescent wāw. This is because its origin is «أُأْتُمِنَ», like «اقْتُدِرَ», with two hamzas: the first a hamzat al-waṣl and the second the first radical of the word. The second occurred quiescent after another like it that was ḍammated, so the second had to be turned into a letter homogeneous to the vowel of the first, and one said «أُوْتُمِنَ».
