In running speech the hamzat al-waṣl falls away and the hamza returns to its state, because the cause of its turning into a wāw has disappeared; rather it is turned into a pure yāʾ in connected speech in the transmission of Warsh and al-Sūsī.
It is narrated from ʿĀṣim: «الذي اوتُمِن» with the alif ḍammated, indicating the hamza by the ḍamma. Ibn Mujāhid said: "This rendering is a mistake." Salīm related from Ḥamza an ishmām (partial rounding) of the hamza with ḍamma; and in the aforementioned ishāra and ishmām there is something to examine. ʿĀṣim also read, in an anomalous reading, «الَّذِتُّمِنَ», assimilating the yāʾ substituted for the hamza into the tāʾ of the form ifta'ala. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "on the analogy of «اتَّسر» in the ifta'ala form from «اليُسْر»; but it is not sound, because the yāʾ is converted from the hamza, so it has the status of the hamza, and «اتَّزر» is colloquial, and likewise «رُيَّا» for «رُؤْيا»." The Shaykh said: "What al-Zamakhsharī mentioned, that it is not sound and that «اتَّزر» is colloquial – meaning that it is an innovation of the common folk with no basis in the language – has been mentioned by others as well: that some substituted and assimilated «اتَّمَنَ» and «اتَّزَرَ», and that this is a poor dialect, and likewise «رُيَّا» for «رُؤْيا». As for this comparison, it either returns to his saying «واتَّزر عاميٌّ», in which case the assimilation in «رُيَّا» is colloquial, or to his saying «it is not sound», i.e. likewise the assimilation in «رُيَّا» is not sound; and al-Kisāʾī has related the assimilation in «رُيَّا»."
And His saying: {أَمَانَتَهُ}: it is permissible that «الأمانة» means the thing entrusted, so it is accusative as mafʿūl bihi of «فليؤدِّ»; and it is permissible that it is a maṣdar in its basic sense, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. «فليؤدِّ دَينَ أمانتهِ». It is not permissible that it be accusative as the maṣdar of «ائتُمِنَ». The pronoun in «أمانتَه» may refer back to the owner of the right, and may refer back to the one who was entrusted.
His saying: {فَإِنَّهُ آثِمٌ قَلْبُهُ}: regarding this pronoun there are two aspects. One: that it is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) and the clause after it explains it. The other: that it is the pronoun of «مَنْ» in His saying «ومَنْ يَكتُمْها»; and this is the apparent.
As for «آثمٌ قلبُه» there are aspects. The most apparent: that the pronoun in «إنه» is the pronoun of «مَنْ», «آثمٌ» is the khabar of «إنَّ», and «قلبُه» is the agent of «آثم», like your saying «زيدٌ إنه قائمٌ أبوه»; and the active participle's governing here is clear, since the conditions for governing are present. This aspect does not work on the view that the pronoun is the pronoun of the matter, because the pronoun of the matter is explained only by a clause, and the active participle with its agent is, according to the Basrans, a single word; the Kufans permit that.
Second: that «آثمٌ» is a fronted khabar and «قلبُه» a postponed mubtadaʾ, the clause being the khabar of «إنَّ». Al-Zamakhsharī, Abū al-Baqāʾ and others mentioned it. This is not permissible by the principles of the Kufans, because for them the nominative pronoun does not refer back to something later in wording, and «آثمٌ» has carried a pronoun since it occurred as a khabar. On this aspect the hāʾ may be the pronoun of the matter or the pronoun of «مَنْ».
Third: that «آثم» is the khabar of «إنَّ» and has in it a pronoun referring to what the hāʾ in «إنه» refers to, and «قلبُه» is a substitute for that latent pronoun, a badal of part from whole.
Fourth: that «آثم» is a mubtadaʾ and «قلبُه» an agent filling the place of the khabar, the clause being the khabar of «إنَّ»; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said it. It is not permissible according to the Basrans, because for them the active participle does not govern unless it relies on a negation or an interrogative, such as «ما قائمٌ أبواك», «وهل قائمٌ أخواك», «وما قائمٌ قومك», «وهل ضاربٌ إخوتك». This is permitted only by al-Farrāʾ among the Kufans and al-Akhfash among the Basrans, who allow «قائمٌ الزيدان» and «قائمٌ الزيدون»; so too in the noble verse.
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «قلبَه» in the accusative, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya attributed to him. In its accusative there are three aspects. One: that it is a badal of the noun of «إنَّ», badal of part from whole; and there is no objection to separation by the khabar – which is «آثمٌ» – between the badal and what it substitutes, as there is no objection to separating by it between the naʿt and the modified, as in «زيد منطلق العاقل», although the governor in the naʿt and the modified is one, unlike the badal and what it substitutes, for the sound view is that the governor in the badal is other than the governor in what it substitutes.
Second: that it is accusative by resemblance to the direct object, like your saying «مررت برجلٍ حسنٍ وجهُه»; on this aspect there is a famous disagreement, with three positions. The first, the position of the Kufans: it is permitted absolutely, I mean in verse and prose. The second: forbidden absolutely, the position of al-Mubarrad. The third: forbidden in prose and permitted in poetry, the position of Sībawayh, and al-Kisāʾī recited for this:
1142 - أَنْعَتُها إنِّيَ مِنْ نُعَّاتِها ... مُدارةَ الأخفْافِ مُجْمَرَّاتِها
غُلْبَ الرِّقابِ وعَفَرْ نِياتِها ... كُومَ الذُّرى وادِقَةً سُرَّاتِها
(I describe them, for I am one of their describers: with round hooves, tightly compact; thick of neck and strong-bodied; high-humped, with firm, well-fleshed backs.)
The reason for its weakness in prose according to Sībawayh is the repetition of the pronoun.
Third: that it is accusative as tamyīz (specification), which Makkī and others related; they weakened it because tamyīz is only indefinite, according to the Basrans; the Kufans do not require its indefiniteness, and from this according to them are: {إِلاَّ مَن سَفِهَ نَفْسَهُ} [al-Baqara: 130] and {بَطِرَتْ مَعِيشَتَهَا} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 58]. [Translator's note: the source prints «[القصص: 85]»; the verse {بَطِرَتْ مَعِيشَتَهَا} is in al-Qaṣaṣ 58.] And they recited:
1143 - إلى رُدُحٍ من الشِّيزى مِلاءٍ ... لُبَابَ البُرِّ يُلْبَكُ بالشِّهادِ
(To large bowls of ebony wood, full of the choicest wheat, mixed with honeycombs.)
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read, in what al-Zamakhsharī transmitted from him, «أَثِم قلبَه», making «أثم» a past-tense verb with doubled ʿayn, its agent latent in it, and «قلبه» the direct object, i.e. "he made his heart sinful", that is, he himself sinned, because he expressed by the heart his whole self, since it is the noblest organ in it. [Translator's note: the source says "doubled ʿayn" while the printed form «أَثِم» shows no shadda; translated as written.]
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read «ولا يَكْتُموا» with the yāʾ of the third person, because what precedes is third person, and they are those mentioned in His saying: {كَاتِبٌ وَلاَ شَهِيدٌ}, and although it is in singular wording the plural is meant, and therefore its meaning was regarded in the reading of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, so he pluralised in «ولا يكتموا».
These verses comprise types of badīʿ, among them: tajnīs of difference in «تدايَنْتُم بدَيْن» and similar cases, and of sameness in His saying: {وَلاَ تَكْتُمُواْ الشهادة وَمَن يَكْتُمْهَا}, and ṭibāq (antithesis) in «تَضِلَّ» and «تذكِّر» and «صغيراً وكبيراً»; they are many and can be drawn from what has gone before, so there is no need to multiply by mentioning them. Al-Sulamī also read {والله بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ} in the third person, in keeping with his reading in the third person.

semin-durr:223-223.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {نِسَآؤُكُمْ حَرْثٌ لَّكُمْ}: mubtadaʾ and khabar. An interpretation is necessary for predicating a maṣdar of a body to be sound. It was said: it is by way of exaggeration, they being made the very action. It was said: he meant by the maṣdar the passive participle. It was said: it is on the omission of a muḍāf from the first, that is: "having intercourse with your women is a ḥarth", that is, like a ḥarth (tilling); and it was said: from the second, that is, "your women are possessors of tilth". «لكم» is in the position of the nominative because it is an adjective of «حَرْث», so it is attached to an omitted word. The khabar is in the singular while the mubtadaʾ is a plural only because it is a maṣdar, for which the most eloquent usage then is singular and masculine.

His saying: {أنى شِئْتُمْ}: «annā» is an adverb of place, and it is used as a conditional and as an interrogative, in the sense of «matā» (when), so that it is an adverb of time, and in the sense of «kayfa» (how), and in the sense of «min ayna» (from where); and the noble verse has been explained by each of these possibilities. The grammarians said: «annā» is for generalising states. Some said: it comes only as a question and as a report about a matter that has several aspects, and so on this view it is more general than «kayfa», «ayna» and «matā». They said: when it is conditional it is an adverb of place only. Know that it is indeclinable because it contains either the meaning of the conditional particle or that of the interrogative, and it is necessarily accusative as an adverbial. The governor in it here, they said, is the verb before it, namely «فأتوا». The Shaykh said: «This is not valid, for it is either conditional or interrogative. It cannot be conditional for two reasons. One, from the side of meaning: when it is conditional it is an adverb of place, as has preceded, and then the speech would require permission in other than the front passage, whereas the prohibition of that is established. The second, from the side of the craft: the conditional noun is not governed by what precedes it, because it has the head of the speech; rather it is governed by the verb of the condition, just as it governs the verb of the condition in the jussive. Nor can it be interrogative, because what precedes does not govern the interrogative, as it has the head of the speech, and because "annā", when interrogative, is satisfied with what follows it of verb and noun, as in {أنى يَكُونُ لَهُ وَلَدٌ} [al-Anʿām: 101] and {أنى لَكِ هذا} [Āl ʿImrān: 37], whereas this one in this verse needs what precedes it, as you see. This is a difficult place that needs reflection and study.»

Then what appears is that it is conditional here and its apodosis has been omitted, owing to the indication of what precedes it, its implied form being: "annā shiʾtum fa-ʾtūhu" (however you wish, come to it); and the states in it have been made like adverbs and given their treatment, likening the state to the adverb of place; and for that reason it is implied with «fī» (in), just as the interrogative «kayfa» was treated as a conditional in His saying: {يُنفِقُ كَيْفَ يَشَآءُ} [al-Māʾida: 64] and they said "kayfa taṣnaʿu aṣnaʿ" (as you do, I do): the meaning here is not interrogative but conditional. So there is an omission there in His saying: {يُنفِقُ كَيْفَ يَشَآءُ}, that is: "kayfa yashāʾu yunfiqu"; and so at every place resembling it. More explanation of it will come. If you say: you have taken «annā» out of true adverbiality and made it for generalising the states like «kayfa», and you said that it requires another clause, like the condition, then is the verb after it in the position of the jussive, considering that it is conditional, or in the position of the nominative, as it is after «kayfa» when used conditionally? I say: it admits both, and the first is preferable because the jussive effect is established, since the utmost that the matter amounts to is likening the states to adverbs because of the stated connection, which is the implying of «fī» in each of them.

None but some jussed with «kayfa», by analogy not by hearing. The object of «شئتم» is omitted, that is: "you wish to come to it", provided it is in the permitted place.

His saying: {وَقَدِّمُواْ}: its object is omitted, that is: the intention of offspring, or the intention of chastity, and the remembrance of Allah, or good, as in His saying: {وَمَا تُقَدِّمُواْ لأَنْفُسِكُم مِّنْ خَيْرٍ تَجِدُوهُ} [al-Baqara: 110]. «لأنفسكم» is attached to «قدِّموا». The lām admits being causal or being a particle of transitivity. The hāʾ in «ملاقوه» may refer back to Allah the Exalted, and then an omitted muḍāf is necessary, that is: "you will meet His recompense"; and it may refer back to the omitted object of «قدِّموا», with an omitted muḍāf also, that is: "you will meet the recompense of what you have sent forward"; and it may refer back to the recompense which the omitted object of «قدِّموا» indicates.

The pronoun in «وبَشِّر» is for the Messenger, peace be upon him, because his mention has run in His saying: {يَسْأَلُونَكَ}; Abū al-Baqāʾ said it, and there is room for consideration in it, because the pronoun of address and of the first person does not need it to be said of them that something indicating them has preceded. It is also possible that it be for anyone from whom giving glad tidings is valid.

semin-durr:224-224.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لأَيْمَانِكُمْ أَن تَبَرُّواْ}: this lām admits two possibilities. One: that it strengthens the transitivity of «عُرْضة», its implied form being: "and do not make Allah something kept ready and lying in wait for your swearing". The second: that it is causal, so that it is attached to the verb of prohibition, that is: "do not make Him a ʿurḍa because of your oaths".

His saying: {أَنْ تَبَرَّواْ}: there are six possibilities in it. The first, which is the view of al-Zajjāj, al-Tabrīzī and others, is that it is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, the khabar being omitted, its implied form being: "that you be dutiful, be God-fearing and make peace is better for you than that you make Him a ʿurḍa for your oaths", or "your dutifulness is more fitting and more excellent"; and this is weak because it leads to the severing of this clause from what precedes it, whereas the apparent view is that it is attached to it.

The second: that it is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and this is the view of the majority; then they differed over its implied form. It was said: "the wish that you be dutiful"; it was said: "the dislike that you be dutiful", said by al-Mahdawī; it was said: "for leaving off being dutiful", said by al-Mubarrad; it was said: "lest you be dutiful", said by Abū ʿUbayda and al-Ṭabarī, and the two recited:

954 - . . . فلا واللهِ تَهْبِطُ تَلْعَةً. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... 
("By Allah, he will not descend any watercourse…")

that is, "lā tahbiṭu", the «lā» being omitted; and the like of it is {يُبَيِّنُ الله لَكُمْ أَن تَضِلُّواْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 176], that is, "lest you go astray". The implying of "wish" is the sound view, for the other implied forms that I mentioned after the implying of "wish" have no evident meaning, because they give as the reason for refraining from the oath the absence of dutifulness, whereas the occurrence of the oath is what is explained by the absence of dutifulness; and no condition and consequence can be formed from the two: were you to say, in the sense of this prohibition and its reason, "if you swear by Allah you are dutiful", it would not be valid; by contrast with implying "wish", for it gives as the reason for refraining from the oath the wish for the existence of dutifulness, and a condition and consequence can be formed from the two: you say, "if you swear you will not be dutiful, and if you do not swear you will be dutiful".

The third: that it is on the dropping of the preposition, that is: "fī an tabarrū", and then the two views come in it: the view of Sībawayh and al-Farrāʾ, so it is in the position of the accusative; and the view of al-Khalīl and al-Kisāʾī, so it is in the position of the genitive. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «"أَنْ تَبَرُّوا" is attached to the verb or to the ʿurḍa, that is: "and do not make Allah, because of your oaths, a ʿurḍa for your being dutiful".» The Shaykh said: «This implying is not valid because of the separation between the governor and its dependent by a stranger, for in his view "لأيمانكم" is attached to "تجعلوا", so it falls as a separator between "عُرْضَة", which is the governor, and "أَنْ تَبَرُّوا", which is in "an tabarrū", and it is a stranger to both. The parallel of what he allowed is that you say "Mur wa-ḍrib bi-Zaydin Hindan", which is not permitted; and they stated that it is not permitted to say "جاءني رجلٌ ذو فرسٍ راكبٌ أَبْلَقَ", meaning "a man possessing a piebald horse came to me riding", because of the separation by a stranger.»

The fourth: that it is in the position of the genitive as ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to «أَيْمانكم», that is, to the things sworn about, which are dutifulness, God-fearing and making peace. The Shaykh said: «It is weak because of what it involves of making the oaths mean the thing sworn upon.» The apparent view is that they are the oaths themselves by which one swears, and there is no need to interpret them as the thing sworn upon, since no necessity calls for it; this is by contrast with the ḥadīth, which is his saying ﷺ: «إذا حَلَفْتَ على يمينٍ فرأيت غَيرها خيراً منها» ("When you swear an oath and see another better than it…"), for it must there be interpreted as the thing sworn upon, whereas no necessity calls for that in the noble verse.

The fifth: that it is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from «لأَيْمانكم», with the interpretation that al-Zamakhsharī mentioned, and this is preferable to the ʿaṭf bayān possibility, since ʿaṭf bayān occurs mostly with proper names.

The sixth, and it is the apparent view: that it is on the dropping of the preposition, not in that earlier way, but the particle is a different particle and what it is attached to is something different, the implied form being: "li-iqsāmikum ʿalā an tabarrū", so «ʿalā» is attached to «iqsāmikum», and the meaning is: "do not make Allah something exposed and made a thing of ordinary use for your swearing upon dutifulness, God-fearing and making peace, which are beautiful qualities, out of fear of breaking the oath; so how about swearing upon what has no dutifulness or God-fearing in it!!!"

As for ʿurḍa, there are three views on its derivation. The first: that it is a fuʿla in the sense of mafʿūl, from al-ʿarḍ, like al-quṭba and al-ghurfa. The meaning of the verse on this basis is: do not make Him exposed to swearing, from their saying "Fulān is a ʿurḍa for such and such", that is, exposed to it. Kaʿb said:

955 - من كلِّ نَضَّاخَة الذِّفْرَى إذا عَرِقَتْ ... عُرضَتُها طامِسُ الأعلامِ مَجْهُولُ
("Of every she-camel gushing behind the ear when she sweats, whose objective is an effaced, unknown tract with its markers gone")

and Ḥabīb said:

956 - متى كانَ سَمْعي عُرْضَةً لِلَّوائِمِ ... وكيفَ صَفَتْ للعاذِلِين عَزائِمي
("When was my hearing ever exposed to the blamers, and how did my resolves become clear to the censurers?")

and Ḥassān said:

957 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... هُمُ الأنصارُ عُرْضَتُها اللِّقاءُ
("… they are the Anṣār, whose objective is the meeting (in battle)")

and Aws said:

958 - وأَدْمَاءُ مثلُ الفَحْلِ يوماً عَرَضْتُها ... لرحلي وفيها هِزَّةٌ وتقاذُفُ
("And a white she-camel, like a stallion, which I one day presented for my saddle, and in her there was a brisk swaying and bounding")

All of this is in the sense of "exposed to such and such".

The second: that it is the noun of what you place across something, so it is from "he laid the stick across the vessel", so it blocks the way to it and becomes a barrier and obstacle; and the meaning of the verse on this basis is the prohibition on swearing by Allah that they will not be dutiful and not fear Him, and saying "we are unable to do that because of our oath".

The third: that it is from al-ʿurḍa, which is strength; one says "jamalun ʿurḍatun lil-safar" (a camel with strength for travel), that is, strong for it. Ibn al-Zubayr said:

959 - فهذي لأيَّامِ الحروبِ وهذه ... لِلَهْوي وهَذي عُرْضَةٌ لارتحالِنا
("This one is for the days of wars, and that one for my amusement, and this one is a mainstay for our journeying")

that is, strength and equipment; and the meaning of the verse on this basis is: do not make the oath by Allah the Exalted a strength for yourselves in refraining from dutifulness.

Al-aymān is the plural of yamīn, whose origin is the limb (the right hand), and it was used for swearing figuratively because the custom of those making agreements was to clasp their right hands. Its derivation is from al-yumn (blessing). And al-yamīn is also the name of the side which lies on the side of this limb, so it is put in the accusative as an adverbial; likewise al-yasār (the left): you say, "Zaydun yamīna ʿAmrin wa-Bakrun yasārahu". Al-yamīn is pluralised as aymun and aymān. Is what is meant by al-aymān in the verse the oath itself or the thing sworn upon? Two views, the first being preferable. The permissibility of its meaning the thing sworn upon, and the evidence from the ḥadīth for it, and the answer to that, have already preceded.

His saying: {والله سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ}: He concluded with these two attributes because of the preceding relevance of the two: swearing relates to hearing, while the intention of dutifulness, being an act of the heart, relates to knowledge. And He put al-Samīʿ first because what it relates to precedes, which is the oath.

semin-durr:213-213.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنذِرِينَ}: two ḥāls from «النبيين». It was said: it is a concurrent ḥāl (ḥāl muqārina), because their being sent was at the time of the glad tidings and the warning. There is something to consider in this, because glad tidings and warning come after the sending. The apparent view is that it is a ḥāl muqaddara (anticipated ḥāl). The meaning of glad tidings and warning has already preceded in His saying: {أَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ} [al-Baqara: 6] and {وَبَشِّرِ الذين آمَنُواْ} [al-Baqara: 25].

His saying: {مَعَهُمُ}: there are two views on this adverb. The first: that it is attached to «أنزل». This requires an interpretation, because attaching it to «أَنْزَلَ» entails that the prophets accompanied the Book in the sending down, whereas they are not described by that, since it is lacking in them. Its interpretation is that what is meant by "sending down" (inzāl) is "sending" (irsāl), because it is caused by it, as if it were said: "and He sent the Book with them", so their sharing with it in the sending down is sound by this interpretation. The second: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «الكتاب», and it is an anticipated ḥāl, i.e. "He sent it down, anticipating its accompanying them." Abū l-Baqāʾ implied it by his saying "as a witness for them and a support", and this is an explanation of meaning, not of i'rab.

The alif and lām in «الكتاب» may be for a specific reference (ʿahd), meaning that it is a particular book such as the Torah, for example, which was sent down upon Mūsā and upon the prophets after him, in the sense that they judged by it and continued to do so; and it may be generic, i.e. "He sent down with each one of them something of this genus". It was said: it is a singular put in the place of a plural, i.e. "and He sent down with them the Books", but this is weak.

This clause is conjoined to His saying «فَبَعَثَ». It is not to be said: "glad tidings and warning arise from the sending down, so how were the two put before it?" For we do not concede that the two occur only by the sending down of a book; rather they may occur by a revelation from Allah the Exalted that is neither recited nor written. And even if we concede that, the two were put first only because they are ḥāls from «النبيين», so it is preferable for them to be attached to them.

His saying: {بالحق}: three views on it. The first: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from the Book as well, according to those who permit multiple ḥāls, which is the sound view. The second: that it is attached to the Book itself because of the sense of the verb in it, since what is meant by it is "the written". The third: that it is attached to «أنزل», and this is more fitting, because making it a ḥāl is not sound except as a corroborating ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), since the Books of Allah the Exalted are never other than accompanied by truth, whereas the original in ḥāls is that they be changing (muntaqila); and we have no need to depart from the original. Also because «الكتاب» is treated as an inert noun (jāmid).

His saying: {لِيَحْكُمَ}: this preposition and its genitive noun is attached to His saying «أنزل», and the lām is for cause. About the latent agent in «ليحكم» there are three views. The first, which is the most apparent: that it returns to Allah the Exalted, because He was mentioned earlier in His saying «فَبَعَثَ الله», and because ascribing judgment to Him is literal. This is supported by the reading of al-Jaḥdarī, as Makkī reported from him: «لنحكمَ» with the nūn of majesty, in which there is an iltifāt from the third person to the first. Ibn ʿAṭiyya thought that Makkī erred in reporting this reading from him, and said: "The people related from al-Jaḥdarī «ليُحْكَمَ» with the verb in the passive." But he should not declare him mistaken, since it is possible that two readings are reported from him.

The second: that it returns to «الكتاب», i.e. "so that the Book may judge", and the ascription of judging to it is figurative, like the ascription of speaking to it in the saying of the Exalted: {هذا كِتَابُنَا يَنطِقُ عَلَيْكُم بالحق} [al-Jāthiya: 29], and the ascription of decreeing to it in his saying:

921 - ضَرَبَتْ عليكَ العنكبُوتُ بنَسْجِها ... وقضى عليك به الكتابُ المُنَزَّلُ
(The spider has spun its web over you, and the revealed Book decreed it against you.)

The ground of the figurative usage is that the judgment is in it, so it was ascribed to it. The third: that it returns to the Prophet, but the Shaykh found this weak because of the singular pronoun, since on this view it should have been plural to agree with «النبيين». Then he said: "What he said is permissible, on the basis that the pronoun returns to the individuals of the plural, in the sense of: so that each prophet may judge by his book." «بين» is attached to «يَحْكم». The containment here is figurative. Likewise «فيما اختلفوا» is also attached to it. «ما» is a relative, and what is meant by it is the religion, i.e. "so that Allah may judge between the people regarding the religion, after they had been agreed upon it." It is weak to intend by «ما» the Prophet ﷺ, because «ما» is for non-rational beings for the most part. «فيه» is attached to «اختلفوا», and the pronoun returns to the relative «ما».

His saying: {وَمَا اختلف فِيهِ}: about the pronoun in «فيه» there are several views. The most apparent: that it returns to the relative «ما» as well, and likewise the pronoun in «أوتوه». It was said: both return to the Book, i.e. "none differed about the Book but those who were given the Book." It was said: both return to the Prophet; al-Zajjāj said this, i.e. "none differed about the Prophet but those who were given knowledge of his prophethood." And it was said: it returns to ʿĪsā because of the indication of it.

His saying: {مِن بَعْدِ}: two views on it. The first, which is the sound one: that it is attached to an omitted element, its implied form being "they differed about it after". The second: that it is attached to the pronounced «اختلف». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«إلاَّ» does not prevent that, as you say: 'mā qāma illā Zaydun yawma l-jumuʿa' (only Zayd stood on Friday)." On this which Abū l-Baqāʾ permitted, the grammarians have much to say. The summary is that «إلا» is not used to except two things without conjunction or substitution, because «إلاَّ» makes the verb transitive, and for that reason what follows it may be attached to what precedes it; so it is like the wāw of maʿa and the hamza of transitivization. Just as the wāw of "maʿa" and the hamza of transitivization do not make the verb transitive to more than one except with conjunction or substitution, likewise «إلا». This is the sound view, even if some differed. If something comes from their speech that suggests the permissibility of that, it is interpreted. Among it is His saying: {وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ إِلاَّ رِجَالاً نوحي} [al-Naḥl: 43-44], then He said «بالبينات»; the apparent sense is that «بالبينات» is attached to «أرسلنا», so two things are excepted by «إلا», one «رجالاً» and the other «بالبينات».

Its interpretation is that «بالبينات» is attached to an omitted element so that that objection does not follow from it. Abū l-Ḥasan (al-Akhfash) and Abū ʿAlī (al-Fārisī) forbade: "mā akhadha aḥadun illā Zaydun dirhaman" and "mā ḍaraba l-qawmu illā baʿḍuhum baʿḍan". They differed about how to make them sound. Abū l-Ḥasan said: "The way to make them sound is to put forward the nominative that follows «إلاَّ» before it, so it is said: 'mā akhadha aḥadun Zaydun illā dirhaman', so «Zayd» is a substitute from «aḥad» and «dirhaman» is an emptied exception from that omitted noun, its implied form being: 'mā akhadha aḥadun Zaydun shayʾan illā dirhaman'." Abū ʿAlī said: "The way to do it is to add an accusative in the wording, so that the implied excepted-from noun appears, so it is said: 'mā akhadha aḥadun shayʾan illā Zaydun dirhaman', so the nominative is a substitute for the nominative and the accusative for the accusative; likewise: 'mā ḍaraba l-qawmu aḥadan illā baʿḍuhum baʿḍan'." Abū Bakr ibn al-Sarrāj said: "You say 'aʿṭaytu n-nāsa dirhaman illā ʿUmaran' (I gave people a dirham except ʿUmar), which is permissible. If you said 'aʿṭaytu n-nāsa dirhaman illā ʿAmran d-danānīra' it would not be permissible, because only one thing is excepted by the particle. If you said 'mā aʿṭaytu n-nāsa dirhaman illā ʿAmran dāniqan' as an exception, it is not permitted, or as a substitution it is [permitted], so you substitute «ʿAmran» for «n-nās» and «dāniqan» for «dirhaman», as if you said: 'mā aʿṭaytu illā ʿAmran dāniqan'", meaning that the restriction falls on the two objects.

Some of the verifiers said: "What Ibn al-Sarrāj permitted of substitution in this question is weak, because substitution in an exception must be accompanied by «إلاَّ», so it resembles conjunction; and just as two conjoined words do not occur after a conjunction particle, two substitutes do not occur after «إلاَّ»."

Once this principle and what people have said about it is known, Abū l-Baqāʾ's analysis in this noble verse falls under this chapter, because it is an emptied exception, and after «إلاَّ» there has occurred the agent, which is «الذين», the preposition and its genitive noun, which is «مِن بعد», and the object of purpose, which is «بغياً», so each of them would be restricted. The meaning: "none differed about it except those who were given it, except after the clear proofs had come to them, except out of envy." If the implied form is thus, then two things are excepted by «إلاَّ» besides the first, which is an agent, without conjunction or substitution. I have gone into this question fully only because of how often it recurs.

His saying: {بَغْياً}: there are two views on its being accusative. The most apparent: that it is a mafʿūl min ajlihi because of the completeness of the conditions; it is an impelling cause. The governor in it is latent, according to what we preferred, namely what «فيه» is attached to, and the pronounced «اختلف», according to those who hold that two things may be excepted by «إلا».

The second: that it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. "being insolent (bāghīn)", and the governor in it is what preceded. «بينهم» is attached to an omitted element because it is an adjective of «بغياً», i.e. "insolence that is among them".

His saying: {لِمَا اختلفوا فِيهِ}: «لِما» is attached to «هَدَى», and «ما» is a relative; the pronoun in «اختلفوا» returns to «الذين أوتوه», and in «فيه» it returns to «ما» and is attached to «اختلف».

{مِنَ الحق} is attached to an omitted element because it is in the position of the ḥāl from «ما» in «لِما». «مَنْ» may be partitive, or explicative according to those who hold that, its implied form being "which is the truth". Abū l-Baqāʾ permitted «مِنَ الحق» to be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «فيه», with «اختلفوا» as the governor in it. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that there is an inversion (qalb) in the sentence and the original is: «فَهَدى الله الذينَ آمنوا للحقِّ ممَّا اختلفوا», and al-Ṭabarī preferred it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "What led him to this implied form was the fear that the wording might suggest that they differed about the truth, and that Allah guided the believers to some of what they differed about, which may perhaps not be true in itself." He said: "Inversion in the Book of Allah without a necessity that compels it is incapacity and poor understanding." End. I say: this possibility which Ibn ʿAṭiyya made the cause of al-Farrāʾ's claim of inversion is not imagined at all.

His saying: {بِإِذْنِهِ}: two views on it. The first: that it is attached to an omitted element because it is a ḥāl from «الذين آمنوا», i.e. "being permitted". The second: that it is attached to «هدى» as the object, i.e. "He guided them by His command."

semin-durr:214-214.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ}: There are four views on this «أم»: that it is disjoined (munqaṭiʿa), so it is implied as «بل» and the hamza. «بل» is for a transitional turning away (iḍrāb intiqāl) from one report to another, and the hamza is for affirmation (taqrīr); the implied form being: "bal a-ḥasibtum". The second: that it is merely for turning away without the implication of a hamza after it; this is the view of al-Zajjāj, who recited:

922 - بَدَتْ مثل قَرْنِ الشمسِ في رَوْنَقِ الضحى ... وصورتِها أم أنتَ في العينِ أَمْلَحُ
(She appeared like the horn of the sun in the brilliance of forenoon, and in its form — or rather you, in the eye, are more beautiful.)

that is: "bal anta". The third, the view of some of the Kufans: that it has the sense of the hamza, so on this view it is used to begin at the start of the speech, and does not need a preceding clause that it turns away from. The fourth: that it is connected (muttaṣila), and that is sound only by implying an omitted clause before it; some implied it as: "So Allah guided those who believed, and they were patient through their people's mockery; will you then follow their path, or do you reckon that you will enter Paradise without following their path?"

«حَسِبْتُم» here is one of the sisters of «ظنَّ», governing two objects whose original is the mubtadaʾ and khabar, and «أَنْ» with what follows it stands in place of the two objects according to Sībawayh, and in place of the first with the second omitted according to Abū l-Akhfash, as that was established. Its imperfect has two forms: with fatḥa, which is the analogical, and with kasra. It has parallel verbs, which will come at the end of the surah. Its meaning is supposition, and it may be used for certainty, he said:

923 - حَسِبْتُ التقى والجودَ خيرَ تجارةٍ ... رَباحاً إذا ما المرءُ أصبحَ ثاقِلا
(I reckoned piety and generosity the best trade in profit, when a man comes to be weighed down.)

Its maṣdar is al-ḥusbān. It is also intransitive when its meaning is reddish hair: you say "ḥasiba Zaydun", i.e. he became reddish, so he is aḥsab, i.e. ashqar (reddish).

His saying: {وَلَمَّا يَأْتِكُم}: the wāw is for ḥāl, and the clause after it is in the position of the accusative as that, i.e. "while there has not come to you the like of theirs". «لَمَّا» is a jussive particle meaning negation like «لم», and it is more emphatic than negation by «لم», because «لم» negates only the time that is connected to the present. The difference between it and «لم» lies in several respects. The first: that the verb after it may be omitted in eloquent speech if an indication points to it, as in his saying:

924 - فَجِئْتُ قبورَهم بَدْءاً وَلَمَّا ... فنادَيْتُ القبورَ فلم تُجِبْنَهْ
(I came to their graves first, and not yet... I called to the graves, and they did not answer me.)

i.e. "wa-lammā akun badʾan", i.e. one who begins, unlike «لم», for which that is not permitted except of necessity. Among them: that it is for negating the past connected to the time of the present, while «لم» is for negating it absolutely or as disconnected, as has passed. Among them: that «لَمَّا» does not enter upon the verb of a condition or an apodosis, unlike «لم». There is disagreement about «لمَّا»: it was said: it is simple; and it was said: it is compounded of «لم» and «ما» added to it.

In His saying {مَّثَلُ الذين} there is an omitted annexed word and an omitted described noun, the implied form being: "and there has not yet come to you the like of the trial of the believers who passed away."

«مِنْ قبلِكم» is attached to «خَلَوا» and it is like an emphasis, since the ṣila is understood from His saying «خَلَوا».

His saying: {مَّسَّتْهُمُ البأسآء}: about this clause there are two views. The first: that it has no position in grammatical analysis because it is explicative, i.e. it explained the likeness and expounded it, as if it were said: "What was their likeness?" and it was said: "Hardship touched them." The second: that it is a ḥāl, with "qad" implied; Abū l-Baqāʾ permitted that, and it is a ḥāl from the agent of «خَلَوا». Making it a ḥāl is remote.

His saying: {حتى يَقُولَ}: the majority read «يقولَ» in the accusative, and there are two views on it. The first: that «حتى» has the sense of «إلى», i.e. "until he says", so it is the limit of the preceding touching and quaking; and after «حتى» only the future imperfect is put in the accusative, whereas this has occurred and passed. The answer: that it is on the narration of a state (ḥikāyat al-ḥāl), he narrated that state. The second: that «حتى» has the sense of «كي», so it conveys cause; but this is weak, because the saying of the Messenger and the believers is not a cause for the touching and quaking, although the apparent sense of Abū l-Baqāʾ's words is that, for he said: "It is read with the nominative, the implied form being: 'they were shaken, so they said', for the quaking is the cause of the saying." «أَنْ» after «حتى» is latent on both views. Nāfiʿ read it in the nominative, as a ḥāl; and a ḥāl is not put in the accusative after «حتى» or anything else, because the accusative-governing particle makes (the verb) purely future, so the two are contradictory.

Know that when a verb follows «حتى» it is either present, future or past. If present it is nominative, as in "He was ill until they no longer hoped for him", i.e. in the present. If future it is accusative, you say: "I walked until I enter the town," when you have not yet entered. If past, you narrate it, and then your narration of it is either according to its being future, so you put it in the accusative on narrating that state, or according to its being present, so you put it in the nominative on narrating that state. So it is correct to say, of the reading of the majority, "narration of a state", and of the reading of Nāfiʿ also "narration of a state". I alert to this only because the expression of some limits "narration of a state" to the reading of the majority, and the expression of others limits it to the reading of Nāfiʿ. Abū l-Baqāʾ said of the reading of the majority: "The verb here is future, with which their state is narrated, and the meaning is of the past"; and he had already explained the nominative by taking «حتى» as causal.

His saying «معه»: this adverb may be accusative by «يقول», i.e. "they accompanied him in this saying and joined him in it", or accusative by «آمنوا», i.e. "they accompanied him in belief".

His saying: {متى نَصْرُ الله}: «متى» is accusative as an adverb, so its position is nominative as a fronted khabar, and «نصرٌ» is a postponed mubtadaʾ. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "According to al-Akhfash its position is accusative as an adverb, and «نصرُ» is nominative by it." «متى» is an adverb of time that is not inflected for case except by being governed by a preposition. It is indeclinable because it implies either the sense of the interrogative hamza or the sense of the conditional «مَنْ»; for it may be an interrogative noun, and it may be a conditional noun, jussing two verbs, protasis and apodosis.

The apparent view is that the clause {متى نَصْرُ الله} is from the saying of the believers, and the clause {ألا إِنَّ نَصْرَ الله قَرِيبٌ} is from the saying of the Messenger, so the saying was ascribed to all in summary, and the indication of the situation clarifies the mentioned detail. This is better than the saying of those who claimed that the sentence has fronting and postponing, the implied form being: "until those who believed say {متى نَصْرُ الله} and the Messenger says «ألا إنَّ»", with the Messenger put first for his rank, and the believers put first for their precedence in time. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is arbitrary and carries the speech to other than its proper sense", and it is as he said. It was said: the two clauses are both from the saying of the Messenger and the believers together, meaning that the Messenger said both together, and likewise his followers said both together, and the Messenger's saying {متى نَصْرُ الله} is not by way of doubt, but by way of supplication, urging that help come quickly. And it was said: the first clause is from the speech of the Messenger and his followers, and the last clause is from the speech of Allah the Exalted, answering them with what the messengers asked and the followers found slow in coming. The upshot is that the two clauses are in the position of the accusative as the object of saying.

semin-durr:275-275.t:
«الرِّبا»: its lām (final radical) is a wāw, from their saying «رَبا يَرْبو»; therefore its dual is formed with the wāw and it is written with alif. The Kufans permitted forming its dual with yāʾ, and likewise writing it so; they said this is because of the kasra of its first letter, and for that reason they applied imāla to it. This is not specific to what has a kasra on the first letter; rather the triliteral of the wāw-final class whose first letter has kasra or ḍamma, such as «رِبا» and «عُلا», has the ruling I mentioned from them; as for what has fatḥa on the first letter, such as «عصا» and «قَفَا», they did not differ from the Basrans. In the Qur'an, in the script of the Companions, it is written with a wāw followed by an alif. The root indicates increase and elevation, and from it comes «الرَّبْوَة» (the rise). Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī said, describing a spear:
1094 - وأسمرَ خطِيَّاً كأن كعوبَه ... نَوَى القَسْبِ قد أَرْبَى ذِراعاً على العُشْرِ
(A dark Khaṭṭī spear, whose knots are like date-stones of hard dates, which exceeds ten cubits by one cubit.)
It is said: it was written with the wāw only because the people of the Hijaz learned writing from the people of al-Ḥīra, and the people of al-Ḥīra say «الرِّبو» with the wāw, so they wrote it so, and the people of the Hijaz transmitted it so in writing, not in pronunciation. Al-ʿAdawī read «الرِّبَو» likewise with a pure wāw after the fatḥa of the bāʾ. It was said: this reader treated connection (waṣl) as pause (waqf), for some of the Arabs turn the alif of the defective noun into a wāw and say «هذه أَفْعَو», and this is of that kind, except that he treated waṣl as waqf.
Abū Zayd related something even stranger than that, saying: "Some read it with kasra on the rāʾ and ḍamma on the bāʾ with a wāw after it", and he ascribed this to error; that is because the Arabic tongue does not leave a wāw after a ḍamma in declinable nouns; rather when that is found it is not left as it is, but the ḍamma becomes kasra and the wāw yāʾ, such as «دَلْو» and «أَدْلٍ», «جَرْو» and «أَجْرٍ». Abū ʿAlī recited:
1095 - ليثٌ هِزَبْرٌ مُدِلٌّ عند خِيسَتِه ... بالرَّقْمتينِ له أَجْرٍ وأَعْراسُ
(A fierce, bold lion at his thicket at the two Raqmas, with cubs and mates.)
The most that has been said about it is that its reader turned the alif into a wāw, as they say in pause «أَفْعَو», then treated it in that way as pause, and the transmitter from him did not firmly retain what he heard, and thought it was with ḍamma on the bāʾ because of the wāw, and so transmitted it. Would that people had left their works free of such readings, which, if the common people heard them, they would spit out, and of their explanations; but those who omit them have come to be regarded by some as ignorant for not being acquainted with them.
It is also said «رِبا» and «رِما», with the bāʾ replaced by mīm, as they said «كََثَم» for «كَثَب». The alif-lām in «الرِّبا» may be that of familiarity (ʿahd), since the legal ribā is meant, and may be for defining the genus.
His saying: {لاَ يَقُومُونَ}: the apparent is that it is the khabar of the preceding relative noun. Some said it is a ḥāl, which is an oversight, though one might force a justification of it by implying the khabar, like the reading of one who read {وَنَحْنُ عُصْبَةٌ} and his saying:
1096 -. . . لا أنا باغياً ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
in one of the two aspects.
His saying: {إِلاَّ كَمَا يَقُومُ}: it has the two well-known aspects: accusative as naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "they do not stand except a standing like the standing of the one whom Satan strikes by his touch", which is the well-known view among the muʿribīn; or accusative as ḥāl from the pronoun of that implied maṣdar, i.e. "they do not perform it, that is, the standing, except resembling the standing of the one whom Satan strikes", and this is the opinion of Sībawayh; I have already presented the investigation of both.
«ما»: the apparent is that it is maṣdarī (verbal-noun forming), i.e. "like the standing of". Some allowed it to be in the sense of «الذي» with an omitted returning pronoun, the implied being: "except like the standing that the one whom Satan strikes performs", and it is remote.
«يتخبَّطه» is on the pattern «يَتَفَعَّلُه», and it has the sense of the unaugmented verb, i.e. «يخبِطُه» (strikes him); it is like «تَعدَّى الشيءَ» and «عَدَاه». Its meaning is taken from «خَبَط البعيرُ بأخفافِه» when it strikes the ground with its hooves. One says: «فلان يَخْبِط خَبْطَ عَشْواء» (so-and-so acts at random, like a short-sighted she-camel). ʿAlqama said:
1079 - وفي كل حَيًّ قد خَبَطْتَ بنعمةٍ ... فَحُقَّ لشَأْسٍ من نَداكَ ذَنُوبُ
(In every tribe you have struck out with bounty, so it is fitting that Shaʾs have a full bucket of your generosity.)
[Translator's note: the verse number is printed «1079» in the source; by the sequence it should be 1097.] And Zuhayr said:
1098 - رأيتُ المنايا خَبْطَ عَشْوَاءَ مَنْ تُصِبْ ... تُمِتْه ومَنْ تُخْطِىءْ يُعَمَّر فَيَهْرَمِ
(I saw deaths strike at random like a blind she-camel: whomever they hit, they kill, and whomever they miss lives long and grows old.)
His saying: {مِنَ المس} has three aspects. One: that it is attached to «يتخبَّطه», in respect of madness, so it is in the position of an accusative; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. The second: that it is attached to His saying «يقومُ», i.e. "they do not rise from the touch that is upon them except as the possessed one rises." The third: that it is attached to His saying «يقومُ», i.e. "as the possessed one rises from his madness." Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned these last two aspects.
The Shaykh said: "He had earlier explained «المسّ» as madness, and what he held regarding the attachment of «من المس» to His saying «لا يقومون» is weak for two reasons. One: he explained «المسّ» as madness, and had explained that their standing will be only in the hereafter, and there they have neither madness nor touch; and it is remote that «المسّ», which is madness, should be a metonymy for eating ribā in this world, so that the meaning would be: 'they will not rise on the Day of Resurrection, or from their graves, because of eating ribā, except as the one whom Satan strikes rises'; for if this meaning had been intended, stating it plainly would have been preferable to the metonymy with the word «المَسّ», since plain statement is stronger in deterrence and restraint. The second: that what comes after «إلاّ» is not attached to what precedes it unless it is within the scope of the exception, and this is not within the scope of the exception; for that reason they forbade that «بالبيناتِ والزبرِ» be attached to His saying {وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ إِلاَّ رِجَالاً} [al-Naḥl: 44], on the implication «وما أرسلنا بالبيناتِ والزبرِ إلا رجالاً»."
I say: As for his weakening the meaning, it is not good; rather metonymy in their tongue is more forceful, and this is not disputed. As for the second aspect, in the preposition-and-genitive and the adverbial what is tolerated is not tolerated in others, and its witnesses are many.
«المَسُّ» is used in their language to express madness; they said «مُسَّ فهو مَمْسُوس» like «جُنَّ فهو مَجْنون». Abū Bakr recited:
1099 - أُعَلِّلُ نفسي بما لا يكونُ ... كذي المَسِّ جُنَّ ولم يُخْنَقِ
(I console myself with what will not be, like one touched, driven mad though not strangled.)
Its origin is that they say Satan touches a person with his hand and kicks him with his foot. Madness is also expressed for vigour, speed and lightness of movement; hence al-Aʿshā said, describing his she-camel:
1100 - وتُصبحُ عن غِبِّ السُّرى وكأنما ... أَلَمَّ بها مِن طائفِ الجنِّ أَوْلَقُ
(After the night journey she wakes as though a madness from a visitation of the jinn had come upon her.)
And another said:
1101 - بَخِيلٍ عليها جِنَّةٌ عبقريةٌ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(On a horse with a spirited, supreme frenzy upon it...)
His saying: {ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ} is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, i.e. "that striking, or that standing, is on account of their fabricating this saying." It is said: «ذلك» is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ whose implied form is "their standing is that." The Shaykh said: "Except that in this aspect there is a separation between the maṣdar and what is attached to it, which is «بأنهم»; though the permissibility of that is not remote, owing to the omission of the maṣdar, so no ugliness appeared from separation by the khabar."
They made ribā the basis and sale the branch, so that they likened it to it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was it not said «إنما الربا مثلُ البيع», since the discourse is about ribā, not sale? I say: it came in the manner of exaggeration, which is that their belief in the permissibility of ribā had reached the point that they made it the basis and norm in permissibility, until they likened sale to it." I say: this is a well-known chapter in rhetoric, and it is the highest rank of simile (tashbīh); from it is the saying:
1102 - ورَمْلٍ كأوراكِ العَذارى قَطَعْتُه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And a sand-tract like the hips of maidens I crossed...)
His saying: {وَأَحَلَّ الله البيع}: the apparent is that it is Allah the Exalted's speech, informing that He made this lawful and that unlawful; accordingly this clause has no grammatical position. Some said: "This clause is a completion of the saying of those who eat ribā, so it is in the position of an accusative by «القول», conjoined to the quoted speech"; this is very remote. I transmitted it from the Chief Judge [ʿIzz al-Dīn in his lesson]. [Translator's note: the source text has a bracketed gap in «قاضي [القضاء عز الدين في درسه]»; translated as printed.]
His saying: {فَمَن جَآءَهُ}: it may be conditional, which is the apparent, or relative; on both assumptions it is in the position of a nominative by ibtidāʾ (inception).
His saying: {فَلَهُ مَا سَلَفَ} is the khabar. If it is conditional, the fāʾ is obligatory; if relative, it is permissible, and the reason for its addition is the resemblance of the relative to the conditional noun mentioned earlier. When it is conditional, another aspect is permissible: that it is accusative by an implied verb that what follows explains, the issue being of the chapter of ishtighāl, with the verb implied after it because it has the head of the discourse; the implied being "whichever person the admonition came to, it came to him"; this is not permissible when it is relative, because the ṣila does not explain a governor, as it cannot validly act upon what precedes it, and the condition for explanation is the validity of acting upon. The tāʾ dropped from the verb for two reasons: the separation between the verb and its agent by the object, and the femininity being figurative; al-Ḥasan read «جاءَتْه» in the original form.
His saying: {مِّنْ رَّبِّهِ} may be attached to «جاءَتْه», being for the beginning of the extent, figuratively; or attached to an omitted element as a ṣifa of «موعظة», i.e. "an admonition from the admonitions of his Lord", that is, some of His admonitions.
His saying: {فانتهى} is conjoined to «جاءَتْه», conjoined with the fāʾ of immediate succession, i.e. his desisting was not delayed after the admonition came.
His saying: {وَمَنْ عَادَ}: the discussion of this «مَنْ», regarding the possibility of conditional and relative, is like the discussion of the one before it. The pronoun in His saying «فَأَمْرُه» refers to «ما سَلَف», i.e. "the matter of what has passed is with Allah", that is, in pardoning it and dropping the liability for it. It is said: it refers to the one who desisted, indicated by «انتهى», i.e. "the matter of the one who desisted from ribā is with Allah, in pardon and punishment." It is said: it refers to the practitioner of ribā, as to whether he will be alerted to desist or return to disobedience. It is said: it refers to ribā, i.e. in Allah's pardon of whatever He wills of it, or in continuing its prohibition.

semin-durr:225-225.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {باللغو}: attached to «يُؤاخِذُكم». The bāʾ has the sense of causation, as in His saying, the Exalted: {فَكُلاًّ أَخَذْنَا بِذَنبِهِ} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 40] and {وَلَوْ يُؤَاخِذُ الله الناس بِظُلْمِهِمْ} [al-Naḥl: 61].

Al-laghw is the maṣdar of laghā yalghū; one says laghā yalghū laghwan, like ghazā yaghzū ghazwan, and laghiya yalghā laghan, like laqiya yalqā laqan; and from the second is His saying, the Exalted: {والغوا فِيهِ}. There is disagreement about al-laghw. It was said: what the tongue slipped into without intent, said by al-Farrāʾ, and from it is the saying of al-Farazdaq:

960 - ولَسْتَ بمأخوذٍ بلَغْوٍ تَقُوله ... إذا لم تُعَمِّدْ عاقِدَاتِ العَزائِمِ
("You are not to be held to account for a slip of speech you utter, when you have not deliberately tied the knots of resolve")

It is related that al-Ḥasan was asked about al-laghw and about the captive woman who has a husband, so al-Farazdaq rose and said: «Did you not hear what I said?» and he recited "wa-lasta bi-maʾkhūdhin…" and his saying:

961 - وذاتِ حليلٍ أَنْكَحَتْها رِماحُنا ... حلالٌ لِمَنْ يَبْني بها لم تُطَلَّقِ
("And many a woman with a husband whom our spears gave in marriage, lawful for whoever consummates with her, though she was not divorced")

So al-Ḥasan said: «How clever you are, were it not for your breaking your oath.» «Laghw» is also applied to any ugly speech.

The Exalted said: {وَإِذَا مَرُّواْ بِاللَّغْوِ} [al-Furqān: 72] and {لاَّ يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغْواً} [Maryam: 62]; and he said:

962 - ورَبِّ أسرابِ حجيجٍ كُظَّمِ ... عن اللَّغَا ورفَثِ التكلُّمِ
("By the Lord of the flocks of pilgrims who restrain themselves from idle talk and from obscene speech")

It was said: it is what is thrown away of speech as unneeded, taken from their calling «laghw» those young camels that are not counted in the blood-money; and from it:

963 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كما أَلْغَيْتَ في الدِّيَة الحُوارا
("… as you disregarded the suckling camel-calf in the blood-money")

It was said: it is what is not understood, from their saying «laghā the bird», it made a sound. And al-laghw is what a person is devoted to babbling; and al-lugha (language) is taken from this. Al-Rāghib said: «"Laghiya bi-kadhā" means he babbled on about it as the sparrow does with its chirping (laghāhu), and from it the speech that a group babbles on with is called lugha, taking it as derived from "laghiya bi-kadhā", that is, he was devoted to it.» Ibn ʿĪsā said, having mentioned that lugha is what yields no benefit: «and from it comes al-lugha, because to those other than its speakers it is laghw»; but they declared him mistaken in that.

His saying: {في أَيْمَانِكُمْ}: three possibilities. One: that it is attached to the verb before it. The second: that it is attached to the maṣdar itself before it, as you say "laghā fī yamīnihi". The third: that it is attached to an omitted word as a ḥāl from «اللغو»; and you can recognise it from the meaning, in that if you made it the ṣila of a relative noun and described «اللغو» by it, the meaning would be sound, that is: "the laghw that is in your oaths".

His saying: {ولكن يُؤَاخِذُكُم}: «lākin» occurs here between two opposites with respect to the existence of the oath, because it is of necessity one of two cases: either the heart does not intend it but it ran on the tongue, and that is al-laghw; or the heart intends it, and that is the binding oath.

His saying {بِمَا كَسَبَتْ}: attached to the verb before it, and the bāʾ is causal as has preceded. For «mā» three possibilities are allowed. The most evident is that it is maṣdarī (infinitival), to correspond to the maṣdar, which is al-laghw, that is: "He does not hold you accountable for the laghw but for the earning". The second: that it is in the sense of «alladhī» (that which), and an omitted returning pronoun is necessary, that is: "kasabathu"; and what favours this is that its being in the sense of «alladhī» is more frequent than its being maṣdarī. The third: that it be an indefinite noun with a qualifier and the returning pronoun also omitted, and this is weak. There is an omission in this speech, its implied form being: "but He holds you accountable in your oaths for what your hearts have earned", so He omitted it owing to the indication of what precedes it.

Al-ḥalīm is from ḥalum (with ḍamma), yaḥlumu, when he pardons while having the power. As for ḥalima al-adīm (the hide), it is with kasra, and its imperfect is with fatḥa, yaḥlamu, that is: it spoiled and became pierced with holes. He said:

964 - فإنَّك والكتابَ إلى عليٍّ ... كدابِغَةٍ وقد حَلِمَ الأَديمُ
("You, and your writing to ʿAlī, are like a tanner after the hide has already rotted")

As for «ḥalama», that is, he saw in his sleep, it is with fatḥa. The maṣdar of the first is al-ḥilm with kasra. Al-Jaʿdī said:

965 - ولا خيرَ في حِلْمٍ إذا لم تَكُنْ له ... بوادرُ تَحْمي صَفْوَه أن يُكَدَّرا
("There is no good in forbearance unless it has quick outbursts that protect its clarity from being muddied")

The maṣdar of the second is al-ḥalam, with fatḥa on the lām; and the maṣdar of the third is al-ḥulum and al-ḥulm, with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, with ḍamma on the lām and with sukūn.

semin-durr:226-226.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لِّلَّذِينَ يُؤْلُونَ مِن نِّسَآئِهِمْ تَرَبُّصُ}: this is a clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar, and according to the view of al-Akhfash it is of the type verb and agent, since he does not require reliance. As for «من نسائهم», regarding this prepositional phrase there are eight possibilities. The first: that it is attached to «يُؤْلُون». Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: how is it made transitive with "min" when it is made transitive with "ʿalā"? I say: the specific oath has been given the sense of distancing, as if it had been said: "they distance themselves from their wives, swearing or taking an oath".» The second: that «ālā» is made transitive with «ʿalā» and with «min»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said it, reporting from others, that one says "ālā min imraʾatihi" and "ʿalā imraʾatihi". The third: that «min» stands in the place of «ʿalā», and this is the view of the Kufans. The fourth: that it stands in the place of «fī», and there is then an omitted muḍāf, that is: "on leaving intercourse with their wives" or "in leaving intercourse with their wives". The fifth: that «min» is redundant and the implied form is "yuʾlūna an yaʿtazilū nisāʾahum" (they swear to keep away from their wives). The sixth: that it is attached to an omitted word, the implied form being: "and for those who swear, from their wives, a waiting of four (months)", so it is attached to what the omitted «lahum» is attached to. The Shaykh implied it thus and ascribed it to al-Zamakhsharī, and there is room for consideration in it, for al-Zamakhsharī said: «It is possible that it be meant: "for them, from their wives, a waiting", as you say "lī minka kadhā".» His saying «lahum» did not intend that there is something omitted, namely the word «lahum»; he only intended to attach «min» to the "istiqrār" (settling) to which «lil-ladhīna» is attached; the utmost in it is that he brought the pronoun of «alladhīna» to clarify the meaning. And Abū al-Baqāʾ went in this direction, for he said: «And it was said: the origin is "ʿalā", and it is not permitted that "min" stand in the place of "ʿalā"; then "min" is attached to the meaning of settling», he meaning the settling to which His saying «lil-ladhīna» is attached. And even granting that the word «lahum» is implied and is intended, then it would be only a badal (substitute) of «lil-ladhīna» with repetition of the governor, or else His saying «lil-ladhīna yuʾlūna» would remain disconnected. In sum, its attachment to the settling is not evident. As for the Shaykh's implying, "wa-alladhīna yuʾlūna lahum min nisāʾihim tarabbuṣun", it is not so, because if «alladhīna» had come thus, not governed by the lām, what he claimed would be easy, but it came, as you see, governed by the lām. Then the Shaykh said: «All of this is weak and the Qur'an is to be held above it; it is attached to «yuʾlūna» only in one of two ways: either «min» is for causation, that is, they swear because of their wives; or it is given the sense of refraining, so that it is made transitive with «min», as if it had been said: "for those who refrain from their wives by ilāʾ".» These are two possibilities with the six preceding, which makes eight; and if you consider generally the giving of a sense (taḍmīn), they come to seven.

Al-īlāʾ is swearing, the maṣdar of ālā yūlī, like akrama yukrimu ikrāman, and the origin is «iʾlāʾ», so the second hamza was changed to yāʾ because of its being unvowelled and the kasra before it, like «īmān».

One says also taʾallā and ayta lā, on the pattern ifta ʿala, the origin being «iʾtalā», so the second was changed for the reason that has preceded.

The oath is called al-aliyya, al-alūwa, al-alwa and al-ilwa; and al-aliyya is pluralised as «alāyā», like ʿashiyya and ʿashāyā, and it is permissible that al-alūwa also be pluralised as «alāyā», like rakūba and rakāʾib. Kuthayyir ʿAzza said:

966 - قليلُ الأَلايا حافظٌ ليمينِه ... إذا صَدَرَتْ منه الأَلِيَّةُ بَرَّتِ
("Sparing of oaths, guarding his vow; when an oath issues from him it is fulfilled")

It has already preceded how aliyya and alāyā are inflected, at His saying {نَّغْفِرْ لَكُمْ خَطَايَاكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 58], the plural of khaṭīʾa.

Al-tarabbuṣ is waiting, and it is the reversal of al-taṣabbur. He said:

967 - تَرَبَّصْ بها رَيْب المنونِ لعلَّها ... تُطَلَّقُ يوماً أو يموتُ حليلُها
("Wait for the misfortunes of fate with her; perhaps she will one day be divorced, or her husband will die")

As for the annexation of al-tarabbuṣ to the months, there are two views. One: that it is a case of annexing the maṣdar to its object, by extension of the adverb until it became a direct object and was annexed to, in this state. The second: that the event is annexed to the adverb without extension, so the annexation is in the sense of «fī», and this is a Kufan position; and the agent is omitted, its implied form being: "their waiting four months".

His saying: {فَآءُوا}: the alif of «fāʾa» is changed from yāʾ, for they say fāʾa yafīʾu fayʾatan, meaning he returned. Al-fayʾ is the shade, because of its returning after the decline of the sun. ʿAlqama said:

968 - فقلتُ لها فِيئي فما تَسْتَفِزُّني ... ذَواتُ العيونِ والبنانِ المُخَضَّبِ
("So I said to her: return! For I am not moved by women with beautiful eyes and henna-stained fingertips")

semin-durr:215-215.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَاذَا يُنْفِقُونَ}: It has already preceded that «ماذا» has six uses, and the verification of the matter is at His saying {مَاذَآ أَرَادَ الله بهذا} [al-Baqara: 26]. Here «ماذا» may be like a single noun with the sense of the interrogative, so it is a fronted object; and «ما» and «ذا» may be (separate), with «ما» a mubtadaʾ and «ذا» its khabar, and «ذا» is a relative: «ينفقون» is its ṣila and the returning pronoun is omitted. «ماذا» suspends the asking, so it is in the position of the second object, and its verification has already preceded in His saying: {سَلْ بني إِسْرَائِيلَ كَمْ آتَيْنَاهُم} [al-Baqara: 211]. «ينفقون» came in the wording of the third person because the agent of the verb before it is a third-person pronoun in «يسألونك»; and "mādhā nunfiqu" (what do we spend) is permitted in speech, as it is permitted to say "aqsama Zaydun la-yaḍribanna" and "la-aḍribanna"; more explanation of this will come at His saying {يَسْأَلُونَكَ مَاذَآ أُحِلَّ لَهُمْ} [al-Māʾida: 4] in al-Māʾida.

[His saying]: {قُلْ مَآ أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِّنْ خَيْرٍ}: in «ما» two views are permitted. The first: that it is conditional, which is the apparent view, to agree with what follows it; so «ما» is in the position of the accusative as a fronted object whose fronting is obligatory, because it has the head of the sentence. «أنفقْتُمْ» is in the position of the jussive by the condition, and «مِنْ خيرٍ» has had its i'rab given at His saying {مَا نَنسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ} [al-Baqara: 106].

His saying: {فَلِلْوَالِدَيْنِ} is the apodosis of the condition. This preposition and its genitive noun is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "so its place of expenditure is for the parents", so it is attached to an omitted element, either a single word or a clause, according to what was mentioned of the disagreement in what passed. The clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of the condition. The second: that «ما» is a relative, «أنفقتم» is its ṣila, and the returning pronoun is omitted because of the completeness of the conditions, i.e. "that which you spent". The fāʾ is redundant in the khabar, which is the preposition and its genitive noun. Abū l-Baqāʾ said on this view: "«ومِنْ خيرٍ» is a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun."

They asked only about what is spent, so how were they answered with the explanation of the place of expenditure, that is, of those spent upon? There are answers to this, among them: that the verse has an omission, namely the one spent upon, which was omitted, the implied form being: "what do they spend, and to whom do they give it?", so the answer came for both: He answered about what is spent by His saying «مِنْ خيرٍ», and about those spent upon by His saying «فللوالدَيْن» and what follows it. Among them: that «ماذا» is a question about the place of expenditure with an omitted annexed word, its implied form being: "the place of expenditure of what do they spend?" Among them: that he omitted from the first the mention of the place of expenditure and from the second the mention of what is spent, and both are intended; something of that has preceded in the saying of the Exalted {وَمَثَلُ الذين كَفَرُواْ كَمَثَلِ} [al-Baqara: 171]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "His saying {مَآ أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِّنْ خَيْرٍ} includes the explanation of what they spend, which is every good thing; and the speech was built on what is more important, which is the explanation of the place of expenditure, because spending is not counted unless it falls in its proper place. [He said]:

925 - إنَّ الصنيعة لا تكونُ صنيعةً ... حتى يُصابَ بها طريقُ المَصْنَعِ
(A kindness is not a kindness until it reaches the proper path of the doing of it.)

As for His saying {وَمَا تَفْعَلُواْ}, «ما» there is only conditional, because its jussive effect is apparent, unlike the first. ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, read «وما يفعلوا» with the yāʾ, in the third person; it may be an iltifāt from the second person, or it may be from implying (a subject) because the context indicates it, i.e. "and whatever people do"."

semin-durr:216-216.t:
It was read: {كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ القتال}: with «كَتَب» as active, its subject being a pronoun for Allah the Exalted, and with «القتال» in the accusative.

His saying: {وَهُوَ كُرْهٌ}: this is the wāw of ḥāl, and the clause after it is in the position of the accusative as that. The apparent view is that «هو» returns to the fighting. It was said: it returns to the maṣdar understood from «كَتَب», i.e. "its prescription and its obligation". The majority read «كُرْهٌ» with ḍamma on the kāf, and al-Sulamī read it with fatḥa. It was said: the two have one meaning, i.e. two maṣdars like ḍaʿf and ḍuʿf; al-Zajjāj said it and al-Zamakhsharī followed him. [Translator's note: the source spells the name «الزمشخري», a slip for «الزمخشري».] It was said: the one with ḍamma is a passive participle and the one with fatḥa is the maṣdar. It was said: the one with fatḥa has the sense of ikrāh (compulsion); al-Zamakhsharī said it in directing the reading of al-Sulamī, except that this is of the category of a maṣdar coming with the augmentations dropped, which is not analogical. It was said: the one with fatḥa is what a man is forced to do, and the one with ḍamma is what he himself dislikes.

If al-karh and al-kurh are a maṣdar, then an interpretation is needed by which predicating it of «هو» is permissible, and that interpretation is either on the omission of an annexed word, i.e. "fighting is a thing of dislike", or by way of exaggeration, or by its occurrence in the place of a passive participle. If we say that «كُرْهاً» with ḍamma is a passive participle, none of this is needed. «لكم» is in the position of the nominative because it is an adjective of «كُره», so it is attached to an omitted element, i.e. "dislike that is for you".

His saying: {وعسى أَن تَكْرَهُواْ}: «عسى» is a past verb transferred to the composing (inshāʾ) of hope and apprehension. It raises the subject and puts the predicate in the accusative, and its predicate is only an imperfect verb joined to «أَنْ». It may come as an explicit noun, as in his saying:

926 - أَكْثَرْتَ في العَذْلِ مُلِحَّاً دائماً ... لا تُكْثِرَنْ إني عَسَيْتُ صائِماً
(You have been excessive in blame, insisting constantly; do not be excessive, for I may be fasting.)

and al-Zabbāʾ said: «عسى الغُوَيْرُ أَبُؤسا» ("Perhaps the little cave (will bring) misfortunes"). Its predicate may also be bare of «أَنْ», as in his saying:

927 - عسى فَرَجٌ يأتي به اللهُ إنه ... له كلَّ يومٍ في خَلِقَتِهِ أَمْرُ
(Perhaps relief will come, brought by Allah; every day, in His creation, He has a matter.)

and another said:

928 - عَسَى الكربُ الذي أَمْسَيْتَ فيه ... يكونُ وراءَه فرجٌ قَرِيبُ
(Perhaps the distress you have come to be in will have near relief behind it.)

and another said:

929 - فأمَّا كَيِّسٌ فَنَجا ولكِنْ ... عَسَى يَغْتَرُّ بي حَمِقٌ لَئيمُ
(As for a clever man, he escaped; but perhaps a foolish, base man will be deceived by me.)

It is complete (tāmma) when it is predicated of «أَنْ» or «أنَّ», because the two take the place of its subject and predicate. The sounder view is that it is a verb, not a particle, because of the attachment of the overt nominative pronouns to it; its pattern is «فَعَل» with fatḥa on the ʿayn, and kasra on its ʿayn is permitted when it is predicated of a first- or second-person pronoun or the feminine plural nūn, which is the reading of Nāfiʿ, and it will come. It is not conjugated but obligatorily stays in the past. The difference in meaning between apprehension and hope by it is that hope concerns what is loved and apprehension concerns what is disliked. «عسى» from Allah the Exalted is obligatory (wājiba), because hope and apprehension are impossible in His case. It was said: every «عسى» in the Qur'an is for certainty, meaning occurrence, except the saying of the Exalted {عسى رَبُّهُ إِن طَلَّقَكُنَّ} [al-Taḥrīm: 5] to the end of the verse. In this verse it is not defective (nāqiṣa) needing a predicate, but complete, because it is predicated of «أَنْ», and it has already preceded that it takes the place of the two objects (subject and predicate) after it.

Al-Ḥawfī claimed that «أَن تكرهوا» is in the position of the accusative, but this is not possible except by a remote affectation.

His saying: {وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ}: about this clause there are two views. The most apparent: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, even though a ḥāl from an indefinite noun without one of the known conditions is rare. The second: that it is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of «شيئاً». The wāw entered the clause that occurs only because its form is the form of a ḥāl; so just as the wāw enters it as a ḥāl, it enters it as an adjective; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this. Similar to that is what al-Zamakhsharī permitted in His saying: {وَمَآ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍ إِلاَّ وَلَهَا كِتَابٌ مَّعْلُومٌ}, for he made «ولها كتابٌ» an adjective of «قرية». He said: "The analogy was that this wāw not come between them, as in His saying: {وَمَآ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَرْيَةٍ إِلاَّ لَهَا مُنذِرُونَ}; it came between them only to emphasize the attachment of the adjective to the described, and like what is said of the ḥāl: 'Zayd came to me, a garment upon him' and 'and a garment upon him'." What Abū l-Baqāʾ permitted here and al-Zamakhsharī there is the opinion of Ibn Jinnī, and the rest of the grammarians differ from him.

semin-durr:227-227.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {عَزَمُواْ الطلاق}: there are two possibilities for the accusative of «الطلاق». One: that it is by dropping of the preposition, because «ʿazama» is made transitive with «ʿalā». He said:

969 - عَزَمْتُ على إقامةِ ذي صباحٍ ... لأمرٍ ما يُسَوَّدُ مَنْ يسَودُ
("I resolved upon staying on for a morning for a purpose; by some purpose is whoever becomes a chief made chief")

The second: that «ʿazama» is given the sense of «nawā» (to intend), so that it is accusative as a direct object.

Al-ʿazm is the tying of the heart and its determination: ʿazama yaʿzimu ʿazman and ʿuzman, with fatḥa and ḍamma, and ʿazīmatan and ʿizāman with kasra. It is also used in the sense of the oath: "ʿazamtu ʿalayka la-tafʿalanna".

Al-ṭalāq is the loosening of the tie; one says ṭalaqat (with fatḥa on the lām), taṭluqu, so she is ṭāliq and ṭāliqa. Al-Aʿshā said:

970 - أيا جارتا بيني فإنَّكِ طالِقَهْ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
("O my neighbour-wife, depart, for you are divorced…")

Thaʿlab reported «ṭaluqat» with ḍamma, and al-Akhfash denied it. Al-ṭalāq may be a maṣdar or a noun of the maṣdar, which is al-taṭlīq.

His saying: {فَإِنَّ الله}: its apparent sense is that it is the apodosis of the condition. The Shaykh said: «It seems that the apodosis is omitted, that is: "let them carry it out". ʿAbd Allāh read "فإن فاؤوا فيهنَّ" and Ubayy read "فيها", the pronoun being for the months.

The reading of the majority apparently means that the returning (fayʾa) and the divorce occur only after the four months have passed. But since al-Zamakhsharī followed the position of Abū Ḥanīfa, namely that the returning is within the period of four months, and the preceding reading supports him, he needed to interpret the verse with what is given here verbatim: «If you say: what is the place of the fāʾ if the returning is before the end of the period of waiting? I say: a sound place, because His saying "فإنْ فاؤوا، وإنْ عَزَموا" is a detailing of His saying "للذين يُؤْلُون مِنْ نسائِهِم", and the detailing follows what is detailed, as you say "I am your guest this month; if I praise you, I will stay with you to its end, and if not, I will not stay except for the time I take to move on".» The Shaykh said: «It is not correct, because what he gave as an example is not a parallel to the verse. Do you not see that the example has a report about the one whose condition is detailed, namely his saying "I am your guest this month", and after the two conditions the answer is stated explicitly, indicating the difference in what the verb of the consequence relates to; but the verse is not so, because those who swear are not reported about, and no ruling is attributed to them; what is judged is their waiting, and the meaning is: the waiting of the swearers for four months is legislated for them after their oath; then He said: "if they return, and if they resolve" — the apparent sense is that it follows the waiting of the legislated period in its entirety, because the returning occurs within it, and the resolve upon divorce after it, since a differing restriction is not indicated by the wording. What fits the verse is that you say: "For the guest, three days of hospitality; if he stays we are generous and preferential, and if he resolves to leave, he may leave", so what first comes to mind is that the two conditions are implied after his being honoured.»

semin-durr:228-228.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والمطلقات يَتَرَبَّصْنَ}: mubtadaʾ and khabar. Is this clause of the type of a khabar in the place of a command, that is, "let them wait", or on its own sense? Two views. The Kufans said: its wording is a command on the implication of the lām of command; and whoever took it on its own sense implied: "the ruling for divorced women is that they wait", so he omitted «ruling» from the first and the maṣdarī «an» from the second, and this is very far-fetched.

«Tarabbaṣa» is made transitive by itself because it is in the sense of «intaẓara» (to wait). This verse admits two possibilities. One: that the object of al-tarabbuṣ is omitted, and this is the apparent view, its implied form being: "they wait for marriage" or "for husbands", and «ثلاثة قروء» on this basis is accusative as an adverbial, because it is a number noun annexed to an adverbial. The second: that the object is «ثلاثةَ قروءٍ» itself, that is, they wait for three qurūʾ to pass.

As for His saying: {بِأَنْفُسِهِنَّ}, it admits two possibilities. One, and it is the apparent one: that it is attached to «يتربَّصْنَ», the bāʾ being causal, that is, "by reason of themselves"; and mentioning the selves, or the detached pronoun, in a construction like this is obligatory, and it is not permitted to bring the attached pronoun; were it said in its like "al-Hindātu yatarabbaṣna bihinna", it would not be permitted, lest the verb of the detached pronoun become transitive to its attached pronoun, other than in the chapters in which that is permitted.

The second: that «بأنفسهنّ» is tawkīd (emphasis) for the attached nominative pronoun, which is the nūn, with the bāʾ redundant in the emphasis, for it is permitted to add it in nafs and ʿayn when they are used to emphasise. You say: jāʾa Zaydun nafsuhu and bi-nafsihi, ʿaynuhu and bi-ʿaynihi. On this basis it is not attached to anything, because it is redundant. It is not to be said: it cannot be emphasis for the pronoun, because it would have to be emphasised by a detached nominative pronoun, since an attached nominative pronoun is not emphasised by nafs and ʿayn except after being emphasised by the detached nominative pronoun, so that one says "Zaydun jāʾa huwa nafsuhu ʿaynuhu"; for this emphasised word left its original state when it was governed by the redundant bāʾ and resembled the dispensable items (faḍalāt), and so went out of the rule of the followers (tawābiʿ) and what is binding in others was not binding in it.
